Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, whoop, the company behind the popular screenless wearable trackers, has launched a social network for users who like sharing their exercise details and fitness efforts called whoop humans. " Members can share their fitness data on the social network, including their sleep, recovery, strain and activities information. Well, Will Ahmed, the CEO of Whoop, described it as the "most verifiably human network ever launched. It's a rather unusual name, so you might be wondering how the company decided on it. In all cases, the data comes from a Whoop wearable. Sebagaimana diketahui, whoop already has teams, which connects users through groups and leaderboards. The idea is for members to be able to congratulate each other when they reach their goals or to be able to remind a friend to take it easy if they see the other's "Recovery" data is low. But the new social network lets users follow friends and family directly to comment and react to their posts. The company envisions a social network, wherein people can check in on each other based on their progress. Hard to imagine most people taking an interest in another's fitness information, but people who are very much into fitness might see value in the social network.

" They can keep those Moments private, however, and, thankfully, they can choose which workout types or achievements appear on the social network. #2. Israel’s VCs see opportunity for challengers in Nvidia’s turmoil

📅 13 Nov 2026

Israel’s VCs see opportunity for challengers in Nvidia’s turmoil

Tanggal: 13 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://techcrunch.com/2026/11/13/israels-vcs-see-opportunity-for-challengers-in-nvidias-turmoil/

Diungkapkan bahwa former nvidia ceo jensen huang’s resignation has been received with worry in israel, the company’s “second home,” as huang described it in 2023. The company’s importance flows both ways, as the semiconductor giant has provided a major boost to Israel’s economic forecasts in recent years.

Diungkapkan bahwa intel, microsoft and many homegrown startups also conduct a sizable share of their r&d in israel. But owing to Nvidia’s stronghold on AI given the centrality of its GPUs for training LLMs and using them, many in the country are wondering how much of a reshuffle will result from its leadership crisis.

Diungkapkan bahwa as with everything at nvidia, huang drove the company to acquire israeli chipmaker mellanox for $6. 9 billion in 2019 and use the company as the base for its largest R&D facility outside of the U. S. Nvidia also made plans to build a multibillion-dollar campus in northern Israel.

“Jensen brought Nvidia to Israel with the acquisition of Mellanox, so there is a strong positive sentiment towards Nvidia and Jensen in Israel’s tech community,” Israeli repeat cybersecurity entrepreneur Pavel Gurvich told TechCrunch.

Diungkapkan bahwa beyond the 6,000 locals nvidia employs, the bigger question is whether the company will remain as committed to israel with someone else at the helm. As a result, his line of succession is being observed just as closely by those who hope the company continues to do so as by those who don’t want it to happen.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the latter have already gathered that they may be in for disappointment. In a 2023 interview that is now doing the rounds on X, interim CEO Colette Kress had declared that as Nvidia’s CFO, she typically started her day “with Israel meetings, and only then continue[d] to California. ”.

Kress may not remain in charge in the long run, but the many names floated for the role include two Israelis, Apple’s Johny Srouji and Nvidia’s Michael Kagan — although they’re not at the top of the still quite tentative list.

Berdasarkan laporan, regardless of who gets chosen, huang’s successor will likely have less of a grip on nvidia and the tech industry as a whole. But investors don’t think that would cause demand for Nvidia’s product to fade away.

Sebagaimana diketahui, according to yanai oron, a general partner at vertex ventures israel, “slower decisions at nvidia could give competitors an opening, but if that uncertainty also slows ai spending, they could end up with a bigger share of a smaller opportunity. ”.

Diungkapkan bahwa nvidia has been responsible for a vast share of the spending in the global ai industry. Under Huang’s leadership, the company used its cash reserves to massively invest across the spectrum, both in companies and in its own next-generation chips.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, such an empire may not be doomed to fall with its architect’s ouster, but it does seem less likely to become a full-on monopoly. According to Adi Levanon, a founder and managing partner at Selah Ventures, “[Huang’s] departure doesn’t dismantle Nvidia’s technology or ecosystem, but it could give competitors more room to shape what comes next. ”.

And now that companies globally are deploying increasingly demanding AI agents into their workflows, there’s been a lot of interest — and some venture capital — flowing into developers of AI-specific chips and inference software that could compete with Nvidia’s.

“These challengers now have a window to prove a different approach delivers better economics; a leadership change alone won’t win them the business,” Levanon said.

#4. More autonomy, fewer NDAs: Volunteers have new requests for brain implant trials

📅 13 Nov 2026

More autonomy, fewer NDAs: Volunteers have new requests for brain implant trials

Tanggal: 13 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.technologyreview.com/2026/11/13/1148474/more-autonomy-fewer-ndas-volunteers-have-new-requests-for-brain-implant-trials/

People with experimental brain implants are pushing for more recognition and respect.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, scientists have been working on ways to decode brain activity for decades. Teams have developed brain implants that can be used to control robotic limbs and computers, and even to “speak. ”.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the people who volunteer for trials of those devices play a vital role in that research, and they ought to be recognized for their contributions, says ian burkhart, who had one implanted in his own brain back in 2014. He’s been working on a set of guidelines for researchers developing brain-computer interfaces (BCIs).

Diungkapkan bahwa ethics guidelines for clinical trials already exist. “These are people who have a device embedded in their brain, are in trials sometimes for years and years … [and contribute] a significant investment of time, of the body, and of intellectual effort. But BCI trials are different, says Jennifer Chandler, a professor of law and neuroethics at the University of Ottawa who also worked on the guidelines. ”.

Sebagaimana diketahui, burkhart was left paralyzed from the chest down following a diving accident in 2010, when he was 19 years old. Around four years later, he volunteered to become the first person to trial a brain implant designed for hand control.

Berdasarkan laporan, he had an array of 96 electrodes inserted into the part of his brain that controls movement. The electrodes were connected to a computer via a cable that essentially plugged into his head. Algorithms on the computer were designed to interpret those signals and deliver them to another sleeve of electrodes worn on Burkhart’s arm, allowing him to control it.

Berdasarkan laporan, the first movements were small, but burkhart was ultimately able to use the system to pour beads from bottles, move small and delicate objects, and even play guitar hero, if only during lab visits. It was a scientific breakthrough.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, burkhart took part in two years-long clinical trials over the seven-and-a-half-year period he had the electrode array implanted in his brain. “It was a fantastic experience,” he says. “But there’s certainly some things that, knowing what I know now, I would want to do a little differently. ”.

Sebagaimana diketahui, in 2022, burkhart cofounded bci pioneers coalition—an organization through which people who have taken part in bci trials can share their experiences, both with each other and with researchers. Over the last year, members of the group have been developing a set of guidelines based on those experiences. The idea is to help academics, clinicians, and companies run ethical trials that respect participants’ autonomy.

Diungkapkan bahwa the guidelines, published on tuesday, lay out a list of recommendations that fall within 13 categories. One, for example, focuses on recognizing and compensating trial participants. During the trials that Burkhart participated in, “I was going into the lab two or three days a week, for four hours at a time,” he recalls. “That’s [easily] a part-time job if you just count the hours you’re putting in. ”.

Diungkapkan bahwa as the trial progressed, burkhart says, he learned more and was able to give more constructive feedback on what was working and what wasn’t. He says he was a key member of the research team. Others who find themselves in a similar position might appreciate being listed as a coauthor on scientific publications or publicly named as a research collaborator, he says. Burkhart and his colleagues acknowledge that not everyone will want this, however.

Berdasarkan laporan, the guidelines also address the thorny question of privacy. That’s important: The public will always be interested in cutting-edge biotechnologies like these—and the guidelines say researchers also have a duty to prepare participants for the possibility of media attention. In some cases, it might be difficult to completely conceal the identity of trial participants.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, things get even more complicated when it comes to the privacy of participants’ brain data. Burkhart wasn’t too bothered about that in his case, where scientists were collecting neural activity related to movement. Research teams will need to access, analyze, and—at least temporarily—store this data. But people who have brain implants designed for turning thoughts into words might feel differently.

Berdasarkan laporan, the guidelines state that brain data “should be understood as the participant’s personal information. ” They are pushing for participants to be able to access their own brain data whenever they want—something that has not always been possible—and want to make sure people aren’t prevented from sharing it with their own doctors because of embargoes or nondisclosure agreements (NDAs) designed to keep findings under wraps from competitors.

Sebagaimana diketahui, “it’s not super common for there to be firm ndas within a lot of the trials,” says burkhart. “But it’s something where we want to make sure that that does not happen. ”.

Berdasarkan laporan, the guidelines also address what comes after a trial. (And we’re talking about brain surgery here. Around five years after Burkhart had his device implanted, the research team ran into some issues with funding. When we last spoke a few years ago, he recalled how he was told he would have to have the implant removed and could have it put back in once the team had secured funding. ).

Diungkapkan bahwa ultimately, he kept the implant until 2021, when it was removed after an infection started to develop at the point where the cable led into his scalp. But losing the device after all those years was difficult; he’d regained the ability to move his arm—and then lost it again.

Berdasarkan laporan, rita leggett, an australian woman who had a device implanted in her brain to treat her epilepsy, has said she felt she “became one” with her implant. When the company that made it went bust two years later, the device was removed against her will—an act ethicists have described as a potential breach of human rights.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, researchers should instead commit to maintaining brain devices for a “reasonable period” after a trial ends, according to the guidelines. Participants should be given plenty of time to prepare for the surgery to remove it. And researchers should set aside extra funds to support trial participants who have to do that.

Berdasarkan laporan, some of the guidelines are vague and may overlap with existing ethics standards. They don’t all spell out explicit solutions. The team hopes to grow and expand on the guidelines over time. They were also developed with feedback from a small group of individuals—the number of people living with BCIs is still very low. Burkhart also plans to discuss them with researchers at an upcoming neuroscience conference.

Berdasarkan laporan, “this is a living document, and this is version one,” says chandler. “It’s just the starting point. ”.

#7. What Is T-Mix? Navigating T-Mobile’s All-New Phone Plans and Perk Scheme

📅 12 Nov 2026

What Is T-Mix? Navigating T-Mobile’s All-New Phone Plans and Perk Scheme

Tanggal: 12 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.cnet.com/tech/mobile/t-mobile-new-t-mix-phone-plans/

Our gifting experts are obsessively searching for holiday gifts that are unique, thoughtful and suitable for any budget.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, our expert, award-winning staff selects the products we cover and rigorously researches and tests our top picks. If you buy through our links, we may earn a commission.

With a new system of "Picks," T-Mobile lets customers mix and match mobile add-ons.

Diungkapkan bahwa t-mobile is remixing its unlimited phone plans and introducing a structure where customers choose which services, like streaming video subscriptions or phone financing, apply to their accounts. Called T-Mix, the lineup is available now and includes four core plans that include “Picks” that can be mixed and matched every 90 days.

Berdasarkan laporan, “t-mobile and [other carriers] have really built a ‘good/better/best’ world” where customers choose prepackaged plans, allan samson, t-mobile chief marketing officer, said during a call with cnet. “We’re going to blow that whole thing up, and you get to individually curate every experience you want. ”.

Diungkapkan bahwa much like with verizon’s current plans, t-mobile’s new offerings let customers pick and choose the perks they want rather than reserving some perks for certain plan tiers, as it had with its former experience plan options. If you wanted a perk such as Hulu streaming, you had to pay up for the pricier Experience Beyond 2. 0 plan. Conversely, even if you picked the Beyond plan for another reason, like unlimited mobile hotspot data, you still got Hulu whether you watched it or not.

Diungkapkan bahwa each of the new t-mix plans includes a core set of high-speed data, hotspot data, video streaming speeds and international options. On top of that – and the feature that gives T-Mix its name – is a selection of Picks, which work like a type of currency to choose perks like streaming services, game passes, and services like DoorDash or T-Satellite. Picks can also go toward financing a new phone.

Sebagaimana diketahui, t-mix replaces the existing experience 2. 0 plans for new customers, though existing customers can stay on their plans.

Berdasarkan laporan, despite the modular nature of picks, t-mobile is still sticking with its one-plan-fits-all policy for accounts with multiple lines. Unlike Verizon and AT&T, where each family member can have their own plan, everyone needs to agree on which T-Mix base to start from: Standard, More, Loaded and T-Mix Saver. The number of Picks you get depends on the plan and the number of lines on the account.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the standard plan includes 50gb of high-speed 5g data, unlimited hotspot data at 3g speeds, unlimited international data while traveling in canada and mexico at 2g speeds, unlimited texting in more than 215 countries and up to 480p (sd) streaming resolution. A single line includes one Pick.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the more plan includes unlimited high-speed data, up to 60gb of high-speed hotspot data (which drops down to an unlimited amount at 3g speeds), 15gb of high-speed data in canada and mexico (then unlimited at 256kbps), up to 5gb of high-speed data when traveling internationally (then unlimited at 256kbps) and up to 4k (uhd) streaming resolution. A single line on More includes two picks.

Berdasarkan laporan, the loaded plan also includes unlimited high-speed data, up to 250gb of hotspot data (then unlimited at 3g speeds), 30gb of high-speed data in canada and mexico (then unlimited at 256kbps), up to 15gb high-speed data when traveling (and down to 256kbps unlimited after reaching that cap) and up to 4k (uhd) streaming resolution. On the Loaded plan, you can also connect a cellular-enabled device, such as a smartwatch or tablet, for $5 an item. A single line includes three Picks.

For those who want just basic phone service, the T-Mix Saver plan includes the same features as the Standard plan, but does not include Picks and is limited to two lines.

Diungkapkan bahwa all plans include unlimited texting when traveling in more than 215 countries, long-distance calling at $0. 50 a minute and T-Mobile’s Basic Scam Shield service.

For each plan, you can choose to finance a new phone using T-Mobile’s Standard 36-month term or the recently introduced Flex 36-month commitment that rolls in all of the upfront costs.

Diungkapkan bahwa pricing (with autopay and not including taxes and fees) for the standard plan starts at $55 for a single line, jumps to $85 for two lines (or $42. 33 a line). 50 a line) and then increases to $100 for three lines (or $33. Additional lines cost $15 more apiece.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the more plan starts at $75 for one line, then goes to $130 for two lines and $155 for three lines. Additional lines add $25 each to the monthly cost.

Berdasarkan laporan, the loaded plan is $95 for a single line, $160 for two lines and $200 for three lines. Adding more Loaded lines costs $40 each.

Berdasarkan laporan, the saver plan costs $45 for a single line and $80 for two lines (the maximum number allowed). T-Mobile is currently running a promotion that brings those prices down to $30 and $65 if you switch from another provider and bring along your phone number.

An account on the first three plans can have up to 12 lines.

One advantage of T-Mobile’s now-old Experience plans was the simplicity of knowing that if you moved up to a higher tier such as Experience Beyond, you’d get a specific set of additional perks.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, picks gives you the flexibility to only activate perks you’ll actually use, but working out which to opt for is a bit complex. With Picks, there are two components at play: How many Picks you get on your account, and when you can change them. It sounds low-key chaotic on the surface, but it will start to make more sense, I promise.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, t-mobile assigns a pick value to the perks it’s offering. For example, one Pick could get you Netflix Standard with ads or the DashPass service by DoorDash. If you want an Apple Music Individual or Google AI Pro subscription, that would use two Picks.

Higher-tier offerings such as Netflix Standard and Xbox Game Pass Ultimate are three Picks each, while Netflix Premium and ESPN Unlimited are four Picks.

Those are all services offered by T-Mobile partners, and can change over time (more on this in a moment).

Sebagaimana diketahui, t-mobile also has its own picks services. T-Satellite can be activated with one Pick, and so can the company’s new Optimized Video Calling service, which gives video calls a higher data priority for better quality.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, if you’re looking to buy a new phone, you could get one for between one and three picks depending on the device — in other words, you can forgo fancy add-on perks to get discounts on a new handset. Phone picks automatically inherit the Flex 36-month financing term.

Berdasarkan laporan, to give picks a real-world analogy, picture a restaurant buffet. You’re given a plate that’s sized based on how many Picks are available to your account. A Standard plan with one line would have the smallest plate (one Pick), while a Loaded plan with four lines would have a much larger plate (11 Picks).

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the picks on an account can be pooled depending on the group’s needs. A family of four on the Loaded plan, for example, might decide to get Netflix Premium to watch movies without ads (4 Picks), DashPass to save money on food deliveries (1 Pick), Xbox Game Pass Premium (2 Picks) and Pandora Plus (1 Pick) for entertainment and then a new phone for Mom (3 Picks).

Diungkapkan bahwa the number of picks you get depends on the plan and how many lines it includes. Not using a Pick doesn’t lower the plan price, and you’re not able to pay more for extra Picks (like adding a Verizon perk, for example) aside from moving to a more expensive plan.

Also, Picks are separate from the company’s perks such as T-Mobile Tuesdays promotions, discounts on hotels and rental cars, Delta premium in-flight drinks and MLB TV.

Diungkapkan bahwa the next picks component is timing. Every 90 calendar days, you can switch your Picks. Did you burn through all the shows you wanted to watch on Hulu? At the next Picks window, you can switch it for another option, or dump some 1- and 2-value Picks and pool them to get a new phone.

Sebagaimana diketahui, if you’re in the middle of the schedule and want to pick up netflix to see what everyone is talking about in season four of the diplomat, you can do that by canceling an existing pick service and adding the streaming service for a fee, which samson said would be in the $10 to $15 range. Or, at any time you can move up to a plan with more Picks (such as from More to Loaded).

The exceptions to that timing are T-Mobile’s Picks; you could turn on T-Satellite if you know you’re going remote backpacking, as long as a Pick is available in your plan.

#13. Silicon Valley claims to know the future. So why did it get the midterms so wrong?

📅 13 Nov 2026

Silicon Valley claims to know the future. So why did it get the midterms so wrong?

Tanggal: 13 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.technologyreview.com/2026/11/13/1148498/silicon-valley-claims-to-know-the-future-so-why-did-it-get-the-midterms-so-wrong/

Tech executives traded their reputations as visionaries for short-term political gain.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the self-styled visionaries of silicon valley, leaders like openai chief executive sam altman and spacex boss elon musk, have built careers claiming to see the future. Long-term vision is currency: Meta’s Mark Zuckerberg built a 10-year road map for Facebook in 2016, and Google famously told investors before its public offering that it was unconcerned with short-term results. And yet there they all were, a mere five weeks before the midterm elections, gathered at the White House to smile for photos with President Trump and sign on to his “Super Intelligence” agenda.

Sebagaimana diketahui, even by the diminished standards of today’s corporate governance, this was a shockingly foolish decision. Despite dozens of polls showing a rising tide of anti-Trump sentiment and bipartisan rejection of AI and data centers, the futurists of the tech elite cast aside long-term corporate interests for short-term political favor. And now, their industry is very squarely in the new victors’ crosshairs.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, for an industry obsessed with pattern recognition, their decision to lash themselves to president trump has proved to be a catastrophic misreading of the political landscape. Now, not only have they jeopardized their companies’ fates, but they’ve also raised questions about their vision and judgment.

Diungkapkan bahwa the people who work for them are just as confused as the rest of us. ” Most employees share concern about potential anti-data-center legislation and are curious how leadership will adjust to a Democratic Washington, DC. Zuckerberg has yet to address the results internally, while an employee at another AI firm said that “leadership has been pretty silent on Slack. Tech workers I’ve spoken to at OpenAI, Meta, and other firms have noted an absence of commentary from their leaders post-election. But more than anything, they don’t understand how their bosses didn’t see what was so blindingly obvious to everyone else.

Sebagaimana diketahui, in silicon valley, the gretzkyism “skate to where the puck is going, not where it has been” is a management maxim; it preaches anticipation and foresight over reactiveness to the present moment. Tech entrepreneurs love a good “pivot,” and companies that can’t change with the times get disrupted and die.

Sebagaimana diketahui, which is why i find it so strange that zuckerberg, openai cofounder greg brockman, and so many of silicon valley’s other prominent ai leaders and venture capitalists have put themselves in a potentially inescapable political bind. In going all in on President Trump’s cultural and business agenda instead of playing both sides of the aisle as corporate America usually does, they’ve built identities they may not be able to pivot out of. Will anyone really believe that Palantir CEO Alex Karp is suddenly progressive after a year of promising “violence and death to our enemies” and telling investors that the company is “completely anti-woke”?.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, i believe this is less a surprise than a very public exposure of a fundamental reality: that tech’s most visible leaders are not all-knowing visionary masterminds after all. Insights about social media or artificial intelligence do not make Zuckerberg or Altman experts on politics, the economy, or much else outside of technology. The instant gratification of presidential access, subsidies, and a say in their own regulation blinded them to the basics of political math that they clearly did not understand.

Diungkapkan bahwa there’s a reason the chief executives of chase, boeing, and other fortune 500 staples don’t go on podcasts to talk about “masculine energy,” or call the president from the stage of a maga-friendly ai summit to label fears about ai a “hoax” and a “scam. ” This is the learned wisdom of decades operating in an environment where the customer changes every four years but contracts run for 10. Most companies play to both sides of the aisle because they know that their business models and multibillion-dollar projects must outlast the current administration. Instead, Big Tech tied itself to Trump and made its most important goals and investments—many related to grid access and data center permits—immediate targets for Democrats.

Berdasarkan laporan, in tech, you can always sunset a feature or update some code. ” As for whether employees expect the company to do a strategic postmortem? “Facebook has never really done that. As one Meta employee who has worked closely with Zuckerberg put it, “Mark is a long-term thinker, but he never charts a plan of how to get there. But in politics, there is no undo button for failures that change public perception. The tech elites’ decision to visibly align their businesses with a temporary movement has left them no credible way to pivot now that the climate has changed. It’s spray and pray and see what happens. ”.

Sebagaimana diketahui, “move fast and break things” might work in a startup, but it’s a terrible strategy for building reputational goodwill. Previous technological leaps, like the rollout of fiber-optic technology and wireless infrastructure, avoided partisan politics. But by kowtowing to the Trump administration, Silicon Valley made artificial intelligence a culture-war issue. Now, when citizens vote on data center proposals from California to Florida, they are no longer considering only technical or economic concerns, but political ones.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, tech leaders didn’t see this coming because they were too focused on the urgency of the ai race to understand how reputational damage could undermine the intangible goodwill—and ultimately the very tangible infrastructure—necessary to win it. The industry’s misreading of the moment has already punctured one myth Silicon Valley holds dear: that its leaders can always see what’s next.

"The Board has full confidence in Colette and the leadership team, and we expect the company's operations, customer commitments and product roadmap to continue without interruption," newly-minted NVIDIA board chair Harvey Jones said in a release announcing Thursday's news.

Diungkapkan bahwa kress is a relative unknown, but is taking lead of nvidia at tumultuous time in the company's history. Before the revelations, the company did not have a succession plan in place. The New York Times later reported that Huang had also had an affair with an NVIDIA executive who reported to him. And for at least the immediate future, it's now on Kress to lead the company. Huang departure comes days after NVIDIA's board said it would investigate Huang after he admitted to having an affair with a former tech executive accused of being a Chinese intelligence asset. Here's what we know about the executive.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, kress worked at three companies before joining nvidia. In 2006, six years after Steve Ballmer took over as Microsoft's CEO, she became the chief financial officer of the company's Server and Tools division. She first spent eight years in finance roles at Texas Instruments before joining Microsoft in 1997. She remained with the company until 2010, when she moved to Cisco. There, she was the senior vice president and chief financial officer of the company's Business Technology and Operations Finance unit.

Sebagaimana diketahui, to hear kress tell it, huang went out of his way to recruit her. Per a 2023 interview, Huang wanted to transform NVIDIA into the dominant player in the nascent AI industry. Sometime before she joined NVIDIA in 2013, the CEO apparently sketched his vision for the company on a whiteboard. Say what you will about Huang's personal life and judgement, the man was an AI visionary.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, it would be almost another four years following kress joining nvidia before a group of google researchers published "attention is all you need," the paper that introduced the world to transformer models, and nearly a decade before the release of chatgpt. Kress partly credits her sons, who were only eight and 10 at the time, for buying Huang's pitch. Despite their young age, the two already knew of NVIDIA and its importance to gaming. In a 2024 Fortune interview, Kress said NVIDIA was the smallest company she had worked for when she joined in 2013.

Diungkapkan bahwa at the start of her tenure, nvidia's revenue was $4. 28 billion for the year. In fiscal 2026, the company recorded a record $215. 9 billion in revenue.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, when nvidia's board of directors announced kress as huang's temporary successor, it said it would consider both internal and external candidates to take on the role of ceo permanently, leaving the door open for her and other current nvidia employees to win the job. In any case, it's far too early to speculate who the company's board might interview for the job. But if you can forgive a writer a tired analogy, if Kress stays on as CEO, she is likely to be a Tim Cook-like figure, one that can stabilize the company and guide it toward continued growth.

"The Board, [executive staff] and I recognize that this has been an extraordinarily difficult period and I want you to know how grateful we are for your resilience, professionalism and continued dedication," Kress wrote in her first email to NVIDIA employees after the transition was announced, according to CNBC.

Sebagaimana diketahui, still, she has a very difficult job ahead of her. Huang has agreed to testify before Congress in a hearing that the House aims to hold before the Thanksgiving holiday. The chair of the House Foreign Affairs committee, Brian Mast of Florida, said he wasn't ruling out the possibility of "public hearings for other people or other things down road. " You can bet NVIDIA is likely to face an intense amount of scrutiny in the coming weeks, particularly when Democrats take control of the House and Senate at the start of next year.

#18. After Jensen Huang, Big Tech Has a Chance to Learn From Nvidia’s Mistakes

📅 12 Nov 2026

After Jensen Huang, Big Tech Has a Chance to Learn From Nvidia’s Mistakes

Tanggal: 12 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.cnet.com/tech/services-and-software/jensen-huang-big-tech-learn-from-nvidias-mistakes/

Tech insiders and commentators say Nvidia will survive Huang's departure, but it's time for more accountability among CEOs.

What now for Nvidia? This was the question on everyone’s lips at the illustrious Web Summit technology conference in Lisbon on Thursday in the hours after CEO Jensen Huang announced his resignation.

Sebagaimana diketahui, huang’s departure followed a series of allegations that he had multiple extramarital affairs, including one with an nvidia employee and one with a woman who has been identified as a possible chinese spy. The company, whose computer chips are at the core of generative AI’s disruptive powers, is valued at around $4 trillion, making it one of the most valuable in the world. A co-founder, Huang has been with Nvidia since its earliest days three decades ago, making it hard to imagine the company without him at the helm.

Diungkapkan bahwa there’s nothing quite like a salacious, market-moving scandal to create a buzz at a tech event. The Web Summit organizers leaned into the news, quickly assembling a panel of tech experts to discuss whether Nvidia was bigger than its CEO.

Diungkapkan bahwa nothing in the allegations changes the fact that huang is probably the godfather of the ai revolution, said investor and financial writer adam kobeissi. “He was the central figure,” Kobeissi said, even if he wasn’t the only person responsible for Nvidia’s success.

Sebagaimana diketahui, “this company is going to survive and thrive with or without him,” he added. “I don’t think this is some sort of bubble-popping moment where everything comes crumbling down. ”.

Sebagaimana diketahui, sweeping financial investments and expectations across the ai industry have driven stock prices and company valuations to dizzying heights, with many critics warning of a bubble just waiting to burst with destabilizing effects. As powerful as Nvidia has become, it could be caught in the center of such a maelstrom.

While such a concentration of power is not the way to create resilient companies, said Ryan LaSalle, CEO of cybersecurity company Nisos, like Kobeissi he thinks Nvidia will weather the storm.

Berdasarkan laporan, interim nvidia ceo collette kress, who has been with the company since 2013, is known for having a ton of loyalty within nvidia, he said. “In a company of that much brainpower, there will be some natural leaders who can help shepherd them to the next chapter. ”.

One big question put to panel participants was whether Nvidia’s board made a mistake allowing one person to have so much power.

Berdasarkan laporan, it wasn’t just a mistake of corporate culture, said carissa veliz, associate professor of philosophy at the oxford institute for ethics in ai. It was also a mistake in terms of democracy.

Diungkapkan bahwa for one person to wield so much power over decisions affecting the economy and national security means something has gone wrong and has revealed how vulnerable we are, veliz said. If we look at the history of corporations, she said, there used to be a tradition of proving to the government that you were doing good for your country to earn your right to exist and get certain tax breaks.

“At the moment, we have shifted from that kind of framework to a framework in which a corporation is allowed to be essentially a kind of psychopath that only cares about its own profits, that only has duties to shareholders and which can be structured in any way, including a very powerful CEO with very little oversight,” she said.

Gil Duran, author of The Nerd Reich: Silicon Valley Fascism and the War on Democracy, said that he thought Nvidia’s errors in the lead-up to this moment would be studied in business and public relations crisis management classes.

“The board was completely missing out on most of the truth and the facts,” he said, referencing news reports that said Huang a year ago hired a law firm known for covering up sex scandals and President Donald Trump in May had been told about the CEO’s affair with the alleged Chinese spy.

“I don’t think there’s any other way to look at it but a catastrophe,” he said.

Duran and Veliz agreed that it was time to ensure tech CEOs face real oversight.

Berdasarkan laporan, “these guys face no accountability and no supervision, and that’s part of the problem,” said veliz. “These kind of small kings have their own small kingdoms… and they get away with almost anything. ”.

CEOs like Elon Musk at SpaceX and Sam Altman at OpenAI have enormous influence not only in their own companies but also across the national economy.

Diungkapkan bahwa what we’re seeing in huang’s downfall is the shattering of a myth about genius founders, said duran. He questioned whether it would spark actual change, however, given that the market’s addiction to the narrative of great, powerful founders.

“The fact that they can just tumble markets with their personal lives that become geopolitical crises – this is an insane amount of power to outsource,” he said.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, if we can tone down the myth, this moment provides a chance to look at where we’ve gone wrong and do better, veliz said. There’s opportunity here, she added – to raise up companies that can build the kinds of technology we need, support democracies rather than erode them, aren’t based on surveillance and prediction, and can behave transparently.

Sebagaimana diketahui, for every other tech behemoth out there, there is plenty to be learned from huang’s downfall. The concentration of power in one individual is not, as LaSalle pointed out, a safe long-term strategy.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, what’s needed is more oversight and accountability from a company’s board of directors. In announcing Huang’s resignation, Nvidia also said it was appointing its first chairman for its board.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, huang’s entanglement with a potential honeypot is also an opportunity for tech companies to think about security, said lasalle. No matter how sophisticated cybersecurity threats are becoming in the age of AI, he added, “people are still the simplest way in. ”.

Diungkapkan bahwa duran warned about the potential damage ahead if we fail to seize this as a moment to change. Nobody wants that, and we have a short window of time to collapse it before they collapse us. “If you look at the AI CEO vision of the future, it’s massive economic destruction so that a handful of people can become trillionaires,” he said. “No one voted for that. ”.

Sebagaimana diketahui, disclosure: katie collins traveled to lisbon as a guest of web summit to serve as a panel moderator. Her reporting from the event was independent of that role.

#20. Specialized’s Tarmac SL9 S-Level is built to wreck your Zone 2 ride

📅 13 Nov 2026

Specialized’s Tarmac SL9 S-Level is built to wreck your Zone 2 ride

Tanggal: 13 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://arstechnica.com/gadgets/2026/11/specializeds-tarmac-sl9-s-level-is-built-to-wreck-your-zone-2-ride/

Specialized’s second-fastest bike may be the smart buy.

Diungkapkan bahwa i love a good zone 2 ride. ” Normally, I’d count on the good imp—the dude with the harp and wings—on my right shoulder to restrain these urges. There’s nothing like getting on the bike, settling into a groove, and letting the miles (and hours) flow by. But sometimes when I hopped on the Specialized Tarmac SL9 S-Level, Zone 2 would turn into a tempo ride. It was like having a little imp—the stereotype dressed in red with the pitchfork—on my left shoulder whispering into my ear: “Go fast. This bike was built to go fast. But the Tarmac is so seductive that he would just shrug and say “he’s got a point. You can do a Zone 2 ride tomorrow. Speed is good. ” And in a moment of weakness, I would drop the hammer and head into the red, just because the SL9 makes that so rewarding.

Berdasarkan laporan, the tarmac sl9 is specialized’s aero road bike, with the s-level sitting just below the s-works in specialized’s top tier of carbon, aero road bikes, where it replaced the tarmac sl8 pro. After it got an update this year, I spent several weeks riding it, putting nearly 1,000 miles on it.

Sebagaimana diketahui, specialized offers the tarmac sl9 in four models, all available with sram and shimano drivetrains (ars tested the sram version). Notably, you don’t need to buy the top-of-the-line bike to get the top-of-the-line groupset. Here’s the breakdown of the Tarmac SL9 lineup (note that the Shimano versions of the Expert is 20 g lighter and Comp is 70 grams heavier than the SRAM versions):.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the $10,500 s-level offers the top-of-the-line sram red groupset and integrated cockpit, just like the $14,000 s-works. Along with the frame, different wheelsets and saddles make the S-Level 500 g heavier than the S-Works. Despite the weight difference, Specialized says the FACT 10r offers the same stiffness and comfort characteristics as its lighter sibling. At 822 g for a 56 cm frame, the FACT 10r is 135 g heavier than the FACT 12r used on the S-Works. But the frameset, wheelset, and saddle differ. With bottle cages, a Garmin mount, and my preferred Shimano XTR XC PD-M9200 MTB pedals, the S-Level I tested weighed in at 7. The major difference is the frame: the S-Level gets the same carbon-fiber FACT 10r frame as the Expert and Comp. By way of comparison, my own road bike—a Gen 8 Trek Madone—weighs in at 7. 98 kg. 71 kg.

Diungkapkan bahwa i rode the s-level all around the chicago suburbs as well as in central illinois. Unlike the Diverge 4 Pro, I wasn’t able to test its climbing ability in the Rocky Mountains. All we’ve got in most of Illinois are short, punchy climbs … and a lot of long flats. I rode The S-Level on everything from freshly laid asphalt to freshly laid chipseal, including a couple of 60-mile-plus rides on the country roads downstate.

Diungkapkan bahwa visually, the s-level is striking. Indeed, Specialized says the Tarmac SL9 is the most aerodynamic road bike it has ever made. Notable changes from the previous-generation Tarmac SL8 to SL9 involved tweaking the head tube, rerouting the rear hydraulic brake hose to accommodate the narrower head tube, and moving to a dropped-down tube for improved aerodynamics. But the most visually striking change is the Win Fin. As the seat tube rises from the bottom bracket, it deviates from the vertical to follow the curve of the wheel as it approaches the seat stays. And it looks aerodynamic. The blue-on-white with gray striping is one of Specialized’s better-looking colorways. When riding with just a single water bottle on the downtube—common in pro races where a full bottle is just a team car away—Specialized claims Win Fin saves riders half a watt.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the s-level i tested came with specialized’s 30 mm specialized cotton tlr tires—used by red bull-bora-hansgrohe on the uci world tour—in a tubeless setup. According to Bicycle Rolling Resistance, the Cotton TLR outperforms the much-loved Continental GP 5000 S TR tires when it comes to rolling resistance (at 28 mm). Using Silca’s tire pressure calculator, I rode with the tires inflated to 73 psi in the front and 75 psi in the rear, a departure from the 62/64 setting on my 32 mm Contis—and there is a slight, but noticeable difference in ride comfort between the S-Level and my own road bike. Mounted on the Roval Rapide CL III carbon wheels with 21 mm internal width, the Cotton TLR tires measured 30. 2 mm wide (my 32 mm Contis are a hair over 33 mm).

Sebagaimana diketahui, on every surface shy of brand-new chipseal, the tarmac felt comfortable and balanced, with the bike absorbing some of the punishment meted out by uneven pavement. What was particularly impressive about the SL9 is how great it feels on long rides. Fresh chipseal is another matter entirely, as it feels more like gravel, which felt jarring on the SL9 S-Level. Some manufacturers are skilled at building aero bikes that feel great on hours-long rides, and the Tarmac is just as good as the Trek Madone SLR 9 AXS Gen 8 I reviewed in this regard.

Diungkapkan bahwa when you’re ready to drop the hammer, the s-level is your willing accomplice. It’s twitchy in all of the good ways, with instantaneous response to the rider’s effort. The SRAM Red AXS groupset makes shifting buttery smooth (and the bonus buttons on the brake hoods allow the rider to change screens on the bike computer without releasing the brake hoods), and the drivetrain (50t/37t chainrings and a 10t-36t cassette) offers gear ratios for every type of terrain.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the first few seconds of a climb on the tarmac sl9 s-level feel like they come for free. Whether I stayed seated or cranked out watts in an upright position, there was no lag or flex as the bike snapped forward. Descents were amazing, and cornering on the S-Level is sublime—I felt balanced and in control at all times.

Sebagaimana diketahui, there are a few nits to pick. The trend among professional riders has been toward shorter cranks because it makes holding an aero position easier and reduces hip and knee flexion. Also, I would prefer shorter cranks on the Tarmac. The reach to the brakes in the drops felt excessive on my first couple of rides, and I had to adjust them slightly to brake easily on descents. To its credit, Specialized reduced the crank length from 172. 5 mm on the 56 cm SL8 to 170 mm on the same-sized SL9, but I run 165 mm cranks on my road bikes and noticed the difference on the S-Level. One demographic that buys expensive road bikes is middle-aged dudes with empty nests and disposable incomes, and they are the ones most likely to appreciate shorter cranks.

Berdasarkan laporan, the 3d-printed power pro mirror is a fine saddle, but there’s a reason i ride with a specialized s-works power with mirror on my trek—it’s more comfortable and offers noticeably more padding around the cutout. And if I owned the S-Level, I’d move to 32 mm tires as soon as I wore out the 30s for better compliance.

Berdasarkan laporan, specialized brags that the tarmac sl9 s-works is the fastest bike ever made, and it claims the s-level is the second-fastest bike ever made. $10,500 is a hefty sum for a road bike, but I’d be a lot more willing to forego the weight savings from the lighter components (frame, wheels, seatpost, bottom bracket, and bearings) of the S-Works—and spend $3,500 less. And it’s nice to get a SRAM Red groupset without springing for the absolute top-of-the-line model. It’s lightweight, it’s fast, it’s responsive, and it’s great on rollers and punchy climbs. The real selling point, though, is how often it made me want to go harder just for the fun of it. I can’t speak to that claim, but the SL9 S-Level checks all of the boxes for an aerodynamic road bike. That little imp has a point: Zone 2 can wait until tomorrow.

But it does feel great underfoot, is very quiet, and has a higher weight capacity (300 pounds) and a slightly longer belt than the Sperax above. The built-in Bluetooth speaker sounds unsurprisingly crappy. —Adrienne So.

It can be controlled via an app or a remote, but it doesn’t automatically sync if you use the remote. But it’s lightweight and easy to move around your home.

Berdasarkan laporan, sperax walking pad: the us consumer product safety commission has warned consumers to stop using several sperax walking pad and treadmill models due to the fall and fire hazards they pose. According to the CPSC, the machines can unexpectedly change speeds or come to a sudden stop, and there have also been reports of overheating and fires. The warning applies to the Pro, Q1, RM-01, and RM-02 models, but I’d avoid this brand altogether.

Berdasarkan laporan, size and storage: walking pads are typically much smaller than traditional treadmills, but check the product dimensions and make sure the footprint will work for you. If you’re working with an especially small space, consider a foldable or under-desk walking pad. If you’re planning to store it under furniture or in a closet when not in use, shop for slimmer models with wheels for portability.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, belt size and track length: the size of your track is dependent on the product’s dimensions, and you should take into consideration how much space you have to work with. But, generally, I prefer wider and lengthier belts that feel more stable to walk on, especially if you’re on the taller side or have a longer stride.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, weight capacity: walking pads aren’t as durable as treadmills and tend to have a lower weight capacity. Check the machine’s limit, and make sure it will work for you and anyone else in the household who will be using it. Per the online reviews we’ve read, walking pads are notorious for falling apart after only a few years or even a few months of use, so it might be worth getting something that’s a little more heavy-duty.

Diungkapkan bahwa speed range: choose a walking pad that offers a speed range that best fits your lifestyle and goals. Most models will generally offer speeds up to 4 mph, which should cover everything from gentle strolls and brisk walks, and is ideal for home office use. There are walking pad-treadmill hybrids that offer faster paces if you’re also looking for a jog.

Diungkapkan bahwa adjustable inclines: some models remain flat, but i prefer the walking pads that feature adjustable levels so that you can customize your cardio intensity as you see fit. Walking at an incline can also strengthen your lower body muscles and reduce anterior knee loading.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, metrics and display: most walking pads have an led display that tracks your steps, distance, time, and calories. Some models also include a remote control and/or app, which can sometimes sync your metrics from the machine, so you can check your workout data on your phone. This may not matter to you if you prefer to use your Apple Watch or fitness tracker.

Price: You can snag a solid, no-frills walking pad for under $200, but if you’re looking for a higher-end model with a surplus of features, it can cost $500+.

Diungkapkan bahwa our remote team members evaluated each walking pad from their own home offices, using the pads during real workdays. Testers of different heights, stride lengths, and lifestyles walked for hour-plus stretches while answering emails, taking meetings, and performing other work-related tasks; we noted how each pad felt over time and whether any annoyances surfaced with prolonged use. We evaluated every model for at least two weeks across the following criteria:.

#26. Nvidia privately confirmed it could track chips to fight smuggling, even as industry publicly questioned feasibility

📅 12 Nov 2026

Nvidia privately confirmed it could track chips to fight smuggling, even as industry publicly questioned feasibility

Tanggal: 12 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.technologyreview.com/2026/11/12/1148483/nvidia-chip-tracking/

The Chip Security Act is getting renewed attention following Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang’s resignation and reported affair with an alleged Chinese spy.

Sebagaimana diketahui, representatives from nvidia told illinois representative bill foster that it would be technically possible to implement the anti-smuggling measures called for in the chip security act, foster told mit technology review in an interview on thursday, even while an industry group claimed they were “potentially infeasible. ”.

Berdasarkan laporan, foster, a democrat who serves on the committee on science, space, and technology, is a cosponsor of the act, which would introduce geotracking requirements to verify the location of advanced ai chips in order to prevent their smuggling to china. It is one of three chip-security bills under consideration for inclusion in the Senate’s National Defense Authorization Act, each of which is drawing renewed attention after Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang’s resignation and reported affair with an alleged Chinese spy.

Berdasarkan laporan, when the chip security act was introduced, in may 2025, lawmakers said the technology to implement it existed, something nvidia has not publicly confirmed. In March 2026, the Semiconductor Industry Association, of which Nvidia is a member, explicitly opposed the bill and wrote that its mandates for chip tracking were “new, untested, and potentially infeasible. ”.

But privately, Nvidia representatives working with Foster told the lawmaker that the company could implement them.

Sebagaimana diketahui, “they never put anything in writing,” foster says, but during technical discussions on the possibility of such safeguards, their reaction was “yeah, of course we can do this. ” This private acknowledgment to Foster goes further than anything Nvidia has previously made public.

Sebagaimana diketahui, other technology nvidia has built for its customers suggests that the company can indeed offer accurate tracking of its chips’ locations. In December 2025, for example, it announced a new tool called Fleet Intelligence that would allow customers to monitor how its advanced chips were performing across different data center locations. In doing so, the tool could indicate which country chips were in, Nvidia confirmed to Reuters, but the company would not elaborate on whether this technology could be used to prevent smuggling.

Nvidia did not respond to requests for comment or confirmation of Foster’s characterization.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, in early october, when lawmakers were reportedly increasingly concerned about nvidia’s role in smuggling, mit technology review asked the company if fleet intelligence could be used to prevent the practice. It declined to answer directly, instead sending a statement: “Governments and media have found insignificant diversion of controlled US products—a drop in the bucket compared to the ocean of domestic compute China already has. ”.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the recent fallout at nvidia involves a number of people and companies alleged to be involved in chip smuggling. A US Commerce Department inquiry into the company was reportedly halted after invention by Nvidia. Alice Huang, with whom Jensen Huang reportedly had an affair, runs Megaspeed, a Singaporean firm now under investigation for smuggling advanced GPUs to China. Megaspeed reportedly bought chips from Supermicro, a company that packages Nvidia’s chips onto servers.

Berdasarkan laporan, the chip security act as drafted would require a mechanism to track the locations of chips, either by inspections of facilities, attestations by companies, or ping-based location mechanisms. The ping-based technique, the hardest option to circumvent, would require the GPU to send a signal of its location when it comes online. In September, the Center for Security and Emerging Technology found it would be the most cost-effective option.

Foster said he did not ask Nvidia’s representatives why they weren’t voluntarily adopting such chip-tracking tools if they could technically do so.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, but if the requirements of the bill pass as part of the senate’s national defense authorization act, the new tracking mechanisms would only tell investigators where the chips are, not offer a way to disconnect them if it’s revealed they have been smuggled. Foster told MIT Technology Review he intends to introduce new, stricter legislation in the new year that would offer a workaround. The new rule would require licenses to operate advanced GPUs, and before a GPU could connect, its valid license would need to be verified.

Sebagaimana diketahui, in the meantime, the controversy at nvidia, foster says, has fueled support among his colleagues for the rules in the bill: “there will be a lot of political pressure, in the wake of everything that’s happened, on the companies to actually do a very good job of the geographic validation of where the chip actually is. ”.

Is Android Settings not delivering enough power? The Essentials app features 30+ mods and tweaks - but you won't find it in the Play Store.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, most android owners know of the settings app, which gives them all the power google assumes they need. Then there’s the Developer Options feature that can be enabled to give users even more power.

Also: I turned an old Android phone into a server for my LAN.

If that’s not enough, there’s now Essentials, a power-user’s toolbox that includes 30+ mods and tweaks for things like button remapping, app freezing, Google Maps battery saving modes, sound and haptics, wallpaper, widgets, status bar icon customization, edge lighting, flashlight pulsing, notification management, Always-On Display, and more.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the only requirement for most essentials features is android 8 or newer. There are a handful of advanced features that require shell providers like Shizuku or even root access, but the majority of features most users will want to enable have no requirements beyond the minimum.

Sebagaimana diketahui, essentials isn’t found on the google play store. Instead, Essentials must be sideloaded from the APK available on its official GitHub Repository. Keep in mind that Google has changed the way apps are sideloaded.

Also: How to sideload Android apps on your phone now.

Sebagaimana diketahui, make sure you understand the new sideloading process before you proceed. You’ll also need to change some permissions, depending on the feature you want to use. For example, to change lock screen shortcuts, you have to enable it in Accessibility Services.

Sebagaimana diketahui, as well, you have to enable restricted settings, which is done with settings > apps > see all x apps > essentials. On that page, tap the three-dot menu and then tap “Allow restricted settings. ”.

Without that feature enabled, Essentials will be hamstrung by Android’s permissions system.

Diungkapkan bahwa essentials is fairly simple to use. You open the app, search for the feature you want to enable, and enable it. It seems every time I go to enable or customize a feature, I have to grant yet another permission. One thing you’ll discover is that you have to enable a lot of permissions for Essentials. I know it sounds like a hassle, but given the extra power you gain, it’s worth it.

Also: How to turn on Android’s Private DNS mode.

Berdasarkan laporan, let me walk you through a feature found in essentials you’ll wish were baked into android. The feature is App Lock, which lets you require authentication for specific apps. This is a handy option, especially if someone gets ahold of your phone while it’s unlocked and tries to open certain apps you’d prefer to keep private (such as your banking app). To use this feature, you have to grant Essentials permission for Accessibility features, which you’ll be prompted to do when you go to enable it.

Sebagaimana diketahui, app lock is found in essentials > security and privacy. Once there, click the On/Off slider to enable App Lock, and you’ll be prompted to grant the necessary Essentials permission in Accessibility. After enabling the feature, tap it, and you’ll be prompted to authenticate with fingerprint, face, or password/PIN (whichever you have set up).

Berdasarkan laporan, on the next page, tap “select locked apps,” and you’ll be prompted to select the apps that require authentication to open. To do that, I tap the On/Off slider for those apps until they are in the On position. For instance, I want to make sure that Authy (my 2FA app of choice), my bank app, and Messages require authentication before they open. The next time I go to open any of those apps, I’ll be required to authenticate via the fingerprint sensor.

Also: This silent Android feature scans your photos for ‘sensitive content’.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, another handy feature is found in notifications and alerts, where you can enable notification lighting, flashlight pulse, notification snoozing, and snooze system notifications. I enabled notification lighting for Messages and Phone, so I will never miss a message or call, even if my phone is on silent mode. You can enable notification lighting and then select which apps it applies to. You can also enable flashlight pulses, so it doesn’t matter if your phone’s screen is facing up or down — you’ll be notified of your messages.

Sebagaimana diketahui, that’s essentially how essentials works. Also, note that Shizuku requires you to enable wireless debugging to start the service. Do remember two things: you’ll be met with a barrage of permission requests, and some of those permissions aren’t possible unless you have root access or Shizuku (an open-source Android tool that lets third-party apps use system-level APIs and ADB (Android Debug Bridge) privileges without requiring you to fully root your device. Once you install Shizuku (from the Play Store), you’ll find detailed (and lengthy) directions on how to do this.

Also: 5 ways I speed up your Android phone beyond clearing system cache.

If you want considerably more control over your Android device, I highly recommend adding Essentials, as you won’t find most of these options in any other tool.

Senior Editor / Home Security and Smart Home.

Senior Editor / Home Security and Smart Home.

Sebagaimana diketahui, android users looking for the most high-tech ways to manage their smart locks at home just got some great news. On Tuesday, Google announced it will start offering digital keys in Google Wallet built on Aliro, a new smart lock standard.

When I tested the predictive, futuristic Schlage Sense Pro lock — which uses ultrawideband technology and Apple Home Keys in Apple Wallet — Schlage told me that other brands were adopting Aliro to bring that same seamless usability to more devices, and now the time has come.

Diungkapkan bahwa the best thing about the lock is that it didn’t require me to tap my phone for an nfc connection or even wave it in the vicinity. The ultrawideband, or UWB tech — think of it like an advanced version of Bluetooth older locks used — sensed a key holder was coming to the door, judged my speed and trajectory based on the signals the lock was getting, and had the door unlocked by the time I reached it, with autolock features locking it back up a minute later.

Diungkapkan bahwa home keys in google wallet, which have already started rolling out to public preview users in google home, offer users a lot of similar tricks with the right smart locks. That’s handy not only for saving time fumbling for your phone at the door, but also if your hands are full or you’re busy talking to someone. When I tested Schlage’s version, it could sense when I was actually approaching and when I was simply walking by the door, too, so the lock didn’t randomly open.

Sebagaimana diketahui, so far, locks compatible with uwb and the “unlock on approach” feature include not only the schlage sense pro ($394. 98) I tested, but also the Aqara u400 ($269. 99) and the European brand Nuki Keypad 2 NFC lock ($179), with more on the way. Aliro was only officially released early in 2026, so it will take time for the standard to be broadly adopted by both locks and digital wallets, especially more advanced abilities like these. The good news is that Aliro includes encryption for security, battery-life savings and other benefits, too.

A representative from Google didn’t immediately respond to a request for comment.

The “unlock on approach” feature of Aliro’s standard digital wallet keys is only one of the advantages of this upgrade, so you don’t need a UWB-compatible lock to get the benefits.

Diungkapkan bahwa according to google, its own home keys in google wallet will offer nfc to tap your phone to unlock the door (no unlocking necessary), let you use the digital key across multiple locks if necessary, and sync your key across compatible devices you use. Other people in the home can add their own home keys to the Wallet, but unlike Apple’s temporary passes, Google says guests and visitors will need to get passcodes instead of digital keys of their own.

Sebagaimana diketahui, what happens if you or someone else loses their phone? in most cases, users can rely on keypad access codes to gain entry instead of the digital wallet. But these UWB locks sometimes forgo a physical key slot entirely: Schlage says its lock doesn’t have a key slot to reduce the risk of lockpicking, but that does limit emergency unlock options.

Berdasarkan laporan, here’s where this new lock technology gets more complicated. Finding a compatible lock is only a part of unlocking all these Wallet key features.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, you’ll also need an nfc-enabled android phone running android 9 or later, such as the google pixel 10 pro or pixel fold. Then you’ll need a Matter-enabled Google Hub with a Thread Border Router, which is typically a separate Google device, like a Nest Hub Max, Nest Wifi Pro system or Google TV streamer.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, with all that, make sure your phone, lock, google wallet app and google home app are all updated, and you should be prompted to create home keys during your lock setup. A new option called Memory summary lets you see and control the things that Gemini AI knows about you.

Sebagaimana diketahui, like any ai, google gemini wants to remember things about you. The purported reason is to help tailor and personalize your conversations. But remember that your personal details may also wind up training the AI or even being reviewed by actual humans. With that in mind, you might want to find out just what Gemini knows about you. And now you can.

Berdasarkan laporan, with a new option called memory summary, you’re able to view the details that gemini has gathered about you over time. These may be tidbits from your conversations or things that you directly told the AI. Even better, you can add or remove any details just by editing the memory or issuing your request directly to Gemini.

This new capability is available in Gemini across the board, so you can access it at the Gemini website, in the mobile iOS and Android apps, and in the Windows and Mac desktop apps.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, launch gemini via the web or in one of the mobile or desktop apps. To proceed, turn it back on. In the left pane displaying your previous chats, select the Settings icon at the bottom. If the option is grayed out, it means the Memory feature is turned off. At the Settings screen, select Personal Intelligence and then click or tap Memory summary. You can always turn if off again afterward if you wish.

Sebagaimana diketahui, you’ll then see the individual details by category. My summary arranged the information across such categories as Essentials, Business & Career, Reading & Interests, and Culinary Preferences. To view a recent history, tap the three dot-icon at the top and select Memory history. Go down the list to see the individual items in each category. This shows you the latest changes and updates to Gemini’s memory.

Also: Stop sharing your passwords with AI agents.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, what if gemini’s memory includes details that are too personal or just incorrect? no problem. At the website or in one of the desktop apps, click the pencil icon at the top. Now you’re able to directly edit the text to add, remove, or revise specific details. You can alter the AI’s memories of you. After you’ve made your changes, just click Save.

Berdasarkan laporan, for example, my summary said that that i lived in madison county. I have no idea where Gemini got that notion as I live in New York. Here, I revised the text and saved the changes, which then synced across the Gemini website and apps.

Berdasarkan laporan, the mobile apps have no direct editing capability. But there’s another method that works both on mobile and on the desktop. Just tell Gemini what change you want to make. At the prompt, type and speak your request, and the AI will carry it out for you.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, as an example, my summary said that i run a business called batter up selling collectible baseball cards. That’s not at all true. #36. In reversal, American Cancer Society urges routine prostate cancer screening

In reversal, American Cancer Society urges routine prostate cancer screening

Tanggal: 12 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://arstechnica.com/health/2026/11/in-reversal-american-cancer-society-urges-prostate-cancer-tests-for-all-men/

Men aged 50–69 and at average risk should get PSA screening every two years.

In a significant update to its guidelines for prostate cancer screening, the American Cancer Society is now recommending that men get routinely screened for prostate cancer with a PSA test.

Men at average risk should get a PSA test every two years from age 50 to 69, according to the new guidelines released Thursday.

Diungkapkan bahwa men considered at high risk due to race and family history should start testing earlier, at 45, and most are recommended to get tested every year. Specifically, yearly testing starting at age 45 is recommended for all Black men, who have higher rates of prostate cancer. Non-Black men should also get yearly testing starting at 45 if a close relative was diagnosed with prostate cancer before age 65, or if more than one of their relatives has had prostate cancer. On the other hand, if only one close relative was diagnosed with prostate cancer and it was diagnosed at age 65 or older, non-Black men in this case should start PSA screening at 45, but are recommended to get testing only every two years.

Men ages 70 to 74 should consult their doctor on continuing screening, while those 75 and up are not recommended to get screened.

Diungkapkan bahwa the new guidance departs from acs’s previous iteration, published in 2010, which made no universal recommendations for routine screening. The recommendation was similar to that from the US Preventive Services Task Force, a federal panel that regularly evaluates evidence and makes recommendations on such preventive medical care. (The USPSTF is currently working on an update to its prostate cancer screening recommendation, though it should be noted that the panel has recently been overhauled by anti-vaccine Health Secretary Robert F. and new members are reportedly rife with conflicts of interest. Kennedy Jr. Men at age 50 were recommended to use shared-decision making with their doctors on whether or not to get tested. ).

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, in announcing the guidelines today, the acs says its updates are based on new evidence since 2010 that shows screening saves lives, and that advances in case management can avoid the concerning harms from overdiagnosis and overtreatment. For many men with prostate cancer, their cancer will never grow or cause harm in their lifetime, while treatment can run the risk of erectile dysfunction and urinary incontinence.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, in the new guidance, the acs adds guardrails, firstly advising all men to be informed about the risks and benefits. If a PSA test comes back high—defined as 3 ng/mL or higher for men under 70 and 6. 5 ng/mL or higher for those 70 and up—the ACS recommends repeating the test before taking any next steps.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, if repeat testing is still high, then men should get either a prostate mri or a validated biomarker test to assess risk. Only if there is a high suspicion of cancer—such as having a very high PSA test result—should men jump to a prostate biopsy.

For men diagnosed with prostate cancer, active surveillance should be the initial management strategy for men whose cancer appears to be at low risk of growing or spreading.

Berdasarkan laporan, “by catching aggressive cancers with a simple psa blood test, you open the door to highly effective treatments that protect your future,” dr. “Meanwhile, lower-risk findings can be safely managed through careful, active surveillance. Shanthi Sivendran, interim chief patient officer for the ACS, said in a statement. ”.

Diungkapkan bahwa prostate cancer is one of the most common cancers in men and the second leading cause of cancer death in us men, the acs notes. Nearly 334,00 men are estimated to be diagnosed with prostate cancer in 2026, and it’s estimated that over 36,320 will die from the disease.

Tech > Computing > Computer Accessories > Components > Graphic cards.

AMD released a new version of its Adrenalin Edition graphics software to address excessive SSD writing.

Machines that use AMD graphics hardware such as these Radeon 6800 cards may be affected by a bug in the company's driver software that is causing unnecessary writing to solid-state drives, which can wear them down over time.

AMD issued a software update on Thursday to fix a driver issue that caused excessive, continuous data writes to solid-state drives across its Radeon GPU lineup.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, first reported on sites including tom’s hardware and neowin, the bug was traced to two pieces of software: amd external events client module and utility, known as atieclxx. exe under Windows processes. exe or atiesrxx. The background service handles monitoring functions, but as some users have noticed, it’s also writing a large amount of data to SSDs, as much as 432GB in 24 hours, according to Neowin.

Diungkapkan bahwa the optional update is available on amd’s website as adrenalin edition 26. 11. In the notes for the update, AMD said the new software addresses “excessive system-drive writes while the system is idle on Radeon RX 7000 series graphics products and above” and “excessive system-drive writes while moving or resizing application windows. 1. ”.

Diungkapkan bahwa this excessive data writing is a concern because it can accelerate the wear and tear on an ssd, potentially shortening its lifespan. According to PC Gamer, that could mean losing 1% of the drive’s health in just a month. As one Reddit poster pointed out, this is not a new bug and, in one case, may have caused SSD degradation for nearly a year and a half.

Company staffers were previously posting on Reddit that a fix was coming.

The cost of SSDs has spiked dramatically in the last couple of years, so it could be an expensive problem to fix if it causes significant wear on a drive.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the same reddit users who helped uncover the bug and spread the word have a few ideas for how to prevent this if you haven’t updated to the new software. exe or atiesrxx. First, check the Windows Resource Monitor (you can access it by pressing Windows key + R and typing “resmon”) and look in the Disk tab to see if you’re experiencing excessive writing to your SSD from either atieclxx. exe processes.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, some who are seeing this are disabling the external events software entirely. ” Once there, you can look for the AMD External Events Utility, open its Properties and set Startup Type to Disabled. msc. You can also stop the process while you’re there for the current session. You can do that in Windows by typing Windows key + R and entering “services. That will keep it from starting up automatically when you reboot. You’ll want to restart your computer after this change.

Diungkapkan bahwa keep in mind that disabling the software could affect some display functions and game performance. Others have tried disabling a Resizable Bar, or ReBAR, a PCI Express process for accessing video card memory. Some have switched to alternative AMD drivers that are only compatible with AMD chipsets, not those with Intel or other chipset motherboards.

These options may be a temporary fix if you’re unable to install the new software, but be warned: Using any of those methods carries the risk of breaking other functions on your machine, so make sure your system has a recent restore point.
