#42. TCL QM7L Mini-LED TV Review (2026)

📅 13 Nov 2026

TCL QM7L Mini-LED TV Review (2026)

Tanggal: 13 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.wired.com/review/tcl-qm7l/

Berdasarkan laporan, are we entering the era of tv “dupes”? because to the untrained eye, or even a reasonably trained one, it’s hard to distinguish tcl’s mini-led-powered qm7l from a lower-end oled. So when your brother-in-law plops down in front of your new TV to watch the Lions and says, “Wow, you splurged, eh?” you can just nod and give a wink. Dupe accomplished.

Diungkapkan bahwa i know this because the qm7l arrived close on the heels of a new budget oled, the roku pro series, so i was able to compare the two side by side. Results: surprising. Although it has a potentially problematic design element and an AI that’s not exactly Claude-level sophisticated, the QM7L might just be the best midrange TV you can buy right now.

Diungkapkan bahwa available in sizes ranging from 55 inches (which i tested) to a mammoth 98 inches, the qm7l boasts a virtually borderless screen that stands on a pedestal instead of the usual feet. That’s a win if you own a small piece of furniture that might not accommodate the width of such feet, and I’d argue it’s more aesthetically pleasing too.

Berdasarkan laporan, however, it does pose a problem: because the pedestal base sticks out in front by a little over 4 inches, it doesn’t allow a soundbar to sit snug up to the screen. You could balance it on top of the base, but that looks awkward. And because it slopes down, the soundbar doesn’t even sit level.

Sebagaimana diketahui, what’s more, although the base has two height options, the taller one leaves the bottom of the tv just 2. 25 inches off your TV stand. That may be enough clearance for ultra-compact soundbars like the Bose TV Speaker, but something like the Sonos Arc, which measures 3 inches high, ends up blocking a sliver of the screen.

Berdasarkan laporan, the pedestal is also kind of a pain to assemble, with little help from the tiny diagrams in tcl’s otherwise decent setup guide. There are eight small screws used to connect the riser to the base, four more to attach it to the TV, and a bit of confusion over which of 10 mounting holes you’re meant to use.

Sebagaimana diketahui, these are hardly dealbreakers. If you’re planning to wall-mount the TV, the base becomes a non-issue. Same if you’re skipping a soundbar altogether. Or maybe you’re willing to live with it sitting out in front a few inches.

Diungkapkan bahwa setting up the tv itself is largely a breeze, especially if you already have the google home app on your phone. Even though I’m an iPhone guy, I was able to scan an onscreen QR code and use the app to move quickly through the setup process. An account sign-in and Wi-Fi network selection later, I just had to wait on a software update before heading to the couch.

Sebagaimana diketahui, tcl’s unremarkable remote has sharp edges, the usual mishmash of google tv buttons, and a pretty disorganized layout overall. On the plus side, it’s backlit and comes with six app-shortcut buttons.

One head-scratcher: The penultimate TV-setup screen notes that I can “customize the star button on the remote,” using it as a shortcut for this or that, which sounds great except that there is no star button.

Berdasarkan laporan, speaking of hallucinations (kidding!), google gemini comes baked into the google tv ui, which is reasonably easy to navigate but not without a few annoyances. For example, the top menu includes a Live TV page—home to various FAST channels, simple enough—but also a TCL page that contains … other FAST channels.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, as for gemini, it’s nice to have but hardly essential. Too bad it’s not hands-free; you have to press and hold a button on the remote to use it. ), it can’t do things like open picture settings or toggling off motion-smoothing—a bummer because those commands would actually save you a little time. The voice recognition is responsive, and the responses arrive quickly. Gemini also dishes up “watch now” options, and you can use it to create custom images and video clips, if you want. Just talk into the remote and you can ask for, say, movies about sharks, or learn who invented the Steadicam. Unfortunately, while Gemini can accommodate basic TV commands (“Start Netflix,” “Mute the sound,” etc. Instead, such requests turn into basic web searches, returning only information on how to access those settings yourself.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, i was a bit disappointed with google tv’s screensaver. You also can’t adjust the amount of idle time before the screensaver kicks on. It lets you draw from various sources, including an art gallery and your own photo library, but it doesn’t offer any “art mode” options like a mat overlay or automated brightness reduction. An art TV this is not.

Sebagaimana diketahui, software quibbles notwithstanding, the qm7l is a joy to behold. Whatever you care to make of TCL's marketing lingo (SQD Mini-LED, the “S” stands for “Super”), the results can’t be denied: dazzling color and ocean-floor blacks that really do bring OLED to mind. In fact, I’d argue that this TV “pops” more than the aforementioned Roku OLED—not because the colors are more vibrant, but because there’s greater brightness behind them.

Berdasarkan laporan, while watching pixar’s coco, for example, both tvs produced glorious hues, but my eye was more drawn to the tcl because the reds, greens, and blues just seemed to burst a bit more. (OLEDs, especially on the lower end, do tend to struggle with brightness, as detailed in my Roku Pro Series review. ).

Diungkapkan bahwa even watching something like east of eden on netflix, with its decidedly muted color palette, it was the brightness that stood out; the qm7l revealed a bit more detail inside the trask house. Interestingly, I also spotted a difference in the Netflix logo: On the TCL, it blazed a fire-engine red; the Roku version looked more subtle, almost orange in comparison.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, make no mistake, both tvs impressed me greatly. But seeing the two alongside each other, I liked the QM7L’s picture just a little better. I also watched sports and played Xbox games—both well served by the panel’s native 144-Hz refresh rate—and marveled at the smooth action and sharp lines.

Sebagaimana diketahui, not everything was perfect, however. There were a few cases where contrast and brightness seemed a little lacking, like during an episode of the criminally underrated Halt and Catch Fire on the Roku Channel. Checking the settings, I found that the brightness had been dialed down quite a bit—but not by me.

Diungkapkan bahwa the prime suspect? tcl’s ai-powered “smart picture optimization,” a common bit of marketing in modern tvs. If there was any behind-the-scenes intelligence at work here, I struggled to find it. Indeed, I had to manually adjust the brightness for that show.

Diungkapkan bahwa even more frustrating, where was motion-smoothing management? this scourge of modern television should be off by default. With the QM7L, it arrives in full ruinous glory—and the AI isn’t smart enough to disable it in situations where it doesn’t belong: namely, everything except sports and gaming. Luckily, it’s not buried 10 menus deep; you can toggle it off pretty easily. But this is one area where Roku proved superior, its Smart Picture Max adeptly adjusting motion-smoothing for most viewing.

Diungkapkan bahwa as for sound, the qm7l is the rare tv that doesn’t straight-up suck, thanks to tiny, down-facing speakers buried inside the cabinet. This one has two Bang & Olufsen–branded cones you can actually see, and because they’re embedded in the backside, they face backward as well. TCL doesn’t specify speaker wattage, but I can attest that they get plenty loud, and do so without distortion. That’s not ideal for a wall-mount situation, as the audio would be forced to kind of squirt out from the sides, but the speakers do sound pretty good when the TV is freestanding. However, I don’t understand why they’re positioned just a few inches apart, as the cabinet appears to have room for much more separation. Consequently, the soundstage feels pretty narrow; there’s very little “surround” to be found here. Even with this above-average audio, you’re still going to want a soundbar—hence my complaints about the pedestal stand earlier.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, but if my main complaints are a wide pedestal stand and so-so ai integrations, that's good news for the qm7l. The most important thing, picture quality, is stunning for the price. You buy a TV for your eyes, and with this one, they're in for a treat.

Diungkapkan bahwa as media headlines focus on jensen huang's resignation and the midterms fallout, you could almost forget that ukraine is still fighting for its life — with all of europe nervously watching. Sebagaimana diketahui, zelenskyy posted on x that the speed limits are being imposed along the war's entire front line and in russian-occupied territory. #45. What to know about this year’s UN climate talks

📅 11 Nov 2026

What to know about this year’s UN climate talks

Tanggal: 11 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.technologyreview.com/2026/11/11/1148308/un-climate-talks/

Climate finance and fossil fuels top the formal agenda at COP31.

It’s that time of year again: Thousands of delegates, lobbyists, and journalists are gathered for the annual UN climate talks, taking place this time in Antalya, Turkey.

Sebagaimana diketahui, cop31 officially kicked off on november 8, marking the beginning of negotiations on one of the biggest stages of the climate world. Turkey and Australia are cohosting this year’s talks, which are scheduled to wrap up on November 20.

Sebagaimana diketahui, this annual gathering can often serve as an indicator of where the world stands on addressing and adapting to the climate crisis. And this year’s talks are sure to be a doozy—expect a lot of back and forth on fossil fuels and climate finance in particular. Here’s what you should know about COP31.

Diungkapkan bahwa in recent years, the tension always feels high when cop rolls around. (COP stands for “Conference of the Parties. ”) But this year feels especially charged: The world is still grappling with the ongoing war in Iran, which has disrupted the Middle East and sent economic shock waves around the world as energy prices have spiked.

Diungkapkan bahwa this year’s cop will be the second without a formal delegation from the us. President Trump formally withdrew the country from the Paris Agreement earlier this year and is in the process of withdrawing from the UN Framework Committee on Climate Change. That’s the treaty that allows formal participation in negotiations.

Diungkapkan bahwa meanwhile, things aren’t looking good for the paris agreement, which was established at un climate talks 11 years ago, setting a goal of limiting warming to 1. 5 °C over preindustrial levels. In a report published in September, the UN Environment Program acknowledged that global warming is set to exceed that 1. 5 °C goal, “likely within the next few years. ”.

Berdasarkan laporan, so as climate talks kick off, there’s an obvious, urgent question looming about how to quickly cut emissions to limit warming. There’s also the major issue of how to pay for efforts to address emissions and to help a warming world endure the inevitable damage.

Sebagaimana diketahui, two years ago, talks ended in a goal of mobilizing $300 billion per year by 2035 to help pay to reduce emissions and adapt to climate change. (Rich nations provided $136. (Such funding has been quite flat over the past few years. ) And last year, the COP30 agreement included a goal of tripling the money for adaptation over that period. 7 billion in 2024, according to the Organization for Economic Cooperation and Development. ).

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the world got a tragic reminder of just how high the stakes are earlier this year, when a glacier collapse caused devastating flooding in the himalayas. The flood killed approximately 1,500 people, left over 5,000 missing, and caused nearly $5 billion in damage. The UN loss and damages fund committed $20 million to helping Nepal recover (less than 1% of the total estimated cost to the country).

Diungkapkan bahwa another key trend to watch is how the formal negotiations engage with the topic of fossil fuels. But it felt as if things took a step back last year, when the final agreement didn’t even mention the phrase “fossil fuels” once. Three years ago, the final agreement text explicitly called for a transition away from them. This will be an interesting conversation, especially because cohosts Turkey and Australia have both faced criticism over their relationships with these fuels—Australia is a major exporter of coal and natural gas, and Turkey’s grid relies heavily on fossil fuels, including coal.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, outside the formal negotiations, cop31 president murat kurum, turkey’s environment minister, is spearheading a side agenda, including two informal initiatives that will be worth watching. These wouldn’t be part of the official agreement text, but countries could sign on to signal support.

Berdasarkan laporan, one is a pledge to make ai more sustainable; this is almost comically squishy, even as voluntary cop pledges go. The text includes explicit wording that it creates no new obligations for countries, so don’t expect anything resembling enforcement there.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the cop leadership is also pushing to make electricity a larger part of member countries’ energy use. Today, only about 23% of global energy is used in the form of electricity. Shifting to more electricity use, and relying on cleaner sources for that electricity, could help drive down emissions. Fossil fuels, like gasoline in vehicles or natural gas for heating, make up the bulk of the rest. The new pledge’s target is for electricity to make up 35% of total energy consumption by 2035.

Sebagaimana diketahui, with leadership billing this as an “implementation cop,” it would be great to see some real, tangible progress on the global challenge of addressing climate change. I’m not expecting anything groundbreaking, but we’ll be tuned in to see what the final agreement shapes up to be.

Sebagaimana diketahui, in its third-quarter earnings call thursday, the neocloud company nebius laid out $40 billion in planned spending for 2027, far more than wall street had expected. It’s an ambitious plan, but it rests on a string of planned projects that are already starting to show cracks.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, nebius plans to fund the buildout by relying on customer pre-payments and loans backed by customer contracts — essentially using the future value of its data centers to finance their construction. But that can be a risky strategy if those projects get bogged down by delays or cancellations.

Sebagaimana diketahui, “building at this scale is hard, and delays are part of our industry right now,” ceo arkady volozh said during thursday’s earnings call. “We are not immune. ”.

Diungkapkan bahwa the earnings announcement comes on the heels of reports that microsoft is cooling on neocloud deals that aren’t delivering on time. That’s a problem for companies like Nebius, whose financing strategy is becoming more dependent on repayments. Because if it can’t get to capacity on time, it will keep piling on costs while revenues slip.

Diungkapkan bahwa one of nebius’ largest customers is microsoft, which is paying for ai computing capacity at a vineland, new jersey, data center that is now months behind schedule. Nebius’ contract with Microsoft is worth up to $19. 4 billion, but it’s already letting deadlines slip. Only just over half of the Microsoft capacity is now planned for delivery by the end of the year, with the rest coming in Q2 2027.

The delay is because DataOne, the third-party operator of the site, “decided to wind down the temporary generation faster than it was expected,” according to Andrey Korolenko, chief product and infrastructure officer, as the site switches over to Bloom Energy fuel cells.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, still, that transition wasn’t entirely by choice. New Jersey regulators fined the DataOne facility $1. In August, the investigative site Floodlight identified at least 45 natural gas generators in operation at the DataOne site, even though it had not received any permits for operating gas generators. 1 million in response, finding that the use of the generators violated federal law.

DataOne is also facing a noise-complaint lawsuit from nearby residents over a constant humming noise allegedly emitted by the data center.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, according to nebius’ summary of its microsoft contract, microsoft can terminate affected service after a grace period if dates are missed and no alternative capacity is offered. The tranches were originally meant to be deployed in 2025 and 2026, so a Q2 2027 delivery date falls well beyond that window. The contract also includes financial penalties for late delivery.

Diungkapkan bahwa nebius said that microsoft “has been part of the planning process. ” Nebius did not say whether Microsoft has agreed to the new dates, but Microsoft has not publicly canceled anything.

TechCrunch has reached out to Nebius, Microsoft, and DataOne for comment.

Diungkapkan bahwa on the call, marc boroditsky, nebius’s chief revenue officer, said the company’s deals with microsoft and meta both came with significant prepayment, which arrived long before delivery. But Bloomberg reported last week that Microsoft is tightening oversight on projects run by third parties, including Nebius, IREN, and Nscale, and debating whether it’s worth signing new agreements. Microsoft also sent employees to the site in New Jersey, per Bloomberg.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, in its own quarterly earnings report, microsoft noted that its capex spend was lower than expected due to third-party delays. The company is clearly not above pulling back from planned agreements where its partner doesn’t meet its share of the bargain. Bloomberg also reported that Microsoft won’t use an option to more than double its Nscale agreement for a Texas data center and recently stopped being an anchor customer for Nscale’s planned Essex site after power delays.

Diungkapkan bahwa nebius says the delays it faces are coming from sites it doesn’t control, with the data centers it is building itself coming online on time or ahead of schedule. Those, Nebius says, will supply most of its new capacity from 2027. New deals signed in Q3 came with prepayments that more than cover the cost of building capacity behind them, says Boroditsky. Nebius ended the quarter with $7. 4 billion in cash.

Sebagaimana diketahui, total prepayments plus asset-backed financing of investment-grade contracts are expected to cover up to 85% of the $40 to $45 billion 2027 capex spend. Boroditsky also said Nebius could “tap prepayments to shore up any additional cash requirements. CFO Maria Del Dado Alonso Sanchez named Microsoft and Meta as contracts that can be financed this way. ”.

Nebius forecast 2027 revenue of $12 to $13 billion, and said it expects to break even on a pre-tax basis by the fourth quarter.

Berdasarkan laporan, nebius reported third-quarter revenue of $981 million, up 571% from a year earlier. Nebius cut its 2026 revenue forecast by $200 million to $3 billion, citing delays to third-party sites like New Jersey. Roughly a third of that was a one-time payment tied to a new partnership model. Shares ended the day down 17%.

#50. You Could Learn to Pilot This Flying Car in Just 5 Minutes

📅 12 Nov 2026

You Could Learn to Pilot This Flying Car in Just 5 Minutes

Tanggal: 12 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.cnet.com/roadshow/xpeng-aridge-land-aircraft-carrier-flying-car/

Our gifting experts are obsessively searching for holiday gifts that are unique, thoughtful and suitable for any budget.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, our expert, award-winning staff selects the products we cover and rigorously researches and tests our top picks. If you buy through our links, we may earn a commission.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, is it a bird? is it a plane? is it a. flying Cybertruck? Nope, it's a modular flying car that will take to the skies next year.

When I first laid eyes on the Aridge flying car at the IFA consumer electronics show in Berlin this past September, I didn’t fully understand what I was looking at.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, taking pride of place on the stand belonging to chinese robotics company xpeng, there was a van that bore more than a passing resemblance to a cybertruck. It didn’t have any wings, and it looked far too dense to fly. Sitting next to it was a kind of oversized drone with a cabin just about large enough to fit two people.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the two vehicles seemed like totally separate entities. It never would’ve occurred to me to assume they were two halves of one system – much less that the drone, with its substantial wingspan, could fold up to fit inside the van.

Diungkapkan bahwa i now understand that this modular two-part flying car system is known formally as the aridge land aircraft carrier. The ground vehicle, also known as the mothership, is a chunky 5. 5-meter-long van that can be driven with a standard license and fits in most parking spaces. It’s designed to store, carry and deploy the electric vertical takeoff and landing vehicle, or eVTOL, including its six foldable rotors, which can fly as high as a helicopter for 30km (about 19 miles).

Berdasarkan laporan, this remarkable creation is the work of deli zhao, founder and president of aridge, which is backed by robotics and auto company xpeng. Speaking at Web Summit in Lisbon on Tuesday, Zhao presented himself as a man who was inspired to pursue a career building flying cars by Harry Potter and the Green Goblin, despite his lack of formal education.

Sebagaimana diketahui, “dreams are very important,” zhao said, as a video of him flying the evtol played on a screen in the background. Anyone can learn to fly the vehicle with just five minutes of training, he added. Or if you’re too tired to use the simple joystick, the eVTOL can fly itself autonomously.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, “everyone here can be a pilot,” zhao said. “Everyone can be a captain. ”.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, this sounds like a story from the very kinds of science fiction that sparked the creation of the land aircraft carrier in the first place – and yet, it isn’t. They’ve been showing up for almost a decade at this point. It’s far from the first time I’ve seen a flying car concept at a tech event. But what marks this one apart is that Xpeng says it has already taken 17,000 orders for the vehicle across China, the UAE and other Asian markets.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, “our advantage is we’re closer to commercialization,” zhao said. Xpeng has established the world’s first mass-production factory for flying cars in Guangzhou, with trial production beginning in November last year. Right now, it’s ramping up capacity and improving quality with the aim of eventually being able to build a flying car in 30 minutes.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, aridge has worked through many different concepts, including flying motorcycles, to finally find one ready for commercial production (plus it has a six-seater air taxi and integrated flying car in the works for the future too). If you have $300,000 going spare, the Land Aircraft Carrier could soon be yours.

Berdasarkan laporan, the vast majority of preorders are from individuals, according to xpeng, but the vehicle has also been designed for use in tourism and search and rescue. Zhao said it solves multiple problems with existing eVTOLs simultaneously: storage (it lives in the back of the mothership), recharging (it charges as the mothership is driving), transportation to and from appropriate flight sites, and ease of use.

Berdasarkan laporan, “i hope to make flying accessible to everyone as soon as possible,” zhao said. Right now, it takes around 20 to 30 hours of training to acquire the sport pilot license you’d need to fly the eVTOL. In China, Zhao said he’s in conversation with the regulator to reduce this, emphasizing his vehicle’s ease of use.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, zhao said he’s learned a lot from the aviation sector in china, where the land aircraft carrier has gone through extensive safety testing and will likely take to the skies first as a consumer-owned product as soon as next summer. Growing its low-altitude economy, which encompasses drone delivery and eVTOLs, is national policy for the country – in spite of calls for more regulation after a deadly crash in Beijing this summer.

Diungkapkan bahwa xpeng is also eyeing the european market, although the regulatory hurdles are likely to be substantial. “Europe’s aviation sector is highly developed,” Zhao said, expressing his respect for the region’s strict rules, but adding that the market was important. The company will also start exploring certification in the US next year, he said. Actual progress will depend on the outcomes, he added.

Berdasarkan laporan, in spite of zhao’s boundless optimism, it’s difficult to buy into the hype around his flying car without witnessing it in action in person. I’ve now seen the Land Aircraft Carrier twice in different locations and videos of it in operation, but I want to observe the eVTOL’s deployment from the mothership and its airborne skills for myself.

Diungkapkan bahwa at one point during his web summit talk, zhao climbed into the cockpit of the evtol on stage. For a moment it seemed as though he might fly it right then and there inside Lisbon’s cavernous ME Arena. The audience raised their phones in unison, only to drop them again in disappointment when they realized Zhao wasn’t actually going to take off.

No matter how idiot-proof it might be to fly, it turns out European health and safety rules still apply.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the us government has expanded the use of an ai tool for advising air traffic controllers to assist in managing air traffic across the entire national airspace system. Airline executives have voiced support for the rollout, but the US labor union representing air traffic controllers has said it was not involved in designing or testing the AI-driven system.

Diungkapkan bahwa the federal aviation administration (faa) says the $875 million smart system has helped reroute 180 flights since being implemented in airspace over washington, dc, on september 21. The agency claims that this saved an average of 10 minutes per flight and almost 80 gallons of fuel per flight—and it is apparently hoping such results can be replicated nationwide through the expanded deployment.

“After a successful initial rollout to the National Capital Region in September, the FAA will now use SMART in the airspace of all 22 centers across the country to reduce delays, reduce fuel consumption and improve the travel experience for the flying public,” according to the agency statement posted on November 10.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the faa fact sheet describes smart as a cloud-based system that combines information about “weather patterns, flight paths, traffic flow and controller staffing metrics” to predict air traffic patterns. It is designed to make scheduling recommendations, identify optimal flight routes, and determine the best order of arrivals for aircraft.

However, a human team of FAA specialists based in DC is ultimately responsible for validating the SMART system recommendations before passing them along to air traffic control facilities across the country, according to the agency.

Sebagaimana diketahui, furthermore, the ai-powered smart system “cannot be used to replace the critical role air traffic controllers play or take over control of an aircraft,” the faa clarified in the september 21 announcement about the initial deployment. Local air traffic controllers can decide whether or not to accept the SMART system recommendations.

The previous FAA announcement included supportive statements from Delta Air Lines CEO Ed Bastian and American Airlines CEO Robert Isom.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, but the national air traffic controllers association, which represents more than 15,000 members, also told flying magazine that it was not consulted or involved in the “design, testing, or implementation of smart and therefore cannot speak to its effect on the air traffic control workforce. ”.

Following the initial deployment in airspace above DC, the FAA expanded the SMART system’s coverage to air route traffic control centers in Atlanta along with Jacksonville and Miami in Florida, according to The Dallas Morning News.

The FAA also shared an example with The Dallas Morning News about how SMART recommended a shorter and faster route for a cargo flight arriving at Dallas-Fort Worth International Airport, although the newspaper noted that the agency did not identify the flight involved and has not provided information about how SMART may have assisted passenger flight traffic.

Ars has previously covered the SMART system’s development and lingering questions about how it works, as well as the air traffic controller shortage and other challenges facing the FAA.

(A government spokesperson told The Mirror that it's reviewing the law on prostitution. ).

AdultFriendFinder — readers’ pick for casual connections.

Tinder — top pick for fast hookups.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the report claims that "visitors to webcamming platforms are no longer just pornography viewers; they become, in effect, pornography directors. " It also contends that camming/livestreaming harms women and girls through sexual coercion and exploitation, security and privacy risks, perpetuates violent attitudes, and normalizes sexual exploitation. The report includes quotes from interviews with APPG and research such as one paper on webcam sex platform competition and another on Romanian women's experiences camming.

"The webcamming trade acts as a magnet for exploiters," Tonia Antoniazzi MP and Tracy Gilbert MP stated in the report's foreword.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, however, dr carolina are, digital criminologist at the london school of economics and political science, told mashable that the report doesn't consider that people can do sex work voluntarily. Berdasarkan laporan, the experiences narrated by participants are horrific and show how these platforms can be used for exploitation, are continued, adding however that the report as a whole seems to blame the job for exploitation, when exploitation is done by perpetrators. Diungkapkan bahwa the report also calls on the uk to outlaw "e-pimping," or individuals who facilitate and profit from another person performing on livestream, and that the country recognize e-pimping as human trafficking. Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, are said the investigations are reputable, but are used sensationally. Meanwhile, she pointed out that research shows that many people choose to do digital sex work for reasons ranging from personal preference to the fact that much of sex work, including camming, can be done from home (which suits immunocompromised people, people with disabilities, caretakers, or those otherwise not suited for a 9-5).

Digital sex work has also been found to reduce violence against sex workers — "an opportunity this report seems to ignore," Are stated.

Diungkapkan bahwa porn filmmaker and performer vex ashley told mashable, "we're seeing an unprecedented rollback of our sexual freedoms and lives online. ".

Additionally, the group's report recommends enabling the withdrawal of consent with the distribution of pre-recorded porn, as well as allowing law enforcement to access all content hosted and streamed by porn sites.

Sebagaimana diketahui, "the withdrawal of consent part of the recommendations is important, and so is the recognition of exploitation for those who extort and abuse cammers," are said. "But giving platforms and the police more surveillance power against an over-policed, over-censored and over-surveilled user base is concerning. ".

Berdasarkan laporan, removing a source of income from marginalized people doesn't protect them, she said, also pointing out that the report doesn't touch on poverty, which is one of the main drivers of sex work. "So this report is removing a source of income for the same women that it claims to protect," she said, "potentially pushing them into more underground work where they may be more exposed to physical violence. ".

#69. Google’s latest Search upgrade promises better answers to your most complicated questions

Google’s latest Search upgrade promises better answers to your most complicated questions

Tanggal: 12 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://techcrunch.com/2026/11/12/googles-latest-search-upgrade-promises-better-answers-to-your-most-complicated-questions/

Berdasarkan laporan, google search is getting better at understanding complicated questions, including those with multiple parts, highly specific requests, or confusing typos. The updates are coming via the company’s newly released Gemini 4 Hydrogen model, which Google claims is its “biggest model improvement to Search yet. ”.

While Google’s frontier models, Gemini 4 Carbon and Gemini 4 Argon, are best at deep reasoning for hard problems, Hydrogen is designed for fast execution across a variety of agentic workflows, or tasks in which an AI carries out multiple steps on its own, the company explained in an announcement.

Diungkapkan bahwa the idea behind the model’s release is that using the most powerful model isn’t always needed — sometimes a faster, cheaper, and reasonably smart one will do. 5 times faster than Gemini 3. Google says Hydrogen completes tasks 2. 8 Flash, its previous fast model, but it’s still pretty smart, even beating the more powerful Gemini 4 Argon on one broad intelligence benchmark, the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index, at its default high thinking level.

In Search, Hydrogen brings several improvements, including a better understanding of user intent, the ability to offer more helpful links and visual responses, and better answers across the different languages supported by Google’s AI Mode.

Sebagaimana diketahui, in terms of intent, google says hydrogen can handle more nuanced and complicated questions more quickly. This means people can ask their questions in their natural train of thought, including those that have multiple parts or that include highly specific requests. Hydrogen is also better at navigating hard-to-understand typos, Google says. Because of its improvements and better ability to follow instructions and call the right tools, Hydrogen is able to more precisely address each part of a user’s question.

Sebagaimana diketahui, its advanced reasoning also improves search’s fan-out technique, which breaks down a single user’s prompt into multiple subqueries. This allows people to discover websites related to the query that they may have otherwise missed, the blog post explains.

The addition of Hydrogen to Search will also mean more images, structured responses, comparison tables, and custom tools will appear as visual responses to users’ queries in AI Mode.

Google also says Hydrogen can work on its own for everyday work in areas like writing code, running tests, or verifying code changes, or it can be paired with Carbon and Argon in workflows that combine several models.

The model offers four thinking levels: low, medium, high (default), and a new, extra-high tier (“xhigh”), all of which are designed to complete tasks faster with fewer output tokens.

Berdasarkan laporan, on multi-step tasks like deep research, data analysis, and broad codebase navigation, hydrogen ranks no. 5 on Agent Arena’s benchmarks, the company pointed out.

Google says the Hydrogen update is rolling out to all Search users globally.

#72. Evolving metal extraction processes

📅 10 Nov 2026

Evolving metal extraction processes

Tanggal: 10 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.technologyreview.com/2026/11/10/1147726/evolving-metal-extraction-processes/

Rethinking how metals are extracted could unlock lower-emission production, make better use of mineral resources, and strengthen critical-material supply chains.

The metals industry has experienced transformational moments before: the Bessemer process, flash smelting, electric arc furnaces, and modern continuous casting all changed what was possible.

Berdasarkan laporan, yet, for more than a century, most extraction processes rely on techniques and pathways that would be familiar to metallurgists from generations ago. Processes have become larger and control systems smarter, but the fundamental science behind separating metals from ores has changed less than many realize.

Today’s materials challenges are different from those of the 20th century, but why are critical metals still produced using largely the same scientific foundations?.

EvoMaterials, a technology platform developed by Outokumpu—the global leader in sustainable stainless steel and the producer of ferrochrome with 67% lower carbon footprint than the industry average—is exploring that question by rethinking how metals can be extracted:.

Diungkapkan bahwa “we decided to go beyond the current constraints and look fundamentally at what’s the best way to do this with the benefit of the scientific engineering knowledge and hindsight that we have today,” says caspar stinn, technical director for extractive metallurgy at outokumpu. “We’re looking at how we can reimagine metals production. ”.

Diungkapkan bahwa as economies expand and the world becomes increasingly electrified, data and scientific models point to rising demand for many minerals, driven by technologies ranging from data centers to aerospace, water treatment, energy systems, and defence. According to Antoine Allanore, professor of metallurgy at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology (MIT) this coincides with many Western economies having reduced their domestic processing capacity for the very metals those industries depend on.

Metallurgy is now strategically important, shaped not only by cost and availability but also by carbon footprint, geographic origin and supply-chain resilience.

Sebagaimana diketahui, that reality is particularly relevant for chromium and other specialty metals used in high-temperature and extreme environments. Chromium-based materials play a critical role in aerospace systems, power generation, corrosion-resistant infrastructure and defense technologies, where materials must perform under demanding conditions.

Sebagaimana diketahui, for decades, metallurgical innovation largely focused on improving yields, energy efficiency and process control. EvoMaterials is based on the idea that some metallurgical processes may benefit from entirely different chemical pathways.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the platform originates from research into sulfidation-based processing technologies, initially pursued to reduce carbon emissions associated with ferrochrome production. Laboratory work revealed broader potential.

Berdasarkan laporan, lab-scale trials demonstrated that these alternative process chemistries could potentially do more than lower emissions. They could recover valuable metals from lower grade resources and industrial side streams while fundamentally altering how separation processes are performed. The opportunity is to rethink how mineral resources are used and how much value can be extracted from them, bringing in greater resource efficiency and stronger industrial competitiveness.

Sebagaimana diketahui, development of the technology began in the united states in 2021 for chromite from outokumpu’s kemi mine in finland, the only chrome mine in the european union and one of the few such operations across the western world. Since then, Outokumpu has evolved the technology through extensive research and development, combining new process chemistries with proprietary metallurgical expertise, supported in part by a non-exclusive patent license agreement from MIT.

Sebagaimana diketahui, “the technology is a new application for separating metallic elements from materials,” explains allanore. Historically, that separation has been achieved using carbon- and energy-intensive approaches. The new method creates a different chemical environment that enables more efficient extraction with fewer losses and fewer unwanted by-products, recovering critical materials from resources considered waste.

EvoMaterials sits at the intersection of several scientific disciplines, a combination that strongly resonates with Stinn, who completed his PhD in Materials Science and Engineering at MIT, where his research focused on low-carbon metals processing and recycling technologies.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, modern materials innovation draws on a growing mix of chemistry, materials science, physics, computational modeling, and engineering. With advanced simulation tools and AI helping researchers identify promising directions, scientific discovery still depends on experimentation and testing in the lab—on getting your hands dirty and doing the hard work.

Berdasarkan laporan, “science today is much more interdisciplinary than it was, and the collaboration across disciplines reveals new scientific opportunities,” says stinn. Engineering can translate those opportunities into more efficient and cost-competitive metals production.

Sebagaimana diketahui, a technically significant aspect of evomaterials is that it’s not a single process, but a technology platform. Allanore compares EvoMaterials to platform technologies in other industries, where a single scientific breakthrough can enable multiple downstream applications.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, once a new extraction pathway has been mastered for one material system, the same scientific principles may be adapted to entirely different metals and mineral resources. The initial application becomes only the starting point.

“The future and the potential impact might be much broader than the original and current developments that are happening,” Allanore explains.

That possibility is increasingly important as industries seek secure supplies of nickel, chromium, molybdenum, and other strategic materials needed for advanced manufacturing.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the broader implication extends beyond metallurgy. Companies that develop proprietary process technologies may create value through production but also through intellectual property and scientific expertise.

Based on Outokumpu’s technology leadership, that transition could create entirely new categories of value, enabling the production of high-value critical materials from ores and resource streams that previously appeared uneconomical or inaccessible.

The result would be a fundamental shift in how metals are manufactured, where sustainability, resource efficiency, supply security, and economic value become outcomes of the same technological architecture rather than separate objectives.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the next step for evomaterials is pilot-scale validation, with a pilot plant in new hampshire to begin operations in the first half of 2027. The facility will scale the proprietary technology from laboratory to one-ton production, providing a step toward industrial-scale deployment targeted for 2030. Beyond producing low-CO2, chromium-enriched ferrochrome and chromium metal, the platform could be adapted to other strategic materials, including nickel and molybdenum.

The work raises a broader question—how many of today’s metallurgical processes would look the same if they were invented from scratch? Or could those routes be designed differently today?.

The next revolution in materials may begin by rethinking how to extract the metals that society depends on.

Read more about this topic and hear more from Caspar Stinn and Antoine Allanore.

#74. Google really needs you to know it cares about smart glasses privacy

📅 12 Nov 2026

Google really needs you to know it cares about smart glasses privacy

Tanggal: 12 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.engadget.com/2314414/google-really-wants-you-to-know-it-cares-about-smart-glasses-privacy/

Public trust in smart glasses is very important for selling lots of smart glasses.

Diungkapkan bahwa the world has changed in the ten years since snap first launched its camera-equipped spectacles. Nowadays, thanks to the rise of platforms like TikTok and Reels, anyone can be an influencer. Not only has the smart glasses market grown, the number of people sharing videos online has also jumped significantly. And the possibility of innocent passersby inadvertently being included in a viral clip is far higher than it was.

Sebagaimana diketahui, it is in this climate that google launches its intelligent eyewear devices today. This year has already seen Meta catch heat for what people called its "pervert glasses" or "creep glasses. " In addition to making people feel uncomfortable about being spied on or filmed without their consent, the controversy has also discouraged existing users of those glasses from continuing to wear them, not to mention possibly putting off potential buyers.

Berdasarkan laporan, google has been working on this launch for years, and it can be easy to see why it doesn't want its own camera-equipped glasses to suffer the same backlash or be painted by the same brush. Google is taking a fairly comprehensive approach that goes beyond device-specific measures, and includes using its wide sphere of influence to prevent surreptitious videos spreading online. It's published a blog post outlining the privacy protections it's bringing to the platform, and they don't just revolve around preventing tampering with the LED indicator lights. Perhaps that's why it's taking pains to make its privacy policies around the intelligent eyewear platform clear today. In fact, Juston Payne, the lead for XR at Google, told Engadget that there are quite a few ways privacy protection has been considered.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, let's start with what's happening on the glasses. It's basically table stakes at this point, but they all have an LED light on them to indicate when someone is taking a picture or recording a video. The light, which sits on the left side of the frame while the camera is next to the right eye, has sensors to detect if it's covered or tampered with and will prevent the capture of pictures or video.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, "unfortunately, some of the glasses that have launched in the past launched without any kind of detection for those things, and that broke trust. "And that's a problem," he added. " Payne said. He also said Google's methods are "pretty effective," though that's something that we'll have to test for ourselves to verify.

Sebagaimana diketahui, and just as there are bad actors who will continue to try to break security protections for any safe in the world or online, there will be people attempting to get around google's anti-tampering measures here. Payne said "there will always be ways around what we build, and then we'll try to fix those holes," and that he expects there will be an ongoing back-and-forth. "But nonetheless, we're very happy with where we're starting on this one. ".

Sebagaimana diketahui, one of the main functions of google's smart glasses is the ability for gemini ai to use the camera to see what the wearer is looking at and provide more relevant information. During this process, the company says that the camera visuals won't be stored in your Gemini history. When there are faces in view, Google says "your glasses are also designed to automatically redact bystanders' faces before Gemini processes the visuals. ".

Sebagaimana diketahui, the camera stream also won't be used in ai training or ad targeting, and google says any data that is sent off the glasses for processing, say in the cloud or on your phone, is encrypted for transit. It's also promising to bring the Private AI Compute processing platform to glasses, enabling these new devices to use the "hardware-secured sealed cloud environment" for greater processing.

Sebagaimana diketahui, while the camera may be the most obvious recording sensor on these devices, they also have four microphones onboard to allow you to speak to gemini or get translations for people around you. Google uses beamforming to help focus on the individuals you're looking at when deciding whose speech to translate, and the company also said it "designed Gemini to focus on your voice by default, and not other voices around you, using directional microphones on the glasses. ".

Payne said that the microphones will filter out "all the world audio, as we call it, the bystander audio," It helps prevent accidental recording of people in your vicinity, but also improves Gemini's effectiveness by making sure it doesn't confuse someone else's heated argument as your query.

Sebagaimana diketahui, of course, to make the glasses more useful, you'll have to grant it access to your apps and personal information. The intelligent eyewear can work with apps like Messages, Keep or YouTube Music, for instance, to send replies or create lists for you. Like on most phones, you'll have to grant permission to specific apps before they can access the camera on your glasses, and even after you do, you can still add or revoke access for every app.

Diungkapkan bahwa google also said you can view your past interactions with gemini, delete individual chats or all of them. You'll also be able to decide if your conversations are used to train AI. And to make sure there's no confusion over whether you left the glasses on or off, and if the microphones or camera might still be tuning in, all the new eyewear have a power switch with a clear red indicator to tell you when they've been shut down.

Diungkapkan bahwa most intriguing are the measures google is implementing across its entire ecosystem. The company said it has protections in place "across Google apps and services to deter misuse of the glasses," and they're pretty far-reaching.

Diungkapkan bahwa for one thing, google shopping and google ads will "ban the sale and advertising of stickers or accessories designed to hide recording lights. ".

Diungkapkan bahwa the company is also working to cull the demand for videos of a harassing or creepy nature. Payne said that one of the problems Google has seen is a small number of people "who use glasses to take creepy videos. ".

Diungkapkan bahwa youtube will "prohibit content that depicts things like harassment and unwanted sexualization. Any video uploaded to YouTube — whether it's recorded on a phone, a camera, or glasses — has to follow these policies, and videos that don't are removed. ".

Diungkapkan bahwa there are also considerations for apps that request permission to use the cameras on these devices. "There's multiple approval layers if an app wants to use the camera," Payne said. "And there's actually some use cases that we're just blanket cutting off. ".

Berdasarkan laporan, to that end, google said that the play store and api policies will "prohibit apps from using the camera for social live-streaming or real-time facial identification, and from changing the behavior of the outer indicator light. " This live-streaming restriction also applies to YouTube.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, of course, since the eyewear will be compatible with ios devices as well, it's possible that someone finds an app of that nature in the app store and uses it. And though Google may ban the advertisement or sale of physical goods that can be used to hide the LED indicator, people could very easily procure one on Amazon or Temu. There's more that needs to be done against this problem, and Google alone cannot cover all bases.

Diungkapkan bahwa sure, there's the honor system approach that most modern recording devices already use. Things like requiring an 18+ Google account to activate an intelligent eyewear device and asking users to agree to not recording others without permission or in sensitive places are in place here as well.

Diungkapkan bahwa but the responsibility of prevention of misuse doesn't just fall to the user or google. "We hope that it resonates with people, and we hope that as a byproduct of that, some others in this space say, 'You know what? We should probably tighten up some of our policies. There needs to be greater collaboration across the industry for these measures to be effective. Payne said that Google is sharing these statements now in an attempt to set an example and send a message. '".

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, payne believes that there is time to regain the public's trust. It allows the company a chance to "reset this conversation a bit, raise the bar on privacy. He said that while there is momentum building in the smart glasses space, it is still early days for the category. ".

Diungkapkan bahwa if it's able to get the attention and cooperation of other players in the space, google stands to benefit. "We think that that will then earn a lot of trust back in the category, then we can focus a lot on how cool and valuable these are. ".

Instead of having marketing teams spend weeks scrolling through social media, building spreadsheets, and sending individual DMs, Nectar wants its agent to handle much of that work automatically.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, nectar joins other companies introducing agentic ai assistants designed to automate influencer outreach, including aspire and grin. U. S. The launch also comes as more brands turn to creators to reach customers. spending on creator advertising is expected to reach $44 billion in 2026, according to the Interactive Advertising Bureau. As companies work with hundreds or even thousands of creators, keeping track of relationships and measuring results can get pretty difficult.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, nectar says its creator agent searches more than 300 million creator profiles to find potential partners, including smaller creators who may not yet have a large following but are gaining traction. The system analyzes videos to understand what creators post about, how their content fits a brand, and whether their previous partnerships are appropriate. It also checks brand safety by reviewing content in context rather than simply searching for specific keywords.

Nectar then creates ranked lists of recommendations and adds new matches as creators become more popular.

Berdasarkan laporan, once it finds a potential match, the agent can draft and send messages in a brand’s voice, create custom landing pages to collect creator information, and help manage contracts, product gifting, and shipping details. It also remembers previous conversations and interactions, so brands can keep track of relationships without relying on spreadsheets.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, “brands can share voice guidelines in any format, and nectar picks up the rest from their history,” ceo misbah uraizee tells techcrunch. Nectar understands what is being said in a video, reads the tone of the conversation, and knows the difference between a quote post on X and a TikTok comment section. A brand should not sound identical in both, and with Nectar it doesn’t. “On top of that sits a set of proprietary guardrails that keep every draft on tone and in context. ”.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, another feature looks for personal milestones in creators’ lives, such as an engagement, a new baby, or completing a marathon. The agent can then suggest a personalized message or gift, helping brands build relationships that feel less like one-off advertising deals.

Creator Agent is available today globally and covers Instagram creators and TikTokers.

The company plans to make the agent available through its Model Context Protocol (MCP), allowing teams to use it through AI assistants such as Claude, ChatGPT, Gemini, and Copilot, as well as their own custom-built agents.

This past May, Nectar raised a $30 million Series A round led by Menlo Ventures and its Anthology Fund, which is a joint initiative launched with Anthropic.

#80. The backlash about data centers might really just be about electricity

📅 09 Nov 2026

The backlash about data centers might really just be about electricity

Tanggal: 09 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.technologyreview.com/2026/11/09/1148194/the-backlash-about-data-centers-might-really-just-be-about-electricity/

Diungkapkan bahwa big tech sees a culture war over progress. But the real fault line is electricity: drawing it from the grid and generating it onsite provoke different kinds of backlash, neither easily solved by public relations.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, this story originally appeared in the algorithm, our weekly newsletter on ai. To get stories like this in your inbox first, sign up here.

Berdasarkan laporan, as voters went to the polls across the us last week, i was in ashburn, virginia, part of what’s known as data center alley—the world’s largest data center hub. It’s also where the backlash now sweeping the country arguably first began taking shape.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, driving through it is surreal. Concrete monolithic buildings loom along every major road, with names like Skybox and CloudHQ.

Diungkapkan bahwa it’s accepted wisdom in big tech that the war against data centers must be about something bigger than just data centers themselves. Two days after the midterms, OpenAI’s chief global affairs officer, Chris Lehane, wrote that data centers “have become a proxy for public unease about affordability, corporate power, and people losing control over their futures. ” It’s a culture war, in other words.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, but spending a few days in data center alley left me wondering if it’s really the proxy that lehane describes. I came away convinced that the data center backlash is more about electricity than Big Tech admits. The industry can improve its image, but it can’t escape the physical consequences of its enormous appetite for electricity.

Sebagaimana diketahui, here’s why. There are two ways to power the sort of data center that AI companies want: connecting to the grid, or generating electricity onsite. In Virginia’s Loudoun County, where data centers are ubiquitous but have been built at a steadier pace than the breakneck expansion now underway elsewhere in the country, most are connected to the existing grid.

Berdasarkan laporan, one facility i went inside, operated by equinix, has massive diesel generators onsite for backup but gets its power from the local utility, dominion energy. Much of Dominion’s electricity is generated by natural gas (which is cleaner than coal or oil, but worse than renewables).

Sebagaimana diketahui, the average data center operating in this part of virginia today has a power capacity of 54 megawatts. That’s more than the power draw of the Denver International Airport.

Sebagaimana diketahui, elena schlossberg, a prominent activist against data centers in virginia, told me she’s “always banging my head against the wall” when the industry paints the fight as a culture war. “It was always about power,” she says—that is, electricity.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, some virginia protesters appear more animated by a broader anti-tech populism than schlossberg, to be fair. But it’s the particular consequences of drawing so much power from the grid that have done the most to shape how the backlash has played out.

Berdasarkan laporan, recent protests have led to new rules from the state that data centers must pay fully for the cost of new transmission lines to the grid and make sure they’re not spread among everyone else. Data center developers told me they’re preparing for new rules that would cut them off from grid power during peak demand. Schlossberg also worries about the downstream effects of a strained grid—for example, that data centers will run more diesel generators or that Dominion Energy will expand fossil fuel inputs rather than renewables to meet demand.

Berdasarkan laporan, the overwhelming majority of ai data centers being built elsewhere in the country are not designed this way. Companies also build diesel generators for backup. The scale desired is so massive that companies are setting up in rural areas where there is virtually no grid infrastructure to connect to. Building there means bringing your own power (so-called “behind the meter” power), in the form of natural-gas-powered turbines. Anthropic, for example, has reportedly agreed to pay $3. 4 billion for gas turbines in what’s described as the largest power generation purchase by an AI company.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, even if grids were nearby, they’d be unlikely to serve the amount of power demanded. The smallest data centers attractive for AI training are 300 megawatts. It’s a lot of power for one industrial site, but not unprecedented: One data center developer told me he’s eyeing a former steel mill already equipped to draw that much electricity from the grid.

Diungkapkan bahwa but the ideal facilities are more like 6,000 megawatts. That’s the estimated draw of the city of Chicago, which is powered by more than 20 power plants within the city alone (and dozens farther out).

Diungkapkan bahwa the notion of data center companies’ bringing their own power might seem attractive at first, because they wouldn’t be straining the grid. But generating electricity at this scale inevitably affects surrounding communities, and when public utilities build infrastructure of this magnitude, communities have traditionally expected a say in where it goes. Now, private companies are undertaking projects on a similar scale.

Diungkapkan bahwa natural-gas turbines of any scale release air pollutants. When diesel generators are used, it’s even worse. And in the unprecedented rush to get these facilities operating, companies have become horrible neighbors (recall that Elon Musk violated air quality laws when he set up dozens of turbines to power a data center in Memphis, according to the Environmental Protection Agency).

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, big tech’s tendency to chalk the backlash up to a culture war obfuscates one simple fact: there’s only so pleasant you can make a small city of computers to live around. Sure, companies can pursue better deals that raise tax revenues, hire local workers, and get more community involvement, as the protests are leading them to do. But if a small town is asked to welcome a Walt Disney World, an international airport, a steel plant, and the power plants to run them all, should we be surprised by its trepidation?.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, again, that’s not to say this is the sole reason for opposition to data centers. Fears of job losses, existential risks, and concentrated corporate power all fuel the backlash, as does misinformation (most facilities use far less water than many people think). Nor is consuming enormous amounts of electricity inherently bad: Many of the advances that have improved modern life have required just that.

Sebagaimana diketahui, but as one developer recently told me, industry insiders see their ambitions as constrained less by public opposition than by a lack of electricity. That should tell us something.

Diungkapkan bahwa so what happens next? it’s possible that newly elected politicians’ actual stances on data centers won’t be as negative as the ones they campaigned on. But what seems true regardless is that if new data centers need their own power generated onsite, they’ll go where there are the fewest people able to resist them. That might mean the Permian Basin, where a network of natural-gas lines can be easy for developers to connect to and populations are sparse. Companies might also try their chances abroad; Google, in fact, announced the day after the elections that it will spend $15 billion on data center projects in Malaysia.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, but there’s one place where big tech may find virtually no limits at all, as elon musk posted just hours after the midterms results came rolling in: “data centers in space looking pretty appealing right now. ”.

#81. The first batch of Android XR smartglasses made me rethink my stance on specs without displays

📅 12 Nov 2026

The first batch of Android XR smartglasses made me rethink my stance on specs without displays

Tanggal: 12 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.engadget.com/2314258/android-xr-smartglasses-hands-on/

I still want models with built-in screens, but Google’s first run of intelligent eyewear has a lot to offer.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the first device powered by android xr came out last year when samsung released the galaxy xr headset. But this fall, Google is taking its augmented reality platform in a different direction with the launch of intelligent eyewear from partners such as Warby Parker and Gentle Monster. This gives Google its own version of lightweight smartglasses to rival competitors like the third-gen Ray-Ban Meta line, and after testing them out, it made me reconsider my feelings about smart specs without built-in displays.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, as this first generation of intelligent eyewear is a bit of a departure from previous android xr devices, i think it's important to get some of the basics out of the way first. For this family of specs, Google is in charge of the OS while Samsung is handling much of the tech — including things like the cameras, mics, touch sensors and more. All of that then gets handed over to Warby Parker and Gentle Monster, who are in charge of the glasses design, lenses, general sales and customer support.

Diungkapkan bahwa right off the bat, this seems like a great division of responsibilities because it allows each company to do what they're best at. Google handles the software, Samsung takes care of the hardware and the real glasses makers ensure you have good-looking frames with the right prescriptions (you can even opt for transition/photochromic lenses). And right out of the gate, it feels like there's already a lot of interesting styles and color combos to choose from, regardless if you're a bit more fashion-forward or if you, like me, prefer a more traditional frame.

Diungkapkan bahwa another important thing to note is that while gentle monster's eyewear will be a touch more expensive than warby parker's models ($449 and $395, respectively), they will have the same general tech specs. Those include the same 2GB of RAM and 64GB of storage, a 12MP camera (that also handles up to 3K video), stereo speakers, far-field mics and a built-in touch sensor. Battery life is also the same across the board with around nine hours of use on a single charge, while the case for the glasses stores enough juice for multiple full charges.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, furthermore, you won't be required to have a paid gemini plan to use any of the features of the glasses; it's all free. These glasses will even work with both Android devices and iPhones with feature parity across both OSes. That said, there won't be any options with a built-in display, which means Google won't have a true rival to the Meta Ray-Ban Display glasses, at least not yet.

Berdasarkan laporan, when it comes to features, it's no surprise that these glasses have a lot of overlap with the ray-ban meta specs. There's also a touch sensor built into the right arm for doing stuff like controlling volume, pausing audio or dismissing Gemini. And of course, the glasses are connected to your phone wirelessly (either Bluetooth or Wi-Fi depending on the situation) so you have access to streaming music, notifications, messages, supported apps and more. There's a physical button near the right temple for capturing images: A short press takes a picture while a long press records videos. However, the real lynchpin of the entire platform is Google's AI, which can be easily summoned via voice controls or by performing a long press on the touch panel.

Berdasarkan laporan, now i'll admit that i don't interact with gemini all that often when i'm using a phone or a laptop. When I already have access to a screen, a keyboard and all sorts of dedicated apps, so I find I can often perform tasks faster manually than asking an AI assistant to do them. But when wearing smartglasses, it's a whole different story. If you want to respond to a text, get turn-by-turn directions or start some tunes, you can do all that hands-free with simple voice commands while keeping your phone in your pocket. Granted, that is sort of table stakes for smartglasses these days, but being able to walk around with your head up while dodging traffic or other pedestrians can't be understated.

Sebagaimana diketahui, but it goes deeper, because thanks to gemini's intelligence and persistent memory between conversations, the ai in your glasses has a much deeper understanding of how to help you. Instead of constantly having to say a wake word all the time, you can have more natural back and forth dialogue. This allows you to get updates on your events, make adjustments to questions and pick up on previous queries even when they happen throughout the course of your day (you can specify how long you want Gemini to remember conversations).

Sebagaimana diketahui, where things get really interesting is the combination of computer vision and ai, which allowed me to do things like pick up a physical invite card and simply ask gemini to add it to my calendar. It can even do rough estimates for how much of a certain food has been added, so if you're not worried about being super precise, you can leave your measuring cups in a drawer. No need to grab my phone, open up an app and add details like the time, date and location myself. I was also able to do things like simply look at a bunch of different ingredients and ask Gemini to make a smoothie from what was in front of me. And if you run out of certain foods, you can easily tell Gemini to add something to your grocery list.

Sebagaimana diketahui, then there are other features like live translation, which feels kind of magical. Not only does this let you switch speakers naturally just by looking at someone else, Gemini will even adjust the output of a translation to sound similar to the original speaker. The glasses are designed so that the mics are directed in a cone-shaped space in front of you, so that even in a room with other conversations going on, the glasses don't get confused. This allows you to follow along in real-time almost as well as someone who speaks the language naturally.

Berdasarkan laporan, that said, the thing that impressed me the most about these android xr glasses is the platform itself. Compared to some rivals where a lot of features feel like a work in progress, Google's OS feels much more mature. This includes little touches like dedicated sounds when Gemini accesses your camera, when the glasses take a photo or video, when Gemini leverages external AI and more. Google has done a pretty good job of translating a lot of the most important features you use on your phone to a medium without a screen.

Berdasarkan laporan, then there's google's approach to privacy, which looks to be a step up from the competition. Furthermore, Google says images and info sent to Gemini will stay on your device and will not be used to train AI or for ad targeting. In addition to each pair of glasses coming with an LED indicator that blocks you from taking pictures or videos when it's covered up or disabled, Google also isn't supporting features like livestreaming video directly from the specs. That might not sound like much, but considering Google owns YouTube and generates billions from advertising, the simple act of leaving money on the table in favor of privacy is a welcome departure from Meta's glasses. Those have always felt like they are meant to expand the reach of Facebook and Instagram.

Berdasarkan laporan, the one caveat to all this is that you do have to buy into talking to and relying rather heavily on gemini. They're surprisingly full-featured, and I don't think it's a stretch to say that compared to rival assistants like Siri, Muse and others, Gemini is the smartest of the bunch. So while I'm still waiting for companies to deliver streamlined specs with built-in displays, these audio-first options feel like much more than a stepping stone towards that. I'm still not sure I'm 100 percent on board with that, but at least for me, these glasses make a better argument for always-on AI support than almost any other class of device I've used. So even if you primarily want these for playing music, keeping tabs on your schedule and getting occasional help from AI, Google's first batch of Android XR-powered intelligent eyewear feels like it's already jumped to the front of the pack.

Pre-orders for the new family of Android XR intelligent eyewear from both Warby Parker and Gentle Monster begin today with official sales slated for December 10.

#83. The Elder Scrolls' most obscure adventure gets a 4K PC makeover

📅 12 Nov 2026

The Elder Scrolls' most obscure adventure gets a 4K PC makeover

Tanggal: 12 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://arstechnica.com/gaming/2026/11/the-elder-scrolls-most-obscure-adventure-gets-a-4k-pc-makeover/

N-Gage exclusive Shadowkey gets an AI-coded glow-up with plenty of new features.

So, you think you’re an Elder Scrolls superfan? You say you’ve been there since The Elder Scrolls Arena on MS-DOS and have logged hundreds of hours in The Elder Scrolls Online? You say you’ve bought all of the roughly 5,000 re-releases and remasters of Skyrim that have been made available in the last 15 years?.

Tell me, then: What do you think of The Elder Scrolls Travels: Shadowkey?.

What’s that? You’ve never played Shadowkey? You weren’t there day one back in 2004, Nokia N-Gage in hand, ready to experience the game’s 176 x 208 resolution mobile hack-and-slash RPG combat for yourself? And you call yourself a real Elder Scrolls fan?.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, well, don’t worry. Now you can fill in this crucial gap in your history without even having to track down functional, decades-old N-Gage hardware. That’s thanks to Shadowkey: Reforged, a free fan-made PC port that pairs updated art with the original game files and scripts for an upscaled, 4K experience that runs natively on PC, no N-Gage or emulator needed.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, moving from a pre-iphone mobile game to a modern pc obviously comes with major graphical upgrades, powered by a completely rewritten pc graphics engine. What was once a cramped portrait orientation on the N-Gage has now been expanded for a 16:9 monitor standard that displays at up to 120 fps (though the game’s logic still matches the original game’s 25 fps). In addition to newly retextured character and environmental models, the new port also sports small touches like bloom lighting, rippling water, and an upgraded interface with sharper text rendering than was possible on an ancient mobile phone.

Berdasarkan laporan, using the original game files (which you can obtain from an easy-to-find legitimate copy of the game, of course) means that reforged‘s quests, dialogue, and game rules are “worked out from the original program,” as the game’s website puts it. That said, the game’s “Modern” mode adds a few touches like smarter enemy AI, fall damage, searchable containers, and a fast travel system that are missing from the original game (and from Reforged‘s more authentic “Classic” mode). The Modern mode also includes some welcome quality-of-life improvements like controller rumble, a smoother on-screen interface, and “better death poses. ”.

Berdasarkan laporan, those with a disposition against vibe-coded clones and ports should know that reforged author dan whelan writes that he used “ai to assist with coding and building the engine, and with debugging,” as well as for the creation of “most of the modern, higher resolution artwork. Whelan has been releasing daily updates to the project and seems set to continue, if the current “Version 0. ” But those who are OK with this AI assistance should be happy to see the project moved from its first playable version in late October to a full-featured “release day” build for Windows, Mac, and Android that came out Wednesday. 2. 9” designation is any indication.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the inherent limitations of 2000s-era n-gage game development (which helped earn the original release some middling review scores) are still pretty apparent in even this reforged remake. Still, it’s nice that Elder Scrolls completionists can now experience one of the series’ least-played releases. At the very least, it’s something to tinker with as we all continue the long wait for Elder Scrolls VI.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, “there's no good news right now for consumers,” ubrani says. “It's unfortunate that the consumers are the ones who are going to struggle because of all this. ”.

Berdasarkan laporan, so maybe the deals won’t be great. If you do that, Ubrani recommends making sure it’s something you actually need. The memory crisis isn’t ending anytime soon, so now might be the time to get something you need. But they might be the best you can get for a while. And something that will keep working for a long time.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, “they should be purchasing the most amount of performance that they can afford today,” ubrani says. “We're going to face elevated pricing for years. You want that device to last you for a while. ”.
