#115. Inside the 42-Year Journey to Bring ‘Neuromancer’ to the Screen

📅 13 Nov 2026

Inside the 42-Year Journey to Bring ‘Neuromancer’ to the Screen

Tanggal: 13 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.wired.com/story/exclusive-apple-tv-neuromancer-creator-interviews/

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, briana middleton has something to show me. “Wait!” she says just as we’re about to end our Zoom call, reaching for something just beyond her screen.

Diungkapkan bahwa “when i found out we were going to be doing this,” she says, “i was at the thrift shop in my neighborhood and i found this. ” Then she points it at the camera: an issue of WIRED from 1995 featuring Keanu Reeves on the cover alongside the line “William Gibson on the making of Johnny Mnemonic. ”.

Diungkapkan bahwa very apropos. The 1995 film Johnny Mnemonic was based on a short story by Gibson, who also wrote the screenplay. Molly, the “razorgirl” Middleton plays in Apple TV’s forthcoming Neuromancer adaptation, made her first appearance in that short story. Her relationship with the protagonist Case, played in the series by Callum Turner, mirrors the one Reeves’ Neo had with Trinity in The Matrix, which is steeped in Gibsoneque lore.

Sebagaimana diketahui, for middleton, to be giving an interview to wired about neuromancer’s epic journey to the screen not long after finding a 1995 issue of the magazine in a secondhand store is so uncanny it almost feels like a glitch. “I was like, ‘This is crazy. “Dude, it was eight bucks,” she says, agreeing that eight dollars is a steal for a vintage WIRED. ’”.

Berdasarkan laporan, maybe all things happen exactly when they’re supposed to. Gibson originally released Neuromancer in 1984, back before hackers were cool. It focused on Case, a young computer jockey who can get online through a jack in his head. Back before hackers were CEOs. He teams up with Molly and a former military man named Armitage to break into the offworld home of the Tessier-Ashpool family, who became astoundingly rich thanks to the tech company they founded.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the book’s novel ideas—cyberspace, brain-computer interfaces, all-powerful ais—were years away from being mainstream, let alone possible. In the years since, there’s been much talk of turning Neuromancer into a movie or TV show, but it never took off, even as Hollywood mined sci-fi for hits.

Berdasarkan laporan, on january 22, all of that will change when apple tv releases its long-anticipated adaptation. Ahead of its release, WIRED got in touch with Middleton, Turner, and showrunners Graham Roland and JD Dillard to find out how they became the first to bring the book to screens—and the burden of taking on one of sci-fi’s classics.

Diungkapkan bahwa graham roland: it's a huge seminal book. I had not read it until the summer of 2020, but I was aware it was one of those white whales. It inspired a lot of things, and people had been trying to adapt it for years.

Berdasarkan laporan, callum turner: the world will be taken on a wild ride. It’s an epic. It’s Blade Runner; it’s 2001: A Space Odyssey; it’s The Fifth Element. This is the first time it comes onto our screens, and that's a big moment for us and fans of sci-fi.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, briana middleton: when we were shooting it and in the thick of it, it was easier to not get freaked out by the expectations. I tried to look at the expectations that people clearly have and the love that people have for this book and what these characters mean. It felt nice to be in a little bubble with the world that we had created. I definitely get freaked out sometimes and I just have to shut my computer and not think about it.

Sebagaimana diketahui, roland: i had a meeting at skydance, and they had given me the book and said, “hey, the rights of this book are going to come available again. JD and I had been friends for years prior to that, and were looking for a way to work together. So I read the book, and really responded to it right away. We’re going to try to adapt it as a TV show as opposed to a movie or several movies. " It made so much sense. He had also had a meeting at Skydance, and they had also given him the book.

Berdasarkan laporan, jd dillard: yeah, there was a wonderful kismet of this moment, and we were like, “wait, we’re both talking to people about this. Why don’t we do it together?”.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, dillard: drake has always been a fan of neuromancer and as a storyteller has great taste, but that's only part of it. The real magic is that he’s built an incredible team at [his production company] DreamCrew that he trusts to bring things to life once he identifies something he loves or believes in. Jason Shrier, who leads film and TV for DreamCrew, is one of the folks in our little brain trust on this show, and someone we pride as always having his finger on the pulse. But he has a relationship with [entertainment company] Anonymous Content, and Skydance, so it was kind of serendipitous that as Drake and DreamCrew had identified the books, all of these parties were starting to form and realize that they could work together to go get the rights. Drake, individually and by way of DreamCrew, is part of the mix and remains an important part of our process.

Diungkapkan bahwa roland: the way it was set up was that william gibson was going to be the decider of who was going to get the rights when they came available. So we went to work on a pitch and with the hope that we would be the people he would choose.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, we had heard that there were some bigger names, much bigger than jd and i. I just felt like there was a counterculture vibe about him and I was like, I don't think it matters that we're nobodies. I think if we can somehow communicate our passion for his book, and not just go and say, “Oh, obviously we’ll take care of your book, you can trust us,” but actually go in and do the work and come up with a thoughtful presentation and a thoughtful pitch, then I think we've got as good a shot as any.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, dillard: i'm sure bill would not mind us sharing this part of it, but it's very easy to look at these big pieces of literature or movies that have stood the test of time and just think that they were immaculately conceived. Just to hear him talk about where he struggled and what he was self-conscious about and then what he was surprised worked and what he wished he could have done, what he wished he had time to do—it was the first time Graham and I both looked at Neuromancer as a living text.

Berdasarkan laporan, dillard: one of the first questions we asked ourselves was “how do you make this feel new in spite of inspiring so many things that have now already come out ahead of this?” it was never going to be our ambition to out-cyberpunk 2077 cyberpunk 2077. An interesting one that came up really early in talking to him was that he had never perceived the world of Neuromancer as a dystopia. But what we could do is talk to Gibson and find out where, for him, some of those big tonal touchpoints are. Even that was a nice thing to just remember as we found our way through it.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the best we could do is bring people to the experience of what it felt like reading it for the first time in 1984. If you put up Blade Runner reference art, you're already behind it. Because anything beyond that, your reference points are already going to be derivative. The joke that we were even making when hiring [production designer] Luke [Hull] was like: Here's someone who's done Chernobyl and Andor, and in our minds Neuromancer is Chernobyl plus Andor. It's old-school and hi-fi and colliding those things together.

Diungkapkan bahwa roland: we didn't want the world of neuromancer to feel like x amount of years after the world that we were living in. In the teaser that opens the show, you see this piece of technology in the late '60s, early '70s that we know did not exist back then in our world. We wanted to announce right out of the gate: Don't be looking for the iteration of whatever phone you have in your pocket 50 years from now. We want this to be its own world.

Berdasarkan laporan, dillard: watching someone hack will only be exciting for so long. But what is stakes-driven is the danger to Case in doing it and the toll it takes on his body. Is he going to get the thing they need for the larger story for himself? Can he prove to himself that he can still do it? All of those things were immediately stickier than just watching him do it.

Berdasarkan laporan, a thing bill [gibson] said really early on is, he had always sort of imagined case as a neurological athlete. We took that and ran with it, in that it should take a toll. There's an expenditure to do this work.

Berdasarkan laporan, turner: i try not to think about how important it is and focus on my job of playing the scenes in front of me. JD and Graham had William Gibson’s approval, the scripts were brilliant, and the world so detailed and real. You can smell this world, which feels unique.

Diungkapkan bahwa roland: i'm so glad that one of the first things we did was go see bill gibson up in vancouver. He took the burden off of us and let us know that he wasn't expecting a literal translation of his text. He's the one that we're really beholden to.

Diungkapkan bahwa even in those early conversations with him, he mentioned, “oh, i always wanted to do a bigger tessier-ashpool story, the story of the family [behind the powerful ai called wintermute]. But if you find yourself looking for other things, other liberties or places to go into and make your own, that would be one. I had a book deadline, and I never really got to expand on that story. ” So that's why we came up with that storyline.

Berdasarkan laporan, roland: before we ever got to hiring the heads of any departments, jd planted a flag and said, “as much as we can, we want an in-camera aesthetic. We want to be practical. ” That really drove the decision to go to Japan, because trying to recreate Chiba City, we already have set extensions, obviously, because it takes place in the future, but the textures of Japan [are there], and we wanted it to feel like you were actually there.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the other thing we did, the thing i had never done on any other show, was we hired our production designer first, before any other head of a department. We knew that while we were still writing we needed that person to help us realize the world. What they were going to do practically—from a props perspective, from a concept art perspective—was going to inform our writing as well.

Diungkapkan bahwa dillard: it is a very bespoke version of the future; everything had to be machined and built and designed. We didn’t have all of these things that you could normally just go to the prop shop and get. But that is what drives the feeling of Neuromancer, feeling textured and grounded and real and a place you could go to, and it is both familiar to the past but aspirational to the future.

On the design of Case’s deck, the terminal he uses to access the virtual world of the matrix:.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, dillard: we saw a lot of decks. " That is the one we went with. If I remember correctly, I feel like we were on the way to being like, "OK, this is the deck. " Then Luke was like, "Sorry, before we make that, here's another one. But we were all resistant to it just feeling like a laptop. We wanted something that was a little bit like a station.

On getting the synth-rock band Son Lux for the score:.

Diungkapkan bahwa dillard: graham and i knew from the beginning we wanted neuromancer to feel different, not feel cyberpunk. In the same way that every other department had to honor retro-futurism in their own way, we wanted to charge our composer with doing the same.

Berdasarkan laporan, they're the best, and a band we've been fans of for a long time. I don't know how many Son Lux concerts I've gone to, and it was really cool in the last few years to see their turn into scores. Obviously, Everything Everywhere All at Once was a big one for them. Ryan [Lott] and the gang just really found Neuromancer's own sonic signature.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, roland: we had finished two or three scripts, and we started having conversations about casting. He was in LA for something else and he came to meet JD and I, and within five minutes of hearing his voice it was like, “This is the guy. It was the first and only meeting we had. Apple had had a great experience with Callum on Masters of the Air and they encouraged us to meet with him. ”.

Sebagaimana diketahui, turner: my vision was aligned with theirs, and luckily they asked me to join. I hadn’t read the book, but I was in a sci-fi mode. I remember we had [Neuromancer] in our house when I was a kid, but I’d never picked it up. I’d read I Am Legend and Do Androids Dream of Electric Sheep? when this came through. Graham and JD had written a wonderful character, and he felt so nuanced and detailed on the page—I jumped off from their starting point.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, case has the right mix of dangerous, courageous, and naive. Joe Strummer was a big influence. There’s an incredible documentary called Streetwise that I used as a base. Thom Yorke. Iggy Pop. There are always many, many things that go into a pot.

On maybe casting the actor who will be the next James Bond:.

Dillard: We're crossing our fingers and toes.

Berdasarkan laporan, dillard: we had case, so it was about “what completes the duo?” it’s a vibe thing; it’s a physicality thing. She could find these neat moments of warmth, but also not have that break her hard shell. They just had such a fun chemistry, and she just had the kind of no-nonsense grit to her. Callum's quite tall. Callum was shooting in Vancouver, and we brought a few people to read across from him. It was Briana for sure. And not that our shorter friends can't kick ass too, but you just wanted it to make sense on screen. I know everybody says this in their interviews about their show, but we really lucked out.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, middleton: i was not familiar with the book, and i had a meeting with david levine at anonymous content. When he initially told me about the character and the fact that she's got lenses over her eyes, I was like, “I don't think I want to do that. That doesn't sound fun at all. ” Then I met with JD and Graham months later, and they just sold me on it.

Berdasarkan laporan, i feel like molly is very funny in our show, and in the book, molly is very cool, and there's a lot that we don't see that is very clearly there. Molly is a guarded character, but there is so much going on, and we do get to see some more of the very human part of her outside of the “razorgirl” badass trope.

Sebagaimana diketahui, middleton: they were stuck on my face. It was double-sided sticky tape basically, but they held on. I think they fell off maybe once or twice throughout the entire shoot, and that includes fight scenes, so they held up. Steps were always a daunting thing. I couldn't really tell when I was going to step off something or be fine.

Diungkapkan bahwa whenever i took them off, it would feel weird. I would feel kind of exposed. I think at some point in the shoot, they started to feel probably how Molly feels, that they are very comforting and very much like, I can hide a little bit.

On having the jack—a brain-computer interface—attached to the back of your neck:.

On William Gibson’s cameo as a patron at the Chatsubo dive bar:.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, roland: we invited him to the set in london. I was like, “Oh wow, I guess they're not here for the scripts. I knew we had a lot of fans of his book working on our crew, but it wasn’t until he arrived that I saw the number of people that had brought their personal copy of Neuromancer hoping to get it signed. ” [Laughs].

Sebagaimana diketahui, dillard: i think we were like, “we want him to get out here, and we know it's a long slog from vancouver, but if we can get him out here, we got to put him in. We have to just immortalize his presence in the show. ” So part of it was timing, but it actually worked out for what we wanted because Chatsubo is such an iconic location in the book, and to see him there as a barfly just was like, “This will be so fun. ”.

On whether the other books in William Gibson’s Sprawl Trilogy—Count Zero and Mona Lisa Overdrive—could find their way onto the small screen:.

Sebagaimana diketahui, roland: it's too early to say at this point. I think we're still kind of focused on getting this one out into the world, but we'll see. I hope so.

On tech entrepreneurs being inspired by Neuromancer:.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, dillard: there's some great tweet that went viral last year that is sort of like, "new tech ceo says they're launching a product called skynet. ” It's like you're missing the point if you're naming the thing after the bad thing.

Sebagaimana diketahui, middleton: our show is asking what happens whenever corporations have unchecked power and when a technology is unchecked and there's no regulations, and our relationship with that technology goes unchecked. I think life gets much, much worse. Our show is asking what we lose without oversight. It's scary. I'm scared.

United Airlines blocks AI agents from booking flights, citing cybersecurity risks

United Airlines said it will restrict access to AI agents seeking to book flights and manage reservations on their users’ behalf, citing a risk to cybersecurity and undermining federal regulations.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the airline is the latest american corporate giant to prevent customers from using ai agents and autonomous assistants to access their systems. The move comes as airlines and banks are struggling to differentiate between real customers and AI systems operating on their behalf, such as when users share their logins with their AI assistants. Sharing passwords with apps and assistants can create security risks if those credentials get leaked or exposed.

Diungkapkan bahwa united warns that “sharing account credentials with personal, third-party, ai assistants can expose sensitive information, and actions taken by these tools may result in unintended purchases, account changes, or use of mileageplus miles. ”.

The airline also warns of a risk of violating federal aviation rules, such as requiring that a human completes flight check-ins to acknowledge that their bags do not contain banned substances.

Berdasarkan laporan, “as a result, united is taking steps to restrict access — directly within our digital platforms and indirectly via travel agencies and aggregators — to prohibit use by unauthorized, third-party personal ai agents or assistants,” the airline said in a statement. “This work includes updates to our booking, ticketing and distribution policies. ”.

The airline’s move follows a warning from banks, including Bank of America, which last week urged customers not to share their passwords with their AI assistants.

#118. Google faces calls for AI moratoriums in schools after Gemini pilot backlash

📅 12 Nov 2026

Google faces calls for AI moratoriums in schools after Gemini pilot backlash

Tanggal: 12 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://arstechnica.com/tech-policy/2026/11/families-fight-to-keep-googles-disturbing-ai-off-school-issued-chromebooks/

Sebagaimana diketahui, families confront google after teen’s lawsuit labels gemini a “suicide coach. ”.

CHICAGO—Families joined protests in seven cities nationwide on Wednesday, rallying against what they see as Google’s bid to entrench its AI models in schools, turn kids of all ages into Gemini guinea pigs, and hook them on AI.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the backlash follows a google statement last week, confirming that there will be no way for students to use google search without ai. While Google claimed it was giving schools “more choice, not less”—by turning off Search, Gemini, and Gemini Notebook by default—it would not provide an option that allowed Search without AI. For students, the only way to avoid interacting with AI was to remember to add “-ai” to every query, parents worried.

Diungkapkan bahwa in chicago, many families showed up to protest google, despite cold, rainy weather. Waving signs, dozens of protesters marched up to Google’s downtown office as workers seemed to be leaving for the day, shouting chants like “Hey Google, nice try, we don’t want your Gemini” and “Hey, Google, leave our kids alone!”.

Sebagaimana diketahui, called to action by a nonprofit grassroots advocacy group, the illinois families for public schools (ilfps), some parents and students had previously won a major ai fight. In August, the group pressured Chicago Public Schools (CPS) to pull out of a Gemini pilot that would have roped in all high school students districtwide—without consulting parents. And now, ILFPS is demanding a moratorium on AI until risks to students are better understood and CPS can draft a policy to protect students from potential learning setbacks or more harmful outcomes from engaging Google’s AI bots. If the group wins, it will join cities like Los Angeles and New York City in cautiously banning AI in schools.

Sebagaimana diketahui, most alarming to parents, google now faces a lawsuit from a 13-year-old student in durham, north carolina named “emma doe. ” Over time, normal school-related interactions with the chatbot led to more intense chats, and ultimately the chatbot allegedly coached Emma to plan her own suicide and funeral. ” As Emma has alleged, she was a happy, well-adjusted, straight-A student when she started using Gemini on her school-issued Chromebook. Emma’s parents had no idea she was using Gemini, as the lawsuit alleged that Google “deliberately” kept them in the dark while driving Emma into so-called “AI psychosis. The school warned her parents and averted the danger after an internal system flagged a chat labeled “Funeral,” but Emma’s story stoked fears of parents joining protests not just in Durham, but also in Boston; Boulder, Colorado; Chicago; Los Angeles; New York City; and Portland, Oregon.

Emma’s lawsuit accuses Google of exploiting its dominant position in education technology and “sneaking” Gemini into Chromebooks, while falsely marketing them as safe.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, “as a direct consequence of google’s choices, emma was baited by its defectively designed products into repeated, unmonitored, sycophantic ai chatbot interactions on her school chromebook without her parents ever knowing. And, but for a fortunate turn of events, Google’s AI may well have manipulated Emma into taking her own life,” the lawsuit alleged. “Google must be held to account for treating the lives of children as disposable in service of its bottom line. ”.

Berdasarkan laporan, google has promised to “continue to engage deeply with educators to ensure we are giving schools more choice, more controls, and improved search for learning. ” However, Google’s statements so far attempting to address parents’ concerns focus exclusively on documented harms to learning. On that front, Google claims that it’s solving the problem of AI eroding students’ critical thinking skills by launching yet another pilot for students. In this pilot, students using AI Mode and AI Overviews will be offered a “step-by-step guided learning through problems, so that students don’t get quick answers to schoolwork,” Google said.

Diungkapkan bahwa cassie creswell, executive director of ilfps, told ars that she’s been an advocate monitoring edtech issues for more than a decade. And even she was blindsided by Google’s AI moves.

Diungkapkan bahwa “i am aware of ai overviews when you search, which have a whole slew of problems, but i did not know that you really actually just have an interface where you can interact with gemini in the chatbot way on everyone’s chromebook still in chicago public schools,” creswell said. “And that’s so disturbing. ”.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, she acknowledged that kids encounter ai on their phones and shared that her daughter said her friends like using chatgpt better than gemini. But she said that the fact that some kids use AI on personal devices doesn’t mean that schools should be encouraging adoption at young ages when kids’ brains are still developing, and risks remain largely unknown.

“There’s all kinds of dangerous things out in the world, but we don’t have our school district handing it to kids at their desk,” Creswell said.

Meanwhile, schools seem to be part of the transparency problem.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, creswell said that currently, the chicago school district “is telling us their official line is that kids don’t have access to generative ai tools and that we don’t need a district-level policy on generative ai because they have guidebooks. ” However, she’s reviewed Google’s CPS contracts, and they suggest that kids are interacting with generative AI and frontier models. The ongoing confusion has led parents to demand “a real policy” that the CPS “board votes on and that has the input of teachers, parents, students, and experts who are not being funded by the tech industry. ”.

Berdasarkan laporan, creswell told ars that parents are particularly upset that google is not transparent about how it processes and uses student data. She’s exhaustively researched Google contracts through Freedom of Information Act requests and told Ars that dozens of agreements she reviewed offer no indication of how CPS partners like Google—as well as Anthropic and OpenAI—are handling student data. Although she understands that “it’s probably just an honest statement of fact” that Google has built AI inextricably into Search, parents have a right to know how their children’s data is ingested into Google’s models, she said.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, “any sort of transparency on what is actually happening in terms of the data that they collect and what they do with it, that is absolutely missing,” creswell said. And “it’s very unclear what data is being saved. ”.

Sebagaimana diketahui, to creswell and other advocates, it seems likely that kids’ data is collected no matter what, since “even if you do ‘-ai,’ and you don’t get a text summary, your search data and what’s being returned is all basically inside the generative ai model. ” Although Illinois law only allows commercial use of de-identified data, parents think Google should clearly explain what steps it takes to ensure data can’t be recombined to re-identify kids.

Berdasarkan laporan, ars reached out to google to see if the company could clarify if creswell’s read is accurate or if there’s any meaningful distinction between adding “-ai” to an individual query versus building a button that would automatically add “-ai” to every query. Google did not clarify, instead emphasizing that schools will control whether students can access the Gemini app, Gemini Notebook, and Search, with options to toggle each off individually, but no option to use Search without AI.

Sebagaimana diketahui, emma doe’s lawsuit alleged that google has taken advantage of a dominant position it has held in schools since 2007 to push ai on kids and seize their data without meaningfully protecting them from the worst potential harms of its chatbot’s sycophantic design. In Chicago, CPS signed a contract with Google in 2020, “long before Gemini was rolled out,” Creswell found. Over the next two extensions of that contract, no updates were introduced to protect students’ privacy as AI advanced.

Berdasarkan laporan, currently, that policy specifies that “we receive customer data through the core services and process it according to the school’s (the customer’s) instructions. This customer data includes anything submitted, stored, sent, or received through Core Services by you or your school. ” Google collects that data on that activity, as well as account information “like name, email address and password” and location information, the policy said.

Berdasarkan laporan, the policy didn’t discuss gemini but noted that data from using core services helps maintain services, improve personalization, and increase security. And “the data we collect in the Additional Services is used across our services to deliver, maintain, and improve our services; develop new services; provide personalized services; measure performance; communicate with you; and protect Google, our users, and the public. ”.

To parents, the policy provides no reassurance that their kids’ data isn’t part of Google’s plan to dominate the AI industry.

“We should not have any child data being collected in a school setting being used for commercial purposes,” Creswell said.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, parents’ privacy concerns go beyond google, creswell noted. But since Google has “captured so much of the education space and so much of the education experience,” parents are focusing their energy on interrogating those AI systems in schools early on.

Diungkapkan bahwa in chicago, a recently re-elected cps school board member, karen zaccor, is pushing for an ai moratorium in schools after talking with city and community colleges about an allegedly noticeable decline in reading, math, and writing skills from students graduating from cps schools. In Emma’s case, Google allegedly suppressed chat logs, and the school withheld safety logs, frustrating parents who already viewed AI as more harmful than beneficial in education.

Sebagaimana diketahui, at the google protest wednesday, parents waved signs that threatened to eject google from schools, with slogans like “no google + no ai = win/win. ” Many kids used favorite cartoon characters from shows like Beavis and Butthead and South Park to slam Google’s seemingly cynical approach to introducing AI in schools. One young girl wearing pink rain boots held up a cardboard sign, declaring in colorful markers, “I like to read!!”.

At its peak, about 60 people stood outside Google’s downtown Chicago office, enduring the rain and listening to teachers and students who oppose reckless AI adoption.

Diungkapkan bahwa one particularly moving speech came from a cps student, reese mackey, who spoke for students. She challenged Google to more carefully weigh the long-term harms of aggressively pushing AI onto students by claiming they’ll be left behind and struggle to find jobs without AI skills. Creswell told Ars the opposite seems true, as Emma Doe’s lawsuit pointed to research branding Gemini as “the most dangerous marketed for use by youth” and “confirming the existence of AI-induced psychosis. ”.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, “what about the future of our youth?” mackey said. “What about the future of our minds?”.

More phones are getting Gemini Intelligence, but only Pixel users can access it in a new way.

Gemini Intelligence is spreading beyond the Google Pixel 11 lineup to the Pixel 10, the upcoming Motorola Signature 27, and several of Samsung’s Galaxy foldables and flagship phones.

Diungkapkan bahwa though google often offers its most upgraded features to other android phone manufacturers, there are some features that are pixel-exclusive or come to pixel users first. This time, Gemini Intelligence is coming to Android Auto, but only for eligible Pixel users.

Also: I’m an Android Auto ride or die – but Apple CarPlay beats it on these 3 features.

Sebagaimana diketahui, google’s blog post states that pixel users with gemini intelligence can expect it to gather information from their apps and surface it to their car’s infotainment screen. Google’s example is that if a friend texts you asking where you’re meeting for Pilates, Gemini Intelligence can find the correct confirmation email and offer to send it with one tap.

To access Gemini Intelligence in Android Auto, the Gemini app and subsequent setup are required; it’s available in select countries to users aged 18 and older, and feature availability will vary.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, with more context about your messages, emails, and calendar events, a more capable assistant can complete cross-app tasks while driving, such as “remind me to buy mom a birthday card before her birthday” or “which route to my dentist appointment will be the fastest?” i often use siri ai in carplay for tasks like these, and gemini operates the same way. However, these tasks require user input first; what makes an AI assistant in in-car software great is when it suggests tasks before you ask for them.

Berdasarkan laporan, luckily for united and other companies blocking ai agents, agentic commerce might not be taking off with regular people. Moon phase today: What the Moon will look like on November 13, 2026

Tanggal: 13 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://mashable.com/science/moon-phase-today-nov-13-2026

Sebagaimana diketahui, the crescent moon is now more visible in the evening sky, with enough of its surface illuminated to start picking out some lunar features. Keep reading to find out what you might be able to see.

Sebagaimana diketahui, as of friday, nov. 13, the NASA's Daily Moon Guide tracker tells us the Moon is in the Waxing Crescent phase, with 14% of its surface visible.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, after nights of darkness and limited visibility, moon gazing is back tonight. If you don't have any visual aids, you'll be able to see the Mare Crisium and the Mare Fecunditatis. With binoculars or a telescope, you'll also see the Endymion Crater.

The next Full Moon will take place on November 24.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the moon takes approximately 29. As it orbits Earth, the amount of sunlight reflecting off its surface that we can see changes, creating the different phases. 5 days to complete one full cycle. This takes us from the New Moon to the Full Moon and back again, before the cycle begins once more, according to NASA.

New Moon - The Moon is between Earth and the sun, so the side we see is dark (in other words, it's invisible to the eye).

Waxing Crescent - A small sliver of light appears on the right side (Northern Hemisphere).

Berdasarkan laporan, first quarter - half of the moon is lit on the right side. It looks like a half-Moon.

Waxing Gibbous - More than half is lit up, but it's not quite full yet.

Full Moon - The whole face of the Moon is illuminated and fully visible.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, waning gibbous - the moon starts losing light on the right side. (Northern Hemisphere).

Third Quarter (or Last Quarter) - Another half-Moon, but now the left side is lit.

Waning Crescent - A thin sliver of light remains on the left side before going dark again.

#127. SoftBank’s billion-dollar loss may have put a cap on AI’s natural gas ambitions

📅 12 Nov 2026

SoftBank’s billion-dollar loss may have put a cap on AI’s natural gas ambitions

Tanggal: 12 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://techcrunch.com/2026/11/12/softbanks-billion-dollar-loss-may-have-put-a-cap-on-ais-natural-gas-ambitions/

SoftBank might not be the first to invest in a hot trend, but when it does, it goes big.

Sebagaimana diketahui, witness its $30 billion bet on openai in early 2025 or its announcement in february that its sb energy subsidiary would spend $33 billion on a 9. 2-gigawatt natural gas power plant. If you can’t be first, be biggest, I guess.

Diungkapkan bahwa that philosophy apparently spilled over into procurement, where orders were also supersized. Starting about two years ago, SoftBank reportedly put down deposits on more than 13 gigawatts of turbines, almost 50% more than it needed.

The decision to over-order undoubtedly helped secure turbines and speed up SoftBank’s projects.

“SB Energy did not have a choice except to overbook turbines in the future if they wanted some turbines right away,” Peter Gardett, CEO of Noreva, told TechCrunch via email.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the energy world was caught off guard by the swiftness and magnitude of ai’s rising power demands. Queues for turbine orders now extend into the early 2030s. As natural gas was shaping up to be a go-to power source for the AI boom, CEO Masayoshi Son bet that by deploying his investment firm’s significant war chest, he could corner a portion of the market. If the AI world wanted power for its data centers, it would have to come to him.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, now that bet appears to have fizzled. SoftBank announced a $7. 1 billion quarterly loss on Tuesday, with over half of that stemming from losses related to power-generating equipment. The investor had paid turbine manufacturers nonrefundable deposits to secure orders, and now it considered much of those worthless.

Diungkapkan bahwa the move was also a costly bit of price discovery, gardett said. Rather than overpay and potentially still be short of turbines, SoftBank overpaid and over-ordered.

“This charge is just that price discovery finally happening,” Gardett said.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the magnitude of that misplaced bet — over $3 billion — reflects some of the electricity mania that has overtaken the ai world. Faced with years-long waits to connect to the grid, many hyperscalers and developers have turned to natural gas as a sort of energy security blanket, something that is proven and familiar.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, as ai data centers spend more time in operation, their operators are getting a better feel for what’s required to keep them operating. Natural gas might seem like a safe bet, but there are still risks, including winter curtailments when supplies dip and demand spikes, Brent Nelson, senior managing director of markets and strategy at Ascend Analytics, told the Equity podcast Wednesday.

Sebagaimana diketahui, in light of that, nelson said the grid might still be their best bet. To make up for the shortfall, large batteries are a cost-effective choice, Nelson said. Most data centers would be best served by a grid connection, albeit a smaller one than they might normally request. They’d help shave peak loads or ride out requests from the utility to curtail electricity use.

Data center operators might be coming to that same conclusion, leading the natural gas market to develop more slowly than SoftBank expected.

Diungkapkan bahwa softbank’s natural gas-related losses are unlikely to have a domino effect, leading to mass cancellations of gas power plants. AI’s power demand appears to be too large for that. For now, natural gas is riding high, though SoftBank may have found its ceiling.

Diungkapkan bahwa “we’re not doing this thing because we like rockets,” he said during the presentation. Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the blacklift rocket will be “simple,” he said, because it will be solely tailored to lift five bluebird satellites into low-earth orbit at a time. Moreover, little is known publicly about the readiness of the upper stage engine, Vira, that AST is also acquiring from Firefly for its rocket.

These structures, as well as flight software, avionics, stage separation, payload fairings, qualification testing, and so much more, can lead to significant delays in the development of a rocket. Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, “first of all, i’m no musk, and i don’t want to be,” avellan said on thursday. … Why? Because we partner with them. “We partner. We don’t compete with them. You know, we partner with them. We enhance. We don’t insult them. We don’t compete. ”.

#134. Phota Labs uses AI to turn everyday photos into professional-looking shots

Phota Labs uses AI to turn everyday photos into professional-looking shots

Tanggal: 12 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://techcrunch.com/2026/11/12/phota-labs-uses-ai-to-turn-everyday-photos-into-professional-looking-shots/

A new iOS app called Phota Labs gives users access to a personal AI photo assistant that turns everyday snapshots into images that look like they were taken by a professional photographer, all while preserving the authenticity of the image.

Rather than giving consumers yet another photo-editing tool, Phota Labs aims to use advances in AI to automate the editing process so it’s easier for anyone to get access to better photos.

The a16z-backed startup was founded by Cecilia Zhang and Zach Xia, who met at Adobe while working on computational photography products, including Project Indigo, Lightroom, and Photoshop.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the duo saw a gap in the editing tools on the market and believed that although editing tools can be powerful for enhancing photos, they aren’t very effective at fixing a photo that wasn’t captured well in the first place. Phota Labs changes that by focusing on fixing the shot itself while preserving the natural appearances of those in the image.

Berdasarkan laporan, “phota is your personal photo assistant that can make great photos for any moment you want to keep before you even ask, which means that it’s a very proactive experience,” zhang told techcrunch in an interview. “Think of it almost like a photographer or virtual photographer who looks over your camera roll and tries to understand what’s happening and how they could have taken that photo for you on the spot for that scene. ”.

The idea is to use AI to transform photos, whether that’s turning a wide-angle group photo into a tighter portrait or transforming a selfie into a regular shot.

Users can choose from different photography styles that determine how AI transforms their images, ranging from subtle edits that preserve the original lens and composition to more dramatic transformations that introduce effects like fish-eye lenses, alternative angles, and entirely different perspectives.

While some people turn to ChatGPT and other generative AI tools to enhance or edit images, these tools can often alter a person’s appearance, especially when working with blurry photos because they don’t know what that person actually looks like.

Berdasarkan laporan, “for phota, we built our own tech,” zhang said. ”We built this personalization technology that actually learns about people’s identity and is able to preserve them in any transformation we do to a photo. ”.

Images edited with Phota Labs feature invisible watermarks that identify them as altered by AI when shared on social platforms.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the startup is initially targeting people who take tons of photos and like to share them on social media, but don’t want to deal with the tedious process of editing photos. Over time, the founders envision a broader audience, from retirees looking to create beautiful photos for their grandchildren to parents who want to share polished family albums with friends and relatives.

Berdasarkan laporan, “we have this obsession with authenticity,” xia said. “I think there’s so much value in connecting AI with real moments and making sure those photos are not perfect, in a sense. That’s why we spend a lot of research into understanding personal context, into building this identity model because we want to make sure the photos are authentic. They’re just better photos of the same moment, rather than saying, ‘Oh, this is an AI image’. ”.

Sebagaimana diketahui, xia said beta users were excited to see better versions of moments they had actually lived and saw the results as photos of real memories rather than ai-generated images. The founders discovered that users were taking more photos because they knew Phota Labs could enhance them later.

Berdasarkan laporan, “we’re turning something that’s unusable into something that people want to print,” zhang said. “People who just love photos but never really got into editing can now experience professional quality that could never have been possible. There’s so many cherished moments for photos, and we really want them to be actually meaningful and something that you can remember. So, I think that meant so much to us. ”.

Sebagaimana diketahui, in terms of funding, the company raised a $5. 6 million seed round led by a16z last year.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, phota labs is launching as a free app to build an initial user base before exploring a freemium model. The startup also plans to launch an Android app in the future.

#135. Over Ubuntu? Fedora is the Linux distro I’d hop to next – here’s why

📅 11 Nov 2026

Over Ubuntu? Fedora is the Linux distro I’d hop to next – here’s why

Tanggal: 11 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.zdnet.com/linux/ubuntu-fedora-migration-linux-distro-hopping/

Our gifting experts are obsessively searching for holiday gifts that are unique, thoughtful and suitable for any budget.

If you're an Ubuntu user considering a leap to Fedora, but you're hesitating, I explain why you should go ahead and just do it.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, in the world of linux, distro hopping is practically a spectator sport. At some point, we get bored with the distro we’re using and decide to try something new. Perhaps there’s a distro that offers better features, works with more hardware, or has a larger support community. There are so many reasons for switching distros.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, also: ubuntu 26. 04 vs. Fedora 44: My verdict.

However, for those new to Linux, the idea of leaving behind a distribution that’s been working just fine can be daunting, especially when you’re considering jumping to a distribution that isn’t as familiar and uses different technology.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, as a new linux user decades ago, i started with caldera open linux 1. 2 (before Red Hat became Fedora). 0 and immediately jumped to Red Hat Linux 5. I stayed with Red Hat for years, until I found Ubuntu (I believe it was version 4).

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, back then, making the jump wasn’t nearly as easy as it is now; in fact, it was unnerving. I was so used to how Fedora did things that I wasn’t certain I’d be able to acclimate.

But I did! And then, after realizing that hopping from one distro to another wasn’t the end of the world, I hopped around for a few years, from distro to distro until I settled back on Ubuntu-based distributions.

Also: Done with Debian Linux distros? Try Fedora next.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, it’s a lot, but it doesn’t have to be nearly as daunting as it seems. In fact, it can be exciting and fun. If you’re considering a jump from Ubuntu to Fedora, let me try to ease your concerns.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, first, let’s get the obvious out of the way: ubuntu and fedora are both linux. It’s not like you’re jumping from Windows or MacOS to Linux. This is a lateral move, which is not nearly as fear-inducing.

Diungkapkan bahwa beyond that, ubuntu and fedora are much more similar than you might expect. They both have GUI tools for everything you need; they’re both secure; they both have great package managers and package manager front-ends; they both make it easy to install all of the software you need (and all of the software you need is readily available); and they’re both user-friendly.

Also: 5 of my favorite Linux distros for AI – and why.

Sebagaimana diketahui, if you get beyond the gui and dip your toes into the command line, they both (mostly) use the same commands. Yes, there are some variations, but when you’re first learning the CLI (if you ever do — it’s not necessary), you’ll find those basic commands on Ubuntu are exactly the same as they are on Fedora.

Diungkapkan bahwa if you migrated from windows to ubuntu, you’ve already experienced what a faster operating system feels like. If you jump from Ubuntu to Fedora, you’re going to experience that again, because Fedora is (somewhat) faster than Ubuntu. The difference might not be as exaggerated as it was when you went from Windows to Linux, but it is noticeable. Animations are faster, apps open faster, and switching between desktops is faster — nearly every aspect of Fedora is a bit faster than in Ubuntu.

Also: Fedora 44 made me forget I was using Linux – in the best way.

I’ve tested several aspects with regard to the speed of Ubuntu and Fedora, and here are my conclusions:.

Sebagaimana diketahui, this is almost a tie. 31 seconds. When rebooting from a logged-in desktop to the login screen, Fedora took 13. 69 seconds, while Ubuntu took 14. The only caveat to that is if Fedora has updates that require a reboot, in which case Fedora takes considerably longer. The only time you have to reboot Ubuntu after an update is if the kernel is upgraded.

Berdasarkan laporan, fedora wins this one, especially when it comes to flatpak and snap apps. Snap apps simply cannot compete with the speed of Flatpak apps (more on this in a bit). 48 seconds, and on Ubuntu the Snap app version of GIMP took 4. On Fedora, the Flatpak GIMP took 3. I tested this by opening a Snap app on Ubuntu and a Flatpak app on Fedora, using GIMP (since I know GIMP takes a while to start). 34 seconds.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, this is one area where ubuntu has a slight edge, but only when installing via the default package manager (rather than flatpak or snap). I tested this by timing the installation of Audacity using each package manager (DNF5 and APT) from the command line. DNF5 installed Audacity in 15. 34 seconds, whereas the Ubuntu installation took 14. 61 seconds.

Sebagaimana diketahui, generally speaking, fedora not only ships with newer apps than ubuntu, but it also gets updates faster than ubuntu. That’s not to say that Ubuntu uses out-of-date packages; rather, Fedora is more cutting-edge than Ubuntu.

Also: 5 premium Linux distros absolutely worth paying for.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, at the same time, that doesn’t mean fedora uses unstable applications. All software that ships and/or is updated on Fedora is well-tested and stable — it’s just fresher.

Berdasarkan laporan, flatpaks and snaps are universal package managers. Fedora ships with Flatpak, and Ubuntu is all-in on Snaps. While these two technologies have the same goal (making software installation easier and more secure), they take different approaches.

Sebagaimana diketahui, first off, flatpak was created by red hat, while snap was created by canonical. Flatpak apps launch faster than Snap apps. Flatpak enforces mandatory sandboxing, whereas Snap makes sandboxing optional. Snap is partially proprietary, while Flatpak is fully open-source. Finally, Snap packages are automatically updated, whereas Flatpak apps require manual updates.

Also: My favorite GNOME-based Linux distros.

Overall, Flatpak is widely considered the superior technology by the Linux community.

In my experience, Flatpak is a better technology for the desktop, whereas Snap is best suited for servers.

Berdasarkan laporan, if you were to look at both ubuntu and fedora, you would swear they use different desktop environments. Both Fedora and Ubuntu use GNOME; the difference is that Ubuntu customizes GNOME to look more like the Ubuntu Unity UI Canonical tested back in 2010. Au contraire, mon ami. Since then, Ubuntu adopted GNOME and customized it so it wouldn’t irk users who had grown accustomed to Unity.

Also: My favorite Linux desktop environment for laptops surprised even me.

Berdasarkan laporan, fedora, on the other hand, sticks with a stock installation of gnome for its flagship release. The good news is that, if you like the Ubuntu take on GNOME, you can install the necessary GNOME extensions (the main one being Dash to Panel) to get a similar layout. You can also get the Unity-like top bar by installing the Unite-Shell extension.

Tech > Services & Software > Operating Systems > Windows > Windows 11.

Berdasarkan laporan, with the november patch tuesday rollout, you can finally customize your right-click menu in windows 11. But don't skip these security fixes.

Sebagaimana diketahui, windows 11 users who’ve struggled to navigate and use the right-click menu in file explorer now finally have some relief. With the November Patch Tuesday Windows update, you’re now able to customize the menu to add and remove specific commands and apps so that only your favorites appear.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, as usual, the monthly update is mandatory, which means it should automatically download and install on your pc. To check, head to Settings and select Windows Update. 9974)” -– pops up as installed with a pending restart, just reboot your computer. If the latest update — labeled “2026-11 Security Update (KB5132061) (26300. Otherwise, click the button to check for updates and allow it to download and install.

Also: You can change Windows settings directly from a search now.

Sebagaimana diketahui, one caveat: microsoft’s monthly updates fully support windows 11 26h2 and 25h2. But support for 24H2 ended last month, at least for the Home and Pro editions. Windows 11 24H2 Enterprise and Education will continue to get monthly security updates, though not regular non-security preview updates, while Windows 11 23H2 Enterprise and Education will receive no more updates after this month.

If you use Windows 11 Home or Pro, be sure you upgrade your system to 26H2 to continue receiving the necessary support and updates.

First and foremost in the latest update is the new customizable right-click menu.

Diungkapkan bahwa the context-sensitive right-click menu is a handy way to quickly access key settings, features, and apps, both in file explorer and on the desktop. The more apps you install, the more cluttered and disorganized the menu becomes. But there’s always been a flaw in its basic design. That was especially problematic in previous versions of Windows. The old-style, classic menu would grow so long that it would be difficult to navigate and let you find the item you wanted.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, with windows 11, microsoft introduced a more modern and pared-down menu. Plus, it may not display every command you need, so you often have to revert to the older classic menu. But this version can also get crowded. You’re then stuck dealing with two separate versions of the same menu, leading to an even more confusing and cumbersome experience.

Also: Windows 11 can run better on PCs with 8GB now, Microsoft says.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the ideal solution is a menu that you can customize yourself, and that’s what we now have, at least that’s what is now rolling out. Microsoft calls this one a gradual rollout, which means you may or may not get it right away.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, to see if and how this is available, open file explorer and right-click on a folder or file. Select that to view all the available options for tweaking it. If the new menu has reached your PC, you’ll see an entry for Customize menu. Alternatively, head to Settings, select Personalization, and then click the entry for Context menu.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, there, you’re able to turn certain file actions on or off, such as send to, print, create shortcut, copy as path, and rotate image. You can also choose which apps appear all the time, either in the main menu or in a submenu. Plus, additional options let you decide where certain commands and actions appear and whether you can still access the old-style menu.

Though the customizable right-click menu is the star of the update, Microsoft has added other surprises as it strives to make Windows more reliable and user-friendly.

Sebagaimana diketahui, also gradually rolling out, cloud rebuild is a new recovery option that lets you reinstall windows 11 via cloud-based system images and drivers downloaded from windows update. The downside is that your files won’t survive. This tool can help you recover Windows when it won’t load and you don’t have a USB drive or your own custom image. But if you regularly back them up as you should, you can restore them after Windows is back in business.

Diungkapkan bahwa to start cloud rebuild, go to settings, select system, click recovery, and then select rebuild pc. If Windows can load, your computer should automatically enter WinRE mode, where you can then choose the cloud rebuild. Your PC will then restart into the Windows Recovery Environment (WinRE) to kick off the cloud rebuild. You should need to make sure your PC is online via a wired or wireless connection.

The November update also enhances or fixes other Windows features and apps.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, file explorer will now more clearly and consistently show you the names, locations, and dates of files when you search for them. Phone Link will preview the text in a recent message if you hover over it. The AutoPlay dialog box that appears when you connect a device like a phone or camera has been given a more modern makeover. The Privacy & security page in Settings now groups together related controls for easier viewing. Plus, there are changes to the Taskbar, Magnifier, Narrator, Xbox Mode, and Live Captions.

And that then brings us to the security fixes.

Diungkapkan bahwa this month’s update resolves 1,094 security vulnerabilities, according to microsoft, with 63 of them rated critical and one already exploited in the wild. That’s fewer than October’s record of 1,400 patches. But it still represents a hefty number as Microsoft and other vendors continue to rely on AI to find and fix security holes.

Also: Windows finally gets a built-in internet speed test tool – how to try it.

Berdasarkan laporan, though labeled moderate, the exploited flaw points to a serious spoofing vulnerability in microsoft outlook. Here, a remote attacker who sends you a malicious email and convinces you to open it could cause Outlook to connect to a network controlled by that attacker. In this case, though, you would not receive any warning. Further, the exploit might reveal your username and password to the sender, potentially allowing them to impersonate you.

“An attacker sends a specially crafted message file and gets the user to open it,” Jack Bicer, Director of Vulnerability Research at patch management provider Action1, said in an advisory.

Berdasarkan laporan, “outlook then connects to a network location the attacker controls, but it skips the usual warning about external content,” bicer explained further. Attackers are already exploiting it, it needs only one click on an email file, and it hits Outlook, which nearly every organization runs. “That quiet connection can leak the user’s NTLMv2 hash, a scrambled form of their login secret, which the attacker can use to sign in as that person. It affects Microsoft 365 Apps for Enterprise and Office LTSC 2021 and 2024. ”.

#145. I’m Begging You, Don’t Let AI Bots Manage Your Money

📅 12 Nov 2026

I’m Begging You, Don’t Let AI Bots Manage Your Money

Tanggal: 12 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.cnet.com/tech/services-and-software/please-dont-let-an-ai-bot-log-into-your-bank-account/

Our gifting experts are obsessively searching for holiday gifts that are unique, thoughtful and suitable for any budget.

Diungkapkan bahwa our expert, award-winning staff selects the products we cover and rigorously researches and tests our top picks. If you buy through our links, we may earn a commission.

Your bank probably won't cover the mistakes you give AI permission to make.

If you’re using AI agents to manage your money, you should probably stop right now.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, agents such as meta’s muse, openclaw and openai’s dots are all the rage in the ai world these days. They promise to do more than chatbots that give you information. Instead they’re tools that can take action if you ask them to.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, when you first sign up for an ai agent, you may be asked to grant permission for it to access your apps, browsers and data so it can work with them. That might put your money at risk in unexpected ways.

Berdasarkan laporan, “the intention might be something simple, like managing a calendar. But that access can give the agent the ability to do much more than the person intended,” said John Strand, the owner of the cybersecurity firm Black Hills Information Security. While you may be giving the agent access to simple smart home routines or getting help planning a trip, your banking information may also be accessible.

It might be tempting to think you can automate your financial chores and have more time for other things, but handing over your account credentials to an agent opens you up to many different things that can go wrong.

Berdasarkan laporan, for one, ai agents might not be as secure as you think. This technology is very new — these kinds of always-on, persistent agents have really only been available for less than a year, and big companies like Meta and OpenAI have just put out their own versions in the last couple of months. These aren’t polished products that have had all the kinks worked out.

Berdasarkan laporan, one of those challenges is that they don’t always behave in the way you expect or do what you want them to. Recent news stories about AI agents hacking other websites — including the AI platform Hugging Face and Australian government sites — have involved agents acting in unexpected ways to achieve an assigned goal. You don’t want AI to act like that with your checking account.

Berdasarkan laporan, there are also plenty of reasons to be worried about the privacy of data shared with agents. Your agent might not meddle in unwanted ways with your money, but it could compromise your login info, letting someone nefarious meddle with your money.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, when agents use your login info, “a bank cannot tell an authorized agent from an attacker using the exact same login,” said ted miracco, ceo of the mobile security firm approov. Until agents carry verifiable identities, scoped permissions and an audit trail, blocking them is the best defensible control a bank has. “That is more of an identity failure than an AI failure. ”.

Berdasarkan laporan, many banks are aware of the risks and are already cracking down on unauthorized use of agentic agents. Charles Schwab’s CEO Rick Wurster told Bloomberg that bots are taking the liberty to move clients’ money.

Diungkapkan bahwa “i get a report on how many times we’ve blocked clients from using one of these agents in a week, and it’s in the tens and twenties — per week — that the big agents are being blocked,” wurster said in a bloomberg tv interview. “What that tells me is that while people love AI, they’re not willing to turn their financial accounts over to them just yet. ”.

Berdasarkan laporan, but that number is likely growing, and with bots going mainstream, it could grow rapidly. More banks are taking action against bots to protect you.

Sebagaimana diketahui, more news of banks standing up against ai caught my attention when i received an email from ally warning me that when customers use an ai service, they’re responsible for any actions that the ai takes. ” Ally gave a warning that if you share your login information with a loved one, they may use that information in a way you didn’t intend — the same is true for AI.

The email goes on to warn that AI can make mistakes and misunderstand your instructions — which could be a big loss for you.

Diungkapkan bahwa a representative for ally said in an email to cnet that ai can create new ways to manage your finances, but ally’s priority is to protect your accounts and personal data. Ally’s email also said that you should understand the risks that come with letting AI access your financial information.

Diungkapkan bahwa “not sharing ally usernames, passwords or security codes is good practice. As the technology evolves, important questions around security, authorization, accountability and customer protection remain areas of focus across the industry,” the statement said.

A spokesperson from Wells Fargo also said in an email to CNET that Wells Fargo has already taken steps to block unauthorized agents from accessing customer accounts, too.

Sebagaimana diketahui, some banks aren’t completely against ai, though. — they just want you to use their features and tools instead. Wurster added in his interview that he recommends for Schwab customers to use Charley, Charles Schwab’s proprietary AI tool, to gather market insights, ask about personal financial information like balances and manage everyday financial tasks like transfers and payments. These measures make it much safer, but in the meantime, it may be best to keep your banking business to yourself.

Personal finance expert Alaina Fingal broke down when you should and shouldn’t use AI for your money matters.

Diungkapkan bahwa “ai can be a helpful tool for managing finances, but i think there’s a difference between using ai to assist with understanding money concepts and allowing ai to make financial decisions for you, fingal said. She recommends using AI as a tool, but not as your financial advisor. You should make any final decisions yourself. Sharing your personal financial data puts you at risk for identity theft and even fraud.

As for letting AI actually access your accounts and do things on your behalf, Fingal said she’s concerned.

Sebagaimana diketahui, “i believe ai is moving incredibly quickly, and the safeguards, regulations, and accountability measures are struggling to keep up with the technology. And we’re prioritizing convenience and innovation without giving enough attention to consumer protection,” Fingal said.

Berdasarkan laporan, if you want to check to see if bots have been meddling in your banking, look at your login history and account activity. That may not mean it’s your AI agent, but it’s worth keeping track of. Strand suggests looking for activity that doesn’t match your pattern — like multiple logins in a short period or access happening at the same time every day. If you notice anything suspicious, contact your bank immediately for assistance.

Sebagaimana diketahui, strand also recommends enabling two-factor authentication now as a preventative step to safeguard your financial data, but it’s also a good time to reevaluate the access you’re giving ai. Strand recommends restricting which applications and sites AI agents can access.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, “check the permissions. Make sure they’re limited to what it needs to do the job you gave it, and remove anything beyond that,” he added.

Berdasarkan laporan, if you’ve already given ai bots access to your financial data, fingal recommends revoking access and changing the passwords that you’ve shared with any ai platform. Next, set up multifactor authentication and transaction alerts to stay alert.

Diungkapkan bahwa most importantly, keep an eye on your accounts. “I tell my clients to take 10 minutes each morning to review their bank transactions; that one habit can give them so much more control over their finances,” said Fingal.

Shang Saavedra, founder of personal finance platform Save My Cents, suggested you regularly revisit your AI agent’s access to apps and data and require it to ask for permission before accessing new data, apps and features.

Diungkapkan bahwa if you decide to use ai for personal finance purposes, set limitations. “I also like using AI to search for book and resource suggestions. “I’ve tested AI with some basic questions and basic calculations, and the information it provides is good for a beginner plan that gives you some pointers as to where to go,” said Saavedra. ”.

But the actual handling of money? Maybe do that yourself.

#147. Man's secret use of synthetic testosterone for cows nearly destroyed his heart

📅 12 Nov 2026

Man's secret use of synthetic testosterone for cows nearly destroyed his heart

Tanggal: 12 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://arstechnica.com/health/2026/11/mans-secret-use-of-synthetic-testosterone-for-cows-nearly-destroyed-his-heart/

Doctors warn that such life-threatening cases are becoming more common.

Diungkapkan bahwa for 11 years, a massachusetts man had an alarming array of health problems, most notably that his heart kept failing. He landed in the hospital over and over again, needed life support at one point, spent years going to specialists, and underwent a barrage of tests along the way.

Sebagaimana diketahui, but through it all, he never revealed a key detail behind his ailments: he was taking powerful, illicit synthetic testosterone derivatives (aka anabolic-androgenic steroids, or aas). One of the drugs he took was approved only for use in animals; it’s primarily used to beef up cows.

Diungkapkan bahwa left in the dark, his doctors had to puzzle this out on their own. In a case report in this week’s issue of the New England Journal of Medicine, they explain how they did it. They also offer a warning: These cases will only become more common, and clinicians need to know what they look like.

Sebagaimana diketahui, “use of aas has now become a major international substance use disorder,” they wrote. In the US, it’s estimated that between 2. 9 and 4 million people, mostly male athletes, use AAS. To put this in a public health perspective, this is more than the number of people in the US with an HIV infection.

Diungkapkan bahwa “clinicians should be prepared to encounter increasing numbers of patients presenting with the long-term effects of aas exposure, including cardiomyopathy, atherosclerotic disease, and anabolic steroid–induced hypogonadism. ”.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, patients also need to be prepared for what recovery looks like, which they described as being “lengthy and varied. ” The man’s case offers a stark example.

Berdasarkan laporan, the problems started when he was 39. Tests suggested he had an acute kidney injury, liver damage, and an injured heart. He luckily recovered—and quickly. His heart only got worse from there, and within hours, he ended up on a type of life support called ECMO (venoarterial extracorporeal membrane oxygenation), a machine that does the work of both the heart and lungs in dire circumstances. Testing of his heart showed that the left chamber was pumping out just 21 percent of its blood in a beat (a normal amount is above 50 percent). He fell ill after returning from a trip to the Caribbean and went to Massachusetts General Hospital in Boston with a fever, chills, and trouble breathing. But doctors were baffled by the cause.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, when he was weaned off ecmo a few days later, his heart function normalized. It was their best guess. Doctors looked for evidence of anything that could have sparked the sudden cardiac spiral. In rare instances, an infection with these germs can lead to a condition called poststreptococcal myocarditis, which could potentially explain some of his symptoms. They found nothing but a mildly elevated level of antibodies against a toxin made by Streptococcus bacteria. They prescribed him antibiotics, as well as drugs to lower his blood pressure.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, two years later, he went to another hospital. But the doctors at the hospital couldn’t pinpoint the problem. This time it was for acute pain in his abdomen and legs. The arteries that supply blood to his kidneys appeared narrowed, suggesting a condition called renal-artery stenosis. Doctors found signs of cell death in his kidneys. There were also signs of inflammation in his blood vessels. They prescribed him anti-inflammatory drugs and sent him on his way.

Diungkapkan bahwa for the next five years, the man started seeing a cadre of specialists to monitor his health, including doctors in primary care, cardiology, nephrology, rheumatology, general medicine, sleep medicine, and psychiatry. When he was about 46, he reported fatigue to his primary care doctor, who found that his testosterone level was low. The man then went to an endocrinologist, reporting not just fatigue but low libido and poor sleep. The endocrinologist recommended treatment for obstructive sleep apnea, which can increase the risk of low testosterone.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, a year later, the man added a hematologist to his rotation of care providers. A routine blood test revealed abnormally high levels of red blood cells (erythrocytosis). The hematologist noted the man also had high blood pressure (150/108 mm Hg) but found everything else to be normal. The hematologist ended up attributing the erythrocytosis to the man’s sleep apnea and renal-artery stenosis.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, it wasn’t until he arrived again at mass general in 2026 that doctors finally put it all together. Now 50, the man was once again experiencing heart failure—and he had again just returned from the Caribbean.

Diungkapkan bahwa in the case report, doctors provided a more complete picture of the man, noting that he lived with his wife and children in eastern massachusetts, worked as a facilities manager, and described himself as a workout “fanatic. He told doctors he had erectile dysfunction and reduced libido for several years. ” He used tanning beds and applied spray tans. They also noticed that he had mildly enlarged breast tissue (a condition called gynecomastia), progressive insulin resistance, decreased levels of “good” cholesterol (HDL or high-density lipoprotein), and fatty liver disease.

Diungkapkan bahwa when he arrived at the hospital, he reported five days of worsening chest tightness and pressure, fatigue, swelling in his legs, and trouble breathing. Doctors described him as “muscular, tanned, anxious, and in mild distress. His blood pressure was high at 146/106 mm Hg. His heart was racing at 134 beats per minute. ” Tests showed his heart was once again failing, with the left chamber pumping out just 20 percent of its blood.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the doctors started reviewing a long list of possible explanations. They ruled out infectious diseases that can cause heart inflammation (myocarditis), as well as autoimmune conditions, medication side effects, and toxins. The explanation they were left with—which also seemed to explain much of his other problems—was high doses of testosterone, or perhaps an AAS.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, illicit use of aas is clearly linked to the heart problems, including the decreased blood pumping the man had, as well as strain and damage. It could also explain his enlarged breast tissue, fatty liver and signs of liver damage, progressive insulin resistance, kidney injuries, high blood pressure, and high levels of red blood cells (erythrocytosis). The sleep problems, fatigue, and low testosterone levels—which doctors previously guessed were from obstructive sleep apnea—could actually be from a drop in natural hormone production after doses of AAS (a condition called hypogonadism).

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, in the man’s lengthy medical history, he had never mentioned using aas or testosterone supplements. When they finally broached the topic, he confessed; he had been intermittently using high doses of AAS to boost his muscles, taking the most recent dose before his vacation to the Caribbean. Doctors prepared to have a delicate conversation to determine if he was secretly using the drugs. The testosterone derivative he used was trenbolone, an AAS only approved for use in veterinary medicine; it’s mostly used in livestock.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the doctors then tested his total testosterone level, finding it was so high that the test couldn’t accurately measure it. The range considered normal for the test was between 249 and 836 ng/dl. The assay’s range of detection was 12 to 1,500 nanograms per deciliter of blood. His level was over 1,500 ng/dl. The doctors gave their final diagnosis: androgen excess–related cardiomyopathy.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the primary treatment for his heart is to stop taking aas. The state of his liver also improved. Doctors prescribed him medications for high blood pressure, heart failure, and diabetes. Four months later, heart tests showed his left chamber was pumping 49 percent of its blood, a significant improvement. But recovery from the AAS-induced hypogonadism was a much longer, more difficult journey. It was made harder because he was over age 35, had taken AAS for more than a decade, and had preexisting dysfunction.

Berdasarkan laporan, six months into his recovery, he still had significant hypogonadism symptoms, which include loss of sexual desire, erectile dysfunction, gynecomastia, reduced orgasmic satisfaction, and ejaculatory disorders. It didn’t work for the man. It’s often used in women to help with fertility, but in men it is sometimes used to try to jumpstart natural testosterone production. He moved on to trying topical testosterone-replacement therapy but continued to have erectile dysfunction. He opted to try a drug called clomiphene, which binds to estrogen receptors. Doctors warn that it could take up to three years for the hypogonadism to resolve.

In the last follow-up at eight months, he reported that he was still off AAS and had no symptoms of heart failure.
