Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, deepmind did not share any plans to release its findings as a consumer product, though the researchers are open-sourcing their code to help others with formal verification efforts. “Verifying Signal’s core cryptography lays the groundwork to secure other vital systems, from medical device firmware to power grid software,” DeepMind added.

#183. 12 12 12 is the final boss of nonlinear TV

📅 13 Nov 2026

12 12 12 is the final boss of nonlinear TV

Tanggal: 13 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://mashable.com/entertainment/12-12-12-apple-tv

From multiple timelines to extended flashback episodes, you can barely get through a TV show nowadays without taking a hop, skip, and a jump through time.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, of course, tv has a rich tradition of playing with chronology. Its use of character-focused flashbacks also lingers today, present everywhere from Paradise to Euphoria. Lost's nonlinear approach revolutionized episodic storytelling, inspiring mystery-box series with several timelines like Westworld and Yellowjackets. While these techniques can build out fun puzzles or deepen our knowledge of characters, they can also devolve into nothing more than flashy gimmicks. Case in point: Apple TV's new heist drama 12 12 12.

Want more film and TV news and reviews delivered straight to your inbox? Sign up for Mashable’s Top Stories newsletter or get Mashable push alerts today.

12 12 12 unfolds across three different timelines: the 12 months of planning leading up to a billion-dollar heist on a Swiss bank; the 12 hours of the heist itself; and the 12 days after, in which FBI agent Jack Strickland (Anthony Mackie) hunts thief Paul Galvin (Jamie Dornan) and his accomplices.

Diungkapkan bahwa if you forget the structure of the show, don't worry. 12 12 12 lays it out for you at the top of every episode with the help of voiceover from Mackie. It also uses a series of split screens to remind you when we're entering a new timeline, be it "The Planning," "The Heist," or "The Takedown. " The amount of hand-holding to get you onboard with the show's premise alone feels tailor-made for audiences who are second-screening the show, a stark contrast from other multi-timeline shows that trust audiences to pick up on context clues.

Diungkapkan bahwa on paper, 12 12 12's timeline idea is fascinating. Yet even though the show is built around nonlinear storytelling, the cracks in its conceit quickly begin to show.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, a large driving force of any heist story is the tension of whether an unlikely team can pull off an even more unlikely robbery. During the "Heist" timeline, we know thanks to the "Takedown" timeline that the money makes it out of the bank vault. During the "Planning" timeline, we know thanks to the "Heist" timeline that the heist will eventually take place. Any supposed roadblocks feel hollow. 12 12 12 undercuts much of that tension from the get-go. Only the "Takedown" causes any adrenaline spikes, as Jack and Paul's cat-and-mouse game begins in earnest, with no definitive outcome spelled out for us.

Sebagaimana diketahui, another driving force of heist stories is the how of the heist, all the delicious twists and turns and plans within plans that play out during the job. These twists could have solved 12 12 12's tension problem. However, the show becomes far too liberal with them down the line, seemingly in hopes of keeping the wool over our eyes, as if to prove we don't actually know the arc of the story.

Diungkapkan bahwa as 12 12 12 veers into increasingly bizarre territory — an incident with an avalanche earned a major groan from me — it sacrifices credibility and character. The former is a charismatic criminal roped into one last job before settling down as a family man. The pair at least fare better than the other underutilized members of Paul's team, most of whom are total afterthoughts. Despite solid performances from Dornan and Mackie, neither Paul nor Jack truly break free from classic heist archetypes. The latter is an overworked agent with an obsessive drive to catch these criminals. Even when they're introduced in the "Planning" timeline, there is no "aha" moment of recognition, because there's so little of them to latch onto in the "Heist" and "Takedown" timelines.

Sebagaimana diketahui, would 12 12 12 work better if it wasn't so tied to tv's nonlinear trend? perhaps. Unfortunately, they're so tied up in clichés that said thrills wear off fast. The heist and its aftermath do come with the occasional slick thrill. The freshest thing about 12 12 12 remains its structure, but in an age dominated by nonlinear storytelling, this seemingly out-of-the-box structure becomes the last thing it wants to be: conventional.

How a breakthrough in electromechanical energy conversion helped shape the motors and generators that drive modern industry.

The dynamo-electric principle: one idea, 160 years, millions of motors.

Berdasarkan laporan, in the annals of industrial history, few innovations have demonstrated such remarkable staying power as the dynamo-electric principle. Discovered by Werner von Siemens in 1866, this groundbreaking principle remains fundamental to modern electrical engineering more than a century and a half later – and continues to shape the technology portfolio of Innomotics, a globally leading provider of electric motors and large drive systems. What began as a breakthrough in electromechanical energy conversion has evolved into a cornerstone of global industry – powering everything from brewery operations in Qingdao to high-voltage drive systems in petrochemical plants.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the year 1866 marked a decisive turning point, not only in the broader arc of industrial transformation but specifically in the realm of electric motion. At a time when Europe was entering a new phase of industrial transformation, Werner von Siemens pioneered the dynamo-electric principle – a breakthrough that enabled electric machines to generate their own magnetic field through self-excitation. This innovation transformed electric machines from laboratory curiosities into practical power sources, enabling the widespread electrification of industry and infrastructure that defined the late 19th century.

Diungkapkan bahwa this electric motor from innomotics was installed in the early 1900s at the historic tsingtao brewery in china and supported production processes for more than 90 years, operating continuously under industrial conditions. Innomotics.

Diungkapkan bahwa the principle itself is elegantly simple: an iron core generates a stable magnetic field; a rotating coil is placed within this field; movement in the magnetic field induces an electric current; part of this current strengthens the magnetic field; and electrical energy is continuously converted into motion. This self-reinforcing cycle made efficient and reliable electric motion possible – and it remains the foundation of modern motors today.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, more than 160 years later, the same fundamental idea continues to power industrial applications around the world. Millions of motors operate reliably under demanding conditions, keeping production running across generations. The dynamo-electric principle made it possible for electric machines to convert electrical energy into motion (and motion back into electrical energy), creating the technological foundation for modern electric motors and drive systems.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, perhaps no example illustrates this longevity better than the electric motor from innomotics at the historic tsingtao brewery in china. Installed in the early 1900s during the early electrification of industrial brewing, this motor supported production processes for more than 90 years, operating continuously under industrial conditions. It became a powerful example of long-term reliability in real-world applications – a testament to how engineering ensures reliable motion across decades.

Sebagaimana diketahui, continuity, however, does not mean stagnation. Sixteen decades after the original breakthrough, innovations continue to emerge that build upon this proven foundation. Two recent developments – the Active Vibration Control System (AVCS) and oil-lubricated rolling bearings (OLRB) – carry this spirit of innovation and ingenuity forward, a commitment that has been recognized with the German Innovation Award.

Berdasarkan laporan, innomotics’ patented oil-lubricated rolling bearing (olrb) technology enhances reliability and reduces maintenance requirements. Innomotics.

Sebagaimana diketahui, avcs helps optimize high-voltage motor performance by actively decoupling motors from their foundations to reduce vibration issues. OLRB helps prevent rolling bearing failures from the start with continuous lubrication, supporting higher availability, less downtime, and long-term cost savings. These innovations demonstrate how the basic principle of 1866 can be enhanced through modern engineering to meet contemporary demands for reliability and efficiency.

Diungkapkan bahwa for three decades, with over 25,000 units driving performance globally, innomotics’ perfect harmony gh180 medium-voltage drive platform has supported reliable operation across industries. Its modular architecture enables efficient power control, high availability, and long-term performance. With thousands of installations worldwide, Perfect Harmony GH180 continues to build on a proven technological foundation, minimizing downtime and ensuring stable production.

Diungkapkan bahwa keeping critical motors running requires the right expertise and innovation spirit throughout the entire lifecycle. Winding Lifetime Analysis (WLA) combines operating history, machine measurements, and physics-based modeling to assess the condition of the winding insulation and estimate its remaining useful lifetime. With Innomotics Customer Services, operators and plant managers gain the insights they need to maintain reliability and optimize maintenance strategies. This enables informed maintenance decisions, reduces uncertainty, and helps minimize the risk of unplanned downtime.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the perfect harmony gh180 delivers efficient, reliable and flexible medium-voltage drive performance. Innomotics.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, what began as a breakthrough in 1866 still brings its value to modern industry. The dynamo-electric principle made efficient and reliable electric motion possible – and it remains the foundation of modern motors today.

As industries worldwide grapple with challenges ranging from energy efficiency to operational resilience, this 160-year-old principle continues to prove its relevance.

Diungkapkan bahwa for plant managers and engineers seeking long-term performance in demanding applications, the message is clear: the foundation laid in the 19th century remains as solid as ever. What has changed are the tools and services built upon it – from vibration control systems to predictive analytics – all designed to extract maximum value from a principle that has, quite literally, powered the modern world for a century and a half.

Sebagaimana diketahui, i never realized the importance of having a universal charger until i traveled to berlin a few months ago. It was a last-minute work trip, so I packed lightly, stashed my go-to portable charger — with its flip-out plug — and flew out not knowing what struggles lay ahead.

Berdasarkan laporan, i had it all mapped out. I’d top up my phone, laptop, earbuds and cameras at the hotel each night, go out for a döner and be ready to tackle all my work the next day. But my lack of an international plug adapter — specifically, US to EU — meant that I’d have to deal with a series of physical, technical and safety obstacles first.

Berdasarkan laporan, had i discovered the anker universal charger sooner, i wouldn’t have gone through the ordeal of finding an electronics store open late on a sunday. That’s because the latest product from the mobile accessory brand takes a kitchen sink approach to charging — whether you need its more excessive features or not.

Diungkapkan bahwa i’ve been testing the $80 anker universal charger, both for general use in the states and abroad, and it’s more practical than i thought. Here’s why it’ll stay in my bag going into the holiday travel season.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the anker universal charger is two things: an international plug adapter and a multiport charger. That covers most countries in the world, including the US, Canada, Japan, China, Europe and the UK. It has slide-out Type A, Type C and Type G prongs that lock each other whenever one is active. Notably, the charger doesn’t have a Type I prong (commonly used in Australia and New Zealand), so it’s not completely universal.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the charger can output up to 100w, either individually through one of the two usb-c ports (labeled usb-c1 and usb-c2) or shared across the third usb-c port, which caps at 15w, and the one usb-a port, which caps at 10w. So if you want the most optimal charging, stick with only one of the main USB-C ports.

Sebagaimana diketahui, in practice, the anker is powerful enough to charge a modern-day iphone or android, smartwatch or laptop. My 14-inch MacBook Pro, for example, supports 100-watt charging, so the Anker is just enough to fast-charge it. It took 33 minutes to charge my MacBook from 0% to 50%, and about 50 more minutes to reach 100% as trickle charging kicked in.

Diungkapkan bahwa the anker wouldn’t be able to hit the 140-watt rating of a 16-inch macbook pro or a similarly specced laptop, though. I also noticed the charger would throttle its output — as shown on its smart display — after prolonged use at 100 watts. That meant when I charged devices back-to-back, the second device charged much more slowly because of the reduced output.

Generally speaking, make sure you’re using a proper, high-quality charging cable with the adapter, as Anker doesn’t include one in the box.

Diungkapkan bahwa one of the key features of the new anker universal charger is the 1. 3-inch smart display on the front. It’s there to show live line voltage, internal thermal readings and real-time wattage draw per port, so you know exactly how effectively it’s charging your device(s).

You navigate the display with short and long taps on the capacitive button below it, which I’ve found less intuitive than just swiping on the display, but at least it reduces fingerprint smudges.

Sebagaimana diketahui, that said, i’ve still found the smart display quite useful, as i don’t have to second-guess whether the cable i’m using or the outlet i’m plugging into can charge my phone or laptop efficiently. There’s nothing worse than plugging a device in, only to come back to it barely charged because the wattage wasn’t as high as you expected.

I’m particularly fond of how the display indicates when an outlet is safe to charge, as it can detect the output (so long as it’s within 100-275V) and signal when there’s excess electrical pressure in the circuit.

This is important when you’re traveling abroad and/or plugging into a high-voltage outlet; if you’re using a charger that’s not rated for the higher capacity, you risk sparking and other dangerous thermal reactions.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the anker universal charger is relatively compact for how much power it delivers. In the past, I’ve lugged around larger charging bricks — such as Apple’s proprietary one for MacBooks — that had fewer ports.

Diungkapkan bahwa for reference, the anker is about the size of a small computer mouse; it’s tiny enough to fit in a backpack pocket, with just enough weight (262 grams) to keep it from shifting when plugged into an outlet. Yet, I wouldn’t say this is a lightweight charger by any means, especially when compared to a conventional plug adapter.

Diungkapkan bahwa the anker universal charger is fairly priced at $80, though it’s still more expensive than generic international adapters that sell for around $20 to $50. Those don’t have a cool smart display, though.

While the price keeps the Anker out of “impulse purchase” territory, I’ve found it easier to justify than most other high-end chargers, given its functionality and safety features.

#189. Rust 1.100

📅 12 Nov 2026

Rust 1.100

Tanggal: 12 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://blog.rust-lang.org/2026/11/12/Rust-1.100.0/

Sebagaimana diketahui, the rust team is happy to announce a new version of rust, 1. 100. 0. Rust is a programming language empowering everyone to build reliable and efficient software.

Sebagaimana diketahui, if you have a previous version of rust installed via rustup, you can get 1. 100. 0 with:.

Sebagaimana diketahui, if you don't have it already, you can get rustup from the appropriate page on our website, and check out the detailed release notes for 1. 100. 0.

Diungkapkan bahwa if you'd like to help us out by testing future releases, you might consider updating locally to use the beta channel (rustup default beta) or the nightly channel (rustup default nightly). Please report any bugs you might come across!.

After 10 years and 5 failed stabilization attempts, the never type is finally stable! This also completes the project goal for this work.

Berdasarkan laporan, the never type, spelled ! in code, is the canonical uninhabited type. It represents the type of diverging computations – computations which never resolve to any value – where any code that follows is unreachable. Expressions that terminate control flow, such as return, break, and std::process::exit, also have the type !.

Sebagaimana diketahui, since having a value of the never type is impossible, rust permits a never-to-any coercion, allowing to turn ! into any other type (this is what distinguishes it from any other uninhabited types). This can be used, for example, to not return a value from one of the branches of a match or an if:.

While the never type could already be used and observed this way, and even named in the return type of functions (-> !), this release allows naming the never type anywhere:.

Berdasarkan laporan, additionally this release changes infallible to be an alias to the never type. That makes all old APIs that used Infallible be compatible with using !. This was the plan ever since the introduction of Infallible and is one of the reasons why the never type stabilization was so hard (waffle gave a talk about some of the troubles of the stabilization).

Diungkapkan bahwa unfortunately, to allow changing infallible, we had to introduce a breaking change. This release changes the "never type fallback" from () to ! in editions before 2024 (i. 2015, 2018, and 2021), similarly to what has already been done in edition 2024. e. This should largely be unnoticeable, but can affect code in some rare cases (for example when ignoring a result of a function returning a generic parameter). Note that this change might also make the compiler detect more code as unreachable.

Berdasarkan laporan, we tried to minimize the impact of this breaking change as much as possible, by providing future compatibility warnings far in advance and releasing fixes to public crates that have been broken by this. If a dependency is failing due to issues with the never type, consider updating it, as a fix might have already been released for it.

Sebagaimana diketahui, this release brings about the stabilization of the core parts of allocator_api, enabling library authors to define custom allocators that can be used together with certain standard library types - currently vec and box. These are enabled through the newly-stabilized Allocator trait.

Berdasarkan laporan, this is the foundation of the allocators 1. 0 project goal. A lot remains to be done still, including expanding the API surface usable with custom allocators and stabilizing their use on more collections and pointer types; with the core trait and design out of the way though, expect to see more being stabilized soon!.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the drop trait in rust makes it possible to run code when a variable goes out of scope, regardless of whether we return, ?, or panic. Drop being a part of types means that in Rust you never have to close a socket.

Sebagaimana diketahui, implementing drop can however feel a little inconvenient when all you want is to run some code unconditionally when a function exits. This is why we’re introducing core::mem::DropGuard: a new helper type that runs a closure when dropped.

Sebagaimana diketahui, dropguard takes two arguments: a variable and a closure. It implements Deref and DerefMut so you can keep working with the variable as normal. But when dropped it runs the closure and consumes the variable.

Berdasarkan laporan, dropguard also implements a dismiss method which returns the variable from the guard without running the destructor. This makes it possible to quickly implement all-or-nothing transaction-like APIs with a rollback. Here is an example implementing a parser which uses a guard to roll back mutations in case of failure:.

As Rust's unsafe code guidelines are still being decided, it became clear that it would be very useful to decide what exactly it means to create zero-sized types in an unsafe way, and what we should recommend for people to do this.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, this question is answered in rust 1. 100 with a single function: std::mem::conjure_zst.

Diungkapkan bahwa instead of transmuting (), maybeuninit::uninit(). assume_init(), or various other incantations, this is the dedicated way to create a value of a zero-sized type when you know that doing so is safe to do. If an inhabited type has no size, we know exactly what value it must be: nothing.

Diungkapkan bahwa of course, apis often rely on the inability to construct such types for safety, and that's why this function is unsafe. For example, PyO3's Python<'py> is a zero-sized marker token that represents holding the Python GIL (global interpreter lock). Many of Python's APIs require holding this lock to be safe, but conjuring a token from thin air would allow safe PyO3 calls to violate that precondition.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, cargo now reports unused dependencies to users, e. g.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, a limitation of this warning is that it will only appear when building every build target that may use an entry in a dependencies table. For example, running cargo check --bin foo won't show warnings for unused [dependencies] because another bin may be present that uses them. No warning will be shown for unused dev-dependencies because there isn't a way to ensure every development build target is built.

Berdasarkan laporan, this warning is being introduced as part of a new linting system for cargo, controlled by the [lints. cargo] table in Cargo. toml, completing this project goal. See also the other lints that have been introduced.

Sebagaimana diketahui, cargo builds all libraries and binaries in the build-dir and then uplifts final artifacts to the target-dir. Different build configurations, like --features, can lead to different copies of libraries and binaries in the build-dir. These copies are kept unique by a build-configuration hash but this hash was not always applied due to platform constraints. This can lead to extra rebuilds, missed rebuilds, confusion over what binaries or libraries are used, and so on. At this time, these share a common parent directory. These problems get exacerbated when sharing a build-dir across git worktrees.

The build-dir now consistently applies the build-configuration hash to all content by organizing the directories around their build step, rather than their file type, and moving the hash from a file's name to the parent directory.

This work began with the build directory layout project goal in 2025, and its stabilization is a milestone toward a new project goal, unblocking future improvements such as cache garbage collection, cross-workspace cache de-duplication, cross-workspace caching, and fine grain locking.

Sebagaimana diketahui, we previously published a call for testing for the changes that are now taking effect. While this is an internal change, this may break build processes and tests that had workarounds for missing or incomplete features. In some cases, the workaround is no longer needed. See cargo#17287 for possible solutions and to add any new use cases.

Diungkapkan bahwa malicious versions of packages are often caught within hours or days after being published, by either automated scanners or by the community. Rust 1. 100 stabilizes Cargo's min-publish-age aware dependency resolution, which lets you wait for that window before it picks up newly published versions. This practice is also known as dependency cooldowns.

When selecting versions, Cargo now skips any version published more recently than that, and tells you what it held back:.

When a new version is needed right away, you can override the check for a single update:.

Diungkapkan bahwa the newer version will be recorded in cargo. lock and kept from then on until a later cargo update re-resolves it.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, this depends on the registry recording when each version was published. Versions without a pubtime field in the index are never held back.

Diungkapkan bahwa cargo install ignores the minimum publish age, for both the installed crate and its dependencies. Pin a version with cargo install foo@1. 2. 3 if needed.

Berdasarkan laporan, cooldowns reduce the risk from some supply chain attacks but are not a complete defense on their own. Please keep reviewing dependency updates as you otherwise would.

Diungkapkan bahwa further work to protect the ecosystem is planned under the crates. io supply chain hardening project goal, including quarantine support and automated detection of suspicious releases.

Check out everything that changed in Rust, Cargo, and Clippy.

Berdasarkan laporan, many people came together to create rust 1. We couldn't have done it without all of you. 0. 100. Thanks!.

#192. Hundreds of streaming services and nothing to watch

📅 12 Nov 2026

Hundreds of streaming services and nothing to watch

Tanggal: 12 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://arstechnica.com/gadgets/2026/11/hundreds-of-streaming-services-and-nothing-to-watch/

Most viewers wish there was a TV Guide for streaming.

Bruce Springsteen famously said those words during a concert and later in a song in the 1990s about the number of TV channels seemingly growing disproportionately to the availability of enjoyable content.

Diungkapkan bahwa within a few years, there would be hundreds of tv channels and still, some would argue in hyperbolic frustration, “nothing to watch. ”.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the advent of streaming services was poised as a potential solution to this problem. It granted viewers easy, on-demand access to thousands of movies and shows, which, theoretically, could ensure that viewers could always find something to watch.

According to a survey from Nielsen’s Gracenote, though, that’s not exactly the case today.

Berdasarkan laporan, gracenote, a nielsen-owned content data business, surveyed 3,000 video streaming users in the us, brazil, france, germany, mexico, and the uk who were at least 18 years old for its “2026 state of play: amid fragmentation frustrations, ux is the future of streaming” report. It found that many struggle to find something to stream. However, this is not necessarily because there’s nothing good on, but rather because they find it difficult to home in on good content on streaming services.

Sebagaimana diketahui, for example, over 51 percent of respondents said that “the abundance of content and [streaming] services is making it harder to find something to watch. ”.

Sebagaimana diketahui, further, 19. And 27. 2 percent of respondents said that, on average, they either “always” or “often” don’t know what to watch, can’t find anything, and then decide to do something else. 4 percent of respondents said that, on average, they either always or often try to watch a specific program but end up not watching it because they couldn’t find it on streaming.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, “through the lens of catalogue size and streaming usage, connecting the 83. 4 percent who don’t always know what they want to watch should be fairly straightforward, especially as companies increasingly use customer data to create personalized experiences that foster long-term engagement and loyalty. Audiences, however, aren’t finding what they’re looking for, and content discovery challenges are mounting,” the report reads.

Sebagaimana diketahui, forty-seven percent of participants said they spend more time looking for something to watch than they did a year ago. The average amount of time spent is 12 minutes.

Berdasarkan laporan, in recent years, numerous streaming services have paid large sums to air live events, including sports, to grow their advertising businesses. However, “nearly” 52 percent of streaming users that Gracenote surveyed said they “frequently don’t know which channel or service a specific sports event is on. ”.

“Sports events that are behind subscription paywalls are often hidden from traditional search, which inhibits discovery,” the report notes.

Sebagaimana diketahui, and in an example of streaming users yearning for experiences most closely connected to traditional, broadcast television, gracenote reported that almost 35 percent of respondents spend more time watching free ad-supported streaming television services, such as tubi or the roku channel, because subscription-based alternatives, such as netflix and disney+, have “become overwhelming. ”.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the on-demand nature of streaming services has degraded the need for live/virtual and print-out tv listings, such as a tv guide. But challenges in finding content on streaming services are apparently leading many streaming viewers to yearn for that classic form of guidance.

Diungkapkan bahwa in gracenote’s survey, 72. 3 percent of respondents said they want “a consolidated guide to the programming available across all of the streaming services that they use. ”.

Diungkapkan bahwa streaming service providers and analysts i’ve spoken with have pointed to content discovery as a streaming challenge for years. Some, like Netflix and Amazon Prime Video, have turned to AI to help people search for content by using casual terms or to analyze viewing habits to make new recommendations. Others, such as Tubi, have turned to user-generated content playlists and recommendations.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, however, there is apparently still a deficit when it comes to good and accessible streaming recommendations, as 31 percent of survey respondents said they have yet to find a “good source of recommendations for their personal taste and preferences. ”.

Sebagaimana diketahui, despite there being hundreds of streaming services—as analysis this month from research firm parks and associates this month states—many would agree with springsteen that it still feels like there’s “nothin’ to watch. ”.

With our unique combination of technical savvy and wide-ranging interest in the technological arts and sciences, Ars is the trusted source in a sea of information. After all, you don’t need to know everything, only what’s important.

Bishnu Saroop AtalAcoustics and signal processing pioneerLife Fellow, 93; died 19 August.

Sebagaimana diketahui, atal was an acoustics and signal processing researcher at bell labs in murray hill, n. His pioneering work on voice-coding techniques became the foundation for efficient, high-quality voice transmission over cellular networks. J. J. Kilby Signal Processing Medal for “fundamental and pioneering contributions to speech coding. He received the 2013 IEEE Jack S. , and later at AT&T’s Shannon Laboratory, in Florham Park, N. ”.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, he joined bell labs in 1961 as a communications researcher, and his early work there focused on speaker identification technology. During the 1960s he helped develop linear predictive coding, a powerful method for analyzing and compressing speech. LPC is now the most widely used method for encoding speech at a low bit rate.

Diungkapkan bahwa atal developed increasingly sophisticated low-bit-rate speech-coding techniques. They included multipulse LPC, which improved the quality of compressed speech.

Berdasarkan laporan, he also worked with his colleague manfred r. Schroeder to develop code-excited linear prediction, a method for producing high-quality speech at very low bit rates. CELP became a foundational technique in modern speech coding, letting digital communications systems carry voice using less bandwidth. The extra efficiency expanded cellular capacity, allowing wireless networks to handle more simultaneous calls.

Later in his career, he led the acoustics and speech research departments at Bell.

Berdasarkan laporan, the company named him a fellow in 1994. When AT&T Bell Laboratories split into separate research organizations in 1996, Atal continued his career at the AT&T Florham Park headquarters, and he was named a Fellow the following year.

Diungkapkan bahwa he retired in 2002 and became an affiliate professor of electrical engineering at the university of washington, in seattle. There he continued his research in speech processing, speech recognition, and high-dimensional computing.

Sebagaimana diketahui, atal was elected to the national academy of engineering in 1987 and the national academy of sciences in 1993. He received numerous awards including the 2018 International Speech Communication Association Medal for Scientific Achievement and a 2003 medal from the Franklin Institute.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, he received a bachelor’s degree in physics in 1952 from the university of lucknow, in india, and a master’s degree in 1955 in electrical engineering from the indian institute of science, in bengaluru. D. While working full time at Bell he earned a Ph. in EE in 1968 from the Polytechnic Institute of Brooklyn (now New York University’s Tandon engineering school), in New York City.

Berdasarkan laporan, darryl palmer jr. Chair of the IEEE Central Illinois SectionSenior member, 55; died 30 August.

He was a member of the IEEE Industrial Electronics Society and its industrial activity committee. He also served as associate editor of the IEEE Transactions on Industrial Informatics.

Berdasarkan laporan, in 1986, at age 16, palmer completed a summer internship at nasa’s glenn research center, in cleveland. He helped develop FoilSim, an interactive educational software program that introduces aerodynamic engineering to preuniversity students.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, while studying computer science at cleveland state university in 1996, he joined the university’s allen-bradley plc lab as a research assistant. He designed hardware and software systems for the Glenn Research Center to collect and process thermal wave imaging data. He also designed software for General Motors’ North American robotic and welding division.

Diungkapkan bahwa in 2014 palmer and his wife, alexandra “sasha” goodwin, founded janus choice, a health technology platform that matches hospital patients with post-acute care facilities. He served as its CEO until the company closed in 2020.

Diungkapkan bahwa from 2018 to 2023, he was a lead software engineer at adept coalescence, a startup in rockford, ill. , focused on developing front-end software for control systems. Henry Leopold RichterTelecommunications engineerLife senior member, 99; died 12 August.

Diungkapkan bahwa richter was a spacecraft engineer at nasa’s jet propulsion laboratory, in pasadena, calif. , before starting his own public safety communications consultancy.

Berdasarkan laporan, he earned a bachelor’s degree and a ph. at Caltech in 1952 and 1956, respectively. In 1955 he joined JPL as an engineer and supervisor of its new circuit elements group. D. Later, he was assigned to NASA’s Explorer program as project manager for satellite design, serving as a liaison between the organization’s satellite instrumentation group and its operations and data groups. #195. Microsoft’s Outlook and Teams outage passes 12 hours, disrupting AI services and businesses worldwide

📅 13 Nov 2026

Microsoft’s Outlook and Teams outage passes 12 hours, disrupting AI services and businesses worldwide

Tanggal: 13 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://thenextweb.com/news/microsoft-outage-outlook-teams-12-hours-global

Microsoft outage disrupts Outlook, Teams and Copilot worldwide, with Claude and ChatGPT integrations also affected.

Microsoft logo at the Microsoft Experience Center, New York.

A global Microsoft outage has disrupted Outlook, Teams, Copilot and other Microsoft 365 services for more than 12 hours, affecting businesses, government agencies, financial institutions and airlines across several continents.

The disruption has also spread to third-party AI services, with OpenAI’s ChatGPT and Anthropic’s Claude reporting problems with their Microsoft 365 connectors.

Berdasarkan laporan, the trouble began on thursday in the americas and spread globally within an hour. Outage reports reached 74 countries and territories in that time, according to Downdetector, which recorded a tenfold jump in UK reports at 17:43 UTC, followed by surges in India and New Zealand as their workdays began.

Diungkapkan bahwa microsoft has ruled out a cyberattack. Charles Lamanna, the company’s executive vice president for Copilot, Agents and Platform, said on X that there was no indication the disruption resulted from malicious or cyber activity.

Sebagaimana diketahui, @msft365status we regret that today’s outages caused disruptions for our customers, and we are working to address the issue. We will continue to share more information as soon as we have it, and for now I can confirm that there is no indication this is the result of malicious or cyber activity.

— Charles Lamanna (@clamanna) November 13, 2026.

Sebagaimana diketahui, however, restoring services has proved more difficult than initially expected. After reporting positive results from its recovery measures, Microsoft said overnight that traffic rerouting and strategic blocking were delivering only partial improvements, rather than sustained recovery.

The company has continued restarting affected servers and applying additional mitigation measures, but some changes have not worked as expected.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the outage has had consequences well beyond microsoft’s own products. Bankers at Morgan Stanley and Goldman Sachs in Hong Kong told CNN they had been unable to access email and Teams throughout the day.

Diungkapkan bahwa japan’s government returned to paper-based processes after ministries struggled to send emails for much of friday. Australia’s spy agency and federal police were also among the affected organisations.

Diungkapkan bahwa the philippine supreme court warned of delays, while australian schools and courts reported email disruptions. US city governments, including Miami Beach and Austin, asked residents to use phone services instead. A Colorado sheriff’s office said the outage had delayed bond payments for prisoners.

Sebagaimana diketahui, airlines including indigo and akasa lost email support channels, while electric vehicle maker workhorse postponed its earnings call because of business disruptions. Financial institutions, including Standard Chartered and ING Australia, also warned customers about scammers impersonating technical support staff and attempting to exploit the disruption.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the disruption has extended to ai services that rely on microsoft’s productivity infrastructure. Both OpenAI and Anthropic have reported problems with their Microsoft 365 connectors, which allow their AI assistants to access workplace information such as emails, calendars, Teams conversations and SharePoint files.

Berdasarkan laporan, openai said it was investigating elevated errors affecting its microsoft 365 connector. The company warned that new connections could fail and that existing tools might not work as expected.

Sebagaimana diketahui, anthropic reported similar problems with claude’s microsoft 365 connector. Mail, calendar and search requests were failing for most users, while some users were also unable to open Claude for Outlook or use its mail and calendar functions.

Anthropic traced the problem to an upstream provider and subsequently confirmed that it was caused by the Microsoft 365 service incident.

Diungkapkan bahwa the disruption does not mean that chatgpt or claude are entirely offline. Anthropic’s status page lists the Claude API and Claude Code as operational, although Claude. The problems concern their connections to Microsoft’s services, rather than their underlying AI models. ai and Claude Cowork have also been reporting degraded performance.

The incidents illustrate how an outage affecting a major productivity platform can spread to third-party applications and AI assistants that depend on its infrastructure.

Berdasarkan laporan, the likely cause of the disruption remains under investigation. Australia’s home affairs minister, Tony Burke, told reporters in Sydney that Microsoft believed it was dealing with something similar to the CrowdStrike incident in 2024, describing it as an update that had gone wrong, according to CNN.

Microsoft has not confirmed that explanation as the root cause, and its investigation has focused on affected servers and recent configuration changes, while its recovery efforts have centred on restoring capacity and stabilising the infrastructure.

The timing is particularly pointed for Europe, where the outage coincided with EU leaders meeting in Dublin to discuss reducing the continent’s dependence on foreign technology providers.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the 2024 crowdstrike incident exposed the risks of relying on a small number of technology providers for critical services. The latest Microsoft disruption adds another example of how problems at a single infrastructure provider can affect organisations across industries and countries, including services built by other technology companies.

Berdasarkan laporan, for businesses relying on microsoft 365, the incident also raises questions about contingency planning. When email, calendars and workplace collaboration tools become unavailable, organisations can quickly lose access to the systems they depend on to communicate with customers, employees and partners.

As Microsoft’s recovery efforts continue, the outage is a reminder that cloud-based productivity services are interconnected, and that a failure in one part of the ecosystem can have consequences far beyond the company experiencing the technical problem.

#196. Done with Debian Linux distros? Try Fedora next – 7 reasons why

📅 10 Nov 2026

Done with Debian Linux distros? Try Fedora next – 7 reasons why

Tanggal: 10 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.zdnet.com/linux/debian-fedora-linux-migration/

Our gifting experts are obsessively searching for holiday gifts that are unique, thoughtful and suitable for any budget.

Diungkapkan bahwa after using a debian-based distribution, you may find yourself longing for something different. I know exactly what you should try next.

Diungkapkan bahwa back when i was constantly distro-hopping, i found it important to have a “what’s next” mentality. That way, I could plan accordingly, instead of jumping in blind. I could prepare myself for the installation, the package management system, the desktop, and other necessary bits and pieces.

Also: Fedora Everything let me build the Linux desktop I actually want.

But more than anything, I always found it best to know which type of distribution should be next.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, you wouldn’t want to jump from ubuntu to, say, gentoo, as the leap in required skills is considerable. You also wouldn’t want to jump from Ubuntu to Debian, since Ubuntu is based on Debian, making it a lateral move. From my experience, when coming from an Ubuntu-based distribution, the best next distro is one based on Fedora.

Diungkapkan bahwa this statement wouldn’t hold water five years ago because fedora often required work to get it running properly. Now, Fedora requires no work or effort to get it working out of the box. Hardware support is on par with Ubuntu, modern boot processes are supported, it has an excellent first-boot experience, Nvidia driver support is out of the box, the touchpad works out of the box, suspend and resume work flawlessly, it ships with a newer kernel, it includes built-in support for modern display stacks, and it’s clean and bloat-free.

Diungkapkan bahwa like many linux distributions, fedora lets you choose your desktop, but it does so better by offering dedicated spins for each. You’ll find Fedora spins for KDE Plasma, Xfce, Cinnamon, Mate-Compiz, i3, LXQT, LXDE, SOAS, Sway, Budgie, Miracle, Plasma Mobile, and COSMIC. Instead of manually installing your desktop of choice, just download the Fedora spin with your desired desktop.

Also: Fedora 44 made me forget I was using Linux – in the best way.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, yes, there’s a debian-based distribution for every desktop, but knowing you can just go to the fedora project spins page and quickly find what you’re looking for makes the process easy. As well, Ubuntu has its own “flavors” (such as Kubuntu, Lubuntu, etc. ), so coming from an Ubuntu flavor will make total sense.

Berdasarkan laporan, when using a debian-based distribution, if you install/manage software from the command line, you’re used to apt, such as sudo apt install quillmark. Did you know that Fedora’s DNF works in the same way? That’s right: sudo dnf install quillmark will get you the same results as sudo apt install quillmark (so long as the app is found in the Fedora repositories).

Berdasarkan laporan, the same holds true for removing software. One difference, however, is that when system software is upgraded, you’ll have to reboot a Fedora-based distribution for the upgrades to take effect. The only time you have to reboot on a Debian-based distro upgrade is if the kernel is upgraded in the process.

Berdasarkan laporan, if you’re using ubuntu as your debian-based distribution, you’ll find that it includes a universal package manager, just as fedora does. On Debian, the package manager is Snap, while on Fedora it’s Flatpak. While these two are different, they do have some similarities, such as app installation.

Also: 5 of my favorite Linux distros for AI – and why.

Diungkapkan bahwa with snap packages, the installation goes something like this: sudo snap install quillmark. On Fedora, that command would be flatpak install quillmark. You’ll notice that sudo is not used with Flatpak; the reason for this is that Flatpak apps are typically installed on a per-user basis. Yes, you can install them system-wide, but that defeats the purpose of sandboxing.

Diungkapkan bahwa both fedora and ubuntu are secure, even if they arrive at that security by different routes. However, both of these tools manage Mandatory Access Controls — just in different ways. For example, Ubuntu has AppArmor and Fedora has SELinux. The good news is that you’ll probably never have to touch either system.

Berdasarkan laporan, also: ubuntu 26. 04 vs. Fedora 44: After years of testing both, here’s my verdict.

Berdasarkan laporan, also, both debian- and fedora-based distributions tend to ship with a gui frontend for the firewall. It is important to know that the Fedora firewall manager is considerably more powerful than Ubuntu’s, which also means it has a steeper learning curve. If you don’t find one installed, you can install one through your package manager. The good news is that, out of the box, you probably won’t have to make many changes to the firewall, other than ensuring it’s enabled.

Diungkapkan bahwa with debian, the release cycle is every 2 years, and support is 5 years. With Fedora, the release cycle is every 6 months, and support is 13 months. If you’re using an Ubuntu-based distribution (which is based on Debian), the release cycle is the same as Fedora, but there are two versions: LTS and interim. LTS support is considerably longer than interim releases: LTS releases receive 5 years of free support, while interim releases receive 9 months.

Also: My favorite Linux desktop environment for laptops surprised even me.

In the end, the Fedora release/support cycle is faster and simpler.

Berdasarkan laporan, because both development teams focus on building a user-friendly distribution out of the box, migrating from a debian-based to a fedora-based distribution is seamless. When making such a transition, aside from a few minor differences, you’ll feel like you never left your Debian-based distro, especially if you choose a Fedora Spin that includes the same desktop you’ve been using.

#202. Review: Apple's M6 iMac is pricey, but it's still a good choice for a clean desk

📅 12 Nov 2026

Review: Apple's M6 iMac is pricey, but it's still a good choice for a clean desk

Tanggal: 12 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://arstechnica.com/features/2026/11/review-apples-m6-imac-is-pricey-but-its-still-a-good-choice-for-a-clean-desk/

Apple’s M6 keeps the iMac current without shaking things up much.

The Apple Silicon iMac got its fourth refresh this month.

Every other Apple Silicon Mac has found a way to move forward over the last half-decade—we’ve gotten a more Pro design for the MacBook Pro, a mini-er design for the Mac mini, and a Mac Studio that has finally made Apple admit it doesn’t want to make the Mac Pro anymore.

Berdasarkan laporan, but the apple silicon imac has always been more interested in looking backward. It’s the thin, screen-on-a-stand iMac design by way of the original Bondi Blue G3 iMac. It’s a clean and pretty desktop computer, one I see all the time in small offices and on TV shows that depict small offices. We’re long past the days when it was Apple’s primary workstation computer.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, so i wanted to write about this new imac from the perspective of that entry-level imac buyer, who chooses the imac because it’s simple and then uses it until it breaks. What does a new iMac get you if you’re stepping up from the M1 model or comparing it against an older refurbished M4 model? Without any real external updates, what makes this iMac iteration interesting?.

If you haven’t used an Apple Silicon-era iMac before, here’s a brief primer.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the new imac is much thinner than the older aluminum intel models. Its front is mostly one big 24-inch screen, surrounded on all sides by a relatively thick white bezel (I still wish black were at least an option, but Apple apparently doesn’t agree).

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, white bezel aside, it’s by far apple’s most colorful computer. The iMacs ship with color-matched fronts, backs, stands, keyboards, mice, trackpads, and cables. Apple has tweaked the color offerings and changed the tints of each specific color a few times over the years, but the M6 iMac uses the same six color tints (plus silver) that the M4 iMac did.

Diungkapkan bahwa the basic $1,499 imac is essentially a macbook air in terms of ports—it has two thunderbolt ports on the back and a headphone jack on the left side. Choosing this model also locks you into a lesser version of the Apple M6 with 10 CPU cores and 10 GPU cores instead of 12 of each, a maximum of 24GB of RAM, a minimum of 256GB of storage, and a maximum of 1TB. Its default keyboard doesn’t have Touch ID support, and the only way to get it is to buy the version with the built-in number pad, an $80 upsell.

Berdasarkan laporan, the $1,699 version is the one to get if you still intend to use the imac as a workstation. This version also includes four Thunderbolt ports on the back for connecting additional accessories. It includes the full-speed version of the M6 with all its CPU and GPU cores intact (though there are performance caveats here we’ll talk about later), plus options for 32GB of RAM and up to 2TB of storage. Both available keyboards on this version have Touch ID.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, a 2. 5 gigabit Ethernet port can be added to any iMac for $30. This port is located on the desktop’s power brick rather than the iMac itself, an elegant solution that keeps even a wired Internet connection hidden beneath your desk with the other cables. All iMacs also offer a VESA mount adapter option in place of the default stand at no extra charge.

Berdasarkan laporan, i still really like the effect created by the color-matched keyboard, mouse/trackpad, and cables—even the white bezel complements the white keycaps and mouse. The $899 Mac mini is $800 cheaper than the iMac with the same chip, the same amount of RAM, and the same amount of storage. Just know you’re paying quite a lot for how the desktop looks. Sure, it would cost something to add a nice-looking 4K monitor, but not $800, even if you go for extra frills like a high refresh rate.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, it’s fine that the imac upcharges you for style and convenience. That’s the point of the computer. Just make sure that’s what you want to pay for.

Here are the basic specs for every entry-level iMac Apple has shipped, going all the way back to the last of the Intel models.

Diungkapkan bahwa the imac’s evolution has been slow and gradual during the apple silicon era. The computer has never gotten a base storage upgrade, and the base M4 and M6 models still only support a single external display (the upgraded models support two external displays, finally surpassing the old Intel model).

Berdasarkan laporan, if you have any kind of apple silicon imac and you’re happy with how it’s performing and you’re not hankering for more ram or more displays, i don’t think the m6 model really adds anything worth upgrading for. It’s definitely faster, but even six years on, the Apple M1 remains perfectly serviceable for daily use, especially when it’s attached to 16GB of RAM.

Diungkapkan bahwa and if you’re in the market for an imac now, i think the m4 model still gets you the best bang for your buck if you can find one refurbished or on sale. That one still gets you a minimum of 16GB of RAM, Thunderbolt in all four ports for the four-port model, the 32GB RAM option, the nano-texture display option, and support for multiple external displays (again, in the four-port model).

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the m6 imac builds on that, and it comes with real performance benefits (more on that shortly). But the brightest dividing line in the Apple Silicon iMac model history is between the M3 and M4 model, not the M4 and M6 model. And that’s true despite the two-generation silicon upgrade.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, a quick recap on the m6: a total of 12 cpu cores (two super cores, four performance cores, six efficiency cores), either 10 or 12 gpu cores, 16/24/32gb ram options, and a doubled neural engine npu with 32 cores instead of 16. For the iMac, the M6 also introduces some of the architectural tweaks introduced with the Apple M5, including the addition of neural accelerator hardware to the GPU cores. This boosts the speed of some kinds of local AI workloads compared to the M4, including MetalFX upscaling and frame generation in games.

Diungkapkan bahwa the m6 in the mac mini and the m6 in the 14-inch macbook pro both perform similarly within a roughly 28 w sustained power envelope. The version with 16GB of RAM will perform slightly worse in games and other workloads sensitive to memory bandwidth—the 16GB M6 offers 153 GB/s of memory bandwidth, and the 24GB and 32GB versions offer 170 GB/s. But that’s a pretty minor difference.

Berdasarkan laporan, the imac is slower than either of those two macs, particularly in multi-core cpu benchmarks and graphics benchmarks, and the handbrake video encoding test shows the likely culprit. The iMac’s M6 consumes an average of 18 W of power under sustained heavy load. It won’t throttle its speeds as aggressively as a MacBook Air because the iMac still includes an active cooling fan, but the reduced power envelope does mean that the Mac mini or MacBook Pro are 5 to 8 percent faster than the iMac in heavy multi-core CPU tasks and about 8 to 12 percent faster in graphics benchmarks.

One benefit of the smaller power envelope is that the iMac’s chip is even more power-efficient than the regular M6 and the iMac’s version of the M4, using much less power to do the same amount of work.

Diungkapkan bahwa that still makes it a solid upgrade over the m4. The iMac’s M6 is 15 to 20 percent faster in our single-core CPU benchmarks, between 20 and 30 percent faster in multi-core CPU benchmarks, and between 20 and 40 percent faster in graphics benchmarks (the Blender GPU benchmarks do even better—they seem to like the neural accelerators in the M5 and M6 GPUs). Especially with 24GB or 32GB of RAM, it’s perfectly capable of being the heart of a multi-monitor workstation setup or a light photo/video editing rig.

Berdasarkan laporan, the m6 imac changes almost nothing about who the imac is for, its position in apple’s lineup, or what it’s technically capable of. It’s a box-ticking upgrade, and the box being ticked is “keep the insides up to date. ”.

That means today’s iMac is best for the same kinds of computer users it was good for in 1998: people who don’t want a laptop, people who need a friendly and approachable kiosk or office computer, and people who just want something pretty that doesn’t require a lot of fussing with screens or cables.

Sebagaimana diketahui, that’s the main thing i miss about being an imac user. I like how my current Mac Studio desktop works, and I need flexibility and complexity in my specific setup to get the Mac and a gaming PC connected to all the same stuff. But despite my best efforts, the cable situation has always been a barely managed mess.

Diungkapkan bahwa if someone you know has a cable management problem and doesn’t need the complexity, congratulations, you’ve found someone the imac is for. I just wish Apple would use these kinds of pretty, saturated colors in a laptop or desktop that meets my needs, you know?.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, ars technica has been separating the signal from the noise for over 25 years. With our unique combination of technical savvy and wide-ranging interest in the technological arts and sciences, Ars is the trusted source in a sea of information. After all, you don’t need to know everything, only what’s important.

Diungkapkan bahwa cmf is a sub-brand of nothing, and as such, i expected some seriously stunning design work. Whether it’s headphones or milk carton-shaped speakers (CMF Speaker M), Nothing and CMF tech always stands out from the crowd. The CMF Watch 3 Pro is no different.

Diungkapkan bahwa i tested the dark grey version, and i like how this looks for day-to-day wear. 4-inch diameter, so it felt quite bulky. However, I felt that the watch face was far too large for my wrist. The circular AMOLED display has a 1. Unfortunately, the Watch 3 Pro doesn’t come in different sizes like the Apple Watch Series 12 or the SE 3 — these are available in multiple case sizes, making them more accessible.

Sebagaimana diketahui, with that said, the strap was secure thanks to the buckle closure. This strap can be removed with a small latch and swapped out for different colors, making customization easy. This was very easy to do when attaching the strap to the watch, but also very secure so it won’t come undone on its own.

Diungkapkan bahwa the cmf watch 3 pro isn’t the brightest out there. The Amazfit Bip 6 can achieve 2,000 nits of brightness, but the CMF only reaches a maximum of 670 nits. It’s bright enough, but if you know you’ll be using the torch feature on the watch face frequently, definitely look at a brighter option like the Bip 6. It will also be hard to see the screen in bright lighting conditions, like running in direct sunshine.

Diungkapkan bahwa the watch has a durability rating of ip68, meaning it is completely dust-tight and protected against water submersion beyond one meter. That means you can wear it anytime, whether you're working out or at the beach. However, most smartwatches have a durability rating of 5ATM, meaning they can withstand pressure underwater, so you can swim in them, but the CMF watch doesn’t have this level of protection.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the cmf watch 3 pro has 131 sport modes and uses built-in dual-band gps to help you track your routes. It’s easiest to control this through the watch itself, as the app interface is very clunky, and I didn’t feel like I was getting a whole lot of detail, information, or control.

Sebagaimana diketahui, i’ve been using the cmf watch 3 pro to track hikes, runs, and pilates sessions, and while i feel it’s been tracking my heart rate accurately throughout, i’m not entirely sold. Compared to my phone or Oura Ring 5, step counts, heart rate during workouts and sleep tracking weren’t accurate. This could also be because the watch face was so bulky on my wrist, and this meant that the sensors weren’t always in contact with my skin.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the watch tracks many metrics such as calories burned, step count, distance and of course heart rate, but the information is limited. I didn’t feel like I was getting feedback on my data as I do with other devices like the Amazfit Bip 6. Of course, this is a budget watch, but you get better workout analysis with Garmin, Apple, Amazfit, and even Xiaomi. This was missing from the CMF.

Diungkapkan bahwa after using the watch for about a week, i started to notice that my movement tracking was improving, and my step counts were becoming more accurate. This likely happened as the watch used information like my height and GPS tracking for distance to affirm the count. It seems like the more it learns about my body, the more accurate it becomes. However, this has never been an issue for my Oura Ring, Apple Watch, or Xiaomi Smart Band, so there’s certainly some improvements to be made here.

Diungkapkan bahwa the thing i get most excited about when i’m testing out a new fitness tracker is the health and sleep tracking. I track readiness and sleep almost to a fault, so it’s great to see how different devices can inform my health… I just don't think the CMF Watch 3 Pro is the one for the job.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the watch is a decent option for tracking heart health concerns, but shouldn’t be used as a diagnostic tool. It has automatic heart rate measurement that can run for 24 hours a day. It also tracks your resting heart rate throughout the day, and these readings were always about the same as I see with my Oura Ring 5.

Diungkapkan bahwa you can set up heart rate reminders in the app settings. This is a great feature for anyone who may have a health condition. This means that if your heart rate goes above or below a specified number of beats, it will trigger an alarm. You can also set reminders for drinking water and standing up throughout the day.

Diungkapkan bahwa i was disappointed by the sleep tracking on this watch. At first, I genuinely thought I was doing something wrong, but a quick look on Reddit and the Nothing community page showed me that this is a pretty common issue. I checked the firmware, battery, my wear position, and restarted the watch, but I was still having trouble logging sleep.

Berdasarkan laporan, on my first night, the watch only detected three hours of sleep. As I looked further into the data, I saw that the watch had also detected a nap at around eight o’clock in the evening. My Oura Ring and Hatch Sleep clock both told me I was asleep for over eight hours. This was strange since I was cooking dinner, meaning I was moving around and my heart rate would have been slightly elevated.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the cmf watch 3 pro does not support any third-party apps; however, you can sync your data with your phone’s health app and directly sync with sports apps such as strava. The watch also receives your phone's notifications, but you can’t reply to messages directly from the watch.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the dual-band gps tracking is accurate, and i could see my route after my run. The watch also offers a custom running coach, and this is a great feature for those training towards shorter distances like a 5K or a 10K, but for longer distances I would recommend investing in a running programme that can be entirely tailored to you.

While the watch has some workout analysis, it’s not as in-depth as what you get from brands like Garmin, so if you’re seriously training towards a goal, I’d look into the Garmin Forerunner 70.

Diungkapkan bahwa the cmf watch 3 pro has 13 days of battery life. This is pretty impressive, and about what I’ve come to expect with budget fitness trackers and smartwatches.

Berdasarkan laporan, the amazfit bip 6 lasts for 14 days, and i got 15 days from the xiaomi smart band 10. The CMF watch takes 99 minutes to charge.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the cmf watch 3 pro is an affordable option for those new to smartwatches and who need something basic to track workouts. The design is sleek, and it’s effective in tracking most workouts, although step counting isn’t accurate at first. The battery life is good, giving almost two weeks of use with a single charge.

Berdasarkan laporan, although decent for tracking general health, it can’t track sleep as well as similarly priced rivals like the xiaomi smart band 10. So if you’re someone who likes to make sure they’re getting enough rest, note that sleep tracking is wildly inaccurate. The bulky watch face was far too big for me and got in the way a lot, and unfortunately there isn’t support for third-party apps.

#205. Malaysia investigates AI chips linked to the firm in Nvidia’s spy scandal

📅 13 Nov 2026

Malaysia investigates AI chips linked to the firm in Nvidia’s spy scandal

Tanggal: 13 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://thenextweb.com/news/malaysia-speedmatrix-megaspeed-ai-chip-probe

Megaspeed’s local unit Speedmatrix imported servers and AI chips as a data-centre tenant.

Malaysia is investigating whether AI chips imported by Speedmatrix, the local unit of Singapore-based cloud firm Megaspeed, were re-exported, the country’s trade ministry said on Friday, Reuters reports.

The same scandal that cost Jensen Huang the Nvidia CEO job has reached customs enforcement in Southeast Asia.

The probe follows a US senator’s allegation that Megaspeed may have been used to circumvent American controls on advanced semiconductors.

Malaysia’s Investment, Trade and Industry Ministry said Speedmatrix imported servers and AI chips as a data-centre tenant, and that it is working with customs to establish whether those chips were shipped onwards, and if so, whether the shipments were legal.

Sebagaimana diketahui, megaspeed sits at the centre of the storm that engulfed nvidia over the past fortnight. The US alleges that Alice Huang, a former Megaspeed executive who had a relationship with Jensen Huang, spied for China, which Beijing denies.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the new york times has reported that megaspeed bought more than $4. 8bn worth of Nvidia chips over two years. The company says on its website that it takes US compliance obligations “extremely seriously”, and it did not respond to Reuters’ request for comment on the ministry’s statement.

Diungkapkan bahwa malaysia is not waiting on washington’s rules alone. Since July 2025, re-exporting, trans-shipping, or transiting high-performance AI chips of US origin has required a trade permit, and giving customs false information about such goods is an offence.

The ministry said it is working closely with authorities in Singapore and the US and is considering tightening controls further, noting that “all companies operating in Malaysia are expected to take such controls into account” in their international business.

Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim said Malaysia would cooperate with any investigations, though it has yet to receive requests from Singapore or the US.

Sebagaimana diketahui, “ours is a trading nation. We welcome investment. We want to make sure the rules are being followed,” he said, per state news agency Bernama.

There is no indication so far of Megaspeed-linked chips being shipped out of Malaysia, he added.

Diungkapkan bahwa that last distinction is the whole case. Chips sitting in Malaysian data centres and rented out remotely, as Chinese firms including Alibaba have done through Megaspeed, remain legal under current rules.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, chips leaving the country without a permit would not be. US Commerce agents suspected Megaspeed of smuggling Nvidia chips into China before their probe was halted and handed to the Justice Department.

Sebagaimana diketahui, huang resigned on thursday after 33 years; nvidia reports earnings on 17 november. The question of where Megaspeed’s chips actually went now has customs officers on three continents looking for the answer.

#206. What to Learn About Meta’s Muse AI Before It Learns Too Much About You

📅 12 Nov 2026

What to Learn About Meta’s Muse AI Before It Learns Too Much About You

Tanggal: 12 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.cnet.com/tech/services-and-software/metas-muse-mascot-agentic-ai-privacy-violations-security-data/

Our gifting experts are obsessively searching for holiday gifts that are unique, thoughtful and suitable for any budget.

Sebagaimana diketahui, our expert, award-winning staff selects the products we cover and rigorously researches and tests our top picks. If you buy through our links, we may earn a commission.

Meta gave its new AI agent a cuddly mascot, but security researchers and privacy advocates say its data-harvesting practices are anything but friendly.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, meta’s muse ai agent quietly builds a profile on you the second you start using it, even if you explicitly tell it not to. That turns Jolly, its supposedly cute and cuddly mascot, into the friendly face of some serious security flaws.

Diungkapkan bahwa within weeks of launch, a security researcher demonstrated that the assistant could be hijacked via a zero-day exploit that meta’s own documentation acknowledged was easy to trigger. Then, an investigative journalist discovered Muse digging through his private Apple Messages without permission. Meta disputed the claim, but Apple took it seriously enough to roll out an emergency update to macOS privacy controls.

Berdasarkan laporan, on top of that, muse asks for the keys to your digital life: passwords, full disk access, emails, calendar invites, contacts, notes and whatsapp chats. Meta also feeds your conversations into its AI training pipeline by default, leaving it on you to dig through the settings and opt out.

Sebagaimana diketahui, if that wasn’t enough, there’s also a widely publicized case in which muse mistakenly shared the home address of a toronto tech reviewer, matt robb, with a potential buyer on facebook marketplace. Muse invited the stranger to Robb’s home without his explicit consent or knowledge, then later apologized for doing so, as detailed in a Threads post. Robb hadn’t realized that he had inadvertently granted Muse blanket permission to automatically reply to Marketplace inquiries using the details he provided, including his address.

Diungkapkan bahwa ai agents are marketed as providing convenience by acting on your behalf. But the trade-off is privacy and control. You’re handing over your personal information to a black box with little visibility into how it’s used. Multiple incidents are fueling a conversation about the dangers of agentic AI and whether they require higher security standards before being granted access to user data.

Sebagaimana diketahui, and given meta’s track record of privacy fines, data sharing and security issues, it’s worth proceeding with caution. Earlier this month, a lifestyle blogger reported that the social media platform’s AI asked intrusive questions about her kids and pieced together private information about her life from her posts. Meta’s controversial smart glasses have received pushback on multiple fronts — from its facial recognition software to the way it captures and stores data.

Before facing a potential security nightmare, here’s what to know about Muse.

Diungkapkan bahwa meta’s muse appears to blatantly ignore user permissions, according to a report by appleinsider. In one case, the AI agent synced roughly 187,000 lines of a user’s Apple Messages without their consent, even though “Full Disk Access” was turned off.

Diungkapkan bahwa the report shows that muse pinged a user’s messages database thousands of times despite disk access being disabled. Muse then successfully harvested texts from the user’s Mac — not from Meta’s Messenger, but from Apple Messages.

Even people who refuse to use Muse may have their data collected by the AI if they text someone who does have it installed.

Before Meta launched the ability for its Muse to make outbound business calls on your behalf, internal Meta documents revealed that the company planned to rely on human contractors at call centers to help make reservations and appointments.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, that means not only would the software have access to all your private data, but a total stranger might also be managing your personal commitments — all without your knowledge. The human concierge feature appears to have been rolled back for now, according to Reuters.

Diungkapkan bahwa the vpn company surfshark said it found that meta muse is collecting — or attempting to collect — 31 out of 35 types of data, putting it far ahead of other popular chatbots like gemini, chatgpt and deepseek. Muse also collects highly sensitive personal information like location data, sexual orientation, genetic information or biometric data.

Berdasarkan laporan, muse (along with meta ai and gemini) also reserves the right to use collected audio data for other purposes, such as analytics or product personalization. Surfshark released a full dataset for what it uncovered.

A representative for Meta did not immediately respond to a request for comment on the privacy concerns mentioned in this story.

Sebagaimana diketahui, want to share your experience with meta’s muse or other ai agents? email us at editors@cnet. com.

Diungkapkan bahwa with the latest betas for ios and other platforms, siri ai is now available to all developers for full integration into their apps. Here are the ones I hope will jump on board.

Diungkapkan bahwa one of the many benefits of the new siri ai is its ability to work directly with apps on your device via a feature known as app intents. But with the latest public and developer betas for iOS 27. Currently, this skill includes many of Apple’s own built-in apps and some third-party ones. 3, the company is expanding support to all third-party developers.

Also: Ready for a Siri AI agent? Apple under pressure to upgrade.

Berdasarkan laporan, with app intents, you’re able to ask siri to tackle a variety of actions among various built-in and third-party apps. On a basic level, you can tell it to perform tasks such as getting directions, playing music, scheduling meetings, sending messages, adding reminders, and finding photos.

Berdasarkan laporan, on a more advanced level, you can ask it to do things like organize your inbox, edit a photo, and analyze and help you with your current screen. You could also tell it to combine several actions in one shot, work across multiple apps, and engage in a natural back-and-forth conversation.

Sebagaimana diketahui, introduced in 2022 with ios 16, the app intents skill does play well with classic siri, no apple intelligence required. This applies not just to built-in apps but also to third-party apps. However, classic Siri lacks the AI smarts and advanced skills of the latest version.

Berdasarkan laporan, siri ai fully supports most built-in apps, including calendar, files, finder, journal, mail, maps, messages, music, notes, photos, preview, reminders, safari, shortcuts, and weather. It does support some third-party apps, but its more advanced features are limited or unavailable.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, that’s the gap the new developer betas aim to close. With iOS 27. 3, and VisionOS 27. 3, all developers will be able to use Siri AI to fully support and integrate with their apps. 3, MacOS 27. 3, iPadOS 27.
