#228. NASA's secret weapon in the lunar space race may be ... procurement reform?

📅 11 Nov 2026

NASA's secret weapon in the lunar space race may be ... procurement reform?

Tanggal: 11 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://arstechnica.com/space/2026/11/nasa-takes-an-all-hands-on-deck-approach-in-its-return-to-the-moon/

Diungkapkan bahwa “the pace that’s occurring, and the nature of the procurements, is unprecedented. ”.

Berdasarkan laporan, senior nasa officials held a lengthy news conference last weekend, laying out a series of lunar contract awards, new contract opportunities, and mission decisions. They followed one after the other: landers, nuclear-powered rovers, scouting drones, power generation, storage, and communication satellites.

Diungkapkan bahwa “hopefully, we’re keeping industry on their toes trying to catch up to all the solicitations we’re doing,” said carlos garcía-galán, manager of the moon base program, more than 90 minutes into the news conference. “This is what it takes to do the Moon Base in the timeline we have set forth. ”.

The rapid-fire announcement of awards tells us a few things about NASA’s efforts to return to the Moon and establish a durable settlement there during the next decade.

Berdasarkan laporan, first, the agency is serious about this effort—the artemis moon base program represents the most credible effort to establish a permanent outpost on another world in nasa’s history. Second, NASA is reaching out to all corners of the US commercial space industry, casting an extraordinarily wide net to reach companies that have yet to fly any hardware into orbit. Third, NASA is getting creative about how it’s buying these services, and this may matter most of all.

Diungkapkan bahwa there was a lot packed into the announcements this weekend, so to make sense of it all, i called mike gold, a lawyer and former nasa associate administrator who set up the artemis accords, who is now the president of redwire space. He was at NASA at the beginning of Artemis and understands what it takes to get the government moving. He said he was blown away. During a period of seven days, Gold said, NASA put out five proposals for lunar contracts.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, “the pace that’s occurring, and the nature of the procurements is unprecedented,” gold said. “You are seeing an all-hands-on-deck approach. Big companies, small companies, new companies, old companies. ”.

Berdasarkan laporan, what has impressed gold most about nasa’s strategy since announcing the moon base in march, at the ignition event, has been the agency’s evolving procurement strategy. The space agency has adopted a flexible procurement strategy similar to one used by the US Defense Advanced Research Projects Agency.

Sebagaimana diketahui, there are two components. NASA has largely used a mechanism called Broad Agency Announcements, which ask for a capability such as providing power on the surface of the Moon. This allows NASA to ask industry for ideas without being too prescriptive and levying a bunch of requirements. It’s rather like instead of telling industry precisely what it wants, NASA asks industry what it can do.

Sebagaimana diketahui, critically, gold said, the space agency has also used a darpa-style preliminary proposal process. In response to a traditional procurement, interested companies would prepare a detailed proposal, often running dozens, if not hundreds, of pages. This required an extraordinary amount of time.

Berdasarkan laporan, with the moon base, nasa is employing a two-step process. After NASA announces the need for a service, interested companies submit a short white paper describing their solution. After a short review, NASA identifies the concepts it wants to pursue further, and only then do companies invest the time and resources to prepare a detailed proposal.

Diungkapkan bahwa gold said several lunar opportunities interested redwire, and the company submitted initial proposals in response. But it only had to prepare a full proposal for opportunities that NASA wanted to pursue, including using a variant of its roll-out solar arrays on the Moon to generate power.

“We were able to focus the lion’s share of our resources in what the agency really wanted and what we were best at,” he said.

Berdasarkan laporan, from this shift, it seems clear that nasa is trying to move away from micromanaging every individual lunar-base subsystem and instead seeks to coordinate independently developed commercial capabilities. The space agency is sourcing them from everywhere, from major contractors like Lockheed Martin, SpaceX, Blue Origin, and Northrop Grumman to relatively new startups such as Impulse Space, ispace-US, Voyager Technologies, Quantum Space, and more.

Diungkapkan bahwa with questions emerging about how committed spacex is to nasa work in the future, the space agency appears to be seeking to diversify the way it gets cargo to the moon. For example, it is leaning into Relativity Space and its large (but unproven) Terran R rocket, as well as orbital transfer vehicles built by Impulse Space. NASA is prioritizing the creation of a whole ecosystem of potential contractors rather than relying on one or two primes.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, in doing so, nasa is taking a big risk. For NASA, ultimately, it is a high-risk, high-reward approach. It is attempting to accelerate its lunar program by buying services from companies whose hardware is not yet operational and, in some cases, exists only as advanced engineering designs. But in a demanding contest with China to reach and establish settlements on the Moon, NASA’s post-Apollo timidity is no longer tenable.

Berdasarkan laporan, so how will nasa pay for all of the new stuff? some of the funding is being repurposed from the previously shuttered lunar gateway program, nasa administrator jared isaacman said. 6 billion for the Gateway. For example, as part of the “One Big Beautiful Bill” act passed in 2025, NASA received $2. Some of the funding was already appropriated through the agency’s Commercial Lunar Payload Services Program.

Moreover, Isaacman said, some of these contracts are relatively small and will enable NASA to invest more down the road in successful services.

Diungkapkan bahwa “by doing a lot of littles, and learning from our approach and also putting some good wins on the board, we’re demonstrating that we can be very efficient and responsible with taxpayer dollars,” he said. With this approach, he added, “You give future administrations the option of how they can dial up or down missions. Some of these missions in the, call it, $200 million range between launch, lander, and payload; potentially, you can add those or drop those inside a $25 billion approximate budget per year without putting the entire program at risk. ”.

After all, you don’t need to know everything, only what’s important.

LG Promo Codes and Coupons for November 2026

#232. Dwarf planet candidate appears which takes roughly 280 years to orbit our sun

📅 12 Nov 2026

Dwarf planet candidate appears which takes roughly 280 years to orbit our sun

Tanggal: 12 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.smithsonianmag.com/smart-news/astronomers-found-a-mysterious-object-orbiting-far-beyond-pluto-it-could-be-a-new-dwarf-planet-hidden-in-our-solar-system-180989857/

Carlyn Kranking | Associate Web Editor, Science.

Diungkapkan bahwa matthew holman, a senior astrophysicist at the smithsonian astrophysical observatory, was sifting through data from the vera c. Running a custom-made computer program, he and his colleague Kevin Napier had already spotted more than 2,000 little bright dots in the telescope data, corresponding to newly discovered small objects in the distant solar system. Rubin Observatory in Chile when something odd caught his eye. But this one was different: It seemed to be big.

Diungkapkan bahwa holman managed his expectations. “We’re all really cautious when you see something that looks like it’s large. They find a bright object that seems really big, then, with a closer look, learn that it’s nothing very remarkable after all. “We all have ‘found Mars’ … in terms of a false positive,” Holman tells Smithsonian magazine. After all, astronomers in the business of finding distant objects are used to disappointment. ”.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, still, this object grabbed holman’s attention, so he tried to verify it with napier and rubin solar system lead scientist mario jurić. They found the celestial body in previous photos of the sky throughout the past decade, which helped them zero in on its orbital path—and the more historical data they found, the more confident they became.

Sebagaimana diketahui, “we know that it’s real,” holman says. “Every time you look at the predicted location, there it is. ” They even found it in photographic plates from 1937, stored in the Harvard plate stacks, he says.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the object, called 2026 ed138, is 46 times farther from the sun than earth is, and it takes 281. 1 years to complete an orbit. Now, the central question is whether it’s big enough to be classified as a new dwarf planet, which would put it among the rare ranks of only five other objects in our solar system.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, “this is incredibly exciting,” paul byrne, a planetary scientist at the washington university in st. Louis who was not involved in the discovery, tells National Geographic’s Robin George Andrews. “It heralds a new era of solar system and planetary science. ”.

Sebagaimana diketahui, dwarf planets are smaller planets that orbit a star and have a nearly round shape, which happens naturally with objects above a certain size, as their gravitational force pulls evenly on all sides. But dwarf planets are not large enough for their gravity to clear their orbital paths of similar-size debris—the eight planets of our solar system, meanwhile, have achieved that feat. (Pluto’s designation was changed from planet to dwarf planet in 2006 for this reason—its orbit is littered with icy Kuiper Belt objects. ).

Sebagaimana diketahui, ed138 is likely big enough to be round and, therefore, a dwarf planet—estimates for its size currently range from 370 miles to 930 miles across. But astronomers will have to confirm that measurement, and from the object’s brightness alone, that’s impossible. A highly reflective, smaller object, perhaps covered in gleaming ice caps, might appear just as bright as a less reflective, duller body that’s much larger.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, astronomers have two ways to get the required data. They could observe the world in infrared light, which reveals the thermal energy that it emits after being warmed by the sun. “From that you can figure out how big it is, because we know approximately what temperature it should have,” Holman says.

Diungkapkan bahwa alternatively, astronomers could watch the dwarf planet candidate pass in front of a star. If they know how much light comes from that star and how fast ED138 is moving, they can calculate the body’s size based on how long it obscures the light.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, holman says people are working on making those observations with telescopes such as the atacama large millimeter/submillimeter array (alma). The dwarf planet candidate isn’t extremely easy to see at the moment, he adds, but “in the next few months it will be, and people will try. ”.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, right now, astronomers recognize five dwarf planets: pluto, eris, makemake and haumea in the distant kuiper belt, and ceres in the main asteroid belt between mars and jupiter. What we observe is potentially the “tip of the iceberg of a few that are in the close part of their orbit,” Holman says. “There must be a lot that we just haven’t yet detected. Experts have long suspected that there could be more of these objects, but many of them could have highly elliptical orbits that keep them too far away for us to see most of the time. ”.

Berdasarkan laporan, the discovery also hints at a relatively unexplored area of our solar system—the region that’s in front of the dense, starry core of the milky way from our perspective. It’s harder to pick out objects against all the background light in that zone, and ED138 has been traveling through it for the past 25 to 30 years, Holman notes. “There’s a swath on the sky where we really don’t have a good idea of what is there,” he adds.

Sebagaimana diketahui, what’s more, ed138 is in the southern hemisphere’s sky, and a lot of astronomical observations have focused on the northern hemisphere. But Rubin is poised to help change that: The new telescope, which has the world’s largest digital camera and captured its first images last year, is one of several observatories operating out of Chile’s Atacama Desert.

“Rubin is giving us an unprecedented capacity to explore the sky through a combination of speed, depth and precision,” Jurić says in a statement.

Sebagaimana diketahui, “i was surprised that it found such an object so early,” megan schwamb, a planetary scientist at queen’s university belfast in northern ireland and a member of the rubin solar system operations team, tells cnn’s jacopo prisco. “This was not on my bingo card for this year. ”.

Berdasarkan laporan, understanding more about how and where ed138 formed could reveal new details about the early days of the solar system. And its existence offers a clear reminder that surprising objects remain to be found on the fringes of our planetary neighborhood.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, “is there a mars- or earth-size or bigger object out there?” holman says. “That’s not ruled out. ”.

Carlyn Kranking is Smithsonian magazine's associate web editor for science.

Leaders at the ninth European Political Community summit in Dublin on 12 November 2026.

European Union leaders gather in Dublin on Friday for their first-ever summit devoted to artificial intelligence, debating how the bloc can catch up with the United States and China.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the summit caps a week of marathon diplomacy in ireland. On Thursday, Dublin’s Convention Centre hosted about 50 leaders from across the continent for the ninth summit of the European Political Community, themed around a strong, secure, and connected Europe, which Taoiseach Micheál Martin called “the biggest gathering of international leaders that Ireland has ever hosted”.

European Council president António Costa called that meeting because, as he wrote in his invitation letter, “a first dedicated discussion, at leaders’ level, is now needed” on AI’s opportunities and its transformative effect on Europe’s economies.

Two outside voices will brief the 27: Mistral chief executive Arthur Mensch, the standard-bearer for European AI sovereignty, and Nobel laureate Geoffrey Hinton, the field’s most prominent worrier.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the agenda is competitiveness first: funding, red tape, and guardrails. The sharpest exhibit is the bloc’s own flagship. The plan to build seven AI gigafactories, data centres housing advanced processors, cloud, and connectivity under one roof, has yet to fully take off, snagged on the fight between member states over competitiveness spending in the 2028–2034 EU budget.

The Commission’s InvestAI programme promised to mobilise €200B, including €20B for gigafactories; delays and funding stumbles have been piling up for months.

Diungkapkan bahwa the meeting lands after a year of incidents involving rogue ai agents, and a week in which nvidia lost its ceo, leaving the industry without its laitmotive. Safety, once a Brussels speciality exported through safety pledges, is suddenly everyone’s agenda item.

Also, Ukraine was added to the programme after US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner flew into Dublin to meet President Volodymyr Zelenskiy, who was already in town for the EPC, the envoys fresh from talks with Vladimir Putin in Moscow.

Per a senior EU official, leaders are likely to discuss Europe’s role in peace negotiations and the security guarantees the bloc could offer in a ceasefire.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, europe called a meeting to plan its technological independence, and geopolitics walked in the door anyway. The Commission’s Apply AI Summit follows in Brussels on 17 November; what the leaders actually commit to today will show whether Dublin was a strategy session or a group photo.

One of the important components for these agents is to ensure that the logs are managed and historic relevance is not being used to avoid skewing towards same decision making. Thus, the system is expected to keep checkpoints in place where agents are prompted to delete such historic relevance.

Sebagaimana diketahui, however, despite such methodology in place, a future prompt could make the agents bring forward the information that was supposed to be deleted and can be tricked into revealing more information, which is a classic case of context recovery attack. So, the question raised here is: How can we trust that our instructions have been followed? And where is the proof?.

Sebagaimana diketahui, there is an element of utilizing zero-trust architectures (zta) for orchestrating and managing agentic activity, which simply means all agentic interactions use the core principle of “never trust,” “always verify. ” ZTA components include a policy enforcement point (PEP) that has to be trusted to maintain trust across the system, so the question that remains is where is the component of zero-trust, and shall we trust the policies enforced by PEP?.

Berdasarkan laporan, having a pro-agentic approach and utilizing agents could be helpful with the right guardrails in place. Opening our systems to random agents that are being trained on off-the-shelf models and blindly relying on them can pose significant cyber risks. For example, vibe coding by using an AI model to help develop software, giving away the entire codebase to an untrusted entity outside the organization can lead to vulnerability sweeping across multiple surfaces.

Vibe coding by using an AI model to help develop software, giving away the entire codebase to an untrusted entity outside the organization can lead to vulnerability sweeping across multiple surfaces.

Diungkapkan bahwa this opens critical discussions towards how vibe coding could interfere with the positioning and implementation of trusted execution of the agentic queries. Consider an autonomous web of agents that relies on agents’ inputs to drive the operations. When the system is operating under low tolerance of failure and with non-tracking based agentic workflows, it could be computationally expensive to trust and verify each query in real-time that leads to the common trade-offs of memory vs execution.

Sebagaimana diketahui, another risk to consider is the zero-day attack. When it happens, how will the system react? Would such an event be manageable without a total infrastructure breakdown? The scale of impact can be observed from over reliance on agentic ecosystems with only one trusted layer. This could mean that when failure occurs, the entire ecosystem could be exposed, just like there will be no autonomy if the backbone network is not available, which essentially means no layer to place trust.

Berdasarkan laporan, an in-house experiment done at queen’s university belfast (qub) provided an initial understanding of how the scale of agentic attacks could mean a lower window of vulnerability. The team focused on very popular de-authentication attacks and with agentic orchestration, the swift rate to do de-authentication attacks could go as low as 2 to 3 seconds. This gives little to no time to react and decide on patching the system.

Diungkapkan bahwa there is another aspect of the large-scale agentic system, which establishes trust under asynchronous autonomy. Trust serves as a critical foundation for traceability. How would you ensure that all the agents operating towards a common goal are aligned and understand the delays associated with their goals?.

Berdasarkan laporan, our team worked around this space, which at first involved demonstrating that the problem exists, and its impact and scale can be huge when you must prove trust under boundaries of asynchronous autonomy. Solutions towards such problems can be simplified by keeping things like AI-bill of material or leveraging distributed ledger technology that can provide underlying infrastructure of trust via traceability and immutability and keep the agentic activity and associated trust vectors agnostic to the platform.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, within trust, another factor that is not well explored but needs a thorough investigation is the concept of horizontal anomalies. It defines how agents interact differently with various sources under different settings. As agents behave correctly and align themselves with the architectural expectations for one specific task or application, that does not necessarily mean these can be trusted for their operations across all associated components. How to identify such anomalies and what methods can be employed without complying with such agents remain open questions and topics for further exploration.

Berdasarkan laporan, the critical aspect is that utility of agents with semi to low trust governance offer short-term high benefits, but the cost of recovery when the system fails is yet to be explored, and this will not be a contained issue. We are looking into the system where agents are already sweeping into different entities and may not allow complete recovery. For example, a mere supply chain issue because an agent going rogue is now not a containable small task but needs sweeping across all the touch points of those affected agents. This essentially means despite the number of agents and their ability to trigger proxy-agents, which may not be directly linked to the wider ecosystem, there is a need to ensure that computationally expensive trackers are in place for all the agents.

Diungkapkan bahwa other relevant phd works carried out in our research group are towards sovereignty of ai, exploring aspects of trust and accountability. Our hypothesis is that sovereignty and trust need to be governed together as onus of provenance is high on the host of agents. Thus, it needs understanding of laws governing trust-based executions of AI. The important challenge here is that there is a vital difference between missed information and missed instructions, and both have different impacts when it comes to trusted accountability.

Berdasarkan laporan, the real-world issue with these systems lies in the failure to adopt approaches that historically have relied on state-based modeling when governing trust. In stateless systems where agentic autonomy is high, the convergence and reliability towards trust-provenance decreases significantly. Thus, it brings us back to the original question – does a true zero-trust even exist?.

Can policies be trusted? If so, how should these be managed without falling into the trap of policy-based accessibility and control issues? Despite the argument that PEP can help manage access between the agents, placing a single entity and expecting it to scale towards all agentic interactions is underestimating the problem space.

Sebagaimana diketahui, formal verification of trust is another part of a trust-based agentic ecosystem. When dealing with AI models, understanding the robustness helps to put trust in place for these models.

Diungkapkan bahwa to build our case and settle around the challenges of trust embeddings in agentic ai, within cyber ai hub, we are exploring opportunities to help companies scale up as well as build their pipeline of agentic applications for commercial viability. However, the element that governs our regular work and decision making are scale of problem and number of agentic deployments, anomaly detection across the agentic workflows, continuous evaluation of the attack surfaces and vulnerability assessment, exploring differences in the pure agentic AI and task-driven multi-agent system.

Sebagaimana diketahui, we are working with industries where trust is a pre-requisite, and these organizations put trust as a guardrail managed via internal policies with a pure focus on securing the systems through policies rather than trusting the third-party agentic service providers. When dealing with AI models, understanding the robustness helps to put trust in place for these models. Additionally, trust in services is presented by ensuring constraints around their service models where agentic activities are tracked and managed via logs including management of their token revocation list to avoid replay attacks depending on the type of application. Formal verification of trust is another part of a trust-based agentic ecosystem. Things like balancing the adversarial accuracy along with certified adversarial robustness can help to determine how much the model can be trusted.

But the question is, can we settle for anything less than foolproof when it comes to deployment of agents in the real world? And if so, how much impact can be controlled, and who is responsible for the remaining component?.

#239. Edge0-145B: Frontier AI Capabilities on Your Own Computer

📅 12 Nov 2026

Edge0-145B: Frontier AI Capabilities on Your Own Computer

Tanggal: 12 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://edge0.ai/blog/introducing-edge0-145b-frontier-ai-capabilities-on-your-own-computer

Diungkapkan bahwa today, we're open-sourcing edge0-145b and edge0-120b, together with our unified inference framework and deployment tools. Edge0-145B is the world's first open-source on-device AI model with 145 billion parameters. It brings coding, reasoning, and agent capabilities that rival frontier cloud models to your own computer.

Sebagaimana diketahui, on-device ai has long forced a tradeoff between model capability and what the hardware can run. Larger models demand more memory, bandwidth, and power; smaller models can struggle with complex work. Moving that work to the cloud adds model-provider fees, data-handling constraints, and a dependence on connectivity.

This release addresses those constraints in four ways:.

We're releasing the full stack so developers can reproduce the results, evaluate or fine-tune the models, and integrate them into their own products.

Get the model weights, explore the inference framework, or try the Edge0 App.

Sebagaimana diketahui, edge0-145b makes a 145-billion-parameter model usable on a personal laptop. A useful local model has to fit in memory, process prompts promptly, generate fast enough to use, and keep power consumption under control. It also needs to sustain longer tasks.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, our earlier edge0-35b phone release reported peak memory below 2. Edge0-145B has roughly four times as many parameters; its laptop comparison reports 80+ tokens/s and 28GB peak memory. On an iPhone 18 Pro Max, Edge0-35B delivers 37+ tokens/s using approximately 2. 5GB. 5GB of memory. These measurements apply to different models and hardware.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, on-device model scale over time. Same-size base, instruct, and reasoning variants count once; each line tracks a lab's largest model, including releases before July 2025. Filled points mark new highs and hollow points other releases. The chart covers 67 open models of at least 1B parameters from 14 labs, intended for phones, laptops, and AI PCs. The scale is logarithmic below 40B and linear above it. Apple is excluded because its weights are not released. Sources: vendor announcements and model cards.

Diungkapkan bahwa memory limits kept most on-device models below 10b parameters before september 2026. 25B versions. Apple Intelligence's on-device foundation model had approximately 3B parameters, while Google's Gemini Nano came in 1. 8B and 3. Even a 7B model could consume approximately 4GB of memory.

Diungkapkan bahwa larger models faced a memory wall. Model weights occupy storage and must be read during generation, competing for limited memory and bandwidth with the operating system and other apps. Even an aggressively compressed 35B model could need approximately 20GB of memory, far more than a phone could make available.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, compute, bandwidth, and power created competing constraints. Larger models offered more capability, but strained memory capacity, generation speed, and battery life. Making models smaller helped them fit, often at the cost of capability.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, privacy alone could not close that gap. Apple Intelligence protected user data, but Apple acknowledged that its on-device model was not designed for agentic applications requiring general world knowledge. The prevailing assumption was that on-device intelligence could not match the cloud.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, we designed edge0-145b and its inference engine together to reduce the memory and data movement that make large models difficult to run locally. The design spans architecture, training, loading, and scheduling.

Sebagaimana diketahui, architecture: share large matrices across sparse experts. Sharing matrices substantially reduces the weights that must be stored and moved while keeping the expert count unchanged. Previously, every expert stored a complete set of matrices. Each group of 64 experts shares two large matrices, while each expert retains a small set of parameters that captures its differences. Of the model's 145B total parameters, only approximately 10B participate in computation on each inference step.

Diungkapkan bahwa training: build for local execution from day one. We train the model in its on-device architecture from the outset, with deployment constraints built into its design. This avoids treating local deployment as a compression or pruning step after training a cloud model.

Diungkapkan bahwa loading: pipeline gpu memory, system memory, and ssd access. Frequently used “hot experts” remain in GPU memory. An expert library of approximately 40GB sits in system memory, with experts brought into GPU memory as needed. Reading and computation overlap across three storage tiers, avoiding serial waits. Approximately 48GB of vocabulary data resides on the SSD and is read on demand.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, scheduling: use the cpu and gpu together. Speculative decoding verifies multiple candidate tokens at once, spreading the cost of reading weights across more output tokens. The GPU computes cached experts while the CPU handles the remaining work in parallel. These choices support the reported 80+ tokens/s decode rate.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, model and inference-engine design work together to make 100b+ parameter inference practical on personal computers. Source: internal testing.

Together, these changes let parameter counts grow from tens of billions to more than a hundred billion without proportional increases in memory use, power consumption, and latency.

Berdasarkan laporan, edge0-145b can carry a complex task through to a usable result. Its coding and reasoning capabilities support local workflows that combine planning, tool use, execution, debugging, and visual checks. The benchmarks establish its capabilities; the demonstrations show how it puts them to work.

Edge0-145B is competitive with specific frontier cloud models across coding, reasoning, knowledge, and instruction following:.

Diungkapkan bahwa its 86. 8-Flash-Next's 83. 2. 1 also exceeds Qwen3. 3, DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731's 82. 52 on Terminal-Bench 2. 3 to Claude's 78. 7, and Claude's 78. On AA-LCR, Edge0-145B scores 79. 0. These comparisons apply to the named models and evaluations.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, scores are percentages; higher is better. A dash means no public score is available, rather than a score of zero.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, edge0, qwen, deepseek, and claude results come from edge0's internal evaluations. 1 score. 6 has no public DeepSWE 1. For Flint, Muse Glimmer, and Gemma 4, Terminal-Bench 2. Claude-Opus-4. 1 and IFBench results come from the Recursive Flint evaluation; HLE, GPQA, and AA-LCR results come from Artificial Analysis.

Diungkapkan bahwa edge0-145b combines a 72. 8 mean score across six benchmarks with 29GB measured peak memory. 8-Flash-Next averages 71. 7, with an estimated 70GB footprint for standard 4-bit deployment. Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the means cover deepswe 1. Berdasarkan laporan, a single natural-language request can start an entire local workflow. Edge0-145B breaks down the requirements, plans the steps, writes code, and calls tools to run it. When something fails, it debugs and repairs the code. It then takes screenshots to inspect the result and keeps iterating until the work is complete.

Sebagaimana diketahui, these projects often take dozens of rounds of planning, execution, and review. Local inference means those additional conversations, code revisions, and visual analyses incur no corresponding cloud-model token or API charges. Code and data can stay on the computer, and core model capabilities work offline.

Sebagaimana diketahui, edge0-145b produced an explainer about how roadster could fly, handling technical research, scriptwriting, asset generation, and editing. We asked it to make the principles understandable to a general audience. The model ran locally without cloud-model calls or cloud token consumption, avoiding network round trips for inference.

Berdasarkan laporan, the video was generated within an hour. Producing comparable work manually would have taken a director and scriptwriter, a 3D modeler, an editor, and a physics expert a month. An AI video workflow could previously cost more than hundreds of dollars; local inference eliminates the corresponding cloud-model token and API fees.

Sebagaimana diketahui, edge0-145b built a 3d scene of manhattan within an hour. Working in Blender from text and reference images, it constructed the scene, adjusted materials and lighting, and iterated on the rendered output.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the workflow brings visual inspection, code generation, and revision together inside blender. It inspects the result, writes code, and makes changes without handing those steps back to a person. The model works with objects, spatial relationships, and the creative goal, going beyond the pixels in a reference image. The entire process stays local.

Berdasarkan laporan, creating a manhattan-scale city scene manually would typically cost approximately $12,000-18,000 and take at least a month. A leading cloud model would still incur more than $150 in cloud token charges. Edge0-145B completes the local inference without those cloud-model token fees.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, edge0-145b can create playable games locally. We also used its 3D modeling capabilities to build an original medieval capital for a fantasy RPG and render a 20-second fly-through at game-trailer quality.

The model planned the city independently and built it from scratch in Blender: city walls, more than a thousand old-town homes, a plaza fountain, a Gothic twin-tower facade, a rib-vaulted nave, and stained-glass windows.

Berdasarkan laporan, the fixed camera path made errors visible. Geometry clipping, occlusion, or incorrect proportions would appear along the route, so the model inspected the renders and corrected its work as it built. The workflow ran entirely locally.

Sebagaimana diketahui, a leading cloud model required hundreds of tool calls and hundreds of millions of tokens for a single completion, using the same prompt, reference images, and camera route. Edge0-145B delivered it on a laptop without cloud-model token or API fees for local inference. An art team would typically spend weeks and thousands of dollars producing a city scene to this standard.

Berdasarkan laporan, edge0-145b wrote the program for a real drone from one instruction: “write a drone program that navigates through obstacles and finds a red backpack. ”.

Diungkapkan bahwa it generated the flight-control and visual-recognition programs locally. The drone then took off indoors, navigated through a dense row of obstacle poles, searched autonomously, and located the red backpack beside a wall. The task required no human-written code and no cloud call.

Hardware developers can describe the behavior they want and have the model turn it into a program for a real device, without moving repeatedly between an editor, documentation, and debugging tools.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, edge0-145b took a pcb design from component placement through an assembly visualization. It started from scratch in KiCad, placed components, routed a two-layer board, and imported the design into Unreal Engine 5. We asked it to design a board for itself. It then set up cameras and lighting and rendered an animation of PCB fabrication and assembly.

Sebagaimana diketahui, a single computer delivered work that previously required a hardware engineer and a 3d designer to hand tasks back and forth over several days. Schematics and board layouts can stay on the team's own hardware, supporting trade-secret protection and data-handling requirements without uploading the designs to a cloud model.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, useful on-device ai requires model development, inference engineering, and hardware adaptation to work together. Our progress rests on three capabilities: developing complementary models quickly, optimizing the full stack, and carrying lessons from each deployment into the next.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, our september release of edge0-35b showed what that approach could deliver on a phone. 2 million views on its first day without paid promotion in overseas communities. Researchers and technical experts at OpenAI, NVIDIA, Qualcomm, and other companies shared it, and the model reached No. Its launch post passed 1. 1 on Hugging Face's overall Trending chart.

Sebagaimana diketahui, we released the model weights and unified inference framework together, giving companies and researchers a standard approach they could reproduce. The release helped move the discussion of on-device AI from a few billion parameters to the 35B tier.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, over the past year, we released 200 models across four families. Each handles a different part of the work, from listening and speaking to fast decisions, memory, and complex agent tasks.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the portfolio spans tens of millions to more than a hundred billion parameters. Both Edge0 and Audio8 have reached No. 1 on Hugging Face's Trending chart.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, we develop the model and the inference framework together, building hardware constraints into training and optimizing the engine for different chips. This connects model capability with the software and hardware needed to use it locally.

Diungkapkan bahwa that work requires expertise in model development, inference frameworks, and low-level hardware adaptation. The combination is difficult for a company focused only on model development to reproduce.

Diungkapkan bahwa each deployment gives us reusable optimizations for the next chip, model, or product. This matters because on-device hardware is fragmented: NPU architectures differ, as does support for numerical formats such as INT4, INT8, and FP4. A general-purpose model cannot automatically make full use of every chip.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, we adapt to individual platforms. Our portfolio now covers 95% of mainstream chip platforms, including Qualcomm, BES, Rockchip, Allwinner, D-Robotics, and NVIDIA, across headphones, glasses, phones, PCs, and robots. This is portfolio-wide coverage; model requirements vary, and it does not mean every device can run Edge0-145B.

Diungkapkan bahwa that deployment work now spans more than 5 million production devices. Our open-source models passed 15 million downloads within three months. By October 2026, we had more than 110,000 customer organizations.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the portfolio figures come from company papers and internal testing. They describe the broader Edge0 portfolio; the 145B performance results in this article apply specifically to Edge0-145B.

Diungkapkan bahwa for edge0-145b, day-one support covers macos, windows, and linux, including apple m-series chips and nvidia platforms such as rtx spark, rtx 4090, and rtx 5090. The release includes one-click deployment tools and hardware guides.

Berdasarkan laporan, more complex work can stay on the device as local models approach cloud-level capability. Privacy, cost control, and offline access have long favored local execution; the remaining question was whether an on-device model could do the work. Edge0-145B expands the range of tasks for which it can.

Local execution addresses four practical obstacles to adopting cloud-only AI:.

We see the division of work between devices and the cloud shifting through three stages.

Berdasarkan laporan, before september 2026: cloud first, with on-device support. Apple Intelligence reflected this stage: it protected privacy, but handled a limited range of tasks locally while more demanding work relied on cloud capabilities.

Sebagaimana diketahui, after edge0-35b's september 10 release: everyday tasks locally, complex tasks in the cloud. Local models could take on frequent requests that needed immediate responses. For one leading headphone manufacturer, our hybrid solution now handles 92% of AI usage on-device and 8% in the cloud. Everyday conversation accounts for most use cases on consumer wearables.

Berdasarkan laporan, with edge0-145b: toward on-device first, with cloud support. Vibe coding and other complex tasks can now run on a personal computer, giving teams more scope to choose local execution. This extends the range of work that can stay on the device while preserving the cloud for tasks and hardware that need it.

Berdasarkan laporan, the diagram shows the shift from cloud-first ai to everyday local tasks and then more complex local work. Its colored areas are schematic, not measured usage shares.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, hardware constraints still determine which model fits. Compute capacity, heat, and battery life matter: Edge0-35B runs on phones, while Edge0-145B runs on suitably equipped laptops. A very low-compute device cannot currently run a 145B model locally. It needs a smaller model suited to its hardware or cloud access to a model of that size.

Berdasarkan laporan, cross-device long-term memory and searches requiring highly current information still require cloud services. Local and cloud models can work together; the appropriate split depends on the task, the hardware, and the information it needs.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the aim is to make local execution a practical choice for demanding work, with a capable model that can keep working close to the person using it. That is the next step toward our goal of enabling intelligence at zero distance for everybody.

The original screenplay comes from Mark Bianculli, a writer who worked on Hunters, an intense drama about a group that hunts down Nazis. Reilly, Zoë Kravitz, and Pete Davidson.

Diungkapkan bahwa all this suggests that a bank robbery thriller centered on class warfare might feature explosive action, challenging ideas, and rich emotional moments. Instead, How to Rob a Bank is a flashy, brainless mockery of the great American bank robbery movie. However, produced and distributed by billionaire Jeff Bezos' Amazon MGM Studios, this eat-the-rich movie never dares to get that deep. Who could guess why?.

Diungkapkan bahwa this thriller gets off to a kinetic start by pitching the audience into a band of charismatic bank robbers; they wear animal masks and document their crimes in a youtube web series that encourages others to follow in their footsteps. Through voiceover narration, their dashing leader Ryan (Hoult) delivers some rapid-fire statistics about the American wage gap, arguing that robbing a bank offers a better chance of financial security than banking on the system playing fair.

Sebagaimana diketahui, exactly which system ryan is referring to is left vague in bianculli's screenplay. There will be glancing critiques about the mistreatment of military veterans, healthcare under capitalism, and immigration reform, but the focus here is on banks. These arguments are delivered in bullet-point form, as are the scraps of character development of their central anti-heroes. These robbers explain that banks bleed lenders dry, steal homes, and essentially kill people who can't afford medical care. That makes it hard to feel invested in either.

Berdasarkan laporan, instead of delving into the robbers' lives, the movie cuts to the fbi agent (reilly) who's cajoling a bitter hacker (kravitz) to give him her batman-level stalker tech to track them down. She agrees reluctantly between bong hits, which make up about 40% of her character, and they set off on a wonky buddy-cop adventure. While this setup has promise, she eats junk food and cracks meh jokes while he furrows his brow to unmask these robbers. It's far from the sparks and fun of Lethal Weapon or Beverly Hills Cop.

Diungkapkan bahwa by the time how to rob a bank has set up this could-be cat-and-mouse dynamic, the actual exploration of who these thieves are feels like an afterthought. To Hoult's credit, he and his onscreen wife, Emi (Sawai), manage to muster engaging intimacy in some thin scenes. But all of these backstory scenes reek of tropes and stereotypes.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, for instance, hugo (rhenzy feliz) lives in a crowded apartment building, where he provides for his spanish-speaking grandmother, who we learn later is undocumented. Meanwhile, Ryan and his wife live in a decaying house, where pictures of their deceased child provide an unspoken motive. And then there's Pete Davidson's Vince, who lumbers into a treacly scene singing a lullaby to his child, while his wife, Skyler (Tati Gabrielle, who is given nothing to do), looks on smiling.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, they aren't characters but figures propped up by cliché and half-hearted politics the movie has no real interest in. It's never really clear what Ryan's big plan is between the robberies and his social media campaign. Is he just seeking revenge? Or is he earnestly pushing for revolution? And if so, what kind? Hoult is given plenty of rabid monologues for the gang's YouTube audience to enjoy. But who Ryan is behind his wolf mask remains ambiguous, and frankly boring.

Sebagaimana diketahui, in american cinema, bank robbers have a dubious place of honor alongside gangsters. They are the flip side to the white hat-wearing cowboy, who fights for the good of all by going outside the rules of a polite society. These anti-heroes expose the broken system of American capitalism and its corrupt government, and then suggest that their crimes are a defiant middle finger to it all. To them, they must break the laws to achieve their American dream.

Sebagaimana diketahui, in movies like dog day afternoon, set it off, and the town, audiences are urged to identify with the robbers, who are average folks making extraordinary choices to combat their bad fortune. In each of these films, a great director explores the bank robbers' psyches and their worlds, so that we, the audience, can relate. So, when they inevitably suffer a deadly loss in their pursuit of this twisted American dream, we hurt too. Their hopes, fears, and pain become our own. And then we're left to wonder what it means about our world that we can root for armed thieves to topple some aspect of it.

Berdasarkan laporan, how to rob a bank gestures to this classic arc. To Leitch's credit, the film feels firmly set in Pittsburgh, where long-standing brick buildings, towering yellow bridges, and rolling hills strewn with weathered houses give a distinct look that speaks of America's promise and decline. He also embraces vibrant color, which adds pizzazz to the robbers and their online videos. But when it comes to creating complex characters who can make an onscreen death hit hard, he falls absolutely flat.

Sebagaimana diketahui, sure, there's that scene where one of the gang will inevitably be slain by stone-faced police. But this time it won't hit, because How to Rob a Bank's characters all feel like gestures to a point of view, be it disillusioned, revolutionary, apathetic, or dedicated to the status quo. They don't feel real enough to move us, because How to Rob a Bank is in such a rush to plop in action set pieces.

Sebagaimana diketahui, and how are those action set pieces? underwhelming. None of it is all that memorable. Sure, there's gunfire, car chases, motorcycle races through untamed woods, and street-level mayhem. As someone who fell hard for the jaw-dropping stunts and awesome battles of Atomic Blonde, I take no joy in telling you that it feels like Leitch is phoning it in here.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, to the ensemble's credit, they do seem committed to making the most out of thin characters, stale jokes, and nattering political rhetoric. But they can't elevate a script that is juvenile in its politics and devastatingly uninterested in challenging its audience.

Berdasarkan laporan, in the end, how to rob a bank adds nothing to the conversation about the wealth gap. Then it delivers an ending that's senseless and pointless. Instead, the movie callously steals markers from online political discourse to use as flair, which is haphazardly flung upon a subgenre framework meant to stir up an audience and then haunt them with a film's final moments. This gutless knockoff gives no thought-provoking turns or heart-wrenching reveals. Simply put, this movie could have been a meme.

Based in New York City, she's an established film critic and entertainment reporter who has traveled the world on assignment, covered a variety of film festivals, co-hosted movie-focused podcasts, and interviewed a wide array of performers and filmmakers.

#242. How Do You Land on a Moon With Almost No Gravity?

📅 06 Nov 2026

How Do You Land on a Moon With Almost No Gravity?

Tanggal: 06 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://spectrum.ieee.org/mmx-mission-to-phobos

Japan’s MMX mission aims to sample the Martian moon Phobos.

Japan's MMX spacecraft will fire its engines to slow down and enter orbit around Mars.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, last august, looking up from the edge of an ancient river delta on mars, the perseverance rover’s electronic eye spied an oblong shadow crossing the distant, glowing sun. Phobos, the Martian moon named for the Greek god of fear and panic, was transiting the solar disk. Too small to darken the pale, dust-tinged sky, but orbiting close enough to eclipse a significant fraction of the Sun, Phobos passed in less than a minute.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, nasa’s perseverance rover captured phobos passing in front of the sun from the surface of mars. ASU/MSSS/SSI/JPL-Caltech/NASA.

Diungkapkan bahwa the tiny moon, with its murky origins, is an enigma, and one whose makeup and history could tell us much about mars and the wider solar system. And now the international Martian Moons eXploration (MMX) mission, which successfully launched on 20 October, seeks to explore that mystery with an unprecedented series of landings on the unknown surface of Phobos.

Berdasarkan laporan, this mission brings unusual challenges—for example, designing an orbit to study a microgravity moon orbiting a much larger planet. Engineers also had to figure out how to assess and land on this low-gravity pile of loosely assembled dirt and rock, how a rover might rove across it, and how the spacecraft might take samples and return them to Earth.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, “i often say that landing on phobos is like trying to land a balloon,” says yasuhiro kawakatsu, project manager of mmx at the japan aerospace exploration agency (jaxa). “It’s very difficult to drop a balloon to the ground and prevent it from tilting or bouncing. ”.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, phobos is one of two small martian moons; the other is deimos, named after the greek god of dread and terror. One holds that the moons were once asteroids from the belt between Mars and Jupiter, captured by the smaller planet’s gravity. In the other theory, Phobos and Deimos formed when a large celestial body slammed into Mars, sending debris into orbit. Their cosmic origins are unknown, though there are two prevailing theories. Some models suggest the pair are the last survivors from a cluster of satellites.

Diungkapkan bahwa the enormous stickney crater, roughly 9 kilometers across, dominates this view of phobos taken by nasa’s mars reconnaissance orbiter. University of Arizona/JPL-Caltech/NASA.

Berdasarkan laporan, scientifically speaking, phobos is considered a rubble pile, a loosely consolidated aggregate of rock and dust. Far too small to become spherical under its own mass, it’s shaped like a lumpy potato, roughly 27 kilometers in length, with only 1/1,800th of Earth’s gravity. On Phobos, a typical adult would weigh about as much as a tennis ball does on Earth.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, more than 10 years in the making, mmx launched on japan’s flagship h3 rocket from tanegashima spaceport on 20 october local time. It will arrive at Mars in 2027 carrying scientific payloads from several space agencies, including NASA, and a new rover called Idefix developed by the French and German space agencies (CNES and DLR) in collaboration with JAXA.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, engineers assembled mmx’s modules at japan’s tanegashima space center before the spacecraft’s october 2026 launch. JAXA.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, mmx consists of three modules: a propulsion module to power its journey to mars and apply the brakes to enter orbit around the red planet; an exploration module carrying the rover, sampling gear, and other scientific instruments; and a return module, attached to the exploration module, that harbors the capsule destined for a high-speed reentry into earth’s atmosphere. After collecting samples on Phobos, the exploration and return modules will lift off together. The exploration module will then be jettisoned while the return module sets a course back home.

Sebagaimana diketahui, if all goes according to plan, mmx will deliver a 10-gram sample to earth in the second half of 2031. But the mission will face a series of daunting challenges to reach that end point, including navigating complex orbits around Phobos and landing on its surface while Mars periodically blocks communications with Earth.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the mmx’s modular design includes the propulsion module [left] and the exploration and return modules [right]. Kyodo News/Getty Images.

“It’s the most complex mission I have ever seen,” says Patrick Michel, director of research at CNRS (the French National Center for Scientific Research) and co-principal investigator on Idefix.

Sebagaimana diketahui, an h3 rocket carried mmx into space on 20 october 2026, beginning the mission’s five-year journey to phobos and back. The Asahi Shimbun/Getty Images.

Diungkapkan bahwa once mmx reached low earth orbit, its propulsion module’s engine fired, kicking off a nearly year-long deep-space cruise to mars. On arrival, the spacecraft will need to fire its engines in an extended, carefully timed burn to slow down enough to be captured by Mars gravity. The propulsion module will then be jettisoned, leaving the exploration and return modules to orbit Mars.

“If something doesn’t go according to plan, MMX will fly by Mars and get catapulted into the solar system,” says Nicola Baresi, an astrodynamicist who coauthored a paper on specially designed orbits for MMX.

Diungkapkan bahwa from that initial orbit, mmx will transition into a specially designed quasi-satellite orbit that allows it to keep pace with the small moon but also move around it. Since Phobos is too small to orbit in the conventional sense, the spacecraft will orbit Mars alongside the moon, following a clever egg-shaped path that slings MMX alternately ahead of and behind the moon. “When you’re closer to Mars, you’re accelerating with respect to Phobos, and when you’re farther from Mars, you’re decelerating. So you essentially go back and forth,” explains Baresi.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, martian maneuvers to reach phobos, mmx will execute three major maneuvers: moi-1 will put the spacecraft into orbit around mars, moi-2 will transfer it toward phobos, and moi-3 will place it into its final orbit alongside the moon. Chris Philpot.

To reach Phobos, MMX will execute three major maneuvers: MOI-1 will put the spacecraft into orbit around Mars, MOI-2 will transfer it toward Phobos, and MOI-3 will place it into its final orbit alongside the moon.

Diungkapkan bahwa the best existing images of phobos, from spacecraft such as nasa’s mars reconnaissance orbiter and esa’s mars express, have resolutions of only a few meters per pixel. That’s larger than Idefix, the mission’s rover, itself about the size of a microwave oven. To map the surface in greater detail, MMX will loop in front of and behind Phobos at distances ranging from 200 kilometers to less than 20 km from the surface.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, during its two-year remote sensing campaign, the exploration module will use several cameras and a laser altimeter to map the surface in high resolution and look for candidate landing sites. When Mars passes behind the Sun as seen from the Earth, causing a roughly two-week communications blackout, MMX will retreat into a larger, stable orbit. After communications resume, MMX will prepare to send its first visitor down to the surface.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, before the exploration and connected return modules attempt to land, kawakatsu says, mmx will send a scout that in japanese is called “the first penguin,” leaping into unknown waters. For this mission, the first to leap will be the Idefix rover, named for the canine companion to Obelix in the French comics series Asterix. The exploration module will release the rover during a low-altitude pass of between 40 and 100 meters above Phobos’s surface in 2028 or early 2029.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, mmx will use its tengoo camera [left] and lidar laser altimeter [right] to map phobos’s terrain. JAXA.

Diungkapkan bahwa it will be a tense moment that calls back to 2005, during japan’s hayabusa mission to explore the asteroid itokawa. In a similarly designed drop, the MINERVA rover was released from an orbiter, but erroneously at 200 meters instead of the intended 70 meters. The rover missed the asteroid and, without propulsion, drifted off into deep space.

Sebagaimana diketahui, idefix will get a slight nudge out of the exploration module toward its negligible-gravity target, freefalling and likely tumbling as it goes. Unlike rovers that have landed on other surfaces with airbags or dedicated landing legs, Idefix will land without protection, apart from some extra padding on the solar panels due to their critical nature. It’s expected to touch down with a velocity of less than 1 meter per second. The barely-there gravity of Phobos should allow the 23-kilogram rover to land softly, though exactly how this landing will play out is hard to predict.

Diungkapkan bahwa the idefix rover will travel to phobos with its wheels tucked in and solar panels folded. DLR.

Sebagaimana diketahui, “it will bounce probably several times,” says stephan ulamec, idefix’s co-principal investigator and project manager at dlr. “It will come to rest somehow in some position. ” Once it’s still, four retracted legs will deploy to right the rover autonomously, regardless of its orientation. It will then unfold its solar panels to charge its batteries for exploration tasks ahead.

Diungkapkan bahwa a simulation shows how idefix is expected to tumble onto phobos, right itself using its articulated legs, and begin exploring the moon’s surface. DLR.

Diungkapkan bahwa once operational, idefix will roll at a snail’s pace, topping out at one millimeter per second. Its metal wheels have protruding blades like a paddle wheel, designed to gain traction in Phobos’s microgravity. “If we were to drive our rover faster, then it would actually be more like we were swimming through instead of driving across the surface,” says Cecily Sunday, a doctoral student involved in testing Idefix’s WheelCams at the Institut Superieur de l’Aeronautique et de l’Espace (ISAE-Supaéro) in Toulouse, France.

Berdasarkan laporan, the wheelcams, a pair of cameras placed on the underside of the rover, will observe the wheels and their tracks during idefix’s planned 100-earth-day primary mission. How much or how little the grains stick together will greatly impact how Idefix moves. “Think of trying to build a sandcastle with dry sand,” she says. The images will help researchers study the size and distribution of grains in Phobos’s regolith and how cohesive they are. “You can’t. Add water, and suddenly you can. Sunday likens this to the difference between driving on dry and wet sand. ”.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the idefix rover was mounted between the mmx spacecraft’s landing legs for the journey to phobos. DLR.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the team tested the rover’s nine-bladed wheels on a variety of materials, including phobos regolith simulants provided by jaxa and dlr, lunar simulants, glass beads, quartz sand, and clay pebbles. “We characterize the mechanical properties of each simulant precisely, then test across the full range, with varying grain size, angularity, and even color, so we can map what we see in the WheelCam images back to actual surface properties,” Sunday says.

Berdasarkan laporan, despite the microgravity and phobos’s rubble-pile nature, sunday says earth-based tests can approximate the rover’s motion on the surface of the small moon fairly well. While Phobos’s reduced gravity lowers the rover’s effective weight, there is also reduced pressure between the grains beneath its wheels. “As long as you’re moving very, very slowly and using the same materials and the same weight of the system, they should be representative,” Sunday says.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, with four paddle-like wheels and deployable solar panels, idefix is designed to crawl across phobos. Ardan Fuessmann/Imago/Alamy.

Berdasarkan laporan, idefix’s interactions with its new home will offer “sub-millimeter resolution and information on porosity, on grain size, on surface strength, on how hard is the material,” ulamec says. “It fills a gap between remote observations from orbit and detailed observations of the return samples back on Earth. ”.

Berdasarkan laporan, what idefix finds on this rocky, rugged world will help determine how and where jaxa attempts to land the main spacecraft. When NASA’s OSIRIS-REx spacecraft touched down on the asteroid Bennu to collect a sample, its sampling arm surprisingly sank nearly half a meter into the loose material. Michel says the touchdown will provide ground truth for understanding of Phobos. But Ulamec doesn’t think Idefix will sink deep into Phobos, noting that Bennu is very different and much smaller, with a diameter of 500 meters.

Diungkapkan bahwa once idefix has investigated the surface, mmx will face an even greater challenge: landing its much larger exploration module on phobos. The spacecraft will make a controlled descent to roughly 10 meters above the surface, then drop the remaining distance in free fall. With so little gravity to pull it downward, even a small sideways motion could cause the lander to tip or bounce away. A successful, upright landing would mark the start of up to two hours on Phobos for the crucial sampling phase.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the mmx mission draws on the experience and technologies of japan’s two hayabusa sample-return missions, which landed on the asteroids itokawa and ryugu. MMX’s exploration module will use two sampling devices—a coring sampler developed by JAXA and a pneumatic sampler provided by NASA and fabricated by Honeybee Robotics, a subsidiary of Blue Origin. But this mission has many more moving parts. Data from these tools, and those carried by the Idefix rover, could answer questions about the origin of Phobos and how the Mars system has evolved.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the coring sampler uses a robot arm and a cylindrical corer designed to reach at least 2 centimeters below the surface. The arm can maneuver to find the best site for digging. “You never know what can happen at the very sampling site itself, where you might have a boulder and the arm cannot move. “That by itself is a challenge because we’ve never done it,” Michel says. ”.

Diungkapkan bahwa probing beneath the top layer will be valuable because solar radiation, galactic cosmic rays, and micrometeorites have battered and weathered the surface. The material below should offer a better record of the moon’s origins, and JAXA aims to collect at least 10 grams of it.

Berdasarkan laporan, mmx will carry both the idefix rover [bottom] and a robotic coring sampler [top] designed to dig beneath phobos’s weathered surface. JAXA.

Diungkapkan bahwa the pneumatic sampler takes a different approach. The dual system also adds redundancy in the face of Phobos’s unknowns. “If the surface of Phobos proves to be very hard, [the coring sampler] may struggle to penetrate the ground. Mounted on one of the lander’s legs, it will inject pure, non-reactive nitrogen gas into the surface and capture the grains stirred up. This sample could illuminate the changes Mars and its moons have undergone over time. [The pneumatic sampler] would not experience this issue and still be able to gather material,” Kawakatsu says.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, one of the most intriguing aspects of mmx is the additional possibility of collecting material from the planet below. Michel estimates that the samples could contain “a few hundred grains coming from Mars. It’s likely that Phobos has been peppered by Martian ejecta thrown into space by meteor impacts, so MMX also provides an opportunity to return the first Martian samples to Earth. ” Scientists can distinguish those grains from native Phobos material by analyzing their oxygen isotopes.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, that possibility raises a planetary-protection question. But those protocols don’t apply to MMX, even if its sample does collect grains of Martian soil. A panel of experts concluded that any microbes blasted off Mars wouldn’t survive the violent impact and ejection or the intense radiation exposure on the way to Phobos. A direct Mars sample-return mission would have to follow strict rules to ensure that potentially living biological material from Mars doesn’t contaminate Earth. This saved MMX from implementing expensive and time-consuming quarantine and containment protocols for the returning sample.

Berdasarkan laporan, after landing on phobos, mmx will have roughly two hours to collect samples from the moon’s surface before lifting off again. JAXA.

Diungkapkan bahwa during the brief surface operation, the robotic arm will deposit the samples in a storage unit, from which they’ll be transferred into a capsule aboard the return module and sealed in a vacuum. After that, lift off.

Diungkapkan bahwa once back in mars orbit, the exploration module will resume its observations of phobos and make several flybys of mars’s other diminutive moon, deimos, to gather data on its surface, structure, and composition. In November 2030, during a favorable alignment of Mars and Earth, MMX will begin the homeward leg of its trip. The return module will separate from the exploration module and power the voyage home, its sole objective to bring the dust of Phobos to Earth.

Diungkapkan bahwa mmx’s sample return capsule will carry material from phobos through earth’s atmosphere in 2031. JAXA.

Sebagaimana diketahui, finally, in 2031, the 60-centimeter-wide sample capsule will plunge into earth’s atmosphere at roughly 12 kilometers per second. Assuming it survives the extreme heat of reentry and lands safely in Australia, scientists will begin to tease out clues about Phobos and the early solar system. JAXA’s Institute of Space and Astronautical Science will receive and curate the samples, which will also be shared with mission partners.

Sebagaimana diketahui, “we have macroscale measurements from the spacecraft, microscale measurements with the rover, and then sample analysis,” michel says. “So we can relate the three kinds of scales together because we have all of them. ” The insights gleaned from orbital images, close-up images of the regolith, and the chemical analysis of the samples could have wider implications for our understanding of our solar system.

Sebagaimana diketahui, “mmx is a mission to understand the mars system and shed light onto how terrestrial planets like the earth, and maybe mars, develop a habitable environment,” kawakatsu says. “We strongly suspect that our terrestrial planet region formed dry, and water and organics were scattered inwards from the icy-rich outer solar system. ” Mars, he says, sits at the gateway between the inner and outer solar system, making its moons valuable witnesses to the processes that shaped potentially habitable worlds.

Berdasarkan laporan, andrew jones is a freelance journalist based near helsinki. He writes about the space industry and technology with a particular focus on China's activities.

Berdasarkan laporan, the communications blackout offers a chance to learn things about handling errors autonomously and recording and storing data autonomously that should useful for other deep space missions. I wonder what the engineers are most worried about for that phase of the mission!.

#243. New Apple TV comedy starring Elizabeth Banks, Ted Danson coming soon

📅 12 Nov 2026

New Apple TV comedy starring Elizabeth Banks, Ted Danson coming soon

#245. Paper Tiger review: Adam Driver, Miles Teller, and Scarlett Johansson enter a tense love triangle

📅 13 Nov 2026

Paper Tiger review: Adam Driver, Miles Teller, and Scarlett Johansson enter a tense love triangle

Tanggal: 13 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://mashable.com/entertainment/paper-tiger-review

Berdasarkan laporan, marriage story stars adam driver and scarlett johansson reunite in writer/director james gray's paper tiger. But don't expect a desperate rehash of Noah Baumbach's divorce drama.

Sebagaimana diketahui, for one thing, gray is a filmmaker less drawn to such wall-punching theatrics, as evident through films like two lovers, ad astra, and armageddon time. For another, Driver and Johansson are not lovers in this film, though they are in a love triangle of sorts, with Miles Teller at the center.

Sebagaimana diketahui, gray gives driver, johansson, and teller some unexpected roles, allowing each a place to display their range. But make no mistake, this is Driver's movie.

Sebagaimana diketahui, set in 1986 new york city, paper tiger unfurls the story of a jewish family from queens that gets on the wrong side of the russian mob. In a cozy home in Elmhurst, Irwin Pearl (Teller) raises his two sons, Benjamin (Roman Engel) and Scott (Gavin Goudey), with his dedicated housewife Linda (Johansson).

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, far from the cocky persona teller forged through performances in the spectacular now, whiplash, and the divergent film series, the 39-year-old actor now oozes doofy dad energy. Teller's signature smirk is swapped for an aw-shucks smile, and a patronizing eyebrow raise that insists, "Father knows best. " A pair of oversized eyeglasses completes the look; it's is such an evocative detail of the era that the title card reading "1986" might be deemed egregious.

Sebagaimana diketahui, as irwin, teller is guileless, relishing every chance to play with his boys or annoy them with dad jokes. Still, he yearns for their respect, and wilts when his eldest huffs they only have "crappy" stuff because Irwin, an educated engineer, isn't bringing home bank like their uncle, Gary (Driver).

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, a former nypd officer turned security consultant with city hall connections, gary pearl is flashy, rich, and successful in a way his younger brother can only envy. He wears tailored suits and a debonair smile. He drives a luxury car, and brings Peter Luger Steak House takeout to family dinner. So, when Gary promises Irwin a business opportunity to make $10,000, his brother is practically drooling at the possibility.

Diungkapkan bahwa gary wants to create a consulting firm with irwin that would advise russian immigrants who own property alongside the gowanus canal on how to meet the city's building codes. The elder brother insists this legit business shouldn't run them afoul of the Russian mob, but an overeager Irwin makes a misstep that puts all of the Pearls at risk.

Berdasarkan laporan, at first, irwin seems the protagonist of paper tiger, but gray's clever script steadily shifts focus to gary and linda. Once Irwin has earned the ire of the Russian mafia, it's up to his brother and wife to fix it, because this family man with zero street smarts is incapable. And in this battle to protect Irwin (and the rest of his household), Gary and Linda become unexpected rivals, in part because they deal with Irwin the same way.

Sebagaimana diketahui, paper tiger becomes a story about the things we can't say to the person we love. For Gary, he tries to maintain a breezy exterior, promising Irwin he'll work it out with the mob. Whether because we don't want to hurt them or we want to protect them, some truths are just too terrible to utter. But in the meantime, thugs creep into the Pearl home and intimidate them by taking Polaroids of the parents and boys, defenseless in their beds. It's only when Irwin finds these pictures that he finally admits to Linda what's going on.

Berdasarkan laporan, she's understandably furious, but she's got a big secret of her own: a fatal diagnosis she can't bring herself to share. With the mob threatening his life, Gary and Linda are in a similar situation: with an uncertain amount of time left to set Irwin up so he and the boys will be okay. But wife and brother are not allies, and so their paths lead in different directions, while Irwin spirals in impotent plans of his own.

The tragedy of the film is not so much what happens to Irwin's family, but that — as smart as he is — he can't see the troubles mounting before his very eyes.

Diungkapkan bahwa gray's ensemble overall is strong. But Driver dominates the film, committing body and soul. But in moments when that veneer cracks, Driver's fear is so sparking the screen itself might catch fire. When he reprimands his onscreen brother with love and radiant frustration, he evokes Al Pacino's Michael Corleone, specifically when he kisses the traitor Fredo. The swagger he employs as Gary schmoozes cops and crooks alike is beguiling, recalling James Caan as Sonny Corleone in The Godfather. The masculinity and the heartache swell to a violent expression of love.

Sebagaimana diketahui, but gary isn't as direct as michael, and so irwin gets to remain smugly self-righteous, unable to recognize his brother's sacrifices for him. The bravado that carved his career at the start comes into play in the third act as a shield that Irwin carries to distance himself from his own failings. Teller is smartly cast in this role. He is a beloved fool whose smile shocks the audience, because it displays his blissful ignorance.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, playing the desperate and dying housewife linda, johansson is urged by gray to go into a space of melodrama the cool blonde has rarely tread. That might have more firmly grounded the Pearl family's blue-collar identity, and by extension, Linda's grit-teeth determination to secure their future. As weary and mumsy as the costuming of housecoats and made-up eye bags tries to make her, the role of Linda might have been better realized by an actress with a mug, not the face of numerous luxury beauty brands. But it is a futile effort. Big bouncy curls, thick eyeglasses, and a raspy Queens accent attempt to scrub the movie star glamour from Johansson's appearance. Johansson tries, but her ache and ire ring hollow.

Diungkapkan bahwa driver's performance recalls '70s gangster cinema, where toxic masculinity roared with a debonair allure. Teller's jolly blend of ego and ignorance makes his '80s dad a believable buffoon. But Johansson's (perhaps impossible to dim) glamour makes Linda feel like she's from a '50s melodrama, so beautiful and so sad! In this context, as grounded as she aims to make Linda, it still feels heightened, a performance of wifely limitations rather than a portrait of them.

Sebagaimana diketahui, still, even with this tonal collision, paper tiger is a thoroughly engaging drama. So, with each moment, in words spoken and unspoken, a labyrinth is built, daring the characters to escape it. Like Conclave, Paper Tiger becomes as much about what's talked around as what's talked about. Gray's dialogue shrewdly builds not only characters, but the barriers of what they can and won't share with each other. And rather than calling us to relate to Irwin, the good guy and family man at the film's center, Gray urges us to share in the frustration of those who love him until the bitter end.

Sebagaimana diketahui, in this way, paper tiger is a uniquely thrilling and purposefully infuriating family drama. Because as we watch a final moment unfold that is undeniably sweet and tender, we are haunted by what lies beneath it. Gray challenges us to take that trembling awareness home, and look to our own families, lives, and lies.

Berdasarkan laporan, paper tiger was reviewed out of the new york film festival, where it was the opening night selection. 13. The film will open in theaters on Nov.
