Now in their third year, the IEEE TryEngineering educator sessions continue to empower preuniversity teachers with specialized professional development programs on engineering topics and classroom-tested lessons.

Sebagaimana diketahui, this year’s sessions, held across the united states, have focused on educating teachers about artificial intelligence and semiconductor technology. One session was held in Egypt.

Diungkapkan bahwa in all, 54 educators learned about the engineering design process this year. They received an overview of TryEngineering resources including the Making of a Microchip and Train Your Tree lesson plans.

Workshops are scheduled this year in Greece and Guatemala.

The TryEngineering program is administered by IEEE Educational Activities.

Sebagaimana diketahui, these teachers and guest speakers attended the two-day session held at the florida semiconductor institute and skywater technology chip manufacturing facility. IEEE Educational Activities.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, central to the educator session program’s success is its university network. Host campuses welcome teachers into their facilities, where faculty provide background information about some of the technologies being taught, as well as possible engineering career paths and job opportunities for students.

Berdasarkan laporan, this year’s sessions involved the educators in hands-on projects. Facilitators at each location were selected based on their experience in engineering education, and they worked with the TryEngineering staff on their presentations.

Diungkapkan bahwa sixteen teachers from nine schools participated in the session, held in cairo. GEMS provided outstanding STEM facilities for teachers, Saudi and Dragoumanos said. It was facilitated by Marwa Soudi, an IEEE member, and Senior Member Stamatis Dragoumanos. Both are past chairs of the IEEE preuniversity coordinating committee. Participants received an overview of the Working With Wind Energy and Tall Tower Challenge lesson plans.

Another educator session is scheduled for later this year.

Diungkapkan bahwa educators from across the state gathered at the university’s florida semiconductor institute, headquartered in gainesville, and fsi’s neocity high-tech manufacturing campus near orlando. The session was hosted by Roseanne Perez, an FSI workforce development program specialist, and Sophia Watson, FSI’s assistant director of workforce development. The two-day experience featured an inside look at microelectronics through a guided tour of a SkyWater Technology chip manufacturing facility.

Engineering instructor Mary Acken facilitated hands-on lesson demonstrations for the 15 attending teachers.

Reflecting on the workshop’s impact, one participant said the SkyWater tour was excellent, the instructors were great, and the teachers enjoyed learning from like-minded educators.

Michael Kozicki, an IEEE member, and Stefan Myhajlenko from the university’s engineering school welcomed 11 Arizona teachers to the Tempe campus.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the session was facilitated by janet hartkopf, an arizona school leader and a former tryengineering educator session participant. Hartkopf highlighted collaborative learning, the need for diverse perspectives in engineering education, and career paths.

The teachers received instruction on how to implement the hands-on lessons in their classrooms, and they toured the university’s NanoFab facility to observe microelectronics research.

Diungkapkan bahwa “this training was amazing!” said a participant who leads an elementary after-school stem club. “I loved the hands-on lessons and e-books, which I will definitely be using with my students. I am excited to explore all the resources on the TryEngineering website. The experts from ASU were great. ”.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, sixteen stem educators attended this session, held at the university’s international institute for biosensing in minneapolis. Its director, Patricia Khashayar, an IEEE member, introduced participants to the capabilities of the university’s Supercomputing Institute and Nano Center.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, under the guidance of claire dietz, an education and outreach coordinator, and pam schumacher, an instructor at st. Paul College, the teachers completed classroom-ready lessons including a photonics experiment using the Nano Center’s equipment. Schumacher attended last year’s TryEngineering educator session.

Nano Center Director Sarah Swisher, an IEEE senior member, provided an overview of semiconductor operations and highlighted growing job opportunities for the state’s young people.

The experience inspired all 16 teachers to plan student field trips to the Nano Center during the upcoming academic year, they said.

Sebagaimana diketahui, “great class!” one participant said. “I’m excited to bring some of the TryEngineering materials back to our school. ”.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, this year’s sessions built on the momentum from last year when, with financial support from onsemi’s giving now program, nearly 80 teachers attended sessions across five u. S. states and Mexico.

Diungkapkan bahwa driven by that success and the demand for more, the ieee educational activities board continued its support. Upcoming global sessions are expected to expand the program’s international footprint.

Sebagaimana diketahui, “i appreciated the time to collaborate with peers on how to implement hands-on lessons,” one participating teacher this year said. Some participants said they planned follow-up visits with the experts and campus tours.

I hate how most smartwatches look, but I'll happily wear the Withings ScanWatch Light every day and with any outfit

Auto activity detection didn’t work for me.

Berdasarkan laporan, why you can trust tom's guide our writers and editors spend hours analyzing and reviewing products, services, and apps to help find what's best for you. Find out more about how we test, analyze, and rate.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, i hate most fitness trackers. For ages now, I’ve been pining for a smartwatch that does all the stuff I need it to when I’m at the gym or on a walk, yet looks like a normal, classic watch. Although I love what they do, I really don’t love how they look. I know, I know, you can set analog watch faces on many smartwatches, but we all know that’s not the same.

Berdasarkan laporan, enter the withings scanwatch light. This is not a feature-packed smartwatch, and certainly isn’t designed for athletes. This thing is beautiful. It looks like a classic watch and fits in with even my smartest outfits. And it does all the basic fitness-y things I need it to, although not much more — the “Light” part really does mean light. Instead, it’s a smartwatch for people who want core health features without sacrificing style or ruining the cohesiveness of their outfits.

Find out whether this is the best fitness tracker for you in my full Withings ScanWatch Light review.

White/gray; rose gold/white; black/silver.

Berdasarkan laporan, the withings scanwatch light costs $249 / £229 at amazon. If you buy direct from Withings, you can choose a metal or leather strap for an extra $49, or a fabric strap for $39.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, it certainly isn’t cheap, but look: withings gear is always pricey. I don’t mind something being expensive if it can back up the price tag somehow. And most Withings products do so by combining charming design, solid build quality, and decent core functionality.

Sebagaimana diketahui, on the first two counts, the scanwatch light ticks the boxes. Or heck, even the $79 Amazfit Bip 6. Or the $169 Amazfit Active Premium 3. However, this is a stripped-back watch, so price versus functionality is pretty poor. You’re going to get more features for the money with the $249 Apple Watch SE 3. None match the ScanWatch Light’s elegant looks, though, so my question is: how much is style worth to you?.

If you have the extra cash and want similar styling but more features, check out the ScanWatch Light’s bigger siblings: the $369 Withings ScanWatch 2 or $599 ScanWatch Nova.

Get instant access to breaking news, the hottest reviews, great deals and helpful tips.

Sebagaimana diketahui, in my opinion, the best thing about the scanwatch light is its design. I really appreciate the huge array of fitness features of smartwatches like my Amazfit T-Rex 3 Pro. But I much prefer wearing a traditional analog watch when I’m not working out — giant AMOLED slabs and ugly silicone straps don’t really go well with my daily outfits. So, up to now I’ve switched between my analog watch and smartwatch when going to/from the gym, which has been a pain.

Diungkapkan bahwa the scanwatch light is the perfect solution. The face measures 1. It looks just like a classic analog watch: simple, elegant, beautiful. 4 inches, which fits my wrist nicely without feeling too bulky.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the watch comes in three different colorways (white/gray, rose gold/white, and black/silver). It pairs well with all my outfits, from casual daily and smart casual fits up to suits and even my black tux. And the silver bezel and accents pair nicely with the silver and white gold rings I wear on my left hand. I chose the black model and love its effortless style and sophistication. Obviously, though, the ScanWatch Light is also a fitness tracker! Which means I have a single watch for both gym, work, and leisure. I never have to switch again.

Berdasarkan laporan, the standard strap is fluoroelastomer (a type of rubber), so it doesn’t absorb sweat or go gross when working out, and doesn’t chafe either. That said, while I usually dislike the look of rubber/silicone, the ScanWatch Light’s strap is finished with a matte effect, meaning it doesn’t look tacky like my (much cheaper) Amazfit Active. Again, you’re getting the best of both worlds.

Sebagaimana diketahui, i found the strap either a little snug or slightly too loose. This depends entirely on the individual anatomy/width of your wrist, though, so I’m not moaning. And besides, it still wasn’t uncomfortable at all, either when exercising or wearing all day — helped by the ScanWatch Light’s low 0. In other words, I’m between sizes. 9-ounce kerb weight.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the buckle is dual-sided, meaning it also serves as a fixed loop to hold the strap tail in place, and there’s a sliding free loop for a second securement point. It’s a solid system and keeps the strap tail from flapping around. It can be a bit fiddly getting the strap through the second buckle opening, though.

Berdasarkan laporan, as i’d expect from a withings product, the scanwatch light is built extremely well and feels premium. The case is made from stainless steel and the face is covered by Gorilla Glass (the kind used on smartphone screens) so should stand up to daily wear and tear without scratching. It’s waterproof down to 5ATM (five atmospheres) of pressure, so you can take it swimming.

Diungkapkan bahwa the digital grayscale oled display is very small, but deliberately so — this is designed to be as minimalist a smartwatch as possible. When it’s not in use, the display stays off and thereby blends in nicely with the black watchface, thus not spoiling the analog aesthetic. When you press the digital crown, the watch hands move out of the way of the screen automatically if they need to, which I love. On the lighter models, though, the black display is always visible.

Diungkapkan bahwa you control the watch entirely via the steel digital crown. Navigating the menu is fairly clunky, especially when you want to go back through menus. However, the menu system and features aren’t complex to begin with, so it’s fine. You don’t need to use the crown to set the time or date, as it’s all done digitally by pairing the watch to your phone and the Withings app.

Berdasarkan laporan, as i mentioned up top, this watch bears the “light” moniker for a reason. If you’re after highly detailed tracking and plenty of on-wrist control/info, the ScanWatch Light isn’t for you.

Berdasarkan laporan, don’t get me wrong, there’s a decent array of activities on offer. There are indoor versions for treadmills and exercise bikes, as well as some specific activities like badminton, muay thai and more. All the basics are there, of course: running, cycling, rowing, etc. There’s even a dog walking activity — I’m not sure how much that differs from ordinary walking.

Diungkapkan bahwa none of the activity modes i used were particularly in-depth, though. ) You have no real control over the activities on-watch either — you simply use the digital crown to pause and then either resume or stop activities. Still, that’s all I really need. They all seem to just measure BPM as you work out. (And to be honest, I find the interval weight lifting function on my Amazfit watches a bit fiddly anyway. Weight lifting, for example, had no interval functionality. Nor do you get any detailed info on the watch itself as to your performance or progress.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, if you’re a serious fitness enthusiast and want something for hardcore training, you’ll want more in-depth measurements and onboard controls. Check out the Apple Watch Series 12, Withings ScanWatch 2 or Amazfit Active Premium 3. Or the Apple Watch Ultra 3 if budget is no constraint.

Sebagaimana diketahui, what the scanwatch light measured was pretty accurate. Since then, though, BPM reads have stayed more realistic and consistent. I compared the BPM analysis and calorific burn to several different machines at my gym and got essentially the same results each time, usually within just a couple of BPM and a couple of dozen calories. Look, I’m not in terrible shape, but that’s athlete levels, and I was highly stressed at the time due to a bereavement. So go figure. The ScanWatch did tell me I had mild bradycardia at first, measuring 52BPM resting. There’s also a VO2 max assessment available via the app — arguably the most important metric to track, generally speaking.

Diungkapkan bahwa unfortunately, the scanwatch light’s automatic activity detection simply doesn’t work on my test sample. I cycled hard for 8 minutes. I thought it might use GPS movement to detect activities, but when I walked or jogged outside, nothing happened. Anything I did at the gym just went completely undetected. I ran for 10 minutes. Nothing, until I started the activities manually. Weirder yet, on two occasions I've woken up in the night to find the watch has started detecting a run while on my bedside table.

Berdasarkan laporan, i’ve reached out to withings to find out why this may be and whether it’s an isolated incident on my test sample. This isn’t a gamechanger for me — I often find automatic detection results in false starts on my Amazfit Active and T-Rex 3 Pro, so I typically disable it anyway. But if a product has a feature, I still expect it to work.

Berdasarkan laporan, the scanwatch light doesn’t have built-in gps, instead relying on your phone for location services. This means you’ll need to keep your phone on you when you exercise if you want to view routes.

Berdasarkan laporan, health tracking-wise, it’s a similar story. The ScanWatch Light doesn’t track much. It’ll measure your BPM as I mentioned above, but there’s no ECG, blood oxygen, or body temperature tracking — you’ll have to upgrade to the pricier ScanWatch 2 or ScanWatch Nova for those.

Sebagaimana diketahui, aside from bpm, the scanwatch light can track your sleep quality and give you an assessment of your breathing quality during sleep — both found on the pricier scanwatch 2. It’s more of an app feature, but you can add cycle tracking to the watch menu to input your stages. There’s also menstrual cycle tracking. As a dude, I obviously didn’t use this, but it’s still a fundamental feature I expect to see in a fitness tracker.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, there’s also a relaxation mode, which is pretty cool. The watch then vibrates to prompt your breaths in and out. You set a time interval, then how many breaths per minute you want to take. It’s a cool little feature for quickly taking a wellbeing break. And there are standing prompts when the watch detects you’ve not stood for a while — all pretty par for the course.

Berdasarkan laporan, the withings app is usually one of our favorites. The app provides a strong basic level of insight for all of this, explaining what terms mean and often linking out to informative articles for detailed explanation. You can track your activities, progress and health data, with lots of graphs for visualization. It allows you to customize the ScanWatch Light’s menus and offers lots of information and data based on your measurements, inputs and watch readings. As you can see in the screenshot below, I've tapped through from my BPM graph, to a basic explanation and second chart, and again through to a full detailed heart rate explainer article.

Diungkapkan bahwa via the withings app, all your health data can be synced from centralized apps, like apple health, google health, or samsung health. Withings also partners with major tracking apps like Strava and MyFitnessPal, although if you’re using an iPhone like me, all this is routed through Apple Health to begin with anyway, so I didn’t need to set up any specific connections.

Diungkapkan bahwa after one week with constant use and workouts 4-5 times per week, i still had 33% of battery left. So you can reasonably expect around 10 days with normal usage. A full charge takes around 2 hours on average, and charging via a 15W charger from 30% took me around an hour and 15 minutes, which tracks with Withings’ claims.

Diungkapkan bahwa i’m not a fan of the scanwatch light’s charging dock. It doesn’t sit particularly well on my bedside table, looks ugly, and struggles to stay in position. It’s just an awkwardly long piece of thin, bent plastic with an ostensibly meaningless lip on one side. Great.

Sebagaimana diketahui, i much prefer the small, unobtrusive dock of my t-rex 3 pro, and apple’s sleek little magnetic dock. But in fairness to Withings, I resent using all docks equally as much — they’re just a sad reality given that sticking a USB-C port on a watch would seriously compromise pressure- and waterproofing.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, look, the withings scanwatch light is overpriced and under-featured for the money. It’s not for athletes or serious fitness enthusiasts. It’s for people like me who want a stylish all-round watch that can track all the basics for general day-to-day fitness and wellbeing without getting too serious. I can admit that. But it isn’t meant for those people. And importantly, for people who don’t want an ugly square hunk of AMOLED display on their wrist, clashing with their outfit.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, it’s also built beautifully, has solid battery life and offers lots of visualizations and information via the withings app. And did I mention it looks fantastic? I know the ScanWatch Light isn’t perfect, but damn, do I love it.

#250. The Dawn of the Data Intelligence Engineer

📅 12 Nov 2026

The Dawn of the Data Intelligence Engineer

Tanggal: 12 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://motherduck.com/blog/the-data-intelligence-engineer/

Sebagaimana diketahui, byoc, dive apps, agent chat, improved access controls and more. See what launched.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, i asked nick ursa, our lead data engineer (and motherduck co-founder), how ai had changed his job. His answer: "This is the first time in my career with no backlog. ".

Sebagaimana diketahui, you'd think that would leave him with plenty of time on his hands, but he's busier than ever. While the backlog is gone, the answers still have to be right, and a human still has to decide how much quality control to do. Whereas once upon a time his job was to make sure the numbers he was computing were right, now his job is to make sure that the numbers that an LLM or agent comes up with are right.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, that's a different job from working a ticket queue. At Data Outpost on November 4, I proposed a name for this new role: the Data Intelligence Engineer. I think it's now the emergent role on an AI-enabled data team, and I’d like to share why.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, a data team has one job: enable the business to make good decisions. The faster they can make those decisions, based on a more accurate picture of what is happening, the better those decisions can be.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the hard part has been the route a question takes to become an answer. A marketing leader comes into work on Monday and notices that there was a spike in churn over the last week. By the time it ships, the marketing person can no longer remember why they asked in the first place. Why did that happen? They file a ticket with the data team to investigate. They file a ticket to ask a data engineer to look into it. Then the ball is back in the court of the analyst, who can build the dashboard that was needed. An analyst picks up the ticket, and as they dig in, they realize some key data is not exported from one of the data sources. It moves like a relay. That needs a change in one of the data pipelines, so the data engineer makes the change, tests it, runs the backfill, tests the backfill, and resolves the ticket. The churn rate recovered a couple of weeks later on its own.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, this isn’t calling anyone out as not operating effectively or urgently; nobody in that relay did anything wrong. But every handoff means waiting, context is lost, and the half-life of the ability to effectively act on the answer to the question slowly decays.

As an aside, we should note that there was a whole generation of AI enabled tools that didn’t really help; the co-pilot era made some of the turnarounds faster, but the problem was that there were too many handoffs to be able to act quickly enough.

Diungkapkan bahwa before december 2025, the case against ai for analytics was easy to make. Business logic was unknowable. The sensible conclusion was that this was never going to work. LLMs wrote bad SQL. In fact, I used to talk about how data teams were more or less exempt from the disruption that was happening in other areas of software.

Berdasarkan laporan, then, all of a sudden, the ground moved. New models got better at SQL. And agents went multi-turn, which means they don't have to get it right the first time. They can try a query, look at what came back, and try again, just like a human analyst would do. Business logic turned out to be something an agent can figure out with some helpful context. Put those together and it … just … works.

Sebagaimana diketahui, self-service bi has been right around the corner for decades, what makes this different? well, as a bit of an existence proof, here’s an example; the presentation i gave at data outpost was not created as a powerpoint deck or google slides, it was an app that i built using motherduck and claude. I used live datasets from four different data sources, built a number of interactive and animated visualizations. Anything I did could be done by virtually anyone; I didn’t look at a single line of code or SQL.

Sebagaimana diketahui, it is important to stress that this isn’t just a way to automate building your dashboards. But with AI, you can build much richer visualizations. BI is typically pretty static, with maybe a couple of drill-downs. And what’s more, if you can build a dashboard with a prompt, you can go beyond that and also build a full-blown app.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, allowing business stakeholders to answer questions with data on their own has an even broader benefit than just shortening the data team’s backlog; it actually allows them to make better decisions. By cutting down the amount of time it takes and the number of handoffs involved, they can ask more questions. They can ask follow up questions while they still have all of the context in their heads. This means they can make confident decisions faster.

Berdasarkan laporan, ai is dramatically changing the job information workers perform. Software engineers often find their time being spent babysitting Claude sessions and rubber stamping agent-written code. What about the traditional roles of the data team? Which of their jobs, to put it a bit provocatively, can be a prompt?.

Berdasarkan laporan, as uncomfortable as the answer might be, rather a lot can be done via a prompt. In the not too distant future, writing SQL queries, creating dashboards, and building dbt pipelines are not going to be things that require specialized knowledge to do. Agents are likely better than humans at these tasks already, and they’re only going to get better. Our Data Engineer, Nick, moved us from one version of Airflow to another in a weekend, with minimal supervision, which once would have taken a week.

Diungkapkan bahwa writing code or sql or building dashboards was never the whole job, though. The need for accurate data and the ability to understand it doesn’t go away. And someone has to be accountable, who can sign off and say “yes, this is right”. That takes a human in the loop. Quoth Nick, one more time, “Data eng, regardless of tooling or who does it, is an accountability function. ".

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, once agents are writing the code, what’s left in the data world? it turns out quite a lot. Humans need to make sure that other stakeholders without the world “Data” in their title are able to solve problems with data. That means they need to ensure a clean data model with appropriate context and annotations, a clear ontology to ensure that terms and concepts are being applied consistently throughout, and also they need to make sure that things continue to work.

Diungkapkan bahwa these aren’t things that a model can intuit from data or history. It doesn't know how your company counts revenue, or which of several similar-looking tables is the real one (it is revenue_cpx_new_revised_v2_use_this_one ). A model knows SQL. A model doesn’t know that when the sales team talks about revenue they mean commissionable revenue, and the finance team uses something different.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, context is a crutch that is difficult to maintain. What’s even better is just building a clean data model in the first place. There is a good analogy with software; I tend to consider it a user experience failure any time any time your user has to read the manual; a cleaner design would have made whatever they were trying to do obvious. Context is just a manual for agents; if you can make the data model simple and clear enough, it can save them a lot of time and energy (and tokens).

Sebagaimana diketahui, the jobs to be done for a data person in the age of ai don’t really match any of the typical responsibilities of other data team members. I think it is different enough to merit a new title, which I hereby dub the “Data Intelligence Engineer”.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the data intelligence engineer automates the data engineer's work (ingestion) and the analytics engineer's work (transformation and modeling) by creating and conducting software agents. They encode their knowledge of the system into shared context that can be used by other agents to answer questions about the organization. These include things like which fields are joinable but also what someone in the company means when they say “ARR”.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, evals are another big part of their responsibility; these are the system tests that validate that when you ask questions with a known answer, the answer is correct. A good eval suite can give confidence that the types of questions that users ask of the system are going to be answered correctly by the agent. Evals also are a way of knowing when something breaks.

Berdasarkan laporan, the goal of a data intelligence engineer is to enable self-service. That is, anyone in the organization should be able to open Claude or ChatGPT or another agent and answer questions correctly about the business, use that to build apps and visualizations, and in the end, make high quality decisions with the benefit of data. When the Data Intelligence Engineer does the job well, everyone who asks a question gets the experience of working with the smartest analyst in the company.

Diungkapkan bahwa day to day, that means they are going to be building frameworks, building the data model, curating the context, preventing things from getting broken, fixing them when they break anyway, running evals, and being accountable for the surfaces the business depends on. We wrote the whole thing up as a job description, because we believe this is the way things are going and it's time to give it a name.

Berdasarkan laporan, if you're a data engineer, an analytics engineer, or an analyst, you'll recognize parts of this. Those roles were already blending into each other, and morphing into something new. This is a role you play, whatever your title says.

Sebagaimana diketahui, it's a fair question. I’ll leave it up to the reader whether they think that stupendously silly mistakes are something new or not. More people building means more chances to be wrong, with less oversight. There is the possibility of making stupendously silly mistakes by acting on the wrong data. The scary thing is that now the data team can be held responsible for them.

Berdasarkan laporan, there are two things that help. The person who lives with the churn number notices when it looks off. The first is that the closer you are to the problem, the better you can spot errors. From experience, we’ve found that results actually improve because the business owner has a fingertip feel on their area; they know when something isn’t right, and can often spot problems even in the source data.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the other thing that helps is that you don’t need to watch everything with the same level of vigilance. Another quotable quote from our friend Nick is that “Agents need supervision proportional to their blast radius. " That is, if something is going to be used for important reporting or decisions, you should pay a lot of attention. If you’re trying to figure out how many sandwiches to order for lunch, it probably isn’t going to cause a riot if you order too many with habanero mustard because Claude imagines it is extra tasty.

Berdasarkan laporan, you can think of this in three circles of supervision. Anyone can build, they hopefully build on a reasonable foundation, but the data team keeps their hands off. This contains key metrics for the organization, things that are important to get right. The data team should make sure that these are high quality and predictable at all times. Finally there is the inner circle, the Core. When something breaks in these dashboards, the data team should make a best effort to fix them. The outer is the Wild West. The next tier is the Curated set. This is a set of dashboards, visualizations, apps, and metrics that is important to the business in some form or another. The board number lives in the Core.

Diungkapkan bahwa on motherduck, we build mechanisms to empower your ai enabled data team. We call the data visualizations that can be created by agents “Dives”. Context lives in Guides, which are markdown files describing your data model and your business. Every person and agent gets its own Duckling, a dedicated DuckDB instance. Flights are vibe-codable pipelines that can pull data into your warehouse and translate it into a sane model. A Guide starts out as private, but an admin can promote it to apply to the whole organization so that every person and agent works from the same definitions. All of these are reachable from SQL, so one person or agent can work a problem across ingestion, transformation, context, and apps without a handoff between tools.

Sebagaimana diketahui, we're in a chaotic moment. Chaos breeds the biggest opportunities, and the tools hand you some real super-powers if you're willing to pick them up. We're all learning how to do this together.

Diungkapkan bahwa the data team isn't going anywhere. Someone still has to own the data model, curate the context, keep things working, and answer for the results. No-backlog-Nick has more to do than ever, and but the job is changing and not going back.

So who's doing this at your company, and what do you call them?.

PS - if you want to see my slides from the talk, check out the Dive Gallery.

#252. AMD plans to invest in PsiQuantum as they team up on quantum computers

📅 12 Nov 2026

AMD plans to invest in PsiQuantum as they team up on quantum computers

Tanggal: 12 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://thenextweb.com/news/psiquantum-amd-partnership-equity-investment-quantum

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the two will co-design the computing systems that run large quantum computers, starting with drug discovery. Neither PsiQuantum nor AMD has said how much AMD will invest.

Berdasarkan laporan, amd plans to invest in psiquantum, as the two expand their partnership on quantum computing. The companies announced the deal on 12 November. Neither said how much AMD will invest.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, psiquantum already uses amd’s versal fpgas to develop its fault-tolerant quantum computer. The new deal adds AMD’s Instinct GPUs, EPYC CPUs and ROCm software. These are chips that engineers can reprogram after manufacture. PsiQuantum brings its silicon photonics, which uses light to compute.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the two will co-design the infrastructure that runs large quantum computers. They will also build hybrid software that mixes quantum, high-performance and AI computing. They expect the result to be the world’s most powerful hybrid computing fabric, the companies said.

“Quantum computing will enable solving problems in healthcare, materials, energy, finance, and other domains that are out of reach today, working in concert with AI and high-performance computing,” said Victor Peng, PsiQuantum’s chief executive.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, working with amd, psiquantum researchers have tuned prism, a machine-learning decoder, to run fast on programmable chips. Its job is to correct errors in real time in large photonic quantum computers. The companies linked a research paper on the work.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the first focus will be drug discovery. PsiQuantum runs its chemistry methods on AMD GPUs. The companies say this has already produced breakthrough results in simulations of covalent inhibitors, molecules relevant to cancer drug research.

The work fits the US Department of Energy’s Quantum Genesis list of science problems for quantum computers, the companies said.

“We see that same opportunity with quantum computing, where leadership in classical computing is essential to building systems at scale,” said Mark Papermaster, AMD’s chief technology officer.

Berdasarkan laporan, psiquantum is the anchor tenant of the illinois quantum and microelectronics park in chicago. The two companies will look at working together there too. They plan to share more at the SC26 supercomputing conference in Chicago, from 15 to 20 November.

Berdasarkan laporan, in october, the pentagon offered psiquantum a conditional $150m loan. The same month, AMD agreed to invest $1bn in Meta. Last week, it reported a record quarter.

#253. Use Your Year-End Review to Reach for a Promotion

📅 05 Nov 2026

Use Your Year-End Review to Reach for a Promotion

Tanggal: 05 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://spectrum.ieee.org/how-to-get-a-promotion

Maintaining a document of your successes throughout the year gives you a starting point.

Brian Jenney is the owner of Parsity, a program that helps engineers through hands-on training.

Sebagaimana diketahui, this article is crossposted from ieee spectrum’s careers newsletter. Sign up now to get insider tips, expert advice, and practical strategies, written in partnership with tech career development company Parsity and delivered to your inbox for free!.

Diungkapkan bahwa when i landed my first job as a software engineer, i had a simple plan: work hard and somebody would notice. Eventually a manager would tap me on the shoulder and hand me a promotion (probably with a nice little speech).

That plan stalled my career for about five years.

Berdasarkan laporan, i switched jobs twice, kept my head down, read a stack of programming books, and sometimes pulled 12-hour days. I was never promoted. At my third job, out of frustration, I started interviewing at other companies and almost immediately got an offer for a senior engineer role.

Diungkapkan bahwa so i went back to my job and quit. I liked my manager and the people I worked with, and they came back with a counteroffer. My team was blindsided. Then someone from HR asked me, “Why didn’t you just ask us?”.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, i took the counteroffer and stayed. Three jobs in, I finally got promoted, and all it took was asking (in the most dramatic way possible).

Today, I would take a different approach.

Diungkapkan bahwa year-end review discussions are a great time to push for a promotion. But at most companies, raises and promotions are largely settled before the formal review conversation happens. If the year-end review is the first time your manager hears you want a promotion, you’re usually too late.

Now is a great time to start the conversation.

Diungkapkan bahwa engineers tend to believe good work speaks for itself. Your manager is juggling a team, a roadmap, and their own boss. It rarely does. They see a fraction of what you do, and the work they don’t see might as well not exist when raises get decided.

Sebagaimana diketahui, perception is reality, so you have to shape it. That means learning to brag a little.

Sebagaimana diketahui, engineers tend to write things like “migrated the billing service. ” A better entry reads “migrated the billing service, which cut failed payments by 30 percent and unblocked the Q3 pricing launch. ” If there’s no number, name who benefited and how.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the document does two jobs. It gives you ammunition when you make your case, and it gives your manager something to ctrl + c then ctrl + v when they argue for you in meetings you’ll never attend.

Sebagaimana diketahui, bragging builds the case. Asking forces action.

If your goal is a promotion or a raise, you might ask: “What would it take for me to get to [the next level] in the next year?”.

Berdasarkan laporan, a good manager will give you an outline that can turn into a plan. (Managers change jobs too. Push for specifics until you have deliverables you can work toward, then send a short recap email so the plan exists somewhere besides your manager’s memory. ).

Sometimes the answer will still be “not this year,” and the reason may have nothing to do with you.

Budgets get frozen, promotion slots get capped, and decisions get made above your manager’s head where even a manager who wants to help can’t.

Diungkapkan bahwa don’t read too much into that. But be honest with yourself, too. Most of the time, a no means there’s something you aren’t doing yet. Find out what it is instead of guessing for five years like I did.

Sebagaimana diketahui, asking costs you one slightly awkward conversation. Sitting back and waiting to be noticed can cost you years.

#256. Bitter Christmas review: Pedro Almodóvar returns with a cerebral, semi-autobiographical drama

Tanggal: 13 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://mashable.com/entertainment/bitter-christmas-review

Sebagaimana diketahui, storied spanish filmmaker pedro almodóvar has built his career on melodramas rich in sex and agony. However, in 2019, he got more personal with Pain and Glory, a semi-autobiographical drama in which Antonio Banderas plays a thinly veiled version of the director as he looks back on his work and life, anxious to move forward with a new project. His latest, Bitter Christmas, serves as a sister film, echoing not only the semi-autobiographical element but also by casting a dashing actor in the role of an aging Almodóvar.

Diungkapkan bahwa leonardo sbaraglia stars as raúl, a filmmaker who's hungry for inspiration for a new screenplay. There, a once-revered art-house filmmaker named Elsa (Bárbara Lennie) seeks to move away from directing commercials and return to screenwriting. In his corner are his much younger partner, Santi (Quim Gutiérrez), and his longtime manager, Mónica (Aitana Sánchez-Gijón). However, Bitter Christmas gets self-reflexive as Raúl's story is interwoven with that in his screenplay. Aside from their similar creative quest, both also have May-December romances with younger men, and both find inspiration for their new project in the tragedy that befalls a friend.

Diungkapkan bahwa in two layers, almodóvar explores what it means to be an artist who may well cannibalize the stories of his loved ones for his art. But he doesn't lose sight of what it means to see your heartache treated as fertilizer to grow that art. In both Raúl's story and Elsa's, the writers are confronted by a female friend is radiantly furious at having her life treated as source material without consent.

So, how do these parallel stories play out?.

Diungkapkan bahwa almodóvar, who wrote and directs bitter christmas, leaps back and forth between raúl and elsa, whose arcs play out in 2025 and 2004, respectively. Despite the decades between them, these worlds are visually similar, alive with the vivid color palettes that are part of Almodóvar's signature style.

Berdasarkan laporan, his characters are beautiful, always, and favor bold hues of red, magenta, gold, and amber. The production design around them is rich with the texture of lives lived: a book shelf thoughtfully organized but clearly oft-visited, a lamp shedding light on simple but elegant illustrations, a strip club for women that's a mix of chic and sleazy. Across both stories, we're invited to understand these people and their alter egos through such tender details.

Berdasarkan laporan, the ensemble cast strides into this world as if it is truly theirs. Determined close-up shots allow for every micro-expression to register, while wide shots remind us of how close these friends and lovers are, and yet how fragile the space between them can be.

Sebagaimana diketahui, sbaraglia is intriguing in the role of almodóvar's first mirror, raúl. Elsa, however, is a more typical Almodóvar figure — a strong-willed woman who won't be bent by the judgment of others. He speaks with passion, intelligence, and a low-burning frustration, which bursts whenever he's challenged. She is robust, defiant, and ruthlessly loyal to her art.

Diungkapkan bahwa by contrast, the boyfriends santi and bonifacio (patrick criado) are defined by their congeniality and sex appeal. But this feels intentional, as if Raúl simplifies his lover Santi into the himbo archetype of Bonifacio. Gutiérrez, playing the older of the two, gets to weave in more nuance than the Golden Retriever boyfriend Criado is given to play. But why? It's in these difference where Bitter Christmas becomes the most exciting for longtime Almodóvar fans.

Is the simplification of Santi meant to convince Raúl that their relationship is not so serious, so if and when it ends, his heartbreak will be lessened by anticipation? Or is the almost puppy-like sweetness and loyalty of Bonifacio meant as a quiet condemnation of Elsa's opportunism, as she treats him with little regard even as he bends over backwards to please her? Basically, are these boy toys not meant to be mocked, but to reflect Almodóvar's own insecurities through their guilelessness?.

However, it's Monica who becomes Bitter Christmas's most compelling character, and I'm not sure if that's intentional or not.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, at first, she seems a supporting character who flutters around the sensitive artist, caring for all the chores, emails, and requests so he won't have to. But no sooner is her dedication defined that she's requesting a "sabbatical. " It's so unusual for this clear workaholic to request time off, much less a lot of time, and with little warning and no explanation, that Raúl is darkly enchanted.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, forged over decades, their professional and personal relationship is impossibly intertwined, so monica soon shares that her dear friend has suffered a horrendous personal loss. ) However, no sooner has she divulged this painful truth than Raúl remolds it for his fiction. She is going to care for her (not terribly unlike Almodóvar's last film, The Room Next Door. Both within his script and in his life, the filmmaker will have to face the friend betrayed in this specific way.

Diungkapkan bahwa when monica sits down with raúl in a garden cafe to lay into him about his selfishness in this creative endeavor, bitter christmas ignites. While much happens in the parallel stories, the energy of Elsa and Raúl feel subdued, as if they are always in their heads looking down on the situation instead of living fully within it. It's possible Almodóvar intended such restraint, but it makes Bitter Christmas feel almost as if the movie is holding its breath, waiting for something profound to hit. That comes when Monica argues for herself, her privacy, and her friend's dignity.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, however, no sooner does bitter christmas open up into something exciting than the film itself ends. There will be no satisfying resolution — perhaps until Almodóvar's next movie.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, at one point in the movie, raúl recognizes that even a minor work from him will be big to his fans. Regarded on its own, this film feels thin. And it seems almost a buffer for those who might critique Bitter Christmas. But Almodóvar devotees might well see it as a Rosetta stone to better understand the revered filmmaker and the whole of his body of work.

Tanggal: 05 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://spectrum.ieee.org/2026-solar-eclipse

With custom-built gear, his team seeks to solve a long-standing solar mystery.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, advanced image-processing software developed by miloslav druckmüller combines scores of individual images, captured during a total solar eclipse and painstakingly calibrated. The techniques reveal fine details in the sun’s corona, which is white in this image. The tiny pink shapes seen along portions of the edge of the blacked-out solar disk are prominences, which are extensions of relatively cool plasma that can jut out hundreds of thousands of kilometers into space.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the sun hangs low over the plains of castile and león, in the north-central region of spain. But from a slope of the mountain Pico Trigaza, it appears that a few puffy white clouds have started to block the sun. That’s vexing.

Sebagaimana diketahui, a group of researchers, some wearing cardboard eclipse glasses, is clustered around sets of portable telescopes and cameras connected to laptops. That’s because the moon began to crawl across it about half an hour ago. All this gear is scattered on tabletops perched on the mountainside. On the computer screens, the sun’s disk looks like a deep orange crescent that is slowly waning. In 25 minutes, it will obscure the sun completely, producing an eerie and wondrous phenomenon—a total solar eclipse.

Diungkapkan bahwa in the late-summer, late-afternoon heat, the researchers watch anxiously as those fluffy clouds linger around the sun. From an abandoned hut on the slope a few meters above, where the researchers have set up camp, one of the grad students emerges and nods toward the cloud formation. “Do you think it will dissolve?” he blurts out.

Sebagaimana diketahui, “it will. ” Miloslav Druckmüller glances calmly at his group of doctoral candidates, now making final checks of the equipment in preparation for totality. Here in Spain, on this 12th day of August, Druckmüller is getting ready for his 19th solar eclipse. He knows from long experience that weather can turn quickly when the moon’s shadow suddenly pushes the temperature down. Plus, there’s no sense in riling up the grad students any more than they already are.

Sebagaimana diketahui, miloslav druckmüller led the design and construction of a unique optical instrument that incorporates eight astrocameras. Each of those spectra, in turn, is associated with a particular ionic species of iron atoms. Because the temperature needed to ionize iron varies depending on the ionic species, analyzing the locations and relative abundance of these ionic species offers valuable insights into the distribution of heat in the corona. Each is equipped with a spectral filter for sensing and recording specific emission spectra from the solar corona. Václav Široký.

Sebagaimana diketahui, during totality, the moon blocks the overwhelming glare of the solar disk, revealing delicate structures in the sun’s outer atmosphere, the corona. Using custom-built telescope systems and image-processing techniques that Druckmüller has spent decades developing, the researchers aim to gain insights into the processes in this enigmatic region that is otherwise hard to study. In addition to imaging the visible coronal light, the team will try to track the dispersal of superhot ions of iron into interplanetary space, which could give rare insights into the pattern of heat emanating from the corona.

And they’ll have 107 seconds to do all that.

Sebagaimana diketahui, druckmüller is a professor of mathematics and image processing at the brno university of technology in the czech republic and a leading figure in the solar wind sherpas, an international team that studies the sun’s corona during total eclipses. In the solar eclipse world, he is nothing short of a legend, albeit a reluctant one.

Berdasarkan laporan, an image from miloslav druckmüller’s first solar-eclipse expedition, to hungary, vividly shows baily’s beads. These elongated white lights along a piece of the left edge of the blacked-out solar disk are caused by beams of sunlight shining through gaps in the irregular lunar surface during the eclipse. The pink shapes are solar prominences, which are jets of plasma extending out into space and held in place by the sun’s intense magnetic field.

Sebagaimana diketahui, he photographed his first solar eclipse in 1999, in what he thought would be a one-off lark. During that eclipse, the moon’s deep shadow missed Druckmüller’s native Czechia by just a few tens of kilometers, so he chased it to Hungary with a 30-year-old Soviet MTO 1,000-millimeter lens. All he remembers from that day is the rush of adrenaline he felt while trying to find the sun in the sky with the lens’s minuscule field of view and keep it in focus for the two minutes of the eclipse.

Sebagaimana diketahui, he insists that he has never enjoyed any of the eclipses he has photographed. There are so many things that can go wrong and you can’t redo it. “In fact, I have never properly seen any of those eclipses. You are just watching the screens, making sure that it’s all doing what it’s supposed to do. ”.

A composite sequence of photographs shows the 12 August 2026 solar eclipse as seen from a slope of the mountain Pico Trigaza in Spain.

Berdasarkan laporan, despite druckmüller’s outward tranquility on this spanish hillside, the stakes are high. Just 45 minutes ago, his group heard from their colleagues in Iceland, where viewing conditions had promised to be better than in Spain. But a vast low-pressure system had clouded the entire sky, leaving all three Iceland teams without a view.

Berdasarkan laporan, on the pico trigaza mountain in spain, two postgraduate researchers used a laser to get a rough, initial alignment for the tracking mount of an optical instrument. The alignment was necessary to precisely compensate for the Earth’s motion.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the corona has been a mystery for centuries. Though dimmer—by a factor of a million—than the sun’s visible surface, the corona is nevertheless extremely hot: about a million degrees Celsius compared to 5,500 degrees on the surface. Because the sun’s nuclear fusion engine churns at the star’s heart, it might seem that temperatures should fall farther from the core.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, to observe the faint corona in visible light, researchers must block the sun’s ferocious glare. But because light bends around the occulter’s edges in an effect called diffraction, it must block an area much larger than that of the solar disk to prevent light from spilling over and ruining the images. Specialized telescopes called coronagraphs do this with an opaque disk called an occulter. But doing so means obstructing the inner part of the corona, which harbors the most important processes that underpin the puzzling phenomena of the sun’s upper atmosphere.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, that’s why total eclipses matter so much to solar physicists. By sheer chance, the moon is exactly the right size and at just the right distance to completely cover the sun during a total solar eclipse. Because the moon is so far away from Earth, the view is not marred by diffraction, and the corona reveals itself nearly all the way down to the sun’s surface.

As astrocameras recorded spectral data about the sun’s corona, a laptop computer [on table, at left] displayed the phase of the eclipse.

Berdasarkan laporan, space probes can image the solar surface in other wavelengths, but those views have limitations, too. Spacecraft such as NASA’s Solar Dynamics Observatory do see the innermost parts of the corona in extreme ultraviolet light, explains Shadia Habbal, a solar physicist at the University of Hawaii and leader of the Solar Wind Sherpas project. “But it cuts off very quickly, so you don’t see its extension into space as well as we can see it in the visible emission lines” during an eclipse. “That’s the biggest advantage,” she says, of solar eclipse photography.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the european proba-3 mission, launched in 2024, simulates total solar eclipses by flying two spacecraft in a formation 150 meters apart with one acting as an occulter and the other as the telescope. The instruments aboard that satellite, however, have limitations compared to the equipment used by the Solar Wind Sherpas team.

Diungkapkan bahwa when druckmüller developed the film from his 1999 eclipse expedition, the photographs didn’t do justice to the event’s eerie beauty. He spent countless evenings applying his expertise in numerical image processing in an attempt to re-create in his photographs the sights he witnessed in that Hungarian corn field.

Sebagaimana diketahui, it took two years, but eventually he succeeded. Where before there were dull views of the blackened lunar disk surrounded by the blunt wisps of the corona, Druckmüller revealed the subtlest details of the magnetic field lines stretching from the sun far into space. As his photographs circulated among solar physicists, invitations to eclipse expeditions began to arrive.

Solar researchers Miloslav Druckmüller and Shadia Habbal have been collaborating for two decades and 15 eclipses.

Berdasarkan laporan, habbal learned about the images from a ph. When Habbal’s team later published the images in a paper, they misattributed them to another researcher. “She really didn’t have a clue. “I wrote her a rather disappointed email and she responded within 10 minutes,” Druckmüller recalls. Druckmüller found out through an astrophysicist friend. student who had seen them at a conference presentation that didn’t credit Druckmüller. D. ”.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the error was corrected, and within weeks, habbal and druckmüller began a collaboration that grew into a friendship. “Milos’s processing brings out details that nobody has seen before, and they tell you a lot about very tiny features in the corona that you don’t see otherwise,” says Habbal.

Berdasarkan laporan, capturing the corona’s delicate structures means finding a way to show its brightest and faintest features in the same image. “But a computer monitor only allows you to display a contrast ratio of one to about 800. “During the solar eclipse, the contrast between the darkest and brightest parts of the corona is enormous, possibly one to a million,” Druckmüller explains. ” (Some modern monitors, particularly OLED ones, can deliver higher contrast ratios. ).

Sebagaimana diketahui, the human eye can adjust to this enormous range of brightness, allowing an observer to see both the bright corona and the faint stars and planets that briefly emerge in the darkened sky. To bring those details together in a photograph, Druckmüller uses custom image-processing algorithms to combine exposures that capture different parts of that range.

Researchers Martin Šebek and Peter Urgoš make fine adjustments to the focus and alignment of the astrocameras on a key optical instrument before the 12 August solar eclipse.

Diungkapkan bahwa to create a single image, druckmüller’s teams need to take 200 individual frames during the eclipse at exposure times ranging from 0. 001 second to two seconds. Dark frames, taken with light blocked from the sensor, help correct for artifacts created by the camera’s image sensor itself. The data must then be calibrated against a vast number of reference images to filter out noise and imperfections. Flat fields, which depict a uniform light background, help correct for defects caused by telescope optics, dust spots, and variations in pixel sensitivity. “It takes the computer more than two days to process one image,” Druckmüller says. Including the calibration data, a single finished image requires about 3,000 input frames.

Berdasarkan laporan, since 2008, teams directed by habbal and druckmüller have traveled to every total solar eclipse, spreading out across multiple locations to hedge against bad weather. For the others, it’s just a short and stressful voyage. About half of the teams return with usable data. For the 12 August eclipse, three groups deployed to Iceland and two to Spain.

Berdasarkan laporan, the teams seek sites close to the center of the band of totality, where the moon blocks the sun for longest. In Spain, the 12 August band of totality cut across the north of the country; the center line of the shadow passed within 11 kilometers of Pico Trigaza, promising Druckmüller and his colleagues a precious 107 seconds of totality.

Diungkapkan bahwa but duration is only part of the calculation. Totality on Pico Trigaza will commence 51 minutes before sunset, with the sun just 8 degrees above the horizon. That low, the rays must pass through a much thicker layer of the atmosphere than when the sun is higher in the sky, increasing the light distortion that complicates photography. At the researchers’ camp on Pico Trigaza, 1,600 meters above sea level, the thinner air should help a bit.

An abandoned hut on the mountain Pico Trigaza in Spain was spruced up so that it could serve as a home base for the research team recording the 12 August solar eclipse.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, “iceland would have been a much better place for us than spain because the sun was higher up, some 25 degrees above the horizon,” druckmüller says wistfully. But Iceland’s notoriously unpredictable weather made Spain an essential backup.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, if you pack a van with thousands of dollars’ worth of cameras and optical gear and then set out on a 2,351-kilometer journey, you shouldn’t be surprised if you finish the trip with a few striking photographs [top]. The sleeping arrangements for the grad students at the Pico Trigaza hut [bottom] were spartan, but the views were first-rate. Top: Martin Šebek; Bottom: Václav Široký.

Berdasarkan laporan, on the mountain, locals have spruced up a rustic, long-unused hut for the researchers, running power cables from a nearby telecommunication outpost and bringing in a water tank. Five Ph. students drove more than 2,000 kilometers from Brno and have spent nearly a week preparing the equipment. They cook on a small propane grill and sleep in sleeping bags on yoga mats. “It’s perfect. “We have plenty of space here to set up our telescopes, beautiful views, and a roof over our heads,” Druckmüller says with a grin. Druckmüller and his wife joined them two days before the eclipse. D. ”.

Diungkapkan bahwa but even the best equipment and a carefully chosen site count for nothing if the clouds roll in. “So much work goes into the preparations and then, if you end up with nothing, you just feel terrible sadness,” says Jana Hoderová, an assistant professor of mathematics at Brno University of Technology and one of Druckmüller’s key collaborators.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, as the moon continues to slide in front of the solar disk, the pesky cumulus cloud that kept everybody on edge begins to dissolve. It’s 10 minutes to totality. The relief is palpable.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the countdown on the computers that control the cameras has begun. The screens are now showing only a tiny orange sliver, and the evening is becoming perceptibly less bright.

Sebagaimana diketahui, twenty astrophotography cameras, most of them drawing power from a car battery that was also buffering the cameras from any grid instabilities, are pointed at the sun. Alongside equipment capturing the corona’s visible light, the team has built an assembly of eight cameras to detect light emitted by various iron ions that arise in the corona.

Diungkapkan bahwa among the optical gear assembled at pico trigaza to capture the 12 august solar eclipse was a unique instrument designed to record the distributions of iron ions in the corona [at left]. Václav Široký.

Sebagaimana diketahui, those instruments looking for iron ions have been put together with resourcefulness and thrift. A colleague of Druckmüller’s laser-cut the aluminum plates holding the carefully aligned lenses in exchange “for two bottles of whisky. The lenses, produced for the defunct camera maker Contax, were bought at steep discounts on eBay. ” The brackets and attachments were 3D-printed at Brno University of Technology. By far the most expensive elements are interference filters that isolate the wavelengths emitted by the iron ions.

Sebagaimana diketahui, around the blackened solar disk rises the magnificent golden halo of the corona. In the hush on the mountainside, it seems that even the birds have gone still.

Sebagaimana diketahui, “that’s something nobody else in the world can do,” druckmüller says with visible satisfaction. The unique technology, codeveloped with Habbal’s Hawaii team, has already enabled researchers to map the distribution of temperatures across the entire corona and to discover previously unseen structures, dubbed “smoke rings,” in the coronal plasma. The photographs also revealed the boundary region where the solar plasma becomes so thin that its ions stop colliding.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the optical assembly designed to record the distributions of iron ions in the corona is outfitted with astrocameras, each of which captures spectra from a different ionic species. To do that, each astrocamera is equipped with a spectral filter whose bandwidth is so narrow—one nanometer—that the filter appears as a mirror. Martin Fornůsek.

Sebagaimana diketahui, “iron is the most abundant of the heavy elements that we see in the solar corona,” says habbal. The larger the loss, the higher the temperature. “And because the corona is so hot, the iron atoms lose electrons and get ionized. ”.

Sebagaimana diketahui, for example, a temperature of around 1. 6 million °C is necessary to produce an iron ion that has lost 12 electrons. 4 million °C is needed to strip an iron atom of 11 electrons. Habbal and her colleagues had long been trying to image those iron ions during solar eclipses. Each of those ions, whether +11 or +12, emits a different wavelength of light, allowing the researchers to map not just temperatures within the corona, but also how those iron ions spread into interplanetary space and distribute heat. But only 1. Once it’s in a particular electrical state, the ion retains its specific ionization, even as it travels outward with the solar wind. But it wasn’t until Druckmüller entered the picture that they were able to develop the gear and the mathematical techniques to do it.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, with just a minute to go to totality, the researchers begin removing protective filters from the lenses. It’s 50 minutes to sunset, and the waning sun has just begun to light up the clouds above the horizon with the first tinge of orange. As totality begins, observers remove their glasses. The hot air cools. Along the edge of the fantastically thin solar crescent, the brilliant orange points known as Baily’s Beads flash and disappear—the last fragments of photospheric light visible through deep lunar valleys. Then, suddenly, the evening begins a rapid and premature descent into darkness. The graduate students remain quietly and intently focused on their gear.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, druckmüller looks up from his camera toward the darkened plains. The sound of camera shutters suddenly fills the air. The sky is ablaze with fiery colors all along the horizon where the deep lunar shadow drops off. Venus burns brilliantly in the southwest, a sharp white pinpoint in the darkened sky. In the hush on the mountainside, it seems that even the birds have gone still. Around the blackened solar disk rises the magnificent golden halo of the corona. Then, as quickly as it fell, the darkness begins to recede, bid farewell with another handful of golden Baily’s Beads.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the crowd erupts in cheers. D. The Ph. students throw themselves at each other and hug like they mean it.

Diungkapkan bahwa “the students did most of the work this time, so i actually allowed myself to really look at it,” druckmüller says. Pico Trigaza may not have been the best for science photography, but from the aesthetic point of view, it was extraordinary. “It was beautiful. ”.

Diungkapkan bahwa the 2026 solar-eclipse team at pico trigaza in spain included [from left] magdalena šrotířová, peter urgoš, martin fornůsek, miloslav druckmüller, václav široký, and martin šebek. Václav Široký.

Diungkapkan bahwa but for druckmüller, this is just the beginning. While other eclipse chasers will race to release their images, he will take his time. He expects to publish the first visible-light images of the corona in about two weeks. Processing the iron-ion images, and uncovering whatever insights they may hold, will take months—maybe even a whole year.

“Probably until the next eclipse in 2027” in North Africa, Druckmüller says.

Who knows? Maybe he’ll even enjoy that one, too.

Diungkapkan bahwa tereza pultarova is a london-based journalist specializing in aerospace and defense technologies. She is a native of the Czech Republic.

I enjoyed this piece very, very much, and I truly hope this team continues its work.

Sebagaimana diketahui, those are some pretty impressive photos! it also seems like the iron ion filtering is pretty unique. I love seeing cases where people build something they want to see in the world with minimal outside support. Seems like it would be a solid return on more public money to seek out and support scrappy projects like this one.
