#259. Apple HomeView review: An adorable smart display that earns its place

📅 12 Nov 2026

Apple HomeView review: An adorable smart display that earns its place

Tanggal: 12 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://9to5mac.com/2026/11/12/apple-homeview-review-an-adorable-smart-display-that-earns-its-place/

Berdasarkan laporan, apple’s homeview smart display is here. It combines a 7-inch display with Siri AI and an all-new software experience that actually feels really familiar.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, i’ve spent the last ten days living with homeview in my kitchen. Here’s everything you need to know.

Diungkapkan bahwa homeview is an adorable little thing. That’s the best way to describe it. A 7-inch square display sits atop a rounded aluminum speaker base. A small, polished metal arm connects it and lets you tilt the display forward and backward.

Diungkapkan bahwa homeview comes in four colors: starlight, rose pink, silver, and space gray. My review unit is Starlight, and it’s very subtle. I had to double-check the box to make sure it was Starlight, not Silver.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the decision to make the display square is interesting. Between that design and the software experience centered around faces and widgets, HomeView really does feel like an oversized Apple Watch for your home.

Sebagaimana diketahui, i really appreciate the square display. It makes HomeView look less like an iPad propped up on a stand and more like a dedicated, purpose-driven device.

Diungkapkan bahwa in terms of specs, the 7-inch display has a 1088 × 1088 resolution, equating to a pixel density of 220 pixels per inch. Max brightness is 500 nits. 3 nits, which means it can go in a bedroom without being a nuisance. It can also dim all the way to 0. It also has True Tone to match your room’s lighting temperature.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, for the past ten days, my partner and i have been living with homeview on our kitchen counter. I don’t think an iPad-style display would look nearly as intentional. We also don’t have much spare counter space. The square display and aluminum base look great in that setting. If HomeView were any bigger or wider, I’m not sure we’d have room for it.

Diungkapkan bahwa in the lead-up to homeview’s launch, i was skeptical of how usable a 7-inch display would be. In practice, I’ve found this to be (mostly) a non-issue. Apple has done a great job optimizing the interface for the display. Text is readable at a glance from a few feet away, timers are nice and large, and the interface adapts to show more information when you’re closer.

Berdasarkan laporan, sometimes i wish it were bigger. Viewing a recipe requires a bit more scrolling than I would like. It’d be nice to fit a couple more widgets on the Modular face. But those trade-offs are easier to accept when I consider how much I appreciate HomeView’s compact footprint.

Diungkapkan bahwa apple touts that the homeview has a custom-engineered acoustic system. There are two custom full-range drivers in the display, paired with a down-firing woofer and two force-canceling passive radiators in the base.

Diungkapkan bahwa in practice, homeview’s sound quality falls somewhere between the homepod mini and the full-size second-generation homepod. Its sound quality won’t blow you away, but it’s respectable for music and podcast playback. I replaced a full-size original HomePod in my kitchen with it, and while it doesn’t sound quite as good, it makes up for it in other ways … like by having a screen.

Berdasarkan laporan, homeview can serve as an airplay target, too, so you can beam content from your iphone or other apple device right to it. You can also AirPlay from HomeView to other AirPlay targets in your house.

Diungkapkan bahwa homeview doesn’t have any buttons, which is a design decision i’ve found very frustrating on multiple occasions. I wish it had volume buttons, so I could quickly adjust the volume without yelling at Siri or using the touchscreen.

Berdasarkan laporan, homeview’s software borrows heavily from ios and watchos. The interface is built around a system of faces with widgets, very similar to the Apple Watch’s complications system. The process of configuring a face will feel very familiar to Apple Watch and iPhone users.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, you can customize faces by long-pressing on them, which reveals a familiar “customize” screen. Here, you can change the style, color, widgets, and background. You can also add widgets from your nearby iPhone. Apple says that widgets are visible to everyone, but widget content is only visible while your primary device is in the home.

Sebagaimana diketahui, i’ve become particularly fond of the modular face, which lets you place four equally sized square widgets. The Photos face is also a delight, essentially turning the HomeView into a digital picture frame. I think it provides a nice amount of glanceable information without feeling too dense. Support for Shared Albums is especially nice.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, i think apple made the right decision by building the homeview experience around faces rather than a traditional app-focused interface. Most of the time, HomeView is just sitting on your counter or table, and you’re not actively interacting with it. That’s why I’ve gravitated towards the Modular face.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the faces system also means that homeview doesn’t constantly draw your attention. Just like the physical design, it’s there when you need it, but otherwise does a good job blending into the background.

Berdasarkan laporan, swiping down from the left two-thirds of the display activates siri ai, while swiping down from the top right takes you to control center (which annoyingly isn’t customizable). Swiping up from the bottom takes you to the Home Screen, where you’ll find a grid of apps and spots to add even more widgets.

Sebagaimana diketahui, there is no app store on homeview. Instead, there’s a collection of built-in Apple apps paired with audio and video apps through its CarPlay-based app system. Here are the Apple apps that are available on HomeView:.

Sebagaimana diketahui, i’m hopeful that apple builds on the app story for homeview sooner rather than later. I don’t think HomeView needs its own App Store, but I do think it needs more apps. This includes more Apple apps and additional third-party apps.

Berdasarkan laporan, i desperately want apple to add the notes app to homeview. My wife and I keep recipes and dinner ideas in Notes, so it would be great to have that experience available on HomeView. It feels like an odd omission right now. HomeView also needs a dedicated Photos app.

Diungkapkan bahwa i think the idea of basing the system on carplay makes sense. There are a lot of similarities in UI between how an app should work in the car and on a smart display. The Audible app, for example, translates really well from CarPlay to HomeView, as does Spotify.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, however, the list of supported categories for carplay is a lot broader than the audio and video category apple is allowing on homeview right now. There are signs this could expand very soon, and I’m hopeful that’s the case.

Diungkapkan bahwa one of the cleverest aspects of homeview is its recipe experience. When you open a recipe in Safari, HomeView gives you the option to convert it into a dedicated cooking interface. You can browse for recipes directly on HomeView, or find one on your iPhone and simply hold it in front of HomeView to hand off the webpage.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, homeview then intelligently detects the actual recipe information and puts it into a streamlined interface. You can view the full ingredient list and measurements, and check off items as you go. The recipe itself is broken down into individual steps. It also intelligently identifies when you need to set a timer and gives you the option to start one directly from the recipe.

Berdasarkan laporan, this is the exact type of feature that’s perfect for homeview, and perfect for a dedicated screen sitting on the kitchen counter. You don’t have to keep reaching for your phone, unlocking it, and finding your place in the recipe.

Berdasarkan laporan, the feature works incredibly well. I tried it with recipes of varying lengths from multiple different websites without any major problems.

Sebagaimana diketahui, there are some limitations, though. It doesn’t solve my frustration with the lack of a dedicated Notes app. Also, as I mentioned earlier, the 7-inch display means there’s more scrolling involved than I’d like. For example, it does struggle if a website splits the recipe into multiple pages. Still, it’s a great example of where this design excels.

Diungkapkan bahwa ultimately, the homeview’s software interface is really well done. Everything feels very smooth. Delightful animations appear throughout the experience, like when notifications or the Siri blob slide in from the top bezel. The software feels familiar because of its similarities to Apple Watch and iPhone, but it’s also clearly purpose-built for the smart display form factor.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, since homeview is meant for everyone in your home, apple had to engineer a multi-user system. HomeView supports up to six people, each with their own personalized Home Screen, widgets, and access to personal information.

Diungkapkan bahwa homeview identifies the different people in your house in two ways: facial recognition and voice recognition. The goal is to recognize who’s interacting with it and customize the experience for that person. So, when I approach HomeView, it can recognize my face and display my calendar, reminders, and messages. When my wife approaches, it can recognize her instead and show her information.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the facial recognition implementation is particularly interesting. HomeView doesn’t have Face ID. Instead, it uses its built-in camera for facial recognition. During setup, you’re asked to turn your head left, right, up, and down so HomeView can capture your face from different angles.

Sebagaimana diketahui, in practice, homeview’s facial recognition works surprisingly well. I was skeptical, but it’s done a good job of identifying both my wife and me. If I approach it and try to open the Messages app while it’s on my wife’s profile, I get a message saying it can’t verify my identity. If I repeatedly try, HomeView disables facial recognition, requiring my wife to authenticate using her iPhone before she can access her personal information again.

Diungkapkan bahwa in addition to protecting personal data, homeview does a decent job of automatically switching between profiles. There’s occasionally a delay of a few seconds, so I wish it were slightly faster.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, homeview is powered by apple’s a18 chip, which enables support for siri ai. However, Siri AI works a bit differently on HomeView than on other Apple devices.

Berdasarkan laporan, homeview can answer world knowledge questions on its own, without relying on a paired iphone or ipad. The difference, of course, is that Siri AI answers these questions well, unlike old Siri. This is basically the trivia questions we’ve all grown accustomed to shouting at voice assistants over the years. On HomeView, the experience is even better because you can visually see the response on the display, often accompanied by images or other visual information.

Diungkapkan bahwa the second aspect of siri ai is personal context. To use Siri AI’s personal context on HomeView, you need an Apple Intelligence-enabled iPhone or iPad in your house.

Apple says that the device must have been recently unlocked and be connected to the same Wi-Fi network as HomeView.

In my testing over the last 10 days, I’ve never run into a situation where HomeView was unable to answer a Siri AI query because my iPhone was unavailable.

Berdasarkan laporan, i’ve found siri ai to be quite impressive and useful since it debuted in september. It’s a huge upgrade over old Siri. Broadly speaking, that experience extends to HomeView.

Diungkapkan bahwa many of the same personal context questions i ask on my iphone can now be answered by homeview. And because of HomeView’s form factor, it’s more useful when multitasking. Instead of reaching for my iPhone or hoping it’s within earshot, I can just ask HomeView.

Here are a few questions HomeView has answered without a hiccup:.

Berdasarkan laporan, in terms of speed, i’ve found homeview to be slightly slower to answer personal context questions than my iphone duo. It’s not a huge difference, but it’s a few seconds each time. I assume this is because HomeView is basically handing off the request to my iPhone, adding an additional step that requests directly on the iPhone don’t have to do.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, siri ai is not without its faults. There are times on HomeView where it just hangs and never responds, or responds with a generic “Sorry, try again later” message of some sort. HomeView’s primary interaction method is your voice, which makes these types of Siri AI failures even more frustrating.

Berdasarkan laporan, homeview can also serve as the command center for your smart home. It has a dedicated Home app, as well as multiple different Home-focused face options. You can also, of course, use your voice to control HomeKit accessories and scenes through Siri.

Diungkapkan bahwa there’s ultimately nothing particularly remarkable about homeview’s support for smart home control. It offers much of the same functionality as the Home app on your iPhone, but in one central location that everyone in your house can use.

Diungkapkan bahwa there is one limitation: you currently can’t use siri ai on homeview to control secure devices like locks and garage doors, even if the device recognizes you. If they are part of a scene, you can tell Siri AI to set the scene and it works. But you can’t individually control them.

Apple tells Joanna Stern that a software update coming next month will add security accessory support to HomeView’s Siri AI.

Berdasarkan laporan, i wish apple would expand what homeview can do for the smart home. It has a built-in camera, so why can’t I use that camera for motion sensing or as a HomeKit Secure Video camera?.

Diungkapkan bahwa i’ve found the screen most useful for quickly checking the status of accessories, like seeing whether a door is locked or glancing at the doorbell camera. For actually controlling accessories, I still find Siri and automations to be the easiest approach. HomeView hasn’t really changed that, although I do appreciate being able to adjust the thermostat right from the kitchen counter.

Berdasarkan laporan, homeview costs $299, which is about $100 less than i expected based on rumors. That’s a surprisingly reasonable price, I think. The key, of course, is whether you’ll actually use it day to day.

Diungkapkan bahwa when you get a new iphone, you already have a pretty good idea of what you’ll use it for and where it fits into your life. New features might change how you use it, but the core functionality stays the same.

Berdasarkan laporan, homeview is very different. It’s a very, very cute little thing. At first, it sits on your counter and is nice to look at. But it takes time to discover how and why it fits into your life.

Sebagaimana diketahui, at first, i had no idea whether i’d actually use homeview. But in the ten days it’s been sitting on my counter, it’s grown on me quite a bit. It’s gone from being a nice-to-have to something I use and rely on for multiple tasks each day.

Berdasarkan laporan, it’s also been interesting watching my partner interact with it. Her first impression was essentially, “It’s cute, but I don’t know what I’ll use it for. ” Over the last week, however, she’s remarked multiple times how much she likes it.

Whether it’s personal context-focused Siri AI interactions, simply being able to glance and see how long is left on a timer, watching the animated album art as a song plays, or the joy of the Photos face, HomeView has earned its spot.

Sebagaimana diketahui, in fact, i moved homeview from our kitchen to my office for a day to test a few features and settings in more depth. While cooking dinner that night, we both found ourselves shouting Siri commands into the air and glancing at the empty spot on the counter, only to remember it wasn’t there.

Sebagaimana diketahui, i think that’s the best example of what makes homeview special. You don’t have to be a HomeKit enthusiast or spend hours tinkering with smart home automations to appreciate it. It’s a device everyone in the house can find their own uses for, and it becomes more useful the longer it’s part of your routine.

Diungkapkan bahwa revenue rose to $980. 8m and beat estimates, but delayed third-party sites push some sales into 2027. Nebius now plans to spend up to $45bn next year.

Arkady Volozh, founder and CEO of Nebius.

Berdasarkan laporan, nebius shares fell 16% on thursday after the amsterdam-based ai cloud company cut its outlook for this year. It also raised its spending plans, CNBC’s Jordan Novet reported. The fall came despite third-quarter revenue that rose 571% from a year earlier, to $980. 8m.

Nebius posted adjusted earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation of $465. Its net loss narrowed to $37. 8m, against a loss of $5. 6m.

Sebagaimana diketahui, nebius now expects 2026 revenue at the low end of its $3bn to $3. 37bn, CNBC reported. 4bn range. Analysts had expected $3. Founder and chief executive Arkady Volozh gave the outlook in his letter to shareholders. For 2027, Nebius expects revenue of $12bn to $13bn.

Diungkapkan bahwa the cut comes from delays at data centre sites that nebius rents from other companies. Some capacity due this year has moved to the first half of 2027. The contracts behind it remain in place, Deborah Sophia reported for Reuters.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, “we have no doubt that this capacity will be sold. Clients are looking for capacity already for 2028, and prices for 2027 are going up. We do not see any risk,” chief financial officer Dado Alonso said, according to Reuters.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, “the demand for ai is real and substantial. Everything else, like building the capacity and financing it, is just a task,” Volozh said on a call with analysts, according to CNBC.

#261. Victorian Psycho review: What if Gothic horror were an eat-the-rich comedy?

📅 13 Nov 2026

Victorian Psycho review: What if Gothic horror were an eat-the-rich comedy?

Tanggal: 13 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://mashable.com/entertainment/victorian-psycho-review

Gothic horror is going from mad to madcap with Victorian Psycho, a horror comedy that follows a murderous governess to her next — and possibly last — appointment.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, maika monroe stars as winifred notty, a governess who is desperate to make a good impression on her new employers, the pound family. At night, strange noises might be heard about their grand house. The family's treasures go missing or are vandalized. Members of the staff vanish without a word. Could it be a ghost or ghoul whose very presence could drive this poor heroine mad? Well, no. The broad strokes of the plotline are tropes of Gothic horror. A seemingly fragile young woman must care for the young, defenseless children of a rich and twisted family. Because from the very start, Victorian Psycho shows us its protagonist is already mad, and also the vicious thing that goes bump in the night.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the title alone gives some clue of the topsy-turvy approach that virginia feito, who wrote the novel and this adapted screenplay, has to the genre. Director Zachary Wigon (Sanctuary) cements this cheeky attitude with an opening scene in which Winifred addresses the audience in voiceover while looking straight into the camera. There's a sense of Fleabag in this distorted direct address to the audience, as Winifred insists she is the sanest person she's ever met.

Diungkapkan bahwa this is just the first red flag, warning that winifred notty is much more than naughty. Soon after, a dismembered human ear tumbles out of her luggage; she regards it with slight irritation. From here, Victorian Psycho blooms into a deliciously bonkers spin on Gothic horror with an eat-the-rich edge.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, on the surface, winifred seems a darling young woman, eager to be accepted into a household that'll appreciate her. She's demure when meeting the servants of the Pound estate, as well as the family themselves. Among them, there is a mightily mustachioed father (Jason Isaacs), a fearsome mother (Ruth Wilson), teen daughter Drusilla (Evie Templeton), and the spoiled little heir to the family fortune, Andrew (Hamnet's Jacobi Jupe).

Want more film and TV news and reviews delivered straight to your inbox? Sign up for Mashable’s Top Stories newsletter or get Mashable push alerts today.

Diungkapkan bahwa but there's a spiky antisocial undercurrent to winifred, especially when she's left alone with the children. Still, few around her could imagine what horrid secrets she's left behind her, and what deranged fantasies fuel her dark heart. She swiftly befriends the children's nurse, Miss Lamb (Thomasin McKenzie), and offers to this wide-eyed waif tales of a ghoul that's prowling the property. She speaks of the wickedness and pain that lie inside all living things, frightening the young Master Andrew, who watches in shock as she bludgeons a fallen deer to death with a rock. For how else to explain the blood all over Winifred's dress?.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, when it comes to winifred's violence, wigon is unblinking in brandishing spurts of blood but knows when to keep certain especially heinous homicides off-camera. This keeps the tone of Victorian Psycho thrillingly zany, despite the grim content.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, as for feito, she seems to pull inspiration from jane austen's brilliantly dummy dialogue for oblivious rich folk. The father bloviates about the value of phrenology, a pseudoscience that proposed personality could be predicted by skull shape. These are caricatures of entitled affluence. The mother punishes a scullery maid by chopping off the girl's long hair after a strand once ended up in her soup.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, like with saltburn, there's a delicious lunacy to watching these careless rich assholes embrace an outsider who's sure to bring them to ruin. Not all of Winifred's targets feel as worthy of her brutal brand of comeuppance. Still, the breathtaking cruelty is part of the fucked-up thrill ride.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the american actress's career has been largely defined by horror since she broke through in 2014 with a supporting role in the gripping thriller the guest and then starred in the std-as-slasher allegory it follows. Though she's done a slew of films since then, horror offerings like Watcher, Longlegs, and The Hand That Rocks The Cradle stand out. Yet here, she's turned from haunted heroines of her filmography and Gothic horror in general to become a compelling monster all her own.

Sebagaimana diketahui, typically, in these types of stories, like crimson peak, the others, or the turning of the screw, the heroine is an innocent with good character and bravery in the face of an inhuman threat. Here, Winifred is that threat, and Monroe makes a meal out of playing the baddie as if she's been starving for the opportunity (though, yes, she's been the villain before).

Sebagaimana diketahui, there's an electrifying mix of menace and mischievousness in her delivery, whether she's flirting with the nurse or threatening a child. However, when Winifred gives over to her dark side, Monroe's performance ratchets into a gnarled physicality of demonic possession, which will likely remind viewers of Lily-Rose Depp's turn in Nosferatu. Her face shifts smoothly from a mask of civility to a reveal of wrath or revulsion. On top of all of this, Monroe offers a sharp humor through unhinged physicality that cuts deep as a shattered tea cup shard through a jugular.

Berdasarkan laporan, in scenes where winifred is spiraling out of control, high-angle cinematography from nico aguilar distorts her proportions, turning this beautiful woman into a warped stranger. Whip pans, rarely used in period pieces, snap from a could-be victim's expression of shock to Winifred's face, and it can feel like a slap to it. But the gnarliest visual choices are when Aguilar gives a point-of-view of objects of violence, like the aforementioned dismembered ear or the rock used to fatally brain the deer. Such choices not only throw an exciting manic energy into Victorian Psycho but also force the audience to feel a part of the action, either to be gobbled up by Winifred's all-consuming darkness or party to it.

Diungkapkan bahwa composer ariel marx embellishes this tone of creepy complicity with a score studded with familiar and strange sounds. Sometimes, there are slippery sounds (maybe a theremin? Or a saw being bowed?) and distorted voices, perhaps the cries of babies. You might hear a plunking piano or stinging strings, common instrumental choices for Gothic horror. These aural collisions of the expected and unexpected reflect how Feito and Wigon build on the bones of Gothic horror, but create something more modern with their mesmerizing murderess.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, in the end, victorian psycho is a hoot, wildly fun, and unapologetically deranged on its surface. Then, just beneath that, Feito, Wigon, and Monroe weave a tapestry of class conflict, sexism, and trauma that urges audiences to probe deeper to understand that while Winifred is a monster, she was not born one. Instead, she was made from a society that regards cruelty as another luxury the ultra-wealthy get to take for granted. Well, that is, until someone reflects it back.

Attendees in Region 4 learn about AI, cybersecurity, and more.

Siva Rama Krishna Varma Bayyavarapu is an IEEE senior member and secretary of the IEEE Computer Society’s Central Indiana Chapter.

To help engineers keep up with emerging technologies such as AI, cloud computing, and sustainable infrastructure, and learn how they can be applied in practice, the IEEE Computer Society’s Central Indiana Chapter recently launched its Tech Talk Series.

Berdasarkan laporan, the live webinar series connects ieee members, undergrad and graduate students, and engineering professionals from ieee region 4 with industry practitioners. The monthly sessions have covered AI governance and security, agentic systems, and related topics. The sessions featured speakers from Apple, software company Tavant, and cybersecurity concern Zscaler.

Upcoming sessions and registration details are available on the IEEE Region 4 virtual events calendar.

Berdasarkan laporan, rather than presenting on emerging technologies only at a conceptual level, speakers discussed the design decisions behind specific tools and systems, how the systems are structured, and implementation challenges. They also shared lessons learned from using the tools in their daily work.

Sessions also include technical walkthroughs and practical examples.

The live format allows attendees to discuss and compare their approaches when evaluating and implementing new technologies with those used by other organizations.

The organizers chose to make the series virtual so that chapter members and other attendees could participate in technical discussions with engineers from major technology companies and eliminate the need to travel.

For young professionals, the sessions connect what they’ve learned in a classroom with the realities of the workplace.

Technical programs such as the Tech Talk Series give professionals and students access to expertise, help create connections across career levels, and make important engineering discussions available to a broader community.

Sebagaimana diketahui, attendees learn how practitioners approach projects such as system architecture, reliability, security, governance, and product delivery. For experienced professionals, the talks offer a forum to examine new ways of designing, securing, and operating software systems, and compare technical approaches. They can ask questions relevant to systems being evaluated or deployed within their organization.

The most recent webinar, Feeding and Fencing AI Agents: Engineering Governed Agentic Systems on Real-Time Data, featured Gajendra Babu Thokala, a senior engineering leader at Apple in Seattle.

The IEEE senior member explained how teams can move beyond adding isolated AI features to applications and instead build governed AI-agent systems that use real-time business data to complete multistep business workflows.

Diungkapkan bahwa another recent session, building ai native products: a playbook for agentic systems, explored how products built around ai agents differ from traditional software. It also covered how agentic systems can help users complete multistep tasks and workflows. IEEE Senior Member Sandeep Shivam, a product and technology leader at Tavant in Dallas, led the webinar.

Those two sessions illustrate the series’ purpose: helping participants understand what a technology can do and what is required to use it responsibly.

Sebagaimana diketahui, future sessions are being planned on areas including enterprise ai, software reliability, and responsible ai usage. In addition to speakers from technology companies, the chapter also plans to invite speakers from startups, universities, and research organizations.

Upcoming sessions are expected to cover cloud platforms, enterprise integrations, and the responsible development of AI systems.

Technical programs such as the Tech Talk Series give professionals and students access to expertise, help create connections across career levels, and make important engineering discussions available to a broader community.

Undergraduate and graduate students are invited to participate to gain exposure to technical decision-making and challenges encountered in professional engineering environments.

#264. Apple TV 4K review: The best streamer comes at a cost

📅 12 Nov 2026

Apple TV 4K review: The best streamer comes at a cost

Tanggal: 12 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://9to5mac.com/2026/11/12/apple-tv-4k-review-the-best-streamer-comes-at-a-cost/

Berdasarkan laporan, it’s been four years since apple last updated the apple tv 4k, but a new version is here. There’s Siri AI support, a faster chip, an improved remote, and more.

Here’s everything that’s changed, what’s better, and whether the new Apple TV 4K justifies its new $299 price.

Berdasarkan laporan, the apple tv 4k’s overall design is largely unchanged. It’s still the same familiar black box that sits underneath your television. The only visual change is that the front status light has moved from the right side to the center.

Inside, Apple has upgraded the A15 Bionic to the A19 chip, touting 50% faster CPU performance and twice the GPU performance.

Diungkapkan bahwa those are great improvements on paper. In practice, I’m not doing anything on my Apple TV that really stresses the performance. Compared to my third-generation Apple TV 4K, I’ve occasionally noticed slightly smoother animations and faster performance in apps that handle more processing locally, like Infuse.

Diungkapkan bahwa i think the biggest advantage of the a19 chip is future-proofing. People tend to buy and keep these devices for years. In fact, I’m still using a first-generation Apple TV 4K from 2017 in my bedroom, and it still works just fine nearly a decade later. The A19 gives the new Apple TV plenty of performance headroom for future tvOS updates and more demanding apps, even if those advantages aren’t particularly noticeable today.

Diungkapkan bahwa the siri remote looks the same as before, but it now supports precision finding in the find my app, making it easier to track down when misplaced. You can also play a sound on the remote to help locate it. I lose my Siri Remote all the time, so this honestly might be the change I’ve noticed and appreciated most in my 10 days testing the new Apple TV.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, it’s worth noting apple also sells the new siri remote separately for $59, and it’s compatible with every previous apple tv 4k generation. You do, however, need a newer iPhone model to use Precision Finding.

Diungkapkan bahwa one of the more interesting new features is support for a four-homepod surround sound system. You need four HomePod (2nd generation) or HomePod mini 2 speakers, arranged in matching pairs at the front and rear of the room. Apple TV automatically calibrates the speakers based on their positions in the room.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, for context, i typically use my apple tv with a stereo pair of full-size homepod (2nd generation) speakers. I’ve spent some time testing the new four-speaker surround sound setup by adding a pair of HomePod mini 2 speakers.

Diungkapkan bahwa my house’s layout isn’t particularly well-suited for a traditional surround sound setup, but to my admittedly untrained ears, this sounds great. I can’t speak to how it compares to a dedicated surround sound system, but I appreciate Apple continuing to expand what’s possible with HomePods and Apple TV.

Sebagaimana diketahui, one of the biggest changes with the new apple tv 4k is the addition of three far-field microphones. This means you can now interact with Siri without picking up the Siri Remote. In conjunction with this, Siri AI is also coming to Apple TV.

Berdasarkan laporan, siri ai brings the same broad world knowledge and personal-context capabilities you’ve experienced on iphone and homeview, but adapts them to finding and watching content on your television. Siri AI on Apple TV requires the owner of your Apple Home setup to have an Apple Intelligence-enabled iPhone or iPad.

Personal context requests also require a paired compatible device connected to the same Wi-Fi network as Apple TV.

What was that TV show Lily recommended a few weeks ago?.

What are some baseball movies I might like?.

What did the vet say after Blake’s vet appointment?.

Berdasarkan laporan, for each example, tvos responded with a dedicated interface on apple tv, showing the answer along with poster art, cast information, and more. It also offers built-in contextual suggestions when you ask for recommendations, so you can refine the results further.

Sebagaimana diketahui, you can also ask siri contextual questions about the show or movie you’re watching. This includes things like “where was this show filmed?” and “when is the next season coming out?”.

Sebagaimana diketahui, i’ve found siri ai’s responses to those contextual questions less accurate. It struggles to accurately identify the show or movie that’s playing, leading to completely inaccurate responses to those types of questions.

Diungkapkan bahwa it’s worth noting that siri ai is also coming to the second-generation apple tv 4k from 2021 and the third-generation model from 2022. The far-field microphones are what’s exclusive to the new hardware. This lets you shout Siri commands into the air without talking directly into the Siri Remote.

Sebagaimana diketahui, in my testing, hands-free siri works relatively well, and it’s convenient to control apple tv without reaching for the remote. It does a good job at picking up commands.

Sebagaimana diketahui, i can’t go any further in this review without talking about the price. The Apple TV 4K (4th generation) costs $299. That’s a huge increase over previous Apple TV models. Here’s a brief history of Apple TV 4K pricing over the years to set the stage:.

Berdasarkan laporan, after apple introduced the $129 apple tv model in october 2022, i started to notice a change. More and more people had Apple TVs when I would visit. Friends and family who had previously bought an Amazon or Roku box, or just used their TV’s built-in software, had purchased an Apple TV.

Diungkapkan bahwa at $299, i worry that type of adoption is going to come to a screeching halt. tvOS is fast, clean, and relatively free of the clutter and advertisements you find on competing platforms. And it’s unfortunate because the Apple TV is so much better than anything else out there. The Siri Remote is excellent, and the integration with the rest of Apple’s ecosystem is hard to beat.

Sebagaimana diketahui, i could justify the $299 price for the apple tv 4k (4th generation) if it were just one option available in a broader lineup. In fact, this is the first Apple TV 4K generation to be sold in just one configuration. If there were lower-priced options for people who don’t need all the bells and whistles. That’s not the case, though. There’s no cheaper version with less storage or fewer features.

Sebagaimana diketahui, to apple’s credit, these are devices that can last for years. The fact that I’m still using an Apple TV 4K from 2017 makes the $299 price a tiny bit easier to swallow, but it doesn’t really change my frustration.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, apple seems serious about its new smart home strategy. There’s the HomeView smart display, a new HomePod mini, and the Apple Home Collection family of smart home accessories launching later this year. One of the best ways to get deeper into people’s homes is by controlling how they watch TV. I can’t help but think pricing the Apple TV 4K out of reach for so many people will hinder those ambitions.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, don’t get me wrong, i love the apple tv. If one of them broke, I would reluctantly pay $299 for a new one. I have three of them in my house. Whether you fall into that category is for you to decide. All I can say is that the new Apple TV 4K is the best streamer on the market.

Sebagaimana diketahui, hubspot co-founder brian halligan is back as chief executive, five years after he stepped down. He replaces Yamini Rangan, who also leaves the board, with immediate effect from 12 November, the company announced. HubSpot calls it a “refounding” of the company.

Halligan told Bloomberg’s Brody Ford that he plans to overhaul HubSpot’s product, culture and sales processes.

Diungkapkan bahwa “i don’t want to see hubspot swallowed up by a private equity firm or shrink,” halligan told bloomberg. “I want to rebuild it and reimagine it. ”.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, hubspot’s shares had lost half their value this year through wednesday, on slowing growth and fear of disruption from ai-native tools, bloomberg reported. The company may have focused too much on short-term financial targets rather than great products, Halligan said.

“I don’t know if you looked at the last earnings, but the numbers aren’t great,” he told Bloomberg.

Sebagaimana diketahui, halligan co-founded hubspot in 2005 with dharmesh shah, its chief technology officer, and ran it for 16 years. He led it through its stock market listing to a market value of more than $30bn in 2021, the company said. He has sat on the board since 2005.

Sebagaimana diketahui, burgess is chief financial officer of adobe’s creativity and productivity unit, a $20bn business, and has been at adobe since 2002. She joins HubSpot on 30 November and takes over as CFO in February.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, many software companies face a crisis of confidence about the ai era, bloomberg reported. Adobe named a new CEO in September, and Workday has also changed its leadership. ServiceNow’s shares had their record 25% drop last month.

Sebagaimana diketahui, hubspot said in october it would cut 660 jobs as it pivots to ai. On Thursday, it reaffirmed the guidance for the fourth quarter and full year it gave on 4 November.

Add in two highly collectible promo Pokémon cards — Espeon and Umbreon — alongside special Pikachu ex promo cards and all the premium extras (playmat, card sleeves, deck box, etc. ), and it’s no wonder that there hasn’t been enough supply to meet the demand.

There are two versions to choose from: the green-and-blue Day edition featuring Espeon ex, and the purple-themed Night collection starring Umbreon ex.

Berdasarkan laporan, both contain 29 standard 30th celebration booster packs and one special classic collection pack, alongside a foil pikachu ex promo card and a matching espeon ex or umbreon ex promo. You'll also get a themed playmat, 65 card sleeves, a deck box, a metal Pokémon coin, six damage-counter dice, and a code card for Pokémon TCG Live.

The accessories and promotional artwork vary between editions, but you’re effectively getting the same level of contents with either box.

With both versions in high demand, there are a few ways to make tracking down an Espeon or Umbreon Ultra-Premium Collection a little easier:.

Sebagaimana diketahui, keep checking the major retailers: walmart, target, best buy, amazon, and gamestop are all worth revisiting throughout the week — as new stock has been constantly reappearing over the last couple of weeks. On the other hand, stock can sell out with little warning, so you’ll need to check regularly.

Diungkapkan bahwa set up stock alerts where available: retailer notifications and independent stock trackers can help you spot fresh inventory without repeatedly refreshing every product page. Best Buy, for instance, even lets you set deal alerts for specific listings.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, compare prices across different sellers: third-party sellers can be a useful way to secure either collection when official stock is unavailable. Just remember to compare their offers against current market prices (available on TCGplayer), as some listings are considerably more expensive than others.

Diungkapkan bahwa check whether you're getting day or night: some retailers list the two versions separately, while gamestop uses combined listings with randomized selections. Make sure you're ordering the right product if you're specifically after Espeon or Umbreon.

Don't overlook in-store availability: Online stock shifts incredibly fast, but checking nearby Target, Best Buy, and GameStop locations could give you another chance to grab a box — as many don’t check physical stores, simply assuming they’ll be automatically sold out, particularly if additional inventory arrives ahead of Black Friday.

It's certainly possible that more Ultra-Premium Collections could come in stock for Black Friday, though no allocations have been confirmed for either collection.

Berdasarkan laporan, with black friday arriving on nov. 27, there's still a little over two weeks for retailers to receive more inventory and, as mentioned, there have been fleeting stock drops across the major Pokemon TCG retailers — even if most of them come via third-party sellers. Keep in mind that due to the demand for the 30th Celebration UPCs, sellers have little incentive to discount listings much below market price (around $360 per Ultra-Premium Collection).

For now, it's worth keeping the retailer pages above close at hand, so you can compare prices for any available stock and decide what’s best for your trading card budget.

#270. Guarding the Gates of Knowledge

📅 01 Nov 2026

Guarding the Gates of Knowledge

Tanggal: 01 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://spectrum.ieee.org/ai-slop-trust-science

Berdasarkan laporan, ai can fake a plausible paper at the push of a button. Can detection tools and peer review keep up?.

Harry Goldstein is Editor in Chief of IEEE Spectrum.

Sebagaimana diketahui, a recent scroll through social media got me thinking about trust. About half my feed was filled with AI slop that astute users would call out as being machine-generated, often to the embarrassment of the rube who unknowingly spread it and sometimes to the delight of the poster who shared it deliberately because they found it amusing or useful for sowing confusion.

Sebagaimana diketahui, remember the good old days of gpt-3 when we could ask the chatbot anything and it would almost instantly and very confidently spit back a plausible but false answer? that’s when the word “hallucination” as applied to ai answers entered the lexicon. That’s the thing about current AI: Trust but verify. Six years and several versions of a few different chatbots later, I still can’t trust the answers I get, even though Claude or Gemini often do useful work for me. And verify you must.

Sebagaimana diketahui, apply that maxim at scale to maintain the integrity of the scientific record and you get an idea of the challenge facing publishers of peer-reviewed scholarship. In “I Used AI to Fake a Scientific Paper,” freelance writer and doctor of applied mathematics Benjamin Skuse tells the story of the human gatekeepers trying to beat back the rising tide of AI slop by attempting to get his own AI-generated papers past IEEE’s defenses.

Sebagaimana diketahui, “he basically hit ‘run experiment’ and ‘write paper. ’ And then he didn’t do a damn thing to it. ” —Eliza Strickland.

Berdasarkan laporan, as features and ai beat editor eliza strickland told me, skuse was surprised at just how effortless it was to generate a paper that was more or less plausible and more or less science. “And then he didn’t do a damn thing to it. He just launched it into the maw of the publishing engine. For one of his experiments, “he basically hit ‘run experiment’ and ‘write paper,’” she said. ”.

Diungkapkan bahwa skuse discovered that the combination of ieee’s human-review processes and research-integrity checker programs are currently keeping pace in what amounts to a cat-and-mouse game against people using free tools. But the more advanced LLMs are no longer making the same dumb mistakes the free versions do. That leaves publishers locked in an arms race between increasingly plausible slop and the systems aimed at detecting it.

Diungkapkan bahwa scholarly publishers aren’t the only ones trying to hold the line against slop. So is that global depository of human-generated knowledge, Wikipedia. For this month’s Five Questions, Strickland interviewed Ellia Lebleu, a founding member of WikiProject AI Cleanup, a volunteer effort to detect and delete AI-generated material from the platform. Lebleu’s team is confronting the same problem as commercial publishers, but with fewer people and fewer tools.

Diungkapkan bahwa “wikipedia is known as a repository of human-generated information, and they want to hold on to that,” says strickland. “Who knows how long they’ll be able to do that. ”.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, if we can’t collectively assume that the scientific record is trustworthy or that basic facts about the world are accurate, then our understanding of what is real unspools into uncertainty. Perhaps that delights quantum scientists and the grifters who thrive in an information environment where there is no shared reality. But that uncertainty ultimately undermines trust in the institutions that exist to curate the corpus of human knowledge and to promote the advancement of science and technology for the benefit of humanity.

Diungkapkan bahwa or maybe in a world where ai is doing the science and writing the papers, it won’t matter whether or not humans trust the outputs. As Strickland put it, “Doesn’t it just feel crazy that we’ll have AI writing for other AIs at some point? We’ll just get left out of the loop. ”.

Harry Goldstein is Editor in Chief of IEEE Spectrum.

Early carmakers decided women wanted cars that were quiet, clean, and easy to start.

Allison Marsh is a professor at the University of South Carolina and the codirector of the Ann Johnson Institute for Science, Technology & Society.

When automobiles were still a novelty, electric cars vied with those powered by steam and internal combustion.

Sebagaimana diketahui, at the turn of the last century, the automobile industry was still new and evolving rapidly. A decade later, that number had increased fivefold. In 1901, the companies produced 7,000 vehicles. In 1898, there were about 50 carmakers in the United States. By 1910, production had reached 181,000.

Berdasarkan laporan, for several decades, electric cars vied with those powered by steam and internal combustion, and nobody was sure which technology would come out on top. Steam-powered vehicles could also become exceedingly hot, depending on the placement of the boiler and the steam piping. Steam had the legacy of locomotive technology behind it but came with a risk of fire. Both gasoline and electric cars faced logistical challenges: How far could you travel without refueling or charging? You could always throw an extra can of gasoline in the back of the car, but charging a battery involved more planning. The infrastructure for long-distance travel was not yet in place.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, before the invention of the electric starter in 1911, gasoline-powered engines had to be started with a hand crank; once running, they were loud and emitted noxious fumes. Fully electric vehicles, by contrast, were easy to start; you just turned on the main battery switch, often with a key, and there was no foul exhaust to deal with.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, electric carmakers looking for a way to differentiate their products decided that these attributes made their vehicles perfect for women. (Electric cars were also marketed to doctors so that they could make house calls in the middle of the night without waking the neighbors. ) General Electric, which made car chargers based on mercury-arc rectifiers, was so captivated by the idea of women driving electric cars that the company created a series of advertisements featuring stylishly dressed women plugging in their cars and posing with their charging stations.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, in ads for its electric car chargers, general electric featured women using the equipment. miSci—Museum of Innovation and Science.

Diungkapkan bahwa a young woman named fannie goodnow was an early ev adopter. She owned a 1908 Bailey Victoria Phaeton, an open two-seater that really did look like a horseless carriage, and she used a GE mercury-arc rectifier to charge it.

Diungkapkan bahwa the mercury-arc rectifier functioned as a diode. In a car charger like the one Fannie Goodnow used, it converted alternating current from the power grid into direct current needed to charge the car’s battery. Coupled with the carbon anodes, the vapor allowed current to flow in only one direction. A small amount of liquid mercury contained in a glass tube would vaporize and glow as electricity passed through it. This unit took about 12 hours to charge a drained battery.

Sebagaimana diketahui, bailey’s first model, the victoria phaeton, used an edison alkaline battery. Unfortunately for Bailey and other carmakers who deployed it, the battery leaked and wouldn’t hold a charge. Edison was forced to go back to the drawing board. Thomas Edison had been working on a lighter, more reliable, and more powerful battery for the auto industry since the 1890s, and announced the achievement with great fanfare in 1903. By 1910, he had a better battery in production, but by then his friend Henry Ford had introduced the Model T, setting the stage for the internal combustion engine to take over the market.

Berdasarkan laporan, while edison toiled to improve his tech, bailey pivoted to a battery from the gould storage battery co. Gould also supplied batteries for railroads, utilities, subways, elevators, and farms. The standard battery had a range of 64 to 80 kilometers; a larger battery with 50 percent more capacity was available for an upcharge. Y. of Depew, N. Goodnow’s Victoria Phaeton used a 30-cell lead-acid battery housed in a wooden box that was suspended under the chassis. With the standard battery, the Victoria Phaeton cost US $2,000 (about $73,000 today, or about the list price of an upscale EV like the Audi Q8 or BMW i5).

Berdasarkan laporan, fannie goodnow’s electric car charger now resides at the heritage museums & gardens in sandwich, mass. Shown here is a 1911 version of that model. But her 1908 Bailey Victoria Phaeton has been lost to history. Sarah Thornington/Heritage Museums & Gardens.

(Modern EV owners can no doubt relate. Berdasarkan laporan, when edison’s improved battery was finally available, bailey began using it in the victoria phaeton and then went on a publicity blitz. Diungkapkan bahwa unable to compete against the rising tide of model ts, s. R. Bailey sold its factory in 1915, having produced about 500 to 600 electric vehicles.

Diungkapkan bahwa although the vehicle fannie goodnow chose turned out to be just a blip in automotive history, i like to imagine her driving about town in a beautiful car that embodied all the quirks of early adoption. Berdasarkan laporan, based on everything above, i shouldnât have any issue with this. And at first, I didnât. It all struck me as a tempest in a (Utah) teapot.

Diungkapkan bahwa house house, an already very successful studio with not insignificant resources, made a real choice to rely on a morally abhorrent software system rather than engage the help of real peopleâwhether in the form of paid contracting or just friendly help. I want to say this not to try to exaggerate the scope of what they did but to make it absolutely clear that there is a real, material dimension to this, even if some want to characterize this issue as a purely abstract test of ritual purity.

Diungkapkan bahwa you may balk at âmorally abhorrent software system,â but bruno dias (the blog post author) is not wrong when he writes âto use llms is to willingly participate in a noxious political project and to use the product of exploitative and morally unacceptable processes. â I wrote about that in âAIâs Chicken Sandwich Problemâ; in short form, LLMs do not exist in a vacuum. As he continues,.

Berdasarkan laporan, iâm not going to try to argue that any and all llm usage is equally bad, but either an ethical boundary exists or it doesnât. There are some ethical faults we generally expect people to not be 100% compliant with, of course, but there are some ethical faults we think itâs reasonable to expect people to never breach without sanction. It is very possible to do things without using an LLM, even things that are hard; and if anything, one of the harms of the âAIâ political project is the propaganda machine dedicated to making you feel stupid and helpless.

And, you know, this is something that concerns me.

Sebagaimana diketahui, i recently wrote, âi think iâd lose something meaningful, something vital, if i couldnât understand the code [that iâve written]âto be able to read it line by line and know what each api call does, why certain choices are better than others, how it all comes together. LLMs and agents appear to âknowâ your codebase inside and out, but they donât actually understand anything other than statistical relationships between words and phrases in specific contexts. â While Iâm not suggesting that everyone who goes whole hog for agentic coding is doomed to lose the ability to understand their own code, thereâs increasing evidence that âde-skillingâ is a real issue, as well as evidence that the more leeway you give coding agents the worse your codebase is likely to get. Anecdotal tales of discovering Claude has written four versions of the same function in different places, finding giant sections of code that never get called, and âbug-findingâ agents that imagine and even create bugs are growing rampant. The LLMs themselves donât even âknowâ theyâre working with code.

Diungkapkan bahwa when i listen to accidental tech podcast and hear arment getting so enthusiastic about coding agents, i admit i have trouble reconciling âi donât like using libraries i havenât writtenâ with âi love having robots write code for meâ. A lot of LLM-contributed code Iâve seen is short, clear fixes and improvements, absurd to point to as poisonous, incomprehensible slop. Sure, itâs absolutely possible for a human to check every bit of LLM-generated code; I have little doubt that the code in Big Walk is code House House fully understands. Reining in your agents flips the complaint in the last paragraph around: the less LLM-generated code you use, the easier that code is to vet.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the larger point here, though, isnât about big walk, or overcast, or how many long-standing minor bugs in macos claude fixed (or how many brand new minor bugs in macos claude may have introduced). Itâs about treating AI-assisted coding as something that must be used now that itâs here, whether we see it as an unalloyed good or as a tool whose benefits outweigh its drawbacks, or even as an unavoidable evil. It is, as Dias writes, very possible to do things without using an LLM, even things that are hard.

Berdasarkan laporan, one could use llms for coding in a limited, intentional way, and the language models we have now are mostly trained on open-source, publicly-available code, making them (arguably) less objectionable than generating images or music or annoying emails pitching vibe-coded markdown viewers. If Claude inadvertently incorporates a meaningful chunk of GPL-licensed code in your non-GPL software, you have a problem. But mostly does heavy lifting in that sentenceâand even if the code is open source, that doesnât mean itâs legal to train on. I suspect this is a problem that already exists in thousands of codebases.

Diungkapkan bahwa we can envision a future that solves the big problems with llm-assisted coding. I suspect any open source license that allows commercial reuse falls into this category, unless one adds an explicit âno AIâ clause. The models run locally, not in data centers that convert electricity and water into money funneled to Elon Musk and Sam Altman; the training corpus only contains code whose license allows training. That future could be right around the corner. But we have to deal with the LLMs we have, not the LLMs we wish for.

Itâs more than a little concerning that otherwise perceptive people donât understand that the same issues that plague those AI-generated posters at their local brewpub apply to everything AI-generated, and everything includes code.

Diungkapkan bahwa iâm not saying you canât use generative ai in the creation of terrific apps; igf award arguments aside, big walk seems to qualify. And the more you delegate to your robot coding assistant, the less you understand. #285. Foundation Models framework

📅 12 Nov 2026

Foundation Models framework

Tanggal: 12 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://developer.apple.com/foundation-models-framework/

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the foundation models framework is the best way to use any large language model in your app. Whether you’re generating a quick summary or creating dynamic agents, the framework has what you need.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the foundation models framework is a native swift api for integrating any large language model into your app — including direct access to the apple foundation models on-device and in private cloud compute. Powerful capabilities like guided generation, tool calling, image understanding, and Dynamic Profiles are built in, so you have what you need to build unique experiences.

Diungkapkan bahwa multimodal prompts let you pass images alongside text so your app can reason about visual content. This opens up new categories of experiences you can build with image understanding — it's as simple as attaching an image to your prompt. The Vision framework is also integrated directly, giving your model purpose-built tools like OCR for precise text extraction and barcode readers for quick code scanning — all on-device.

The Foundation Models framework gives you direct access to the on-device foundation model at the core of Apple Intelligence so you can build experiences that are smart, private, and work without internet connectivity.

Berdasarkan laporan, on-device models are highly useful for many tasks, yet sometimes you need a larger model for a more complex workflow. The Foundation Models framework now extends to server models — like Claude, Gemini, and more — all through the same Swift API, with full support for features like tool calling and guided generation. Any model provider can create a Swift package conforming to the Language Model protocol, a fundamental component of the framework that allows you to pick the right language model for your app.

Sebagaimana diketahui, for those just getting started, developers who are enrolled in the app store small business program and have fewer than two million first-time app store downloads can access the apple foundation models running on private cloud compute with no cloud api cost. * This delivers frontier-level intelligence with unparalleled privacy protections, ensuring that your users' data is not stored or accessible to Apple or anyone else.

Berdasarkan laporan, dynamic profiles are new declarative apis for continuously updating your session's model, tools, and instructions on the fly. Rather than creating a session with a fixed configuration, you define profiles — each with its own model, temperature, reasoning level, and toolset — and swap between them within a single continuous session. The session transcript is shared across every profile switch, so your app gets more contextual intelligence with less prompting. Dynamic Profiles are designed to be adaptable building blocks: use them to build AI agents, skills, or any other high-level abstraction your app needs.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the evaluations framework gives you the ability to test your prompts and validate that your intelligence-powered features work correctly across dynamic conditions, going beyond what unit tests alone can catch. Whether you're iterating on instructions, switching models, or tuning a Dynamic Profile, Evaluations gives you confidence that your app's behavior holds up before you ship.

Berdasarkan laporan, the new fm command line tool in macos 27 lets you streamline scripting, automate model workflows, and accelerate your development without writing a line of app code. You can prototype quickly, giving you a fast path from idea to implementation.

To help you get started with adopting emerging AI patterns, the Foundation Models framework utilities package adds experimental abstractions on top of the framework — including custom skills, context management helpers, and a Chat Completions client that connects to a hosted model of your choice.

The Foundation Models SDK for Python extends the framework into the Python ecosystem, letting you integrate with popular tooling and evaluation packages in Python.

This webinar will present two applications of coupled electromagnetic and thermal modeling in COMSOL Multiphysics: eddy-current thermometry in metal plates and microwave-assisted processing of ceramic-loaded resins. Diungkapkan bahwa a personal ai report, commissioned by qualcomm technologies, built on a survey of more than 12,000 people across key geographies worldwide (the u. S. , U. K. , Germany, India, Brazil, and China) focused on the rise of personal AI in intelligent wearables looks deeply at these developments.

The smartphone is no longer the center of that universe; though it’s still incredibly important, in this personal AI paradigm, the AI is the UI.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, survey respondents are less interested in single devices and are responding more to the idea of connected ecosystems. As people expand their roster of devices, it only makes sense. Instead of relying entirely on a smartphone and a laptop, respondents also have connected technology in their cars, as well as intelligent wearables like smartwatches, smart glasses, hearables, and other wearables like rings, pins, and pendants. Instead, the AI agent that knows the user and works across all of those devices becomes the unifying factor.

In the car, it suggests the best route and briefs them on their meeting agenda. No one device has to do everything; each plays the role it is best suited for, coordinated by a personal AI agent that understands the user’s context and acts only at the user’s direction.

Sebagaimana diketahui, with this in mind, simply adding more hardware to the mix isn’t sufficient. Even though respondents will be open to new form factors, they’ll demand more from their ecosystem of devices. Diungkapkan bahwa artificial intelligence is entering a new phase, one that is deeply personal, continuously present, and seamlessly embedded into the devices we wear every day. Diungkapkan bahwa intelligent wearables comprise much of the hardware of this “ecosystem of you. ” Consumers are interested in ecosystems instead of single devices, and they’re looking for agentic AI capabilities that understand and act on their behalf.

#294. The Unexpected History of 'Black Friday'

📅 12 Nov 2026

The Unexpected History of 'Black Friday'

Tanggal: 12 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://lifehacker.com/the-real-history-of-black-friday?utm_medium=RSS

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, since the 1950s, black friday—once simply known as "the day after thanksgiving"—has grown into a quasi-holiday in the united states marked by steep discounts, ceaseless shopping, and occasional violence. But more recently, Black Friday has also metastasized. It's not a day anymore. (Speaking of which, check out Lifehacker's Black Friday coverage. It's a week, a month, a veritable state of mind. We got all the deals, baby!).

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, while pre-dawn trips to the mall are waning as online shopping grows, in-person shopping on black friday is still a big deal in the u. S. —it’s estimated that around 80 million Americans visited a brick-and-mortar store on Black Friday in 2025. But how did Black Friday come about, and what does it all mean?.

Berdasarkan laporan, “black friday” in the united states originally referred to the start of the panic of 1869, when the collapse of the price of gold devastated the national economy. The phrase gradually caught on. “Black Friday” as a description of the day after Thanksgiving dates back to 1951; the term first appeared in the journal Factory Management and Maintenance, where it referred to the number of employees who skipped work on the day after Thanksgiving. Around the same time, the police in Philadelphia and Rochester started informally using “Black Friday” to describe the traffic and crowds that appeared in their cities as shoppers hit the stores on the day after Thanksgiving. It was picked up by national press in 1975 when the New York Times used "Black Friday" specifically to describe the day after Thanksgiving and the shopping and sales it brings.

Berdasarkan laporan, but even before it had a name, black friday was a thing. By the early 20th century, retailers sponsored Thanksgiving Day parades that traditionally ended with an appearance by Santa Claus, as if to say, “Now it’s time to shop for Christmas. ” By unspoken agreement among retailers, Christmas-themed advertisements rarely appeared before Thanksgiving in our grandparents’ day. The day after Thanksgiving has been known by merchants as the start of the shopping season since the late 1800s. This informal bargain obviously no longer applies.

Berdasarkan laporan, referring to a day as “black” traditionally denotes a period of calamity or tragedy, leading some to suggest different names for the day. In the early 1960s, Philadelphia merchants suggested “Big Friday,” a name which did not catch on, leaving retailers with the weak explanation that the “black” in Black Friday refers to the black ink denoting profits in a ledger. Oft-repeated lore suggests that retailers are "in the red" all year, and only start making an annual profit at the end of the year, but big retail chains generally make money all year long.

Berdasarkan laporan, a more modern issue with the name is that black friday sales now last for days or even weeks, beginning in early to mid-november and bleeding over into the following saturday, sunday, “cyber monday,” tuesday, and beyond, leading people to say things like, “do you want to go black friday shopping this sunday?” so far, alternative names like “five-day frenzy” and “the day i get to trample someone to save $8 on a nespresso” haven’t caught on. But here’s hoping.

Berdasarkan laporan, beginning around 2010, an insatiable thirst for profits led many retailers to push the start of black friday shopping to thursday (aka thanksgiving day). The trend led to widespread backlash, with many Americans appalled that employees were forced to work on Thanksgiving or angry that consumerism was encroaching upon a holiday meant to celebrate colonialism. on Thursday. m. Toys R Us opened that night. By 2011, Walmart was opening its doors at 10 p. Kmart opened Thanksgiving morning. By 2021, most major retailers had relented and elected to remain closed on Thanksgiving.

Diungkapkan bahwa the term “cyber monday” describes the boost in online retail sales on the monday after thanksgiving, sparked by workers returning to the office and getting right to online shopping. 28, 2005, in a Shop. 25 billion online on Cyber Monday 2025, according to Adobe Analytics. Americans spent $14. The term first appeared on Nov. Since its early 2000s birth, Cyber Monday has become the biggest online shopping day of the year. org press release entitled “'Cyber Monday’ Quickly Becoming One of the Biggest Online Shopping Days of the Year," which may be the most influential press release ever written. So is Cyber Monday bigger than Black Friday? Retailers really don't care: Analysts now tend to mash everything into the category of "Black Friday–Cyber Monday" (or even "Cyber Week").

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, if all this naked consumerism makes you a little squeamish, you're not alone. Anti-consumerists have named the day after Thanksgiving “Buy Nothing Day,” which you can celebrate by doing charity work, cutting up your credit cards, or simply not purchasing anything. Pioneered by artist Ted Dave and popularized by Adbusters magazine, the first Buy Nothing Day was celebrated in Canada in 1992.

Diungkapkan bahwa it’s hard to measure the success of the alternative holiday. On the other hand, maybe big retailers are losing millions because someone on Bluesky reminded you not to shop. Both online and brick-and-mortar retail sales have increased sharply since 1992, suggesting Buy Nothing Day’s effect is negligible. Sure.

Sebagaimana diketahui, depending on how you measure it, black friday has resulted in between one and 17 deaths. Jdimytai Damour is the only person killed directly due to a Black Friday sale: The 34-year-old worker was trampled to death by a surging crowd at a Long Island Walmart on Black Friday in 2008. If you include car accidents, shootings, retail worker suicides, and fatal heart attacks, Black Friday’s death toll balloons to 17, with 128 reported injuries.

Black Friday violence has even inspired a horror flick: Eli Roth's 2023 holiday-themed slasher Thanksgiving opens with a hilariously brutal Black Friday riot at a big box store, setting off a chain of events that involve a lot of people being murdered by a dude in a Pilgrim mask.

Diungkapkan bahwa i mean, yeah, of course. Savings from Black Friday shopping are often illusory—big-ticket “doorbuster” items generally sell out quickly, leaving behind goods that are, by and large, priced the same as they would be at any other time of year. Some retailers even mark up products ahead of Black Friday so the discounts look bigger. Critics of Black Friday point out that there are arguably better times to buy a new TV (like the week before the Super Bowl), not to mention plenty of other goods. If you're buying online, your browser history, location, and cart contents can tweak the prices you see on Black Friday, as they can on any other day.

Sebagaimana diketahui, yet despite protest holidays, the unpleasantness of shopping when stores are overcrowded, and the frustration of hunting for bargains that often aren't that great to begin with, black friday stubbornly remains an unofficial holiday, celebrated by over 100 million americans in one way or another. What that says about our country's relationship with capitalism is unclear, but personally, I’m going to continue my own day-after-Thanksgiving tradition of eating pie for breakfast and thinking about going for a walk, but then watching The Quick and the Dead instead. I'm not protesting anything; I just don't need the hassle.
