#297. Systems Thinking Is Vital in the Age of AI

📅 28 Oct 2026

Systems Thinking Is Vital in the Age of AI

Tanggal: 28 Oct 2026 | Sumber: https://spectrum.ieee.org/systems-thinking-vital-in-ai

Machines can automate drudgery but engineers make key decisions.

Sufian Aldogom is an IEEE member, a research affiliate at MIT, and a senior leader at Google in Sunnyvale, Calif.

Diungkapkan bahwa modern engineering projects increasingly combine human judgment with machine capability. The engineer can then bring the results to specialists who understand the parts AI cannot judge on its own, such as whether a design can be built safely, whether it makes sense in a particular setting, or how it might affect its users. An engineer can define a problem, then ask an artificial intelligence tool to search relevant research and technical standards, generate design options, test them in simulation, and compare the results. The final decision about whether and how to move forward remains a human responsibility.

Diungkapkan bahwa ai can help engineers do early project steps that once required several people with different technical skills. The engineer’s role is therefore expanding from performing each technical step to deciding how people, machines, and specialists’ knowledge should work together on the project.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, engineering has always been divided into disciplines, and for good reasons. Electrical, mechanical, civil, software, and other engineering fields require deep knowledge that takes years to develop. AI does not replace that need. It simply changes how easily engineers can explore the parts of a problem that sit outside their own specialty.

Sebagaimana diketahui, consider a software engineer working on a medical device. AI can help the engineer review relevant biomedical research, understand unfamiliar terms, analyze data, and build an early model.

Berdasarkan laporan, that does not make the engineer a physician or biomedical expert. It allows the engineer to ask better questions before working with the experts.

Diungkapkan bahwa the same is true in energy, transportation, manufacturing, and many other fields. A problem might begin as a software issue and then quickly involve hardware, safety measures, economics, human behavior, and regulations.

Engineers do not need to master every field; they need to recognize which expertise the problem requires and bring the right people and tools together.

Berdasarkan laporan, systems thinking thus becomes especially important. It requires looking at the whole problem: understanding how its parts affect one another, identifying constraints and failure points, and making trade-offs.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, ai adds a new element to the process. Engineers must decide not only how the technical parts fit together but also what work to give to AI, what a person must check, when a specialist should make a decision, and when the problem needs to be redefined.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, an engineer’s value is not in knowing everything. It is in knowing how to frame the problem, how to ask the right questions, how to test the answers, and when another expert must lead the project.

Berdasarkan laporan, this aspect is crucial because technical challenges in engineering are seldom static. As new insights emerge, objectives might shift, unseen limitations can surface, and the initial premise might prove flawed. Rather than rigidly following the starting specifications, an effective engineer adapts and refines the scope as a deeper understanding of the system develops.

Thus, engineering extends beyond mastering technical concepts; it is an adaptable, structured approach to navigating evolving challenges.

Diungkapkan bahwa new evidence can change the goal, reveal a hidden constraint, or show that the original hypothesis was wrong. Effective engineers go beyond merely acting on the initial problem statement. They update it as the system becomes better understood.

In that sense, engineering is not only a body of technical knowledge, it is also a disciplined way of thinking about a project.

Berdasarkan laporan, ai can produce convincing answers even when its assumptions are weak. It can summarize research without understanding which evidence is strongest, or optimize a design for the wrong goal. It can generate code that works in one test but fails in another. Such limits make human expertise more important, not less.

Diungkapkan bahwa machines are useful where speed, scale, search, pattern recognition, and data generation matter. People are essential where context, values, responsibility, and judgment matter. The challenge is to decide where each belongs.

Sebagaimana diketahui, an ai system might generate several designs for a medical sensor, for example, and predict how each will perform. A clinician can determine whether the sensor can be realistically used. An engineer can test the predictions and reject designs that violate technical requirements. Patients and practitioners might reveal problems that neither the engineer nor the developer considered. The final solution emerges from combining the perspectives.

The engineer is still a builder and specialist but increasingly also a coordinator of knowledge.

Berdasarkan laporan, an engineer’s value is not in knowing everything. It is in knowing how to frame the problem, how to ask the right questions, how to test the answers, and when another expert must lead the project.

Diungkapkan bahwa the broader form of engineering creates an important role for ieee. Its societies already bring together expertise in various technologies, engineering education, technical standards, and other fields. That makes IEEE well placed to help engineers work across specialties without weakening the value of specialization.

Diungkapkan bahwa ieee could create more communities organized around problems that require expertise from several fields. Examples include trustworthy clinical AI, resilient infrastructure, energy reliability, scientific discovery, and safe autonomous systems. An engineer could begin in a home discipline and then work with specialists from other IEEE communities as a project requires.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, ieee also can help set practical standards for human-machine collaboration. Engineers will need clear guidance on when AI-generated work must be checked, how uncertainty should be documented, when a specialist must make a decision, and who is responsible when a system uses both human judgment and machine output.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, those questions are becoming part of everyday engineering. They should not be left to each company or project manager to answer independently. A professional organization can provide common expectations that follow engineers as they move between jobs, industries, and technical fields.

Berdasarkan laporan, ai does not make engineering disciplines less important; it makes the connections between them easier to use. Systems thinking helps them understand how different parts of a problem fit together. Deep expertise gives engineers the foundation to judge what is sound. AI can extend engineers’ ability to explore, test, and communicate across fields. Human judgment gives the work direction and responsibility.

Sebagaimana diketahui, an engineer is not defined only by a job title or a fixed set of tasks. An engineer is someone trained to understand complex systems, define and redefine problems, bring together the knowledge and tools needed to solve them, test whether solutions work, and take responsibility for the outcome.

That is what it means to be an “unbound” engineer.

The boundaries between specialties become easier to cross, and machines might take on more of the technical work, but the core of engineering remains human: deciding what problem is worth solving, what evidence is good enough, how the pieces fit together, and what to do when the answer is uncertain.

Sufian Aldogom is an IEEE member, a research affiliate at MIT, and a senior leader at Google in Sunnyvale, Calif.

#299. Five Things I Wish I'd Known Before Getting a Foldable Phone

📅 12 Nov 2026

Five Things I Wish I'd Known Before Getting a Foldable Phone

Tanggal: 12 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://lifehacker.com/tech/what-i-wish-i-knew-before-getting-a-foldable-phone?utm_medium=RSS

Diungkapkan bahwa the iphone duo might be the highest profile foldable phone to date, but it’s by no means the first. Personally, I’ve had my eye on the Google variant, the Pixel 11 Pro Fold—and recently I finally took the plunge. I thought I’d done my research to know how different having a foldable phone would be, but I still had a bit to learn. Here are some of the things I wish I’ve learned along the way after making the jump to foldables.

Diungkapkan bahwa one of the most notable aspects of the iphone duo is how wide its screen is, even while closed. And there’s a good reason for that: The larger screen while open has exactly the same 1. 41:1 aspect ratio as the smaller screen while closed. This has a ripple effect on how every app you use looks and feels—and whether you like Apple’s approach is largely a matter of personal preference.

Berdasarkan laporan, compare with my pixel 11 pro fold, which features an extremely tall 2. 17:1 aspect ratio when closed, but a nearly square 1:04:1 aspect ratio when open. On the outer screen, apps are a little less wide than on my old phone, but there’s plenty of space for reading books or articles on the inner screen.

Berdasarkan laporan, i like the tall, thin display personally because it feels easier to reach buttons with my thumb, and the wider display is better for reading. However, this approach can occasionally result in some odd app layouts. Not every app is designed for tablets, especially on Android, and shifting the aspect ratio between the inner and outer display sometimes means re-rendering or even restarting an app entirely to load properly.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the iphone duo has a more consistent aspect ratio and general feel between the inner and outer display, but it comes at the cost of a really wide phone. Neither approach is better or worse on its own, but it might be worth going to a local store to get your hands on the phone you’re thinking about before buying.

Diungkapkan bahwa for years, the screens on most smartphones have been made of increasingly tough and scratch-resistant glass. So tough that you might not even need a screen protector anymore. On a foldable phone, that can be true of the outside display, but it’s very much not when it comes to the inner, foldable display.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, screens might be foldable, but the strong, durable glass that makes your phone so scratch-resistant isn’t. No matter what foldable phone you use, the covering on the inner display will be more flexible, and thus softer. Apple uses a nano-texture polymer film that can be replaced, but the film on most foldable phones cannot. That means if they get damaged or scratched, those marks will be there for the life of your phone.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, if you (like me) haven’t considered a screen protector in a while, it might be time to try one again, at least for the inner display. It’s also worth keeping in mind how rough you plan to be with your phone. Construction sites or factories might not be the best home for a foldable phone you plan to open a lot, but an office job should be a bit safer.

Sebagaimana diketahui, similar to the screen protector issue, cases can be more of a headache. Most rigid cases will come in two pieces, and the piece that covers the outer display can be shockingly minimal—barely more than a frame, for some of the cases I looked at. A poorly made case can be brittle or pop off more easily, so it’s more important to get a high-quality one.

Sebagaimana diketahui, if you like to use your phone case as your wallet, it’s also important to be wary of cases that aren’t specifically designed for your model of phone (and maybe some that are). A lot of wallet cases are built to unfold to reveal your phone’s screen on one side, and your cards and ID on the other. But depending on how your foldable phone unfolds, it could be awkward to reach the inner screen.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the hinge also introduces more spaces for dust and debris to get into your phone. That mainly applies to what can get inside and damage the components inside your phone. Despite the extra moving parts and gaps, most foldable phones still offer the now-standard IP68 dust and water resistance rating. It’s still possible for hair and dirt to get gummed up in any pinchable spaces, so look out for any case that might provide even more nooks for dust to collect in.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, i’ve set up most of my apps how i like them by now, but when i first got my foldable phone, i had to revisit some settings i thought i was done messing with. One of the most notable examples was my ebook apps: I was previously using a single-column, medium-font layout, but it looked ridiculous on the inner display. After switching to a two-column layout, it not only felt more natural, but a lot like reading a regular book.

Diungkapkan bahwa similarly, there were some uses for my calendar app that got a whole lot more useful. I’ve never really been able to use anything other than either the one-day or Schedule view if I want to make out anything, but on the inner screen, I can finally look at my week at a glance. But that meant tweaking some things—like showing reminders, which fit naturally amid my events in Schedule view, but become a cluttered mess when I saw 14 different reminders to take my meds at once in the Week view.

Berdasarkan laporan, most apps do a decent job of automatically adjusting to different screen sizes, but i found a few outliers that i had to figure out myself. As an example, Google Docs would default to a view with extremely tiny text when I first started using it. This is, for some reason, enabled by default when opening a document on the larger inner screen. It took me a bit to figure out that this was due to a “Print layout” toggle in the document’s settings. It can take some time to learn the eccentricities of all your apps, but it’s worth poking around when you can.

I know, it sounds so obvious, right? The outer screen is the one you’ll use most often, so how could you forget about it? But when you unfold the inner screen, the outer one is still useful in some surprising ways that I hadn’t even considered until I went poking around in some of my apps.

Sebagaimana diketahui, one of the most adorable examples is the made you look feature in the pixel’s camera app. When unfolded, you can take a picture using the rear camera and see a preview like normal, while the outer screen shows silly animations to capture the attention of a baby or toddler that you want to look into the camera. Admittedly, this is an older feature, but it’s a clever one. For adults, you can also use the outer display to get a selfie preview while using the rear-facing camera.

Diungkapkan bahwa the outer screen is also just better for some things. YouTube is one of the few apps that has a unique layout designed for a partially folded screen, with the video playing on the tilted-up portion of the screen, and video controls on the bottom portion.

Berdasarkan laporan, however, in my experience, it was a lot nicer to watch a youtube video by just propping up the outer screen by unfolding the phone a bit, like a kickstand. My Pixel even detected when YouTube was in full-screen mode on the outer display and would be more forgiving of unfolding the phone without switching to the inner screen. The phone anticipated I might just want to prop up the smaller screen, which I thought was a nice touch.

#300. Llama.cpp: 6.5x faster prompt processing on Arm with a NEON kernel

📅 13 Nov 2026

Llama.cpp: 6.5x faster prompt processing on Arm with a NEON kernel

Tanggal: 13 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://github.com/hardwiredagent/silicon-forge-arm-neon-study

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, arm neon kernel for llama. cpp tiled K-quant matmul - benchmark study, patch and tools.

Sebagaimana diketahui, llama. The reason is one routine: the "tiled K-quant matmul" added in September 2026 (llama. cpp PR #27851, by jbooth with bartowski) has inner kernels for AVX-512 VNNI, AVX2 and AVX only. cpp reads prompts several times slower on Arm CPUs than on x86 for low-bit quantized models. On Arm, the formats without another kernel (Q3_K, Q2_K and the IQ family) fall back to a path that unpacks the weights again for every dot product.

This repository adds the missing Arm inner kernel (NEON with the dot-product instruction, SDOT) and measures it on three generations of Arm server cores.

Sebagaimana diketahui, prompt-processing speed, tokens per second, before -> after (speedup). 5 1. Qwen2. 5B, 4 threads, 512-token prompt.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, largest measured gain: 6. Generation speed is unchanged. 5x (IQ3_M on Neoverse N1). Formats that already had an Arm kernel (Q4_K_M, Q5_K_M, Q6_K, Q8_0) do not change.

Berdasarkan laporan, full tables, including generation speed and the x86 reference: results. md. Raw llama-bench output: results/bench/.

Diungkapkan bahwa the patch is 164 added lines in two files of llama. cpp v0. 9. 0 (ggml/src/ggml-cpu/tiled/):.

The portable driver, the tile format, the unpackers and the test are upstream's and are unchanged.

Diungkapkan bahwa the same change is also provided as whole files in src/patched/, and as the kernel alone in src/neon_kernel. inc with the script that splices it into pristine v0. 0 files (tools/apply_neon. 9. py).

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, before and after come from the same binary: ggml_cpu_tiled_mm=0 switches the routine off, which is the path stock llama. 9. cpp v0. 0 takes on Arm.

Sebagaimana diketahui, a reality show with a complex history as relates to the traitors, the premise being so similar that it may well have served as an inspiration. Eliminations are done via quiz: The group is grilled on the information they've collected about the mole, and whoever knows the least gets the boot. Here, players participate in collaborative missions in order to build a prize fund. Stream the most recent seasons of The Mole on Netflix.

Berdasarkan laporan, if there were a prize for dramatic title (and set design), you could do a lot worse than this one. In this South Korean reality show, 12 celebrity contestants are challenged to build a prize pot through strategy games. Anyone who finds themselves without a single Piece is out. Sometimes they're collaborative, sometimes entirely competitive, and sometimes a blend, but prizes come in the form of "Pieces" that can be won or lost (and that eventually combine to create their own final puzzle). Pieces can be spent to buy advantages, and also traded, so the show turns on players forming alliances in order to build the prize pot and survive as long as possible. Stream The Devil's Plan on Netflix.

Sebagaimana diketahui, here, a bunch of strangers are holed up in an apartment building, cut off from the outside world—and each other. Players judge the competition based on their interactions, determining the "Influencers" who will get to decide on the eliminations. The show ran for seven seasons on Netflix, and is moving to Hulu for the forthcoming eighth. Players can only interact via a custom app, and, thus, can portray themselves however they want, whether that means being 100% genuine (unlikely!) or creating a whole new persona. Stream The Circle on Hulu.

Sebagaimana diketahui, you show up at a fancy hotel, and someone hands you a suitcase containing one million dollars. If the truth is discovered via a vote, that former millionaire is ousted and the money is concealed in another suitcase until the final contestants are given the opportunity to swap bags with someone who they think has the money. It's yours to keep—as long as you can keep it a secret. In this one, all the contestants get a suitcase, and only one contains the money. Much as with The Traitors, the goal is to figure out who's keeping the secret, with challenges designed to help flush that person out. Easy come, easy go, I guess. Stream Million Dollar Secret on Netflix.

Sebagaimana diketahui, i'm a little more into the normies on traitors myself, but there's no question that a big part of the appeal (for most seasons) is watching reality-show celebs go at it with cash on the line. Sebagaimana diketahui, this is not a reality show, but rather a drama about a reality show that may well slake your thirst for treachery while offering up consequences a bit more dramatic than the bruised egos and hurt feelings of the traitors. At first, the contestants pool their resources so that everyone gets more money—until they learn that people on higher floors are getting more. Diungkapkan bahwa this one plays a bit like the traitors in reverse: a $250,000 prize pot is, right off the bat, allocated to all 11 contestants who get to hang out in a luxurious villa. Challenges along the way force contestants to reveal embarrassing and sometimes ugly truths about themselves that may well put them on the outs with the others. Stream The Trust on Netflix.

Sebagaimana diketahui, blending the big brother-esque social aspects of traitors with survivor's love of the great outdoors, this one drops four teams of four into the alaskan wilderness (moving to panama for season three). In the same way that The Traitors creates a tension between competition and cooperation via its communal prize pot, Outlast sees its contestants forced to maintain relationships whether they like it or not. Diungkapkan bahwa the tasks on traitors aren't typically the most thrilling part of the show, which makes this james bond-branded competition a solid match if you want more complicated and better developed challenges. Diungkapkan bahwa squid game: the challenge would probably be a more reasonable choice for this list—given that it's a proper reality show and not a blood-chilling thriller. A bit like The Traitors if all of Alan's murder schtick were literally true. But I'm sticking with the original drama here since, as perfectly entertaining as that spin-off is, it feels like it misses the point. In the original (surprise smash hit) drama, 454 needy contestants are recruited for a new reality competition in which they're tasked to play rather simple children's games—with deadly consequences that are cheered on by the wealthy financiers who are willing to pay good money to watch both the poors go at each other, as people turn on each other to survive and to win the rather shockingly large prize. Stream Squid Game on Netflix.

Diungkapkan bahwa news of jensen huang’s affair with an alleged asset of china’s ministry of state security was first met with a muted response in silicon valley—including inside nvidia itself. Huang’s resignation, after news of two other alleged romantic relationships with Nvidia staffers, has left both the company and the broader AI industry stunned.

Sebagaimana diketahui, as revelations about huang’s initial affair came out earlier this week, rank-and-file nvidia employees at first pursued business as usual, according to two current and three former employees at the chipmaker, speaking anonymously to protect relationships at the company. They trusted the board to investigate and act accordingly, but few workers thought Huang would actually leave.

Berdasarkan laporan, nvidia’s roughly 60,000 employees are loyal to the point that its global turnover rate is reportedly among the lowest in tech. Workers say they have heard it called having “green in your blood” or being “green-pilled” or on “team green,” referring to the company’s signature color. Huang was the company’s soul and the founder who stuck with it through challenges for 33 years. Employees appreciated that he kept layoffs rare and red tape sparing.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, “in just three days we went from superhero cape to ‘oops, i forgot my pants,’ and nobody’s quite sure how to swallow that,” one employee said. One former employee insisted in Huang’s defense that something “more sinister” must have been in play, and that affairs alone shouldn’t have led to his departure.

Sebagaimana diketahui, huang’s peers in silicon valley echoed that sentiment, remaining vocal in their support of the embattled ceo even after his ouster. “One mistake does not erase a lifetime of leadership and contribution in building NVDA,” venture capitalist Antonio Gracias wrote on X earlier this week, using the company’s ticker symbol.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the new york times reported on wednesday that huang has also had an extramarital affair with a vice president at nvidia, and reuters revealed on thursday a second “intimate relationship” with an employee. Before those alleged affairs became public, multiple industry executives told WIRED that Huang is “irreplaceable” and that his biggest mistake, aside from his relationship with Alice Huang, was admitting the affair in writing to the whole company.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, that appears to still be the prevailing sentiment. “A founder who has spent 30 years building such a unique company so capably has earned the presumption that he should keep leading it,” venture capitalist Sarah Guo wrote on X after Huang resigned, and a few hours before the Reuters report.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, authorities and nvidia’s board have yet to formally accuse huang of wrongdoing in his interactions with the businesswoman and suspected intelligence asset alice huang, and china has denied that she’s a spy. President Donald Trump said on Tuesday that the FBI “is looking into it. ” Nvidia’s board has stated that it doesn’t believe Huang compromised any secrets, but it has hired the law firm Wachtell Lipton to investigate.

Add to all that, some corners of Nvidia had already been whispering about the relationship with Alice Huang; one venture capitalist who declined to be named recalled a recent dinner where an Nvidia executive claimed there had been rumors about Jensen’s romantic relationship with a young Asian woman.

Berdasarkan laporan, on monday, the venture capitalist had estimated a “less than 10 percent” chance huang would lose his job at the top of the world’s most valuable company. “People are going to hate him for three months, and forget this ever happened. “The wind’s going to blow over on this,” they said. ”.

The big anxiety in Silicon Valley remains the possibility that instability at Nvidia will burst an AI bubble, but analysts aren’t so sure.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the chief executive of one ai company, who spoke on condition of anonymity so as not to affect business relationships, says nvidia’s recent bankrolling of ai startups and even buying companies such as model-hosting provider hugging face has helped prop up the need for chips. A “new professional CEO won’t do any of that,” meaning “systemic risk for the AI trade and AI bubble increases substantially,” the entrepreneur says.

Berdasarkan laporan, between bubble talk and huang rumors, nvidia shares in recent days have sunk to their lowest point in more than a year. Nvidia reports its latest quarterly earnings next week.

Inside Nvidia, meetings, projects, and the company’s aggressive culture are rapidly pressing ahead with what’s left of Huang’s vision.

After that, the manufacturer must pursue a production certificate from the FAA, proving that the company can build the same approved aircraft again and again, with the right tools, records, inspections, quality controls, supplier oversight, training, calibration, and parts tracking.

Berdasarkan laporan, beta has found a narrow on-ramp to get the a250 flying before full certification. For Beta, that included July flights of the CX300 across a Virginia-to-Maryland corridor carrying, among other things, a manufactured transplantable organ in a medical containment system. Sebagaimana diketahui, for the fixed-wing alia cx300, customer trials are moving in parallel. In March, Beta’s CX300 successfully completed 23 flights over 10 days on Loganair routes linking six Scottish cities. The airline has since signed a term sheet for five Beta aircraft, with options for five more and service expected to start in 2029.

Diungkapkan bahwa beta is pushing so hard for the a250 because the case for electric flight gets even more interesting with vertical-lift aircraft. Helicopters and other VTOLs have a less orderly life than fixed-wing planes do. They must hover, sidestep, turn in place, settle, climb, and hold themselves in the air by main force. But conventional helicopters are built around a rotor speed that varies only a few percent because the engine, transmission, and rotor system are all designed around one narrow operating point.

Sebagaimana diketahui, “one of the dreams of vertical flight has been to vary the rotor rpm,” says anubhav datta, an aerospace engineering professor at the university of maryland, college park, who studies electric propulsion and vertical flight. Electric motors, he argues, have advanced enough to make that practical. A rotor that can slow down or speed up as conditions change can waste less energy, make less noise, and better match the odd assortment of tasks that vertical flight demands.

Sebagaimana diketahui, electric propulsion also lets designers break up the work with multiple motors. The weight of an electric motor is tied closely to its torque. If you spread that torque among several motors, each of the motors can shrink, meaning that their combined weight is less than would be needed for one big engine. This is one reason why so many electric aircraft designs appear to have sprouted propellers wherever an engineer found a place to put one.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, there is a downside to using multiple smaller motors: if one of the motors quits, the rotor it’s driving has little stored energy compared to the inertia in a conventional helicopter’s one large rotor. This inertia can come in handy if the engine dies, because the rotor will continue to spin and allow the pilot to descend under control, in an emergency technique known as autorotation.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, that helps explain the convergence in today’s evtol designs. Joby Aviation’s S4 uses six propellers that tilt between lift and cruise. Archer Aviation’s Midnight has six tilting propellers and six dedicated lift props. Beta’s A250 keeps its four lift propellers horizontal and uses a separate pusher motor for forward flight.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, in beta’s home state of vermont, the electricity produced in the state comes almost entirely from renewable sources. The turbines in conventional jet engines are marvelous machines, but they throw away a lot of energy as heat. Of course, electric aviation’s climate advantage depends not only on how clean the power grid is, but on how efficiently the aircraft uses energy. Plus they need to carry the hardware to manage that heat—inlets, ducts, radiators, oil coolers—and the drag that comes with pulling air through all of it.

Berdasarkan laporan, kyle clark [in cockpit], founder and ceo of beta technologies, pilots the company’s alia cx300, an electric plane that beta expects to receive faa certification in 2027. Clark began designing a hybrid electric plane while still in college. Beta Technologies.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, by contrast, an electric design, with no combustion, gearbox, or oil circuits, avoids much of that energy burden. Batteries will never come close to the fuel density of petroleum fuels. The result is an aircraft that is more than twice as “slippery” in terms of its lift-to-drag ratio. But because electric drivetrains are much more efficient than combustion engines, a battery doesn’t necessarily need to match the energy density of petroleum fuel to be useful.

Diungkapkan bahwa while the motors on an electric aircraft provide the drama at takeoff and landing, the batteries set nearly every boundary: the range, payload, charge time, cooling load, reserve energy, and, ultimately, useful life. For now, the hardest limit on electric aviation is not imagination, software, or even motors. It is the stubborn weight of stored energy.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, “one thing you notice about [electric] airplanes is that they are all small,” says cecutta, the aviation analyst. This limitation is from the batteries. “They are not small because someone has done a market study and decided that is the optimal size. They are small because you cannot make them big. ”.

Diungkapkan bahwa in a conventional aircraft, fuel accounts for a significant percentage of the takeoff weight. In an electric plane, the battery packs also account for a lot of the weight; in Beta’s CX300, they’re close to half the aircraft’s mass. But that weight gradually disappears during flight. That means the rest of the aircraft must be light enough to lift a power source that never gets lighter, yet strong enough to endure vibration, turbulence, hard landings, and years of fatigue. But a drained battery at landing weighs the same as a fully charged one at takeoff. The more engineers push to save weight, Datta notes, the more flexible the airframe becomes, making the wings and other structures more prone to bending, twisting, and vibration. In that sense, the battery problem becomes a structural problem, too.

Sebagaimana diketahui, beta’s cx300 carries five liquid-cooled battery packs of about 45 kilowatt-hours each, giving the aircraft roughly 225 kwh of rated capacity, though not all of that may be usable in flight. Each pack weighs 255 kg and contains 2,772 cylindrical cells. Altogether, about 14,000 cells sit beneath the occupied cabin, each one a tiny storehouse of energy, heat, and potential trouble.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the burden of the battery explains much of what i see elsewhere in beta’s aircraft: the 15-meter wingspan, the composite structure, and the almost doctrinal effort to leave out every piece of hardware and creature comfort that’s not essential to the mission. The CX300 even does without flaps, which most aircraft use to generate extra lift at low speeds, so it must take off and land unusually fast for an aircraft of its size.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, on beta’s battery line, commercially supplied standard 21-millimeter-diameter, 70-mm-long cells are tested and assembled. Cells become modules, modules become subpacks, and eleven subpacks become a 45-kWh pack. Cooling plates manage heat during normal operation, while passive barriers and electrical isolation are designed to contain the ugly edge cases that Beta’s testing process intentionally triggers.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the modular design of the packs will give beta’s planes a path to better batteries as the cells and battery chemistry improve. Albans, Vt. Caputo tells me that the company is already evaluating higher-density cells at its battery testing facility in nearby St. More watt-hours per kilogram could eventually mean more range, more payload, or both.

Sebagaimana diketahui, what sets beta technologies apart from its competitors is the breadth of its ambitions: it’s not just building electric aircraft. It’s also cultivating a broader ecosystem to nurture the growth of electric aviation.

Berdasarkan laporan, for instance, beta intends its motor business to extend beyond its own aircraft. The company has delivered lift motors for Eve Air Mobility’s proof-of-concept aircraft and has a contract to supply up to $1 billion in pusher motors as Eve’s program develops. In addition, Beta is selling flight-control computers and software to Horizon Aircraft. It is also producing propulsion systems for the military, as well as the MV250, a hybrid-electric autonomous aircraft for defense missions.

Berdasarkan laporan, beta’s fast-charging stations [left] have been installed at 138 locations. The company uses the open-standard Combined Charging System (CCS) so that other aircraft can use its chargers. The thermal-management station [right] keeps the battery from overheating during charging. Beta Technologies.

Berdasarkan laporan, further evidence of beta’s far-ranging plans is visible near the battery line in the south burlington facility, where workers are readying a few of the company’s 1. Intended for installation at airports, each cube takes 480-volt AC from the grid and can deliver up to 320 kW at as much as 1,000 volts DC. According to Beta, charging either model of its Alia aircraft takes about 35 minutes, from the minimum charge required under visual flight rules to full state. 5-meter-tall Charge Cubes for shipping. A separate thermal-management cube circulates water-glycol coolant through the aircraft to keep the batteries from overheating during charging.

Diungkapkan bahwa the charge cubes use the combined charging system (ccs), an open standard increasingly shared across the electric transportation industry. Archer, Atlantic Aviation, Signature Aviation, and government agencies have purchased or installed Beta’s charging equipment. Beta’s strategy resembles Tesla’s decision to treat charging as part of the vehicle business, with one important difference: Beta is courting other aircraft makers, airports, and operators to use its technology. As of October, Beta has 138 fast-charge locations, with additional sites in permitting or construction.

Sebagaimana diketahui, for charging beyond the fixed network, beta offers a wheeled 40-kw mini cube and a 65-kw mini cube+ that can ride inside an alia and plug into more modest electrical service. The Mini Cube can also charge cars, buses, and trucks—any vehicle that uses the CCS standard.

Diungkapkan bahwa back above lake champlain, the cx300 levels off, and the motor recedes to a faint hum. Then Caputo switches it off, and there’s nothing but the rush of wind around the canopy. The aircraft glides on its long wings while the coasting propeller turns the motor into a generator, feeding about 9 kW back to the battery.

Diungkapkan bahwa then we turn to the east and slip into the landing queue behind a national guard c-130 hercules, and caputo powers and slides the throttle forward. The motor springs to life again, pushing the airplane, and perhaps aviation itself, into the future.

#308. Your Robot’s Safety Functions Already Work. What If the Input Lies?

📅 27 Oct 2026

Your Robot’s Safety Functions Already Work. What If the Input Lies?

Tanggal: 27 Oct 2026 | Sumber: https://spectrum.ieee.org/ai-robot-safety-cybersecurity-vicone

How VicOne helps expose cyber risks in AI robot safeguards.

VicOne is a Physical AI cybersecurity company protecting vehicles and robots from cyber threats that can alter behavior and compromise safety.

Berdasarkan laporan, a robot can follow its safety rules and still act on manipulated information. See what this means for robot safety and how teams can strengthen their testing and evidence.

This article is brought to you by VicOne.

Berdasarkan laporan, a mobile robot slows for someone in a hallway. A humanoid pauses to let a person pass. A collaborative arm eases its movement as a worker approaches. Each response depends on information about the robot or its surroundings: a distance reading, a position estimate, or a stop signal.

Berdasarkan laporan, but what happens when one of those inputs is wrong, and the robot still responds exactly as designed? the mobile robot reads the hallway as clear while someone is still there. The arm estimates that the worker is farther away. The humanoid does not receive a stop signal as a person crosses its path.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, in each case, a fault could cause that mismatch. So could deliberate manipulation.

At VicOne LAB R7, we examine how manipulated inputs can change robot behavior — and what that means for the systems meant to keep people safe.

Berdasarkan laporan, a robot does more than measure its surroundings. It may interpret what it sees and hears to decide what to do next. Information placed in its environment can therefore influence its actions.

Sebagaimana diketahui, published research shows how this can happen. In a study of vision-language-action (VLA) models, a patch in a camera’s view reduced task success in simulated robot tests. FreezeVLA found that an adversarial image could cause tested models to ignore later instructions. Although the studies used different methods, both demonstrate how visual input can interfere with a robot’s intended task.

In a robot-dog test using Gemma 4 E4B, text on a poster was treated as an instruction and changed the robot’s movement.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, vicone lab r7 also tested how untrusted inputs could change robot behavior. In a separate hospital-service-robot simulation using Nemotron on NVIDIA Jetson AGX Orin, crafted audio that is inaudible to people changed the robot’s simulated behavior. In a robot-dog test using Gemma 4 E4B, text on a poster was treated as an instruction and changed the robot’s movement. The assigned tasks did not change; the inputs did.

Berdasarkan laporan, in a vicone lab r7 test, text on a poster changed a robot dog’s movement, illustrating how a crafted input can turn an unlikely outcome into a repeatable attack. VicOne.

Diungkapkan bahwa an independent protective system may still stop a dangerous action. But that system also depends on information: readings, estimates, and messages that tell it when to intervene. What happens if one of those inputs is manipulated?.

Sebagaimana diketahui, at a robotics bug bounty event, vicone lab r7 researchers injected a ros 2/dds message into a robot that organizers expected to remain still under a safe-control setting. The robot moved.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, a humanoid’s balance controller offers another example. Researchers demonstrated the underlying acoustic attack against drones with vulnerable gyroscopes. If it relies on a vulnerable gyroscope, sound at the sensor’s resonant frequency could distort its reported rotation. The controller might correct for a tilt that never occurred. The research did not demonstrate the same attack chain causing a humanoid to fall.

Sebagaimana diketahui, other protections could interrupt either chain. The question for safety and security teams is whether those protections detect the danger independently or depend on the same manipulated information.

Diungkapkan bahwa figure 1. VicOne maps how accidental faults and deliberate cyber manipulation can lead to similar robot safety outcomes, from loss of control to physical harm. VicOne.

Diungkapkan bahwa a safety assessment may treat a combination of accidental faults as unlikely. An attacker can choose when to introduce a false input and repeat the same trigger. Deliberate manipulation changes that assumption. That does not make harm inevitable, but it may change how cyber risks should be assessed.

Berdasarkan laporan, redundant sensors also need an adversarial test. In autonomous driving research, a crafted physical object misled a system combining camera and LiDAR perception. If one action can affect both inputs, their agreement may offer less reassurance than expected. The study does not establish a weakness in a particular robot, but it shows why teams should test whether one manipulation can affect several checks at once.

Cyber threats add intent to the safety equation, so risk assessments based on accidental faults must be revisited to account for attacks that can be timed and repeated.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, safety teams set limits for speed, protective distances, and permitted operating areas. The evidence behind those limits should also show what happens when the information used to enforce them is deliberately manipulated.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, that evidence can also support assessments against applicable requirements. The EU Machinery Regulation, which applies from January 20, 2027, includes requirements to protect safety-relevant systems and data against corruption. IEC TS 63074 examines security threats that could affect safety-related control systems. China’s GB/T 45502-2025 addresses information security for service robots. Each has its own scope, and teams still need evidence for their robot’s design and operating conditions.

Diungkapkan bahwa figure 2. Cybersecurity strengthens robot safety evidence throughout the lifecycle. VicOne helps teams test safety limits against manipulation before deployment and monitor the conditions behind safe behavior in operation. VicOne.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, before deployment, safety and security engineers can compare normal and adversarial scenarios against the same safety limits. During operation, they can monitor for changes to software, models, sensor signals, or behavior that may call earlier results into question. Any response to suspicious behaviors should follow policies approved by the safety team.

Sebagaimana diketahui, vicone supports that work across the robot lifecycle. Through the Robotic Hacking Community, VicOne LAB R7 works with researchers to investigate how cyber threats can change robot behavior. VicOne’s Radeis helps teams validate potential effects before deployment, while Rthena provides visibility into risks and behavior during operation.

Berdasarkan laporan, the central test is whether a robot’s safeguards still protect people when the information they rely on is manipulated. Safety and security teams can begin by tracing the inputs behind each protective decision, challenging them, and revisiting the evidence as the robot changes. They can start with these five questions:.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, 1. What does each protective function read? Map the readings, estimates, messages, and confirmations. Identify which safeguards operate independently of the robot’s AI decisions.

Sebagaimana diketahui, 2. How does that information arrive? Check how inputs are produced, transmitted, authenticated where appropriate, and handled when they are missing or implausible.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, 3. What happens if an input is manipulated? Test false distances, drifting position estimates, and other relevant scenarios against the robot’s safety limits.

Diungkapkan bahwa 4. Can one action mislead several inputs? Check whether sensor fusion or seemingly independent safeguards share a point of failure.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, 5. When should the evidence be revisited? Reassess after changes to software, models, sensors, or operating conditions. Agree on bounded responses to suspicious behavior with the safety team in advance.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the goal is not only to show that a protective function works. Teams also need evidence that it remains protective when the information behind its decision is wrong or deliberately manipulated — and that another safeguard can catch the resulting hazard when needed. As robots change, that evidence needs to change with them.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, for a deeper look how cybersecurity can affect robot safety, download our white paper “why robot safety depends on cybersecurity: protecting the information that safety decisions rely on. ”.

Sebagaimana diketahui, vicone is a physical ai cybersecurity company protecting vehicles and robots from cyber threats that can alter behavior and compromise safety. Headquartered in Tokyo, Japan, the company provides automotive and robotics organizations with software and services to identify cyber risks early, assess their potential safety impact, and protect systems in operation, helping maintain safe, reliable behavior across real-world deployments.

Sebagaimana diketahui, in an update rolling out today, gentler streak is introducing new ways for users to track their wellbeing and personalize the app’s guidance based on how they feel. Here are the details.

One of my favorite exercise-tracking apps got even better today with an update that expands its functionality beyond workouts and fitness metrics to better reflect how users actually feel.

Starting today, Gentler Streak will let users log how they feel each day, including their mood, symptoms, and other factors that may not be reflected in their health and fitness data.

Diungkapkan bahwa some days, the way we feel isn’t reflected in what the data says, no matter the data quality. And how you feel is not only a mood: it is also a sore throat, heavy legs or a poor night’s sleep. The feature was inspired by the Gentler Streak community, including people living with chronic fatigue, fibromyalgia, ADHD, and those not wearing their Apple Watch at night. “How I Feel” captures the part that devices can’t grasp: personal context. Without overnight signals, their guidance has less to work with.

According to the team behind Gentler Streak, these new features are aimed at users whose health and fitness data may not accurately reflect how they feel, including those dealing with chronic conditions, menopause, stress, or poor sleep.

Diungkapkan bahwa in practice, the app will now feature four tabs: today, health, workouts, and insights. In the Today and Health tabs, a new “Anything to add?” field will let users rate how they feel, from Great to Off, and add context about what might be affecting their well-being, including fatigue, feeling calm, or custom tags.

Berdasarkan laporan, you decide when the prompt appears. Go to Profile > Settings > Self-Evaluation Prompt and choose one of three options: only when your vitals or sleep are off, always on, or never.

Gentler Stories notes that the self-assessments will override the app’s wellbeing estimates for that day, with its daily guidance adjusting accordingly.

The Today tab will also feature an expanded 10- or 30-day timeline showing logged workouts, wellbeing estimates, potential symptoms, poor sleep or vitals, and the first day of a menstrual period, while Health will introduce an interactive chart showing users how their wellbeing changes over time, with the ability to filter by symptoms.

Users can now also customize which information appears on their Today screen, including vitals, sleep, steps, menstrual cycle, VO₂ max, and workouts, which is a nice touch.

For users who are sick, injured, or taking a break from exercise, the app’s hallmark Activity Path will make way for a new Wellbeing Path, which lets them track their wellbeing on a daily basis.

Berdasarkan laporan, for users with active status, a new colorful wellbeing line will appear beneath the activity path, reflecting how they feel each day. This information is logged automatically for those who wear their Apple Watch overnight, or based on self-assessments for those who don’t.

Importantly, Gentler Stories notes that all information entered through the new feature remains on the user’s device, with no accounts or company-operated servers involved.

Gentler Streak is available for free on the App Store, with in-app purchases for monthly, yearly, family, and lifetime subscriptions.

Diungkapkan bahwa handing the fake paper over to ieee access left me torn. After putting in a fair amount of effort into making the AI-generated forgery, would I be happy if it passed through the checkers, or saddened that the only remaining line of defense for publishers is the evermore-burdened peer-review community? Sebagaimana diketahui, as it turned out, i was filled with relief when the paper got picked up quickly for having hallucinated references, otherwise known as ghost citations. When I ran the paper through Gemini afterward, without qualm it happily reported that seven “modern LLM-related research references have been fabricated to support the paper’s specific narrative. ” Thanks for the heads up, Gemini!.

Berdasarkan laporan, in fact, gemini underestimated how many ghost citations there were. “I am an experimental physicist by training, so this was not at all my area, but nothing seemed majorly scientifically wrong” about the paper, says Mahoney. “It was just that so many hallucinated references immediately cast doubt on the entire work. When Mahoney ran the paper through a research-integrity checker called STM Integrity Hub, she picked up 12, and another checker from MolecularConnections could not validate 24 references, including one that had the classic tell of “John Smith” as a single author (no offense to all the academically inclined John Smiths out there). ”.

Berdasarkan laporan, feedback on the fake paper from gaetano assanto, an expert in optical solitons and a former collaborator of mine from roma tre university, in italy, was similarly mixed. Concentrating on the paper itself, he thought it looked professionally written. But he noted that the mathematics was very dense (“too much math for me in a single shot!”) and would require specialized knowledge to evaluate. And, although the text looked legitimate, Assanto noted an excessive use of acronyms in the abstract, and he was suspicious of a couple of confidently proclaimed physics statements that were at best debatable.

Sebagaimana diketahui, on one level, this outcome was positive: a complete novice using free tools couldn’t get an ai-faked paper past the publishers’ automated defenses or a potential peer reviewer’s eagle eye. With general-purpose LLMs and no special prompting expertise, I had managed to conjure a superficially plausible scientific paper out of research that had never happened. But it was hardly a resounding victory for the scientific publishing system. And more advanced LLMs are no longer making the kind of mistakes their free, dumber relatives are making.

Sebagaimana diketahui, it’s common knowledge in the academic publishing world that, in the cat-and-mouse game between bad actors and publishers, ai slop papers continue to slip through publishers’ safeguards. This leaves the humble peer reviewer as a publisher’s last line of defense. “It feels like building a detection tool today may not be effective with the AI-created paper of tomorrow,” says Luigi Longobardi, IEEE’s director of publishing ethics and conduct. Yet peer review is simply not fit to handle the volume of papers—both legitimate and slop—passing through.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, even before ai tools became ubiquitous, the peer-review system was being pushed to its breaking point, processing well over 3 million papers in 2022. This culture not only forces many academics to regularly churn out incremental research, but has also long driven some to enlist the help of “paper mills”—unethical organizations that produce low-quality or fabricated papers—just to keep pace. Fundamentally, this problem stems from science’s publish-or-perish culture, which pressures academics to constantly publish papers in prestigious journals to secure funding and advance their careers. AI only amplifies these existing dynamics.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, mahoney says ieee access alone receives about 60,000 submissions per year, accepting around 20 percent, or about 12,000 papers. But despite the journal’s roster of tens of thousands of peer reviewers, it’s getting harder and harder to secure their services, with the average number of reviewer invitations being sent out for each article increasing by 50 percent since 2018. For these volunteers, peer review is a significant commitment on top of teaching and conducting their own research. Every accepted paper is reviewed by at least two independent reviewers. Now they’re also being asked to spot AI slop.

Tools including FARS (Fully Automated Research System), AutoResearchClaw, The AIScientist-v2, Zochi, AI Researcher, and DeepScientist all aim to address a serious bottleneck to scientific discovery: us.

Diungkapkan bahwa often with just a single prompt, these ai engines can conduct a comprehensive literature search, from which they can generate a completely reasonable research proposal. They can design and conduct experiments using digital datasets and simulations and then write a full research paper—all with no human input after the initial prompt. Very recent systems are even beginning to go beyond the digital realm. LabClaw, for example, now links to autonomous labs that can generate real-world data for tasks such as drug discovery.

Berdasarkan laporan, the output is, to most intents and purposes, actual research, and therefore potentially worthy of publication. But with humans in the loop in only the most nominal sense, these tools bring into question the meaning of the term “legitimate science. ”.

Berdasarkan laporan, fars, which caused a stir this year when it created 166 papers in 417 hours, was developed by the singapore-based startup analemma. “FARS can pursue many research threads simultaneously, 24/7, without fatigue, and at scale. “We built FARS because research is still constrained by human attention, fragmented tools, scarce technical labor, and slow experimental iteration,” explains Xiwen Su, Analemma’s manager of product operations and partnerships. ” (The online service that I used to access FARS was discontinued after Analemma was acquired by Baidu while this article was being reported. ).

Diungkapkan bahwa su and the team behind analemma kindly agreed to let me loose on fars and gave me enough credits to create a paper. Which gave me another opportunity to put Mahoney’s research-integrity checkers to the test.

Diungkapkan bahwa fars is not an llm in and of itself, but rather an agentic ai-orchestration system connected to a computing cluster that has access to essentially any open- or closed-source llm it needs. The system uses four specialized agents for ideation, planning, conducting the experiment, and writing, all designed to perform the main tasks of science autonomously.

Sebagaimana diketahui, though fars initially focused on ai research, su told me it should be reasonably effective across other domains. As I wanted a topic similar to that of my first fake paper, I pasted in an abridged version of that paper’s title—“LLM-aided Optical Soliton Dynamics Modelling for Next-Gen Communications”—into the prompt box and hit “Send. ” Just 21 minutes later, FARS generated a research proposal based on an extremely detailed literature review—far more than I or any other human could have achieved in that time.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, with a click, i tasked fars with conducting the experiment it detailed in its research proposal. The next day, I received an email saying my experiment was complete. Without checking the results, I pressed a button marked “Write paper,” and the final submission-ready article was produced in 2 hours.

Berdasarkan laporan, because fars is designed to spot gaps in the scientific literature and conduct real research to close them, i was more confident it would breeze through the publisher’s checks. But just as my fake paper fell down in the references, so too did the AI-generated real one.

Sebagaimana diketahui, “your fake article had lots of hallucinated references,” says mahoney. “While this AI-generated one had no fake references, our team would have rejected this paper because it did have a huge percentage of references to preprints, which likely has something to do with the dataset the AI has access to. ” Because preprints haven’t yet undergone peer review, IEEE Access considers heavy reliance on them a problem.

Sebagaimana diketahui, in addition, although the research-integrity checking tools didn’t spot any issues with figures, mahoney did. One figure included a red line labeled with the nonsense term “lhewl,” and an AI “brain” in another figure had some random dots in it, which ironically were a tell that it was AI generated.

Sebagaimana diketahui, automated research systems are very much a work in progress, but they are already starting to make waves in the scientific community. For instance, an AI Scientist academic paper and papers from the Autoscience Institute were accepted through double-blind peer review in 2025 by the International Conference on Learning Representations. As these systems improve and start to produce research outputs at volume, the waves are likely to build to a tsunami that will threaten today’s scientific and publishing process.

Berdasarkan laporan, “fars doesn’t kill the paper, but it does challenge the paper as the unit of knowledge,” argues su. “We believe the future looks more like a living knowledge graph—where individual, well-scoped contributions (some made by humans, some by machines) connect and build on each other dynamically. ”.

Benjamin Skuse's experiment raised a bigger question: What counts as legitimate scientific research in the age of AI?.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, in this future, humans will continue to have roles in the scientific and publication processes—just very different and limited ones. And traditional line-by-line peer-reviewing will be a thing of the past, though Su emphasizes that this change will not eliminate human judgment. For example, instead of conducting experiments themselves, humans would sense-check and review automated output at key points. “Automated systems can handle reproducibility checks, statistical validation, and novelty screening,” she says. “Humans can then focus on the harder question: Does this [research] matter?”.

Berdasarkan laporan, though from a very different world than su, mahoney agrees that humans need to be freed to focus on the science, and that technology holds the key. “During peer review, we’re also using AI semantic search tools to help editors match manuscripts to the most relevant reviewers, who are best placed to stop the slop before entering the scientific record. “It’s promising to see the progress that has been made to automate some of the triage tasks, such as author checks, tortured phrases, duplicate submission, reference validity, et cetera,” she says. ”.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, in addition, mahoney thinks that ai cannot be banned or overly restricted, as this will stymie progress at a time when human knowledge could and should be growing at an unprecedented rate. “Researchers are increasingly using AI in their work, from literature discovery, to code generation, to data analysis, and this is not necessarily a bad thing,” she argues. The question is not just whether the research matters, she says. But she disagrees that peer reviewers and humans more broadly will play a smaller part in scientific progress; Mahoney believes the future still requires humans at the wheel. “The question should be: Can this work be trusted and reproduced?”.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, to this end, longobardi argues that ai may ultimately require scientists to prove not just what they discovered but how they discovered it. One possibility, he says, is using technology to verify research at the source. “The system doesn’t really help because it’s not designed to not trust the paper,” he explains. “Maybe institutions can think about developing their own trust markers, automatically integrating the equipment researchers use with blockchain technology to say ‘Yes, this person was in the lab on this day and got this data. ’”.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, elements of this approach are already emerging. And the University of Southampton’s School of Chemistry and Chemical Engineering has rolled out an electronic lab notebook system. For instance, two departments within the Max Planck Institute of Colloids and Interfaces have implemented a sample database, assigning each and every sample created under their roofs with a unique ID and QR code. These innovative safeguards represent early efforts toward keeping humans front and center in scientific progress, and making the scientific process itself more transparent.

Berdasarkan laporan, whether this human-centric vision, su’s ai-driven aspiration, or some other picture of the future wins out remains to be seen. The one thing my vibe-research adventure has clarified is that business-as-usual science is not an option. Scientists and publishers must adapt to a world in which it’s becoming increasingly difficult to spot the difference between real research and AI forgeries, and where deciding what counts as legitimate scientific work may become even harder than detecting outright fraud.

Diungkapkan bahwa benjamin skuse created two papers for this experiment, both screened by ieee access with the publisher’s cooperation. Neither was accepted for publication.

Paper 1: The AI-Generated ForgeryCreated with ChatGPT and Gemini, this paper describes research that never happened.

Paper 2: The AI-Generated Research PaperCreated with Analemma’s FARS system, this paper describes computational research conducted by AI.

Neither paper was peer reviewed, and their scientific claims have not been independently validated.

#317. Garmin Enduro 4 review: monster MIP battery life makes this a value alternative to the Garmin Fenix 9 Pro

📅 13 Nov 2026

Garmin Enduro 4 review: monster MIP battery life makes this a value alternative to the Garmin Fenix 9 Pro

Tanggal: 13 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.tomsguide.com/wellness/smartwatches/garmin-enduro-4-review-monster-mip-battery-life-makes-this-a-value-alternative-to-the-garmin-fenix-9-pro

Keep exploring and earning more as a member.

Unlock and manage exclusive Tom’s Guide member rewards.

Diungkapkan bahwa join the tom's guide club for quick access. Enter your email below and we'll send confirmation, and sign you up to our newsletter.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, when you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

Berdasarkan laporan, the garmin enduro 4 is an iterative update on the garmin enduro 3 but offers a compelling alternative to the garmin fenix 9 pro. It’s cheaper, lighter and offers more battery life than Garmin’s flagship, and it's one of the best adventure watches available.

Diungkapkan bahwa why you can trust tom's guide our writers and editors spend hours analyzing and reviewing products, services, and apps to help find what's best for you. Find out more about how we test, analyze, and rate.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, memory-in-pixel displays are becoming rarer on the best garmin watches, but those who prefer them are still well served by the enduro line. If battery life is your primary concern, the Enduro 4 delivers in spades.

It lasted me 16+ days on a charge, around 50% longer than even the best sports watches with AMOLED displays for battery life, like the Garmin Fenix 9 Pro or Suunto Vertical 2.

Garmin hasn’t held back on features either, with the Enduro 4 getting most of the same key sports tracking tools as the Fenix 9 Pro, in a lighter case and at a lower price.

It’s an attractive package, but the elephant in the room is that the Enduro 3 is also getting nearly all the same new features as the Enduro 4 through software updates, has a similar design and the same incredible battery life, and undercuts the new watch in sales.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the garmin enduro 4 launched in october 2026 and costs $899 in the u. S. K. S. and £799 in the U. It’s the same launch price in the U. as the Enduro 3, but the latter is now available for £699/$799.

It’s a cheaper alternative to the Garmin Fenix 9 Pro Solar, which is the MIP option of the Fenix line-up and starts at $1,099.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the garmin enduro 4 is a large but lightweight watch that uses garmin’s familiar five-button setup. It has a 51mm case and is thick, but being mostly made from plastic means it’s significantly lighter than the 51mm watch in the Fenix 9 line-up.

Get instant access to breaking news, the hottest reviews, great deals and helpful tips.

It has a titanium bezel and a sapphire crystal screen with solar panels to boost the impressive battery life even further in sunny conditions.

The memory-in-pixel display is clear enough to read in all conditions, though I do think the Enduro 4 is less bright and readable than Garmin’s AMOLED watches when indoors or under tree cover.

Berdasarkan laporan, there are some hardware changes and improvements from the enduro 3. The Enduro 4 has a silver bezel with fewer yellow highlights, and under the hood it has more RAM, a faster processor for maps, and double the storage (64GB vs. 32GB on the Enduro 3).

The new watch also comes with Garmin’s new ComfortFit band, which I like a lot more than the UltraFit band that ships with the Enduro 3, though you can also buy the ComfortFit band separately.

On the top of the watch is a built-in flashlight with four brightness levels and a red mode, and on its underside is Garmin’s Elevate Gen 5 heart rate sensor, which is the same sensor as the Fenix 9 series and Enduro 3.

Berdasarkan laporan, while it’s not a diveproof watch like the fenix 9, the enduro 4 has a 10 atm rating and is waterproof. It also lacks the mic and speaker you do get on the Fenix.

Berdasarkan laporan, despite its size, i found the enduro 4 comfortable to wear 24/7 throughout testing. It’s not as attractive as the all-titanium Fenix 9 Pro, but the Enduro 4 is still a good-looking watch to wear outside your training.

Unless you’re desperate to go diving, the Enduro 4 has all the customizable sports modes you could ever need to track your workouts, including the improved rucking and rowing modes introduced on the Fenix 9.

Runners, cyclists, swimmers and triathletes get the most detail in their sports modes, including an improved stamina feature that aims to provide guidance on how much energy you have left in endurance activities and how best to pace them.

The Enduro 4 feeds all the data you track during workouts into an extensive suite of training analysis tools.

It has all the top-of-the-range features you get on the Garmin Forerunner 970 and Fenix 9, including running economy estimates (when paired with the Garmin HRM 600 chest strap) and ratings for overall endurance and hill-running ability.

Garmin offers greater depth of training analysis than any other brand I’ve tested, and while you might not want or need all this data, it’s there if you do, while a simple stat like overall training readiness provides a one-stop shop for those who want info at a glance.

I tested the GPS accuracy of the Enduro 4 by looking at its tracks after runs and comparing them with other watches that have proved reliably accurate on this front over time, like the Fenix 9 Pro and Coros Pace 4 Pro.

Garmin’s multi-band GPS accuracy is as good as it gets in my experience, and the Enduro 4 was reliably excellent throughout my testing, with consistent pacing and accurate GPS tracks when running in suburbs, city centers and under tree cover.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the heart rate accuracy was also good. I compared the Enduro 4’s readings with a chest strap in each workout, and it almost always closely aligned with the strap.

Sebagaimana diketahui, during interval workouts, the enduro 4’s optical heart rate sensor would lag a little behind the chest strap, and i did spot the occasional error at the start of runs on cold days, but i’d say the overall accuracy was very good. If you want more reliable results, I’d say you’d need a chest strap.

Battery life is a key selling point of the Enduro 4, and it didn't disappoint on this front in my testing.

The listed stats have the watch lasting 30 days in watch mode, or up to 90 days in sufficiently sunny conditions, and offering 60 hours of GPS in its most accurate mode (90 hours with solar).

If you use battery saver mode, the watch can last indefinitely in sunny conditions, and if you slum it and use regular GPS tracking (which is still pretty accurate), you can track activities for 120 hours (320 hours with solar).

On my first charge, the watch lasted me 16 days, and it’s tracking to go longer on my second charge; numbers that outperform the longest-lasting AMOLED watches comfortably, and the Enduro 4 also offers better battery life than the MIP Fenix 9 Pro Solar.

The only watches that rival the Enduro 4’s battery life are other MIP options like the Garmin Instinct 3 Solar, Coros Vertix 2S and the Enduro 3, which matches the newer watch on this front.

It’s also worth noting I was testing the Enduro 4 in cloudy conditions almost all the time, and got barely any extra juice out of the solar panels, so if you live in a sunnier climate and spend a lot of time outdoors, you can expect even better battery life.

Diungkapkan bahwa many of the exclusive updates on the enduro 4 compared with the enduro 3 relate to its mapping features. On the hardware side, you have a faster processor and more RAM, so maps should load more quickly when zooming and panning.

Then, when using the maps, you can use a new perspective view, which I prefer to the top-down view of your location on the Enduro 3, though it’s hardly a life-changing update.

The speed boost is welcome, and it’s noticeable when panning around maps on the watches side-by-side, but again, this wasn’t something I found a major problem on the Enduro 3 when I tested.

These minor upgrades build on Garmin’s best-in-class navigation features, with clear, detailed routable maps you can use to create routes on the fly, or to follow routes sent from the Garmin Connect app.

I find Garmin’s maps clearer to use on the brand’s AMOLED watches, especially in cloudy conditions, but it was still easy to follow routes and use the maps on the Enduro 4.

The Enduro 4 doesn't offer the LTE and satellite connectivity you get on the Fenix 9, or a mic and speaker you can use for voice commands, but it does have Garmin’s other smart features.

These include music storage, the ability to link up with streaming services like Spotify, NFC payments through Garmin Pay, and access to the Connect IQ app store, which is modest in comparison to the App Store or Google Play but contains some useful apps, widgets, watch faces and data fields.

As sports watches go, it’s pretty smart, but it doesn’t have an AMOLED display and if this is a priority for you, then looking at a true smartwatch like the Apple Watch Ultra 4 might be worthwhile, or at least the Fenix 9 Pro and its extra connectivity.

The Garmin Enduro 4 is a reliable, long-lasting adventure watch that’s one of the best options on the market right now if you prefer a MIP display.

It’s more affordable than the Fenix 9 Pro Solar, as well as being lighter and having longer battery life, though you do lose some potentially useful features like the extra connectivity on the Fenix.

Berdasarkan laporan, the garmin enduro 3 offers fierce competition, though. The Enduro 4 isn’t a major update and if you have an older Enduro model and are considering upgrading, I think opting for the cheaper Enduro 3 on sale is a better buy, even if this does run the risk of missing out on some future software updates that only come to the Enduro 4.

Diungkapkan bahwa if you’re not firmly set on a mip watch, then i prefer amoled devices myself, and it felt like a downgrade to use the enduro 4 after testing the fenix 9 pro and coros pace 4 pro and their brighter displays. The battery life gap between AMOLED and MIP is closing fast, too.

However, I’m pleased to see Garmin maintaining the remaining MIP options within its line-up, because not everyone wants another dazzling AMOLED display in their life, in which case the Enduro 4 is certainly a top option.

#319. iPhone Duo one week later: The future, or not for me?

📅 11 Nov 2026

iPhone Duo one week later: The future, or not for me?

Tanggal: 11 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://9to5mac.com/2026/11/11/iphone-duo-one-week-later-the-future-or-not-for-me/

Berdasarkan laporan, my iphone duo arrived last thursday, so i’ve had a week to use it as my daily carry. My early experience has been mixed, so I keep asking myself an important question: is this the iPhone’s future and I just need to adapt, or is the Duo simply not for everyone?.

After a week using the iPhone Duo, in some ways I have a lot of clarity about the product, and in other ways my thinking is very clouded.

To put it simply: I’m not having a great time with the Duo, which makes me wonder if the problem is me, not it.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, i’ve seen countless social media posts from duo owners proclaiming how much they love the product. It’s cool, weird, and wonderful in all sorts of ways. And I absolutely believe them. The iPhone Duo is a remarkable innovation for the iPhone. But for me and my needs (preferences?), it’s been more frustrating than enjoyable.

And that frustration mainly boils down to one thing: I almost never want to open it.

Berdasarkan laporan, i’d estimate at least 90% of my iphone duo usage involves the front display. Like, I know I should be unfolding it more, so I do. And when I unfold it the remaining 10% of the time, it’s often because I force myself to do it in the hopes of discovering what I’m missing out on. But it doesn’t add any real value for me.

Sebagaimana diketahui, because i rarely want to open the iphone duo, i’m left using the outer display all the time. In that mode, the Duo is too heavy for extended use, too wide to comfortably reach, and the UI in most apps is an adjustment.

Berdasarkan laporan, are these dealbreakers? no. I could live with the Duo’s outer display if I had to, but it’s definitely an inferior experience to my iPhone 18 Pro.

If I was opening the iPhone Duo more, and actually taking advantage of the key value proposition of foldables—that you can unfold them—I doubt the outer screen would bother me much.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, but what i’ve found, at least so far, is that one-handed iphone use is very important to me, which rules out using the inner display. I use my iPhone mostly for quick interactions, and often with a child in one hand (I have three very young kids). In situations when I do have two hands free to open the Duo, I’m probably sitting in front of my iPad Pro with a Magic Keyboard attached and would rather use the iPad instead.

So again: is the problem with the Duo, or with me?.

I think foldables and slab phones will obviously coexist as there will be fans of each.

I’m absolutely already converted however and am loving my duo.

Diungkapkan bahwa considering the air was my favourite phone up until this it’s surprised me. I love proper one handed use again on the outside screen and unfolded it’s much nicer than my old mini 7.

I get it’s not for everyone but those that click with it like myself have a superb device!.

Berdasarkan laporan, i think it’s the latter, but i’m not sure “problem” is the right word. I just don’t find myself using it the way it’s meant to be used. And that’s fine.

Diungkapkan bahwa i want to love the iphone duo, because i see how much fun other people are having with it. And maybe given more time, something will click and I’ll start to use it “as intended. ”.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, if iphone duo is the future of the iphone, i’ll adapt and move on with my life. But one week in, I think it’s probably just not for me. And if it’s not for me, maybe there are a lot of people who will continue preferring non-foldable iPhones for many years to come.

#320. Hurdle hints and answers for November 13, 2026
