Hurdle hints and answers for November 13, 2026

Tanggal: 13 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://mashable.com/entertainment/hurdle-hints-answers-november-13-2026

If you like playing daily word games like Wordle, then Hurdle is a great game to add to your routine.

Sebagaimana diketahui, there are five rounds to the game. This can give you several clues or none, depending on the words. The first round sees you trying to guess the word, with correct, misplaced, and incorrect letters shown in each guess. If you guess the correct answer, it'll take you to the next hurdle, providing the answer to the last hurdle as your first guess. For the final hurdle, every correct answer from previous hurdles is shown, with correct and misplaced letters clearly shown.

An important note is that the number of times a letter is highlighted from previous guesses does necessarily indicate the number of times that letter appears in the final hurdle.

#321. IEEE Xplore Digital Library Adds AI Assistant

📅 26 Oct 2026

IEEE Xplore Digital Library Adds AI Assistant

Tanggal: 26 Oct 2026 | Sumber: https://spectrum.ieee.org/ieee-xplore-digital-library-ai

The search tool offers summaries and verifiable source links.

Claire Olini is the senior manager for IEEE Corporate and Strategic Product Launch and Engagement.

Michael Spada is director of IEEE Product Launch and Engagement Strategy.

Sebagaimana diketahui, ieee recently released the ieee xplore ai research suite, built on the full text of millions of peer-reviewed publications in the ieee xplore digital library. The library offers full-text access to IEEE standards, journals, magazines, conference proceedings, and more.

Researchers who use the AI suite to search the digital library receive answers grounded in verified scientific results, ensuring a high level of accuracy and trust.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, powered by a proprietary ai system optimized for stem literature, the suite introduces powerful, intelligent features within the digital library. The suite enables users to seamlessly search and discover articles to accelerate their comprehension of complex technical papers.

The system surfaces deep insights, replacing the typical keyword queries with natural, conversational research workflows.

Diungkapkan bahwa as ai tools become more common in conducting research, ieee collaborated to build the suite around a simple principle: answers should be trustworthy, not just fast, says w. Clem Karl, vice president, IEEE Publication Services and Products.

Diungkapkan bahwa “ai can be a highly effective and beneficial tool that can help researchers accelerate discovery, enhance decision-making, and surface new connections,” karl says. “However, many AI engines present a great risk of hallucinating answers or introducing bias into otherwise credible research. With this in mind, IEEE has taken a responsible approach in our AI strategy by developing concrete safeguards to ensure our solution is rigorously grounded in scientific evidence that users can trust.

Berdasarkan laporan, “as stewards of the scholarly record, we held the new ai engine to the same standards as the peer-reviewed research we publish: a researcher shouldn’t have to trust an answer; they should be able to verify the work behind it. ”.

The IEEE Xplore AI Research Suite was developed in close collaboration with global scientific and library communities.

Diungkapkan bahwa the development process began with research into user needs and the challenges associated with existing ai research assistants. More than 3,000 testers—including engineers, scientists, and library information professionals—provided feedback to refine the AI engine and support research workflows.

Berdasarkan laporan, to mitigate the risk of ai hallucinations, the search-retrieval process is limited to querying the millions of ieee peer-reviewed full-text documents, alongside an expertly curated dataset of stem metadata. If the AI tool is unable to find relevant scientific content within the defined dataset, it is designed to inform the user rather than generate fabricated answers.

Sebagaimana diketahui, “ieee is committed to providing the technical community with a highly precise and reliable research experience,” says steven heffner, ieee’s chief publication officer and managing director of ieee publications. “The IEEE Xplore AI Research Suite offers something unique in that it is the only AI research assistant that leverages both the full-text and metadata of IEEE’s peer-reviewed content, rather than abstracts alone.

Berdasarkan laporan, “the difference is significant: our internal testing showed a threefold increase in result quality and accuracy across every key metric. These results underscore how critical full-text grounding is for technical research. ”.

For more information about features and coverage, or to request a demo for your organization, visit the IEEE Xplore AI Research Suite website.

Claire Olini is the senior manager for IEEE Corporate and Strategic Product Launch and Engagement.

Michael Spada is director of IEEE Product Launch and Engagement Strategy.

#326. Build a Hidden Lock With a Magnetic Imager

📅 26 Oct 2026

Build a Hidden Lock With a Magnetic Imager

Tanggal: 26 Oct 2026 | Sumber: https://spectrum.ieee.org/magnetic

Stephen Cass is the special projects editor at IEEE Spectrum.

Berdasarkan laporan, only a programmable secret gesture with a magnet can open this lockbox. It’s a proof of concept. (Or a hammer. ).

Sebagaimana diketahui, like many a nerd, i have a certain fascination with locks. This originates in reading the memoir Surely You’re Joking, Mr. Feynman as a teenager, in which Richard Feynman recounts picking locks and cracking combinations while at his day job working on the Manhattan Project at Los Alamos. I currently have a couple of locksport pick sets and training locks that I purchased at hacker conferences over the years (although I’m still terrible at it), and I delight in the YouTube exploits of folks like the LockPickingLawyer.

Diungkapkan bahwa all of which left me wondering if i could try building an interesting lock. One dodge that lockmakers have long used to challenge would-be plunderers is to conceal the existence of the lock itself. A modern variant of this is the magnetic lock, where a magnet is held or slid against an innocuous portion of a door or box, releasing a catch. The problem with this is that, once you guess the location of the lock, any strong magnet will open it.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, so i started thinking about embedding an rfid reader under the surface and resigning myself to keeping track of yet another access card. But then I stumbled across something much more interesting: SparkFun’s US $100 magnetic imaging tile. I realized I could use this to build a magnetic lock that opens with a programmable secret gesture.

Sebagaimana diketahui, i used a few discrete components to drive the servo motor and put the lock into program mode [top], controlled by a teensy 4. An array of Hall-effect sensors detect magnetic fields [bottom]. 1 microcontroller [middle]. James Provost.

Diungkapkan bahwa the magnetic imaging tile is a small-run sparkfun board based on the work of peter jansen. These sensors can detect both the magnitude and polarity of a magnetic field, and the board can report its measurements hundreds to thousands of times per second, depending on how much processing power your microcontroller has available. It features an 8-by-8 grid of Hall-effect sensors, and uses an SPI interface to talk to the microcontroller of your choice. This is easily fast enough to capture the motion of a magnet being moved by hand across the board’s sensor area—my secret gesture.

Berdasarkan laporan, an interesting thing about using magnetic fields is that if i was in extreme paranoia mode, i could shield the entire lock behind copper sheeting, something i couldn’t do with an rfid reader. The copper sheet would act as a Faraday cage, blocking any RFID signal, along with any other electromagnetic fields an attacker with an EMF meter might use to locate the lock.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, i chose a teensy 4. 1 as my microcontroller. I like the Teensy because it offers loads of input/output, a 600-megahertz processor, a megabyte of RAM, and a built-in SD card, all in a slim package with an equally slim $32 price tag.

Wiring the Teensy to the magnetic-imaging tile was trivial, only complicated by the fact that one side of the board has a silk-screen error that misidentifies the SPI connections (SparkFun says this will be fixed in future runs of the board).

In extreme paranoia mode, I could shield the entire lock behind copper sheeting.

Berdasarkan laporan, to create the gesture-recognition software, i once again turned to vibe coding. If you read my Hands On piece in the April 2026 issue of IEEE Spectrum on creating a teletext suite for ham radio, you’ll know I’ve been grappling with how vibe coding should be used in DIY projects, if at all. So this time, instead of letting Claude write all the software, I confined it to writing just two support libraries, which you can find in our online repository at https://github. com/IEEESpectrumHandsOn.

Berdasarkan laporan, one library is in charge of recording a lock gesture and saving it to the teensy’s nonvolatile storage. The other library monitors the tile and reports whether or not a newly detected gesture passes a selectable threshold to be considered a match.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, i wrote the top-level code myself to keep it as diy as possible. This code handles things like a button that puts the system in gesture-recording mode after a brief delay, the indicator LED for recording mode, and the code that operates the physical locking mechanism.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, hall-effect sensors rely on a current passing through a p-type slab of silicon. A magnetic field passing through the silicon deflects charge carriers toward the edges of the slab, creating a voltage proportional to the field [left]. By looking at the intensities of the voltages across an 8-by-8 grid of sensors, the microcontroller can reconstruct a gesture [right]. James Provost.

Berdasarkan laporan, of course, i needed something to lock to demonstrate my proof of concept. I bought a wooden craft box and removed the existing lid latch. These include a battery pack, the recording button, and a small additional board with two NPN transistors. These convert the Teensy’s 3. I will be the first to admit this mechanism goes beyond “simple” and into “simplistic,” but it’s sufficiently robust for my demo. I glued a notched beam inside the lid and built a mechanism that uses a servo motor to rotate another beam in and out of this notch. The box has ample room for the magnetic imaging tile to be mounted against one wall, along with the Teensy and other supporting electronics. 3-volt control signals to a 5-V signal needed to drive the servo.

Sebagaimana diketahui, once it was all put together, i soon discovered that the small size of the magnetic tile’s sensing area—just 3 centimeters square—made it easy to fit the tile inside the box but hard to do the unlock gesture on the outside so that it is read correctly. Using the pattern as a camouflaged reference grid I can make a repeatable gesture within the confines of the sensor area. I created a Celtic knotwork pattern that runs in a band across the front of the lockbox (I used an online knotwork generator and then projected and traced the pattern onto the box). (To make the gestures I’m using a magnetic stylus borrowed from a ferrite core-memory kit we featured in 2022. Marking the outline of the sensor area on the outside defeated the point of having a hidden lock, so instead I once again turned to mining my Irish heritage. ).

Diungkapkan bahwa there’s obvious room for improvement in any more serious installation. The biggest drawback currently is that if the box is locked when the battery runs out, you can’t open it again without breaking something. This could be solved by adding a hidden inductive charging coil. Nonetheless, the demo lockbox works well—now I just have to think what I should store in it!.

#330. How to Make Sure an 'Onion' Site on the Dark Web Is Legitimate

📅 11 Nov 2026

How to Make Sure an 'Onion' Site on the Dark Web Is Legitimate

Tanggal: 11 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://lifehacker.com/tech/how-to-make-sure-onion-site-on-dark-web-is-legitimate?utm_medium=RSS

Diungkapkan bahwa the dark web isn't just for illicit activities. In fact, many legitimate online platforms maintain a ". onion" domain on the dark web for privacy reasons, including media outlets like ProPublica and BBC News, social media sites like Facebook, and privacy-conscious communication platforms like Proton Mail and SecureDrop.

Berdasarkan laporan, but this also provides perfect cover for criminals and hackers who create clones of legitimate dark web sites to steal sensitive data and cryptocurrency from privacy-conscious users. And given that onion links are long and jumbled, it’s easy for users to accidentally click on the wrong link and end up on a fake website instead of the real one. When the FBI seized 276 onion addresses during 2014's Operation Onymous, they found that 153 of them were phishing sites.

Berdasarkan laporan, thankfully, tor browser already has a cryptography-backed feature that can verify the authenticity of an onion site, by confirming whether it has end-to-end encryption and extended validation certificates. Here's how this feature works, where it falters, as well as what other red flags you should look for.

Berdasarkan laporan, while phishing on the dark web works as it does on the clear web, scammers have a few unique advantages due to the secretive nature of the environment. Most importantly, you can’t just glance at an onion link to tell if the site is genuine. Normal website URLs tend to be short and memorable, while onion links are 56-character strings of alphanumeric text that look mostly like gibberish.

Berdasarkan laporan, when you try to connect, tor browser verifies the url against the originating website’s cryptographic key, which is how you know nobody has hijacked the address or tampered with it midway. But since this has the unwanted effect of making domains harder to recall, scammers have a much easier time generating lookalike addresses or creating website clones.

Sebagaimana diketahui, for example, many popular websites use “vanity prefixes” to make their onion addresses more easily identifiable or to add some branding appeal. That means their 56-character onion link starts with something like “facebook,” “bbcnews,” or “ciadotgov. ” But scammers can use a free tool like mkp224o to generate lookalike addresses with the same vanity prefix as the legitimate website, which gives users a false sense of security.

Sebagaimana diketahui, of course, most dark web users don’t type addresses directly into tor browser; they use dark web directories like the hidden wiki to find useful onion sites relevant to their search. Scammers will create fake search engines or link directories to point users to their fake websites, like when the Ahmia search engine discovered that a copy of its platform was directing users to 255 cloned services back in 2015.

Diungkapkan bahwa of course, it’s possible to orchestrate phishing attempts that don’t involve cloning sites at all. Researchers at Freie Universität Berlin describe a sophisticated technique where attackers serve the real website through their own reverse proxy, which lets them manipulate parts of the site or log your online activity without your awareness. In 2019, ESET even found a trojanized version of Tor Browser that replaced Bitcoin addresses on websites to direct payments to hackers. So both genuine websites and your browser itself are also vulnerable to manipulation if you download or access them from an unverified source.

Sebagaimana diketahui, there are a few best practices to avoid phishing attacks when using the dark web. None of them are foolproof on their own, but together, they considerably lower the risk of ending up on a fake or manipulated website.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the tor project has a feature called onion-location, which lets clear web websites advertise that they have a dark web version available for users who prefer more privacy. If opening a regular TLS-backed website using the Tor Browser reveals a purple “onion available” button in the address bar, you can click on it and be redirected to the official onion link associated with that site.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, on the desktop version of tor browser, you can access an onion site using a shortened version of its url called an onion name. For now, this feature only works with SecureDrop, so newsrooms can establish tip lines with addresses like mysitename. tor. securedrop. onion, which would then redirect to the 56-character original onion address. This feature is in active development, so more platforms might support it in the future.

Berdasarkan laporan, when you load up an onion site using the tor browser, you’ll see an onion icon on the address bar, which confirms that your connection is end-to-end encrypted. But you can also click on the onion icon to check if the site has an Extended Validation (EV) certificate, which tells you that its authenticity has been verified by a trusted certificate authority like DigiCert. While not every legitimate onion site will have an EV certificate, famous ones like Facebook tend to.

Sebagaimana diketahui, on the other hand, if you see a caution sign next to the onion icon, that means the site is using a self-signed or expired certificate that isn’t guaranteed by a trusted authority. It may also imply that the site is being served over an insecure URL. This doesn’t definitely tell you it’s a phishing site, but it’s a red flag to watch out for nevertheless.

Sebagaimana diketahui, don’t rely on search engines, link directories, reddit threads, or telegram channels too heavily on the dark web. Once you’re sure you’ve found the onion address for a genuine site, bookmark it so you can access it directly the next time you want to visit.

If you realized that you’ve been the victim of a phishing attempt, the first step is to close the browser window with the fake site and access the real onion address to reset any account passwords you may have accidentally divulged.

Diungkapkan bahwa also, generally try to enable two-factor authentication and pgp logins on any dark web account that supports it for added security. And if you downloaded Tor Browser from anywhere other than the official Tor Project site, uninstall it now and grab a fresh copy from the official address.

Banks and financial institutions are warning customers to beware of scams and phishing attempts as cybercriminals may take advantage of the global Microsoft outage to target individuals and businesses.

Berdasarkan laporan, “stay alert and protect yourself,” standard chartered singapore said on social media. “A technology outage can create opportunities for scammers. ”.

Diungkapkan bahwa “scammers may contact you offering to resolve the microsoft or other systems issues,” said ing australia. “Do not allow anyone access to your devices without confirming with the organization through their publicly listed contact number. ”.

The Bank of Queensland said that scammers may ask for personal details or One-Time Passwords and warned customers to “hang up immediately” if they receive a suspicious call.

Berdasarkan laporan, customers have been advised to not click on links or open attachments from unknown sources, and never share pins or passwords. Other banks have told their customers to be cautious of anyone claiming to be tech support personnel, and to report unauthorized transactions and suspicious messages.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, technology journalist jacob ward told cnn that the “the ripple effects” from the outage could “go on and on. ”.

“Not only are people’s emails down, the systems they rely on to protect themselves from email based attacks, those are down as well,” he said.

The Microsoft outage has caused at least one American company to postpone its quarterly earnings call.

Workhorse Group, a Detroit-based electric vehicle manufacturer, pushed their Q3 earnings call to Monday, citing the technology outage.

“The rescheduling is due to business disruptions caused by the global Microsoft outages taking place today, November 12,” the company wrote to investors on Thursday.

Diungkapkan bahwa earnings calls are typically held virtually, either via a conference call or video webcast system, allowing company executives to discuss financial results with investors and analysts. Participants dial in by phone or join online.

Sebagaimana diketahui, workhorse postponed its earnings call until monday, november 16 at 4:30 p. m. ET.

The global Microsoft outage was not caused by a cybersecurity breach, a Microsoft executive confirmed late Thursday.

“We will continue to share more information as soon as we have it, and for now I can confirm that there is no indication this is the result of malicious or cyber activity,” Charles Lamanna, executive vice president of Copilot, Agents, and Platform at Microsoft, said in a post on X.

Diungkapkan bahwa earlier, australia’s home affairs minister tony burke said the company had told him that they “don’t believe they are dealing with a cyber attack. ”.

“They believe they are dealing in some ways similar to what we saw with respect to CrowdStrike where there is an update that has gone awry,” Burke added during a press conference in Sydney.

Burke was referring to the 2024 software glitch at cybersecurity firm CrowdStrike that crashed computers, canceled flights and disrupted hospitals all around the globe, causing billions of dollars in losses.

Australia’s spy agency and federal police were among the organizations hit by the Microsoft outage on Friday local time.

The Microsoft outage highlights the “inherent dangers” of companies that depend on a handful of tech giants for critical global infrastructure, an expert told CNN.

“If one of those firms suffers a major outage, it has the potential to dramatically reduce business productivity globally during the outage time,” Computing Professor Toby Murray, of Australia’s University of Melbourne, said.

Murray added that the outage affecting Outlook and other major services like Microsoft Teams is “incredibly widespread, and its ramifications extend well beyond being able to send and receive work emails,” making it difficult for businesses to operate.

Diungkapkan bahwa “outlook and teams are critical global business infrastructure. This outage is making it difficult for many organizations to properly field customer service requests received over the phone, as well as disabling their email communications,” he added.

Mark Gregory, Associate Professor at Australia’s RMIT University School of Engineering, also said the outage highlights how dependent businesses and government agencies have become on technology providers.

it was “unthinkable” that a company like Microsoft could have a global outage after previous incidents.

Diungkapkan bahwa “the idea that after the crowdstrike outage and after other outages that we’ve seen, that a company like microsoft could have an outage that would be global in nature is unthinkable. ”.

Gregory was referring to the 2024 software glitch at cybersecurity firm CrowdStrike that crashed computers, canceled flights and disrupted hospitals all around the globe, causing billions of dollars in losses.

He highlighted the need for better contingency plans when critical services go offline.

#338. From Chip Lab to Center Stage

📅 23 Oct 2026

From Chip Lab to Center Stage

Tanggal: 23 Oct 2026 | Sumber: https://spectrum.ieee.org/preethi-ashwath-chip-designer

This integrated circuit designer explains wearables to consumers.

Joanna Goodrich is the associate editor of The Institute.

IEEE Member Preethi Ashwath is one of the few women who work in analog integrated circuit design, where about 11 percent are female.

Diungkapkan bahwa many engineers are more comfortable working behind the scenes developing technology than speaking to consumers about products. But Preethi Ashwath has learned to take center stage, talking about the “hearable” and wearable devices she has had a hand in developing as an analog integrated circuit designer in the consumer electronics division at Analog Devices of Wilmington, Mass.

The IEEE member is one of the few women who work in the specialized field, where about 11 percent are female, according to career platform Zippia.

Preethi Ashwath Employer Analog Devices, in BostonTitle Integrated circuit designerMember grade MemberAlma maters SJB Institute of Technology in Bengaluru, India; University of California, Irvine.

SJB Institute of Technology in Bengaluru, India; University of California, Irvine.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, ashwath stepped out from behind the scenes last year to meet with attendees at the consumer electronics show (ces) in las vegas. She demonstrated Analog’s new earbuds, which track people’s heart and lung health through vibrations in their ear canals.

Diungkapkan bahwa after she demonstrated her ability to explain the technology to consumers in simple terms, analog selected her to represent the company at other events. She says she has “come to see speaking as part of contributing to the field, rather than something separate from technical work. ”.

Berdasarkan laporan, she also gives technical talks on various aspects of electrostatic discharge (esd) and other topics, as well as participates in panel discussions, she says, because they “reach engineers well beyond my immediate team. ”.

Ashwath is an active volunteer with the IEEE Circuits and Systems Society.

“Whether through designing semiconductor products, publishing technical articles, reviewing conference papers, or speaking at industry events, I try to contribute to the growth of the engineering community and the advancement of the field,” she says.

Ashwath, who grew up in Bengaluru, India, learned about electronics engineering from her high school physics tutor.

Berdasarkan laporan, that introduction led her to take electronics as one of her core courses in her final years there. At the time, Ashwath’s older sister was pursuing an engineering degree.

“Between my interest in electronics and seeing her already on that path, it became clear to me that engineering was the way to go,” Ashwath says.

Berdasarkan laporan, after earning a bachelor’s degree in electronics and communications engineering at the sjb institute of technology, in bengaluru, she wanted to pursue a career in very-large-scale integration. But that changed once she moved to the United States and began her master’s program in electrical engineering at the University of California, Irvine.

Diungkapkan bahwa she discovered her passion for circuits and devices during an internship at intel in santa clara, calif. She learned about circuit design, package design, and reliability verification tools such as Ansys Totem.

Diungkapkan bahwa “seeing every layer of the chip development process gave me a more complete picture of what goes into building a semiconductor product,” she says. “Through that experience, I realized I felt most connected to design.

Berdasarkan laporan, “it was the hard work and creativity that drew me in. You start with a specification, build a circuit, simulate it, then wait for the chip to come back from fabrication. When your design works, it’s a real feeling of satisfaction. It teaches you patience and perseverance. ”.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, after attaining her master’s degree, she was hired by intel as an analog design engineer. She gained experience in mixed-signal circuit design before joining Analog. In her current role, she works on consumer hearables such as earbuds and wearables including fitness trackers and health monitors.

Her main focus is designing ESD pad rings, the borders of specialized circuits built around a microchip’s outermost edge to protect it from the discharge, which can damage circuit paths or introduce latent defects that lead to failures later in the chip’s life cycle.

Berdasarkan laporan, “on a chip with multiple voltage domains, you have to plan how the protection structures are placed and connected across the whole pad ring—and get it right,” ashwath says. “A mistake there could cause a chip to fail in the field in ways that are very hard to debug afterward.

Sebagaimana diketahui, “it’s detailed work that requires understanding both the device physics and how the whole chip fits together. ”.

Berdasarkan laporan, part of the job is designing and creating an integrated circuit’s building blocks, including esd protection structures and other mixed-signal blocks. Ashwath conducts rigorous checks to verify they work as intended before being integrated into a chip.

She collaborates with ESD advisors, layout designers, and the digital team that designs the chip’s digital logic.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, “i work with them to make sure my analog circuits and their digital blocks work together correctly,” she says. “No two days look exactly the same. ”.

Diungkapkan bahwa in 2024 she was recognized with the company’s impact award for her “exceptional work on a critical project with significant cross-functional business impact. ”.

Ashwath was selected to represent Analog at events after a senior leader encouraged her to ask for high-visibility opportunities, she says.

Diungkapkan bahwa “most of my time is spent on designing circuits and simulations,” she says. “At CES, I stood in front of customers, engineers, and members of the press, explaining our technology and answering questions on the spot. ”.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the earbuds she demonstrated monitor minute vibrations from a user’s heart and lungs, according to the analog website. The vibrations can detect arrhythmia, a leaky heart valve, or fluid in the lungs.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, “hearables are evolving from playing back audio to becoming health-monitoring platforms,” she says. “The ear turns out to be a good location for picking up physiological signals, so these devices can capture vital signs while someone is simply wearing them normally.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, “the hard part is achieving high signal quality. The signals you’re trying to detect are very small and buried in the noise from the person’s movements and the surrounding environment.

Berdasarkan laporan, “that’s where analog front-end design becomes critical. Extracting a meaningful signal from a noisy real-world environment is fundamentally an analog problem. ”.

Being face-to-face with customers at the conference was new to her.

Berdasarkan laporan, “what struck me most was seeing how people react to the technology,” she says. “When you’re designing a block, you’re focused on specifications and margins. At CES, after explaining what the product does, I had a better understanding of why it matters to them.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, “that connection between the circuit work and the final product is something you don’t always see from the design bench. ”.

Berdasarkan laporan, since the ces, ashwath has presented other technologies she’s worked on. , she demonstrated the A2B Automotive Audio Bus to the audio industry. At the annual National Association of Music Merchants show in Anaheim, Calif. The bus uses a low-cost unshielded twisted-pair cable to carry multichannel digital audio, control data, synchronized clock signals, and power in fewer than 50 microseconds, according to Analog.

Sebagaimana diketahui, “ieee connects you with academia, which you don’t get much exposure to once you’re in industry. That connection between industry and academic work is valuable in both directions. ”.

At the company’s Global Technology Conference—an internal event held in Boston that draws engineers from the company’s more than 50 sites around the world—Ashwath led a demonstration of its solutions for augmented reality smart glasses.

Diungkapkan bahwa “each of these events has a different audience,” she says. “Learning to explain my technical work to different people has become a skill I’ve acquired. ”.

The most rewarding part of her job, she says, is seeing the end result of her work.

Berdasarkan laporan, “you spend months on a design, and there’s a long wait between finishing it and finding out whether your instincts were right,” she says. “When the measurements match what you simulated, that’s the most satisfying moment in this job.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, “the other part is knowing my work ends up in a real product. The circuits I design go into devices people actually use every day. ”.

Sebagaimana diketahui, like many engineers, ashwath joined ieee to access research published in the ieee xplore digital library. It keeps her current in a field that keeps moving, she says.

During her first year of membership, in 2021, she discovered other perks including networking and educational opportunities.

Diungkapkan bahwa “ieee connects you to a community outside your own company,” she says. “Attending lectures and technical talks exposes you to approaches and problems you wouldn’t encounter in your own work. ”.

She eventually began seeking out volunteer opportunities, specifically with IEEE conferences and journals, because they are “how you stay current with what’s happening in circuits and systems beyond your own day-to-day work,” she says.

Diungkapkan bahwa “as an analog designer,” she says, “being connected to that broader community matters. The field moves, and you need a way to keep learning from it. ”.

Berdasarkan laporan, she serves as a peer reviewer of papers for several ieee conferences including the ieee international symposium on circuits and systems and the ieee international midwest symposium on circuits and systems. MWSCAS is the oldest U. S. ISCAS is the flagship conference of the IEEE Circuits and Systems Society. conference on the technologies.

Berdasarkan laporan, “someone has to assess whether submitted work is technically sound and worth presenting,” she says, “and that only happens if practicing engineers are willing to put in the time. ”.

The combination of learning from the community and contributing to it is what makes her membership worthwhile, she says.

Diungkapkan bahwa “analog design is a field where you’re always learning. Just when you feel you understand one architecture, there’s another one to learn,” she says. “Being an active learner isn’t optional in this field; it’s the requirement, and being part of the IEEE community helps with that.

“IEEE also connects you with academia, which you don’t get much exposure to once you’re in industry.

Berdasarkan laporan, “reviewing papers means reading what researchers are working on, which is often quite different from how the same problems get approached in a product environment. That connection between industry and academic work is valuable in both directions. ”.

Sebagaimana diketahui, joanna goodrich is the associate editor of the institute, covering the work and accomplishments of ieee members and ieee and technology-related events. She has a master's degree in health communications from Rutgers University, in New Brunswick, N. J.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, if you’re an engineer, you may feel like your skills aren’t commanding the premium they once did. Many engineers have faced layoffs or restructuring. Diungkapkan bahwa “chatgpt answered that in five seconds. Why can’t you?”.

Sebagaimana diketahui, generative ai (and the marketing behind it) gives people the illusion that the work is simpler than it is. A working demo hides complexity, and once someone has a website that works, they may decide they no longer need engineers, or start to distrust the ones they do have.

Diungkapkan bahwa engineers have a unique position in the ai space, because you have the capacity to understand how these models work much better than the average person. Use this to your advantage.

Sebagaimana diketahui, learn how ai models work. You don’t need to become a full-blown AI researcher. Sebagaimana diketahui, teach upward. Turn that knowledge into teaching moments for the people who lead you. Diungkapkan bahwa consider the criticism of today’s processes. Some of what we do has been treated as ceremony for too long. Be willing to say, “you know what, maybe you’re right, this process is too slow for the speed we can work at now. ” Conceding that earns you the credibility to defend the steps that matter.

I still believe that speed at the cost of everything else is harmful—but that’s a topic for another time.

Berdasarkan laporan, find your voice. Engineers at the forefront of AI adoption need to push back and explain why we do things the way we do. Nobody else in the room is going to do it for us.

Berdasarkan laporan, your goal, in my opinion, is to save your organization from buying into the hype so much that they chase the wrong thing. Our job, before and after AI, is building safe and useful products for human beings, and engineers are still best suited for that.

Those visits can be subject to lobbying rules, so the organizers told Jathar that: “You are representing the organization, not your own views. ” He would need to stick to the talking points IEEE-USA had prepared for all its participants, regardless of their specialty, to promote across several congressional offices.

Sebagaimana diketahui, on jathar’s first visit, those organizational talking points included advocating for funding smart grids, authorizing department of energy research, and investing in stem education. IEEE-USA’s priorities didn’t all overlap directly with Jathar’s work, but they were broad enablers of science and technology and, he says, “STEM education funding is close to my heart. That represents one of the trade-offs of access in Washington. ”.

Berdasarkan laporan, anyone can approach their representatives in washington with their personal priorities, jathar notes, but given how pressed for time congressional staff are, they are more likely to prioritize a meeting that represents the views of as many of their constituents as possible. “I could have gone outside the IEEE structure,” Jathar says, but congressional staff “are more likely to listen if you are part of a much bigger organization. ”.

Sebagaimana diketahui, for jathar’s first congressional visit, organizers assigned him to call on the offices of several representatives from both political parties based on where he lives: representatives greg casar (d-texas), lloyd doggett (d-texas), and barry moore (r-ala. “Meeting a staffer or a senior member from their office is good. ). They tend to relate to these issues more than a representative, because a representative has 10 different high-level things they have to worry about whereas the staffer can be more focused on the policy details,” Jathar says.

Sebagaimana diketahui, a typical visit like this may last anywhere from 15 minutes to an hour, so jathar kept his talking points simple and short. You can always bring that out later if they ask more questions. “First and foremost you’re gonna get a very small window,” he says, “Make sure you’ve got everything ready to present in bullet points and not a lot of jargon. ” Simple visual aids, in the form of one-page handouts, may be helpful for communicating numeric or technical information, too.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, “if you leave it to the lobbyists, they’re understandably going to do what’s in their clients’ interests. ”–Staffer for the House Committee on Science, Space, and Technology.

Berdasarkan laporan, the house science committee staffer agrees: “i prefer meetings where people know what they want and know what we’re doing in congress. ” In addition to having a clear request, the staffer says engineers and other advocates should keep track of where Congress is in its cycle: Is it appropriations season, and when is the next budget being set? How far along is a given piece of legislation in the process, and what is realistic to change at that point?.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, during jathar’s 2025 visit to one capitol hill office, he learned firsthand the importance of preparation. For one of the three representatives he visited, staff politely pointed out that the legislator they worked for was not on the committee with jurisdiction over the IEEE-USA talking point they were discussing. “They explained that there are only certain things [the legislator] can do on that issue and that there are other people we need to talk to, to achieve more,” Jathar recalls.

Sebagaimana diketahui, earlier this year, jathar decided to go back to capitol hill with his newfound knowledge, again within the framework of an ieee-usa visit. This time he was able to provide something else legislative staff want from engineers: authoritative technical knowledge.

Diungkapkan bahwa “when i introduced myself as a software developer to one staffer, his first question was, ‘do you think ai will replace coders?’ ” jathar says. The conversation went back and forth, with the staffer asking Jathar and his other engineering companions questions. Jathar went on to explain that his company developed an open-source business-management software it calls ERPClaw, designed to be used with AI agents such as OpenClaw. That led naturally to discussing the role of open source in AI, which plays a role in one of IEEE-USA’s proposals for democratizing AI. This time Jathar was able to align his organization’s advocacy with his expertise and the staffer’s areas of interest.

Berdasarkan laporan, it’s too soon to know what legislative impact that advocacy might have, but it’s the sort of informed, relevant proposal that legislative staff seek out. “The people who build trust have more cachet with congressional staff because they’ve asked for something that’s reasonably thought out,” the House Science Committee staffer says. In turn, congressional staffers can advocate better within their offices for policies brought to them by people they trust.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, and talking about the issues you care the most about can deepen that trust. The House Science Committee staffer once visited Congress as an advocate before switching to the other side of the table. “I was making a pitch that was given to me without a lot of personal buy-in,” the staffer says. Instead, “you should feel emotionally connected to any issue you’re advocating for. On that visit, as on Jathar’s, the professional society organizing the visit provided a pitch. ”.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, jathar’s support for the open-source movement is like that. “We can progress a lot faster,” Jathar says. Open source gives smaller companies a foundation they can adapt and build upon, while allowing other developers to extend that work. “I’m not doing it only because it’s good for my business, but because I feel it’s good for any technological advancement. ”.

Diungkapkan bahwa lucas laursen is the technology policy editor at ieee spectrum. He covers how emerging technologies are changing the balance of power between companies, governments, and individuals. The rest of the time, he worries about his own balance on a bicycle, skis, or the side of a mountain.

I also know that things work somewhat differently in each country--are there readers in India or Germany or Chile who might be able to share their experiences working with lawmakers there?.

10 Hacks Every Reddit User Should Know

Berdasarkan laporan, if you're looking for discussions, recommendations, or advice online, it's hard to avoid reddit. From mainstream sports to niche crafts, it does seem that there's some kind of Reddit community for everyone. (And if there's not one, you can make one yourself. ) If you're using Reddit, here are 10 hacks you should know about to improve your experience on the site.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, reddit used to let everyone view your post and comment history, but in recent years, you can make your profile private. Alternatively, you can follow the direct link to Reddit's profile settings page. If you want to do this, click your profile icon once you've logged in to Reddit, and go to Settings > Profile. You can hide your posts, comments, and the subreddits you're a part of. Click the drop-down menu next to Content & Activity, and select Hide all. You should also turn off Online Status on the same page to stop people from seeing when you're using Reddit.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, old reddit lets you use the site's classic design, and i prefer it to the more modern ui. As long as it's around, you should switch to Old Reddit for a cleaner reading experience. reddit. You can also visit old. It's no wonder that Reddit is making it harder to access this version of the site. You can do that by going to Reddit Settings > Preferences and enabling Default to Old Reddit. Old Reddit looks dated, but it doesn't have infinite scrolling, distracting animations, and a bunch of features designed to increase the time you spend on the platform. com, though you'll need to sign in for access.

Diungkapkan bahwa many subreddits use custom themes that range from beautiful to borderline unusable. If you want a more consistent UI across the site, you should disable these custom subreddit styles. Go to Reddit Settings > Preferences and turn off Use community themes. If you're using Old Reddit, click the preferences button in the top-right corner, and under "display options," disable allow subreddits to show me custom themes.

Sebagaimana diketahui, reddit's social features are useful if you have friends on the site, but in most cases, those features are annoying at best. On the same page, click Who can send you chat requests, and pick Nobody. Go to Reddit Settings > Privacy, and turn off Allow people to follow you. To keep all of this at bay, you should disable the site's social features. If your post or comment goes viral, be prepared to deal with waves of weirdos who find it entertaining to send unsolicited advice or opinions. You can also turn off Show up in search results to remove your profile from Google searches.

Berdasarkan laporan, a multireddit is a feed that shows posts from a customized group of subreddits. To create one, click the Create custom feed button in the left pane in new Reddit. You can think of it as a way to break out of Reddit's algorithms, and create your own Reddit feed. It's a great way to create interest-specific feeds, and if you make them private, no one else can see them. Be sure to select the Private button to keep it from showing up for others. I even have one for gaming, and one for fountain pens. I use multireddits to follow all sports-related subs I'm interested in. In the Old Reddit design, click the Create button in the left pane. You can add as many subreddits as you like to the list, and bookmark the feed to access it whenever you wish to.

Berdasarkan laporan, if you want to reduce reddit's tracking, you should turn off ad personalization. I recommend uBlock Origin, which is one of the best ad blockers you can install, though most can hide Reddit's ads on desktop. To block Reddit's ads altogether, you can use any ad blocker you like. Go to Reddit Settings > Privacy, and turn off Personalize ads. On mobile, you can try using AdGuard or Wipr to hide in-app ads in Reddit.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, reddit has recently adopted an instagram-like experience for its feeds. " If you dislike this change, you can bypass it. I use Reddit on mobile Safari, and I recommend an extension called Sink It for Reddit. , and instead offers "For You" and "Following. It can automatically redirect you to Old Reddit, and there's a feature that optimizes it for mobile, which brings back the old sorting options. It removed the ability to sort posts by new, controversial, best, etc. You can also use third-party apps such as RedReader for Android, or RDX for Reddit on an iPhone or iPad to restore the old sorting options for Reddit posts.

Diungkapkan bahwa reddit doesn't let you sign up without an email address or phone number anymore. This makes it a little annoying to create burner accounts, but it's not impossible. In fact, you can create multiple Reddit accounts with the same email address, as long as you use aliases on Gmail or any other email service of your choice. For more privacy, you can use services that provide disposable email addresses, such as Yopmail.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, after all these years, reddit's built-in search still leaves something to be desired—at least, on the surface. To find posts on Reddit faster, use search filters on the site. For instance, adding "title:" to your search will limit the results to post titles, and boolean operators such as AND, OR, and NOT also work for advanced searches on the site.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, ieee life fellow manfred “fred” j. Schindler has been elected as the 2027 IEEE president-elect. He will begin serving as president on 1 January 2028.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, schindler, who was nominated by the ieee board of directors, received 16,421 votes in the election. Senior Member David Alan Koehler received 13,874 votes.

Diungkapkan bahwa schindler’s top 3 goals as president-elect strengthen ieee’s connection with industry by coordinating events across geography, industry, and technology to revitalize professional activities, especially ones for young professionals. Champion the improvement of IEEE’s digital infrastructure to eliminate manual processes and modernize interfaces. Prioritize the advancement of technology to benefit future generations by expanding and supporting IEEE initiatives and programs.

At press time, the results were unofficial until the IEEE Board of Directors accepts the IEEE Teller’s Committee report in November.

Schindler, an expert in microwave semiconductor technology, is an independent consultant supporting clients with technical expertise, due diligence, and project management.

Berdasarkan laporan, throughout his career, he led the development of microwave integrated-circuit technology, from lab demonstrations to high-volume commercial products. He has numerous technical publications and holds 11 patents.

Sebagaimana diketahui, schindler served as cto of anlotek, and director of qorvo and rfmd’s boston design center. He was applications manager at IBM, engineering manager at ATN Microwave, and a lab manager at Raytheon.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, an ieee volunteer for more than 30 years, schindler served as the 2024 vice president of ieee technical activities and the 2021–2022 division iv director. Walter Cox Award. He received the society’s 2018 Distinguished Service Award and its 2015 N. He was chair of the IEEE Conferences Committee from 2015 to 2018 and president of the IEEE Microwave Theory and Technology Society (MTTS) in 2003. His award-winning micro-business column has appeared in IEEE Microwave Magazine since 2011.

He also led the 2025 One IEEE to Enable Strategic Investments in Innovations and Public Imperative Activities adhoc committee.

Schindler is an IEEE–Eta Kappa Nu member and a MTTS honorary life member.

#352. The Apple Watch's New 'Siri Recap' Feature Is Even Creepier Than I Expected

📅 11 Nov 2026

The Apple Watch's New 'Siri Recap' Feature Is Even Creepier Than I Expected

Tanggal: 11 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://lifehacker.com/tech/apple-watch-new-siri-recap-feature?utm_medium=RSS

Sebagaimana diketahui, the “siri recap” feature that apple announced in september is finally available in a developer beta, and i’ve spent the last 24 hours with the feature turned on. It’s even more unsettling than the “Live Rewind” feature that launched at the same time. It listens to all my conversations, and produces summaries that are both helpful and deeply creepy.

Diungkapkan bahwa i have a button in the watch’s control center that can turn the recapping abilities off, but if i forget to do so, siri listens to everything. I’ll get a recap of my entire evening, presented in roughly hour-long chunks, including things I would have completely forgotten I had even heard about.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the recaps somberly mention silly memes my kids were laughing about, and make major bullet points out of offhand remarks from brief conversations. If a conversation sticks to a single topic, I’ll often get a reasonably good summary of it, with specific facts and numbers highlighted; but just as often, Siri will get confused and mix up several topics or completely mishear a name or phrase.

Apple has four features that it considers part of “audio intelligence":.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, music recognition, better known as shazam. We’ve had a version of this on the Apple Watch for a long time now, although it has some improvements and now identifies music automatically.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, sound recognition, which can notify you about doorbells and babies crying. A version of this launched in 2020 as an accessibility feature.

Live Rewind, which gives you an on-wrist transcript of the last 15 seconds of detected speech.

Siri Recaps, which summarizes entire conversations for you to read on your phone.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, live rewind had the flashiest demo from the apple event: a server rattled off the day’s specials at a restaurant, and then the apple watch-wearing diner checked his watch to see a readout of exactly which dishes had just been mentioned. The utility is both obvious and kind of unnecessary: Why wouldn’t you just ask the server to repeat the list while they’re standing right there?.

Diungkapkan bahwa i haven’t found myself using live rewind, except out of curiosity about how the feature works. I discovered that it doesn’t pick up song lyrics very well, and also that by the time I think to check what was just said in a conversation, more than 15 seconds has passed since the part I was unsure about. I haven’t yet found a reason to use it for real.

Berdasarkan laporan, but siri recaps? those are both useful and unsettling. We stopped by the library, and along the way we chatted about a variety of things: holiday travel plans, library policies, and the possibility of humans living in space in the future. I enabled the feature, and decided to test it out later. But since it was on, it dutifully listened in as I picked up my son from school and gave him an update on an ailing family member’s health. Siri was listening to it all.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, at least for now, the feature is only available in a developer beta, so sign up for that now if you want to try it. (I have a 16 Pro, so I'm good. You'll need an Apple Watch Series 12 (or Ultra 4) and an iPhone 16 or better, excluding the 16e. ).

Diungkapkan bahwa after you're updated to 27. You'll need to set a passcode on your watch, and you'll be guided through a step to upgrade your audio connection. , if you want it on for the work day but off for the evening). to 5 p. m. 3, go into the Watch app, tap Siri, and turn on Siri Recap. The control center on the watch will have a button you can use to turn Siri recaps on and off at will. m. You can set a schedule for when it should listen (for example, 9 a. To read your recaps, go to the Siri app on your phone.

Sebagaimana diketahui, as promised, the recaps do not identify speakers. This is probably good for privacy and for relationships; there’s no way to prove that your spouse said such-and-such exact thing. They do not contain an exact transcript, and there is no way to listen to a recording to check what exactly was said. I can also tell people I am not recording them, and technically be correct.

Berdasarkan laporan, but still: i feel weird publishing the contents of these recaps, because they do contain things that people said to me in what they assumed was a private setting. I’m not sure if the watch was unable to hear us over the music, or if Siri is programmed not to listen when music is being played. (Interestingly, it did not recap any of the quiet conversations I had with fellow sopranos while the tenors were rehearsing their part. I had the feature on when I attended a choir practice, and Siri recapped the brief chats I had with other choir members before and after practice. ).

Sebagaimana diketahui, because speakers aren’t identified, it seems siri doesn’t know what to do when there is a disagreement. But when my son and I disagreed about how likely space colonization might be in the future, the recap didn’t reflect the separate positions that were put forth. A human note-taker would jot down that Person A made a point in favor of something, and person B made a point against. It summarized the conversation as including “debating the feasibility and timeline of human space colonization and asteroid mining,” which isn’t exactly accurate, but close enough.

Sebagaimana diketahui, when it comes to the content of the discussion, the recap notes a bullet point of “skepticism regarding permanent space colonies within the next 100 years. ” It didn’t include my reasons for being skeptical, and didn’t mention my son’s opposing viewpoint at all. If I were using this recap to jog my memory of the conversation, it wouldn’t be all that helpful.

Sebagaimana diketahui, details are sometimes egregiously incorrect. Names in general seem to be a problem; I recommended a book to my son, and the recap includes notes about the content of the book, but not its title. ” The family member we discussed is not anybody’s father. After a discussion about a family member’s health, the recap had notes on the prognosis of “father. The book’s author appears in the introduction to the recap (sort of a summary of a summary), but not in the content of the recap itself where the book is mentioned.

Diungkapkan bahwa i should probably turn siri recaps off. It seems wrong to let people chat with me without letting them know that their conversation is being. well, not technically recorded, but basically recorded.

Berdasarkan laporan, but it’s so tempting to leave it on so that i can review my day. Some of the details in the recaps are useful, like the dates that were discussed as options for a holiday party. The recaps will be deleted in about a week (unless I save them to the notes app), so if I want to remind myself of a conversation a few days ago, I should be able to scroll back through my recaps and find it.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, i would be a fool to rely on the recaps, though. Specific details can be wrong, as I mentioned. The most important points of a conversation are often left out; Siri doesn’t know what’s actually important, and there’s no way to guide it as to what to pay attention to. There’s also no way to control when a “conversation” starts or stops, unless you are turning the recap feature on and off from the watch.

Berdasarkan laporan, and there’s more: not only are names usually omitted (wait, who did she say i should ask about that project?), the few identifiers that make it into the recap, like names of events, are often wrong. About all the recap could usefully do is to remind me that something about AP U. The recap got all of these things mixed up with each other and was wrong about pretty much every detail. S. Subjects of discussion are often conflated in really unhelpful ways: My husband mentioned paying for certain course registrations for one of our children, and later I talked to that child about an unrelated exam. History was discussed. Reading the recaps can be like reliving your day entirely in the passive voice.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, it’s not just you. Microsoft’s 365 business and enterprise services suffered a major outage on Thursday, preventing users of its popular cloud suite from accessing their accounts.

Berdasarkan laporan, around 10:40 am et on thursday, microsoft posted on its 365 status page on x that it was “investigating reports of users experiencing issues when accessing or using microsoft teams functionality in north america. ” By just before 1 pm ET, it said it was aware of “issues accessing Exchange Online mailboxes through multiple connection methods in the Americas. ”.

Microsoft later said that its network was also “experiencing elevated load across multiple regions, which is likely contributing to the connectivity errors,” but that the issue was related to servers going offline, not due to increased traffic.

Sebagaimana diketahui, around an hour later, microsoft said it had “begun redistributing connection traffic across our broader worldwide infrastructure to help balance the load” and was “aggressively pursuing all pathways to reduce impact. ”.

Berdasarkan laporan, “we've paused all deployments. We're moving additional traffic off the affected infrastructure, and we're restarting affected servers to return them to service,” Microsoft wrote.

In an update on its status page, Microsoft said impacted services may include Exchange Online, Microsoft Teams, SharePoint Online, Microsoft Copilot 365, and Microsoft Defender XDR.

Diungkapkan bahwa “we are aware and investigating reports of users experiencing issues with microsoft 365 services, primarily issues with exchange online,” a microsoft spokesperson tells wired in a statement. “We appreciate our customer's patience while we work to restore services as soon as possible. ”.

Outage reports on the service uptime tracking website Downdetector began falling around 1:15 pm ET after a large spike in users reporting issues with Outlook and other Microsoft 365 products around noon.

Diungkapkan bahwa it is currently unclear when the outage may be over or what its cause may be. In a status update on X posted just before 3 pm ET, Microsoft said “a problem” was “causing servers to fail automated health checks and become unavailable” but that it was attempting to reboot its systems to hopefully bring them back online.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, outages in cloud services occur frequently, and their causes can vary. Configuration errors, resolution issues with the Domain Name System, and cyberattacks can all cause connection errors. There is currently no indication that a cyberattack caused the current Microsoft outage.

Berdasarkan laporan, while major microsoft outages are relatively rare, they are far from unprecedented. In July 2024, a corrupted update from the security firm CrowdStrike caused the “blues screen of death” on Windows machines around the world, while a separate but nearly simultaneous outage knocked out Microsoft Azure services for hours, causing untold millions of dollars in lost revenue due to companies’ inability to function as normal.

#356. How Wikipedia’s Editors Keep the Online Encyclopedia Human-Written

📅 21 Oct 2026

How Wikipedia’s Editors Keep the Online Encyclopedia Human-Written

Tanggal: 21 Oct 2026 | Sumber: https://spectrum.ieee.org/wikipedia-wikiproject-ai-writing-cleanup

AI-generated text is harder to spot, but that hasn’t deterred them.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, eliza strickland is ieee spectrum's features editor. She also covers AI and biomedical engineering.

Ellia Lebleu is a cofounder of the WikiProject AI Cleanup effort to keep Wikipedia human-written.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, ellia lebleu is a founding member of the wikiproject ai cleanup, a volunteer effort launched in 2023 to find and remove ai-generated material from wikipedia that breaks the website’s guidelines. When the cleanup began, AI writing was often betrayed by conspicuous clichés. Today, the project’s volunteers are developing tools to detect subtler forms of machine-generated content and debating AI’s role in the world’s most widely used encyclopedia.

When did you realize Wikipedia had a problem with AI-generated material?.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, ellia lebleu: it was around december 2023. A few other editors and I were chatting on Wikipedia’s Discord server, and we had all seen very strange articles with the same odd characteristics. ” They sometimes had conclusion sections, or sections called “Why is this important?” That was very typical of ChatGPT in 2023 and early 2024 but very odd for Wikipedia articles—and very easy to spot. They repeated phrases like “stands as a testament” or “rich cultural heritage. Then I decided, let’s create an official project on Wikipedia so more people can deal with this.

Diungkapkan bahwa ellia lebleu ellia lebleu is a founding member of the wikiproject ai cleanup. D. Lebleu is pursuing a Ph. in AI at the Inria Center of the University of Rennes, part of France’s national research institute for digital science and technology.

Diungkapkan bahwa ellia lebleu is a founding member of the wikiproject ai cleanup. D. Lebleu is pursuing a Ph. in AI at the Inria Center of the University of Rennes, part of France’s national research institute for digital science and technology.

How do editors spot AI-generated writing today?.

Sebagaimana diketahui, lebleu: by 2025, the signs of ai writing were becoming subtler and more structural. For example, AI loves the “rule of three,” negative parallelisms, and other structures of speech that aren’t conclusive by themselves but become meaningful as they accumulate. We also look beyond the article. If someone writes five articles of thousands of words each in 5 minutes, there is reason to suspect AI.

Does the AI problem just appear in the main text, or also in citations?.

Berdasarkan laporan, lebleu: fake or misleading citations have become a major worry. More often, it finds a real source but gets its content completely wrong. Sometimes an AI hallucinates a citation entirely, although that’s much rarer today because of retrieval-augmented generation that allows the AI to find sources. AI citations that don’t actually support what is being written are extremely commonplace.

Berdasarkan laporan, english wikipedia recently prohibited editors from using llms to generate articles. How much AI-generated content is still getting through?.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, lebleu: i’ve been working with [ai-detection company] pangram to estimate the proportion of ai-generated content. I tested it on Wikipedia content from before ChatGPT and found no false positives, so its results provide a very conservative lower bound. In early 2026, that went down to 15 or 16 percent. In late 2025, it flagged perhaps 20 percent of new articles and drafts as AI-generated. But we don’t yet know whether that’s because our recent policies have had an effect or because models are getting more powerful and Pangram hasn’t had time to adapt.

Berdasarkan laporan, lebleu: another wikipedia editor has made an ai source verifier, which goes through the sources on a page and checks whether they match the claims. But if you want something that works at scale and filters out obvious cases, it’s a good first step. Since it is itself an AI model, there is no guarantee that it will be correct every time. The Wikimedia Foundation is also working on a tool called Paste Check, which can flag text pasted directly from some AI chatbots.

Berdasarkan laporan, and we’ve seen claude sometimes say, “i can’t write a wikipedia article; it would go against wikipedia’s policies. ” If all major AI companies implemented that kind of prompt refusal, it wouldn’t solve the problem entirely, because there are still open-weight models that can be tweaked to avoid restrictions. But it would help with people who use commercial models and aren’t especially familiar with the technology.

Can you tell if the rule prohibiting AI writing is working?.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, lebleu: it’s still a little early to tell. But again, we don’t yet know if that is because models are getting better or because beginners are learning the rules. We see possible effects, such as prompt refusal and the apparent slight drop in AI-generated content. The vast majority of AI-generated content is submitted by beginner editors, so we’ve made many efforts to make the rule very visible in welcome messages, editing help, and advice.

What if AI becomes capable of writing truly reliable Wikipedia articles?.

Berdasarkan laporan, lebleu: that’s one of the big questions we’re facing. When the guideline was passed, it was for very practical reasons: We were flooded with AI content, we didn’t have good tools, and we needed to put a stop to it. Many people have called Wikipedia “the last good place on the internet. But since then, it has taken on a more philosophical dimension. ” Being a place that was, in theory, free from AI slop has become part of Wikipedia’s identity.

Berdasarkan laporan, a lot of wikipedia’s communication is now centered on the idea that we’re a human-written encyclopedia. Even AI companies find that interesting. It can be valuable to have a purely human-written corpus on which to [train] AI systems. The fact that Wikipedia is still that, and will remain that for at least the near future, makes it a precious resource that isn’t replicated anywhere else.

But will the people who read and contribute to Wikipedia want it to become partially AI-generated if that makes it more comprehensive? We could preserve Wikipedia’s identity as a human-written corpus while also offering an AI-assisted option.

Has Wikipedia reckoned with the idea of “Google Zero”—a possible future in which websites no longer get traffic from Google search?.

Sebagaimana diketahui, lebleu: if everything goes through ai search and websites plummet to zero visibility, how do we expose wikipedia and show that it can be edited and that people can still contribute? wikipedia is frequently cited in [google’s] ai overviews, but users may only see an ai answer citing wikipedia. They may not realize that Wikipedia is a living project they can edit and contribute to.

Berdasarkan laporan, the wikimedia foundation is working on an attribution framework that could give ai users more information about the article [being cited]: when it was last edited, how comprehensive it is, whether editors have flagged problems, and perhaps even a call to action. In the future, readers might even contribute through AI models: “The AI cited Wikipedia, but there seems to be an error. Can I make an edit request and add this other source I found?”.

Berdasarkan laporan, i can see a very strong symbiotic relationship between wikipedia and ai models in the future. Yesterday, AI was something to clean up. I don’t see Wikipedia disappearing, but I can see it taking a very different shape. Today, it’s a tool to help us with the cleanup. Tomorrow, it will be the air we breathe.

Diungkapkan bahwa a condensed version of this article appears in the november 2026 print issue as “ellia lebleu. ”.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, eliza strickland is ieee spectrum's features editor, where she helps develop and shape the magazine’s longform stories. She also oversees Spectrum's coverage of artificial intelligence and biomedical engineering. She holds a master’s degree in journalism from Columbia University.

Sebagaimana diketahui, i feel like all of us human writers are going to have to grapple with ai-mediated readers, whether we use the ai to augment our content or our readers use ai to engage with our writing. Here's to figuring out together how to ensure our words still shine through the AI layer.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, ai slop is a small problem for wikipedia. The bigger problem is very biased editing on anything with even minimal political implication. And that's a human problem, not AI.
