#357. Turning a 22-year-old Postgres type-confusion primitive into RCE

📅 09 Nov 2026

Turning a 22-year-old Postgres type-confusion primitive into RCE

Tanggal: 09 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://mehmetince.net/part-3-6-how-i-ended-up-turning-a-22-year-old-postgresql-type-confusion-primitive-into-rce-cve-2026-6460/

If you had told me in April 2026 one question “Mehmet, can we use managed PostgreSQL for this project?” would send me into the deepest rabbit hole of my life, I would have laughed.

Berdasarkan laporan, months later, i finally found the bottom of that rabbit hole. It was a 22-year-old zero-day in PostgreSQL core.

In this blog post you will read a story of how I ended up uncovering a new class of type-confusion vulnerabilities in PostgreSQL.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, this is the 3rd part of blog post series named “systemic risks in the managed postgresql industry”. For those who have missed the first two part, feel free to start from 1st and 2nd which will give you a complete context of this madness.

Diungkapkan bahwa i gave postgresql a value inside a composite type, changed the type of one of its fields, and asked it to read the value back. That type confusion led to one of the most reliable memory-corruption exploit I have seen. But I did not start by looking for a PostgreSQL core vulnerability.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, i was exploiting pg_clickhouse, and getting that exploit to work left me with a question about how postgresql understands its own data. With an AI agent as my teacher, I worked through the internals one question at a time. Then a seemingly unrelated conversation gave me the idea that connected it all, and eventually I found myself staring at a primitive that had been there for for awhile.

This is the full true story of how those pieces came together, I am sure you will enjoy this story.

Sebagaimana diketahui, during june and july, i had been exploiting memory-corruption vulnerabilities across several postgresql extensions. One of the extensions that I achieved code execution was pg_clickhouse. That case study has its own story, which I will share in the future.

Berdasarkan laporan, what matters here is what that exploit forced me to learn. A ClickHouse Array is not a PostgreSQL array, right ? So the extension had to rebuild its elements as Datum values in the format that PostgreSQL expected. pg_clickhouse translates ClickHouse values into native PostgreSQL values. A mistake in that conversion was what eventually gave me a code execution.

Sebagaimana diketahui, this was my first time meeting with things like datum, oids etc in the postgresql universe. I learned only enough to finish the exploit, but one question remained in the back of my mind:.

How does PostgreSQL itself decide what a value is? And how does it process and represent it?.

Somewhere around late July, I finally got my head out of the extensions and just followed that question into PostgreSQL core.

Disclaimer: I reported pg_clickhouse oob write + read chain to the vendor and they fixed it at Jun 23.

Sebagaimana diketahui, i started learning with a very simple query. What happens when I run the simplest query SELECT 1337?.

While I avoided all the black magic in Postgres internals, I kept this crash course on the basics of data types.

Diungkapkan bahwa the database scanner looks at the query, recognises select as a keyword, and 1337 as an integer token. Then it creates a parse tree for the query. Next, PostgreSQL walks the tree and transforms it into a typed query tree.

Berdasarkan laporan, parse tree looks like above. But I just wanted to better understand things like what is the consttype 23 ? why constvalue has [ 57 5 0 0 0 0 0 0 ]  and where is my 1337 value ? At this point, I asked Opus 5 to prepare me a full deep-dive course on PostgreSQL types. Spending a few days around there and talking with my agent, whom I named pg_expert taught me these:.

constvalue 4 [ 57 5 0 0 0 0 0 0 ] can be converted to hexadecimal, making the value easier to recognize:.

On my little-endian system, the bytes were stored least-significant first:.

Berdasarkan laporan, so 1337 had not disappeared. But why do we even have 8 bytes [ 57 5 0 0 0 0 0 0 ] instead of simply 4 bytes ?.

Diungkapkan bahwa that was because constvalue was not declared as an int32. It was declared as a Datum, which was 8 bytes Our value 1337::int4 value stored at the lower four bytes of that generic carrier.

How can that same 8-byte Datum represent a text, an array, or custom types ?.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, chatting with my pg_expert agent taught me more. A Datum does NOT know what it represents.

Berdasarkan laporan, the eight bytes carrying 1337 did not contain a hidden label saying “i am an integer. ”. PostgreSQL knew its type only because of this consttype = 23.

That number is an OID (Object IDentifiers) pointing to a row in the pg_type system catalog.

Sebagaimana diketahui, that means the pg_type row shows what the value means and how postgresql will use it. So far, it’s brilliant and easy to understand. But what about the text type ?.

Sebagaimana diketahui, for text, typlen = -1 means that the representation have a variable length. And typbyval = false means that the Datum carried a pointer.

Berdasarkan laporan, so the same 8-byte value stores a memory address for the text. Datum can pass the value either by value itself or by reference to it. Nice, I love the elegant abstraction Datums provides!.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, so far everything makes sense, but i wanted to better understand the  typinput and typoutput columns too. These functions convert the value provided by the query into a native Datum or vice versa. So I ran this again.

But then I added quotation marks to see if PostgreSQL has dynamic type casting/recognition or something:.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, i was a bit confused at this moment. I initially thought unknown meant “PostgreSQL does not know the type. ” So I went back to chatting with my pg_expert agent, who is teaching me everything so far. I learned that unknown is an actual PostgreSQL type with OID 705, used for string literals whose final type hasn’t been decided yet!.

Again, this makes super sense because PostgreSQL deliberately assigns untyped string literals this temporary type because the same text could eventually become many different things!.

Diungkapkan bahwa for example, the query supplies the target type int4. PostgreSQL looked up the typinput function for int4 and called int4in() and when its need to be printer it use int4out().

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, up until this point, typinput and typoutput looked like ordinary conversion mechanism to me. pg_type contained many different native functions for many different types.

Sebagaimana diketahui, while learning more about these functions, one detail stayed with me. An output function did not inspect a Datum and discover its type. It simply trusted all the values and flags around the Datum.

Diungkapkan bahwa int4out() extracted an integer because postgresql had already selected it as the output function for int4. A different output function could interpret the same generic carrier according to completely different rules.

I still remember that, at that very moment, I was actually thinking about the TOCTOU Vulnerabilities class of the web apps I have been exploiting/fixing for years and years.

“What if I could somehow change the type between the moment PostgreSQL constructed a value and the moment it used that value?”.

Diungkapkan bahwa if i can do this, we might be able to force postgresql to process a datum created for a completely different type as if it were the type the function expects. Having a type confusion in PostgreSQL can actually give me an opportunity to abuse all the other functions in PostgreSQL internals.

Berdasarkan laporan, so i went back to learning more about what i can use to force postgresql to natively call different types’ output functions for my int4 value. It turns out that the LANGUAGE internal feature can be used for that purpose.

Diungkapkan bahwa the language internal allows a superuser to create an sql function pointing to native code already compiled into postgresql. I created the following one.

Sebagaimana diketahui, then i gave it the same int4 value. and my local-backend crashed!.

I’m pretty sure the PostgreSQL experts reading this wouldn’t be surprised by this crash, but it surprised me a lot!.

Berdasarkan laporan, it sent me in a completely different direction. I built a working exploit using this type-confusion feature to exploit LANGUAGE internal against security extensions deployed by managed PostgreSQL providers. That research eventually became a part of the Part 2 story.

For a while, I moved on and left this type-confusion question behind.

Roughly two weeks later, something completely unrelated brought me back to it.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, let me take a small detour. This Postgres article series is all about telling you my story in the end, isnt it ?.

I do not remember the exact date, but during one of our runs or walks, my partner Bilge (Staff Machine Learning Engineer at EDB) and I were discussing second-order SQL injection in the PostgreSQL AI extensions and the possibility of tricking AI features of these extensions to hallucinate and produce malicious SQL queries.

That conversation led to chatting about prepared statements.

I first learned about SQL injection around 2005, and God knows how many times I have exploited it since.

Twenty years later, most libraries and frameworks still rely heavily on string escaping to generate secure SQL queries, even though RDBMSs have a beautiful feature named prepared statements.

Berdasarkan laporan, i studied them when i was a uni student, mostly to see what could still be exploited even if the target app uses prepared statements. Things like triggering excessive SQL cold parsing and stuff like that.

But more importantly, for years I taught SQL Injection to thousands of my trainees with this concept:.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, “knowledge is knowing a tomato is a fruit; wisdom is not putting it in a fruit salad. ”.

Sebagaimana diketahui, in my version, the sql query is the recipe and the values are the ingredients. Prepared statements let the database understand the recipe first, then receive the ingredients separately. So even a value like ' OR 1=1 -- may look evil, but it remains data and never gets the chance to rewrite the query.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, i had always seen this separation as a security feature. Databases can finish all the parsing first and wait for me to execute it. But this time, I noticed something in the middle of the convo with Bilge. Before execution, I can run whatever query I want.

I can alter types before executing the query!.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, so the idea is simple; i could prepare a query, change something, and execute it later. But change what? PostgreSQL is not gonna let me redefine what the built-in types int4, text, or UUID mean.

Diungkapkan bahwa i was not thinking about composite types at this point. Honestly, I barely knew what they were. I asked Claude agent pg_expert a much simpler question:.

Which PostgreSQL types can I create, use inside a prepared query, and then alter it before running execute ?.

Sebagaimana diketahui, that question led me to composite types. In PostgreSQL, a composite type represents the structure of a row. It is essentially a custom, user-defined data type that acts as a container for multiple fields, each with its own name and data type. [1, 2].

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, it had its own type oid, but its attributes defined the current row layout. I can change the attribute a type from UUID to another type without replacing the composite type itself.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, i created a one-field composite where the attribute started as uuid. Then I prepared a query, changed that attribute to bytea, and executed the prepared statement.

I knew I had found exactly the kind of type confusion I had been looking for!.

I knew this was no longer a superuser-only LANGUAGE internal behaviour I had exploited before.

Diungkapkan bahwa i knew that i could trigger this crash as a lowest-privileged login role on any postgresql instance. Probably all the Postgres-compatible offerings too (more about this later).

Diungkapkan bahwa last but not least, i already knew that controlled uuid bytes reaching the wrong native consumer, bytea in my case, had serious exploitation potential. These two have the most reliable exploit primitive I have seen in the PostgreSQL exploits.

Before diving into the Hacking PostgreSQL internals, we need to learn a few things about PostgreSQL to better understand the rest of the article!.

Sebagaimana diketahui, bytea is postgresql’s data type for storing arbitrary binary data. Internally, it uses a variable-length representation called varlena. PostgreSQL places a small header before the bytes to describe their size and storage format.

The header tells PostgreSQL which representation it is looking at and how large the complete value is.

Diungkapkan bahwa we do not need to understand every varlena representation. For the rest of this article, we only need to know two things.

Sebagaimana diketahui, for example, a normal inline example of the five ascii characters hello. That 24 can be decoded as 0x24 >> 2 which is 9. So 4-byte header + 5-byte payload = 9 bytes!.

Diungkapkan bahwa the most important example, external representation, when header starts with 01 postgresql believes the value is not stored inline at all. Instead, it treats the bytes as a reference to an expanded object somewhere in memory.

So the following data after the header is just object reference pointer instead of the data itself.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the uuid i supplied contained exactly sixteen bytes, starting with 01 and 02. While attribute a was still UUID, there was nothing special about 01 02 or the fourteen zero bytes following it. They were simply controlled UUID data.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, alter type changed the current definition of attribute key from uuid to bytea, but it did not convert or rewrite the binary value already stored by the prepared query. During EXECUTE, PostgreSQL still had exactly the same bytes.

Diungkapkan bahwa when we execute the query, postgresql need to return the value of our type pg_temp. poc, in order to do that, it calls the composite output function, record_out().

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, so record_out() looks at the  pg_temp. poc’s attribute key and says ‘That is bytea’ and selects byteaout().

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, but the data  byteaout()  takes is our old uuid bytes that we can control. This is where the type confusion happens!.

All of these means, we can literally create any varlena representation we want by fully controlling the headers and following 12 byte!.

PostgreSQL thinks it needs to reach the ExpandedObjectHeader but its address is 00000000 because thats what we have written inside the UUID, therefore local-backend crash.

Diungkapkan bahwa before byteaout() could print the value, it first needed to convert this external representation into something it can print. I learned that PostgreSQL calls this process detoasting.

Berdasarkan laporan, when we run execute pc_crash, the call path is as follows. The relevant path looked like this.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, postgresql then passed the null pointer to eoh_get_flat_size(). The important line inside that function was effectively:.

Sebagaimana diketahui, eohptr is what we influence and we choose 00000000 in our poc, which is a null. Therefore PostgreSQL crashed while trying to read its eoh_methods pointer because it believed it had received a valid external expanded object and followed the normal code path to process it.

The exploitation idea: replacing NULL with our fake object that could make PostgreSQL follow to our own choosen methods!.

ExpandedObjectMethods contains two native function pointers.

Normal code uses those methods like this to convert an expanded object into its flat representation whenever it’s needed.

Diungkapkan bahwa this is not normally an attacker-controlled callback interface. These are trusted internal representations created by PostgreSQL. The output functions can assume the pointer, header, and methods table are not malicious.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, these are indirect native function calls. PostgreSQL obtains the function addresses from the object’s methods table and then calls them. That is something we can actually use to change the control-flow path.

Diungkapkan bahwa before going further, i needed a simple model for the objects involved. I named the two fake objects according to what they represented.

So our plan is that the UUID pointed to H, H pointed to M, and M contained the native function addresses that we wanna cal.

Berdasarkan laporan, the important detail is that postgresql used h twice. Lets remember the actual C code.

First, it treated H as an ExpandedObjectHeader and read the eoh_methods pointer at offset +0x08.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, that pointer led to m, where we had placed the address of system(). PostgreSQL then called the selected method and passed the original object pointer, H, as its first argument.

In other words, H helped PostgreSQL find system(), and then the same H was handed to system() as its parameter.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, fortunately, the first eight bytes of h came before the eoh_methods pointer. I could place the NULL-terminated command id>x in those bytes while keeping the address of M at offset +0x08.

Diungkapkan bahwa as i have heavily talked about exploiting extensions vulnerabilities on managed-postgres providers at part 1, we dont get to read /proc/self/mem due to hardening. Our exploitation plan is very clear but the challenge is we need to leak addresses of these objects.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, i started to chatting with my pg_expert to find more about postgresql operation that could return a pointer-valued data while sql expected an ordinary integer. The moment I prompted the agent, it went to.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, “oh actually we have talk about this during pg_clickhouse exploit back in july. Do you remember the ClickHouse Array is not a PostgreSQL Array ?”.

Sebagaimana diketahui, it was a twist of fate. I had ended up exactly where the original idea had started.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, postgresql arrays store their element type inside their binary representation. unnest() trusts that internal type when deciding how to extract each element.

The array says its element is text, so unnest() returns a pointer-valued text Datum and SQL processes it as text.

But what if the array internally says text, while the surrounding SQL contract says bigint ?.

Because text is passed by reference, unnest() returns a Datum containing the memory address of the text value! But the surrounding SQL expression expects a by-value bigint, so PostgreSQL prints those same pointer bits as an integer.

In other to say this, we can exploit exactly same type confusion vulnerability to alter the arrays’ text element type to bigint so that unnest() will return the memory address instead of the value! aka leaking memory address!.

Diungkapkan bahwa the smallest postgresql array needs 48 bytes. A single UUID gives a 16 controlled bytes. So we can simply combine 3 UUIDs next to each other to build exactly 48 byte fully controlled data structer!.

Berdasarkan laporan, the animation above shows how three uuids become one 48-byte array carrier. I prepare those bytes while all three attributes are still UUIDs. From there, I exploit the same type confusion for only the first UUID a to bigint[]!.

Berdasarkan laporan, so unnest() extracts the element as text and returns its pointer, while sql expects a bigint and exposes that pointer as a memory address. The final +4 skips the text header and lands on my controlled payload.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, a direct text to bigint confusion would only reinterpret the old text bytes as an integer. The array was important because it forced PostgreSQL to first produce a real pointer and then expose those same pointer bits as a bigint.

Berdasarkan laporan, once i have reached that point, i started thinking about different scenarios of where we can alter the attribute types before execution. All the other possible ways of keeping the old value alive.

I found the same underlying mistake around RowExpr, JSON conversion caches and different places.

9 November 2026 The PostgreSQL security commits landed as part of a much larger release containing 52 new CVE.

6 of those 52 CVEs are directly connected to this article.

The reason why I have fallen into that rabbit hole 5 months ago was because I needed to better understand the how managed-database industry works before making a decision because at the end of the day, we all can outsource the infrastructure but we can not outsource the risk.

When the vulnerability belongs to PostgreSQL core, how does the industry coordinate to protect its own customers?.

So I ported the my locally working exploit to almost every managed PostgreSQL platform I know and privately shared reproducible PoCs with their security teams.

I haven’t seen any vendor who is not affected by this vulnerability! including those who has Postgres compatible offering.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, databricks security team engineers validated all the exploits immediately. Thanks to Aaron and his team.

Sebagaimana diketahui, google escalated the alloydb reports to its highest priority p0. I am genuinely grateful of all the support from Google Cloud VRP team since day one!.

Berdasarkan laporan, supabase team received the full details around mid august. Thanks to endless support from the Etienne since I first contacted him.

Diungkapkan bahwa ubicloud members reached out to me after my part 1 article published and then they introduced me with the clickhouse team. Both parties are also read in somewhere at end of August.

AWS Aurora/RDS and Microsoft Azure PostgreSQL teams received the reports and working PoC at mid August.

Berdasarkan laporan, but what i respected the most is that some vendors brought their most senior engineering members to start implementing their own mitigation. They did not want to leave customers exposed while waiting for the upstream release cycle.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, i spent 20 years of my life around security communities around the globe. eu this year was quite suprized me. But I really need to say that the support, positive approach and the respect I have seen my time at PGCONF. Have no idea PostgreSQL community at europe has such a family kind vibe.

Diungkapkan bahwa after my talk “nobody gets to be superuser (until i broke in)” at pgconf. eu last month Valencia, I have received amazing support from everyone, specially the respected members of the community who are effortlessly fixing these vulnerabilities whenever someone sends an email to the securit@ address.

Diungkapkan bahwa i owe so much of where i am today to open source. Being able to contribute to PostgreSQL and its ecosystem in my own way means a lot to me. I’ve spent my life learning by hacking things, understanding how they work, and making them more secure. Seeing those contributions so warmly welcomed means even more.

My talk this year was not recorded upon my request, but I receive a lot of invitation from different countries for their local PostgreSQL meetups.

If you’d like to hear the whole story, I’ll be presenting the 90 minutes edition of it at the Prague PostgreSQL Meetup on Monday, 30 November.

Diungkapkan bahwa come join me. I PROMISE IT’LL BE WORTH IT!https://cloomba. com/e/prague-postgresql-meetup-8-2026-11-30.

Diungkapkan bahwa (if you’ve made it this far, i’d love to hear your thoughts! feel free to leave a comment or ask me anything. ).

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the mutable-row-type primitive dates to commit 077db40fa1f3, introduced on may 5, 2004 with alter table. ALTER COLUMN. TYPE.

Berdasarkan laporan, the exploitation technique i used relies on commit 1dc5ebc9077a, introduced on may 14, 2015, which added expanded-object pointers and their native method callbacks. Later than many other primitives I discovered during exploiting 20+ variants.

Sebagaimana diketahui, i am not claiming that cve-2026-6460 is exclusively “my vulnerability. ” PostgreSQL treated it as an umbrella issue covering a much wider family of composite-type problems. Its commit credits many researchers whose reports may have involved overlapping discoveries, separate variants, or completely different journeys into the same systemic weakness.

Diungkapkan bahwa that is the reality of vulnerability research in the age of ai. This article only tells the story of how I reached it without any cyber enabled models back in August 2026.

#358. 10 Movies Like ‘Interstellar’ You Should Watch Next

10 Movies Like ‘Interstellar’ You Should Watch Next

Jeff Somers is a freelancer who has been writing about writing, books, personal finance, and home maintenance since 2012.

Diungkapkan bahwa jeff has published nine novels and more than 70 short stories; his story ringing the changes was selected for inclusion in the best american mystery stories 2006. He holds a bachelor’s degree in English and previously worked in medical publishing as a production editor.

Sebagaimana diketahui, when not writing, jeff spends his free time fixing up his old house. He has tackled a wide range of DIY projects, including remodeling a bathroom entirely on his own in two weeks, and building a roof deck that hasn't fallen down yet. You can find him on Bluesky.

This is Streamalikes, where you can find a curated list of recommendations to stream based on what you already like.

Berdasarkan laporan, christopher nolan’s 2014 megahit interstellar has it all: big sci-fi ideas, cool robots, ugly crying, and a matt damon character in need of rescuing. Grounded in the intensity of the human experience, this story of humanity’s potential extinction and the sacrifice of one man to save it doesn’t just deliver exotic planets and thrilling spaceship maneuvers; it also provides all the feels as Joseph Cooper (Matthew McConaughey) sacrifices everything he has in an effort to save the entire human race. It’s one of the best science fiction films ever made, with Nolan’s signature complexity, time manipulations, and emotional wallop. If you love this movie, here are ten more that offer a similar viewing experience.

Diungkapkan bahwa if you loved both the special effects in interstellar that make space travel feel viscerally thrilling (and terrifying) and the mind-blowing concepts, this is the film for you. Clarke) traces humanity’s development from mildly smart apes to spacefaring capitalists who discover a mysterious obelisk on the Moon that sparks a mission to Jupiter. While it operates in a colder emotional key than Nolan’s film, 2001: A Space Odyssey absolutely delivers on the epic side of things (and the cool—if slightly deranged and deadly—artificial intelligences). Stanley Kubrick’s 1968 epic (written by sci-fi master Arthur C. Stream 2001: A Space Odyssey on HBO Max or rent it on Prime Video.

Sebagaimana diketahui, if you’re looking for more existential missions with somewhat reluctant heroes in space, project hail mary is your next stop. It’s got the same emotional volume and big ideas as Interstellar, and fans of Nolan’s film will love it. Brilliant molecular biologist Ryland Grace (Ryan Gosling) winds up forced to go on what is assumed to be a fatal, one-way mission into deep space to try to find a way to save humanity, unexpectedly assisted by a charming alien he names Rocky. When the Sun begins to dim due to the interference of an alien entity, scientists identify the one nearby star that isn’t being similarly affected. Stream Project Hail Mary on MGM+ or Philo, or rent it on Prime Video.

Diungkapkan bahwa part of what makes interstellar so compelling is the stakes: the human race is slowly dying, and a handful of people must make incredible sacrifices to save it. That’s the vibe of Sunshine, set in a future where the Sun is dimming and a spacecraft is dispatched to deliver an enormous bomb designed to reignite the Sun’s fusion cycle. But the mission is the second attempt after the first ship vanished mysteriously seven years earlier, and when the new crew stumbles on the derelict wreck of the first mission, things quickly descend into violence and madness—but the crew remains determined to save the world, no matter the cost. Rent Sunshine on Prime Video.

Sebagaimana diketahui, interstellar works in large part because of the emotional dynamics at play. As she slowly builds to an understanding of how the aliens communicate and perceive time itself, her own heartbreak and loss come into play, giving this film a similarly devastating emotional punch. McConaughey’s character leaves his children behind and is forced to witness them growing up without him, missing out on their lives and saddled with the knowledge that they resent him despite the necessity of his mission. Arrival is a First Contact story focused on language—linguist Louise Banks (Amy Adams) is drafted into an effort to understand the strange, complex language of the aliens. Stream Arrival on Kanopy or Hoopla, or rent it on Prime Video.

Berdasarkan laporan, family dynamics and the toll of lonely space missions fuel ad astra, a film with the same emotional core as interstellar. When bursts of energy emanating from Neptune threaten to end life on Earth, his son, Roy (Brad Pitt), is dispatched to try to make contact with his father. Thirteen years ago, Earth lost contact with him. It’s an epic journey with a powerful climax that will satisfy fans of Interstellar in every way. Twenty-nine years ago, famed astronaut Clifford McBride (Tommy Lee Jones) led the Lima Project, a space station around Neptune searching for intelligent life. Stream Ad Astra on Netflix or rent it on Prime Video.

Berdasarkan laporan, ridley scott’s prequel to alien has its flaws, but if you’re looking for a sense of epic spacefaring adventure in the same key as interstellar, it’s perfect. Accompanied by a colorful crew and the android David, they discover an apparently abandoned outpost of the species dubbed the Engineers. When two scientists discover a star map apparently left behind by ancient aliens, they secure funding from the Wayland Corporation to organize a space expedition to the indicated planet. The story wrestles with questions about humanity’s origins, purpose, and potential—but this being an Alien film, things quickly turn horrifying. Rent Prometheus on Prime Video.

Sebagaimana diketahui, adapted from carl sagan’s 1985 novel, contact follows astronomer dr. The signal turns out to be a set of instructions for constructing a one-person spacecraft of some kind, and Arroway is eventually selected as the candidate to take the journey. Plus, there’s the added bonus of seeing one of the greatest trick shots in cinematic history. Ellie Arroway (Jodie Foster), who becomes involved with an effort to decipher a signal originating from the star Vega. There’s a sense of courage in the face of the unknown that’s similar to Interstellar, as well as the thrill of strapping into a spaceship and pressing the ignition. Rent Contact on Prime Video.

Berdasarkan laporan, stanislaw lem’s 1961 novel solaris explores what lem saw as the impossibility of ever understanding a truly alien life. If your favorite part of Interstellar is the ending when things get trippy and weird, you’ll probably love Solaris. The two major adaptations—Andrei Tarkovsky's 1972 version and Steven Soderbergh’s 2002 take starring George Clooney—are both worth watching, but Tarkovsky’s film is a masterpiece of psychological horror. The story is set mainly aboard a space station orbiting a planet covered in what appears to be a sentient "ocean" and chronicles the strange haunting and inexplicable experiences of the humans living on the station. Stream Solaris on HBO Max, Plex, or Tubi, or rent it on Prime Video.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the story of a mission to jupiter’s moon europa to search for intelligent life, europa report has the same sense of terrifying excitement that accompanies interstellar’s missions to the different candidate planets. Leaning into the fragility of life in an environment not designed to support it, the mission crew face a steady stream of loss and danger as they work to catch sight of alien life on the frozen, deadly moon, ultimately faced with making terrifying sacrifices in order to provide humanity with the answers that it seeks. Stream Europa Report on Netflix, Kanopy, or Hoopla, or rent it on Prime Video.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, a film based on a 1956 epic science fiction poem written by a swedish nobel laureate might seem like an unlikely match for fans of interstellar, but it’s actually perfect. When one such ship, the Aniara, is damaged and veers irreversibly off course, the passengers and crew are faced with the knowledge that they will sail off into the void without hope of rescue. The film offers a different perspective on the existential crisis of humanity’s extinction, exploring the worst-case scenario to its bitter, bleak end. As the Earth becomes uninhabitable, humanity begins launching ships to colonize Mars. Within a few years, despair has driven some to suicide and madness, while others cling to the possibility that they might yet find a way back. I tested the DJI Osmo 360 II and Insta360 needs to be seriously scared

Diungkapkan bahwa the dji osmo 360 ii is the first (and, as i write this, the only) 360 camera to shoot 8k at 60fps. This makes it my top choice for high-octane 360 footage like motovlogging or extreme sports. S. Unlike its predecessor, the 360 II has user-replaceable lenses, and while battery life isn’t mind-blowing, it’s good enough at 8K/60fps. The only things I don’t like about the Osmo 360 II are its sky-high U. price and the internal audio wind reduction, which isn’t anything to write home about.

Diungkapkan bahwa why you can trust tom's guide our writers and editors spend hours analyzing and reviewing products, services, and apps to help find what's best for you. Find out more about how we test, analyze, and rate.

Diungkapkan bahwa “uh oh,” is what insta360 will doubtless have thought when the dji osmo 360 ii launched. And it should’ve been worried. Up to now, Insta360 has been the undisputed king of 360 tech. But that reign has come to an end.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, it all comes down to one thing: 8k/60fps, which the dji osmo 360 ii can shoot. Insta360 is simply not there yet with the tech, and in fairness, that’s understandable. The flagship Insta360 X6, meanwhile, cannot, topping out at 8K/50fps. 8K at 60fps in 360 degrees puts extreme demands on a pocket-sized camera, its processor, memory, battery and thermals.

Berdasarkan laporan, but somehow dji has achieved it – which means it’s now ahead in the race. Even if the Osmo 360 II isn’t the best 360 camera in every area, it does the most important thing right now. It gives content creators the flexibility of 4K reframing from 360 footage at a frame rate fast enough for high-octane footage, and usable enough for YouTube.

So should you buy this camera? Find out in my full DJI Osmo 360 II review.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, unsurprisingly, given this is a flagship 360 camera, the osmo 360 ii isn’t cheap, opening the register at a whopping $699 in the u. S. S. It’s also worth noting that, resulting from its feud with the U. S. at Amazon for the standard bundle with basic accessories. If you want accessories, the Adventure Combo I tested, with extra batteries and a selfie stick, costs $829. tariffs on Chinese goods. Of course, this is thanks to U. government, DJI has withdrawn first-party support in the States, meaning no care plans if the camera needs repair.

Sebagaimana diketahui, in the u. K. And U. K. , the Osmo 360 II starts at £509, which undercuts the Insta360 X6 by over £100. consumers also get access to a wider range of accessories bundles at Amazon, so they can tailor their spend to exactly what they need.

Sebagaimana diketahui, this pricing is comparable to the insta360 x6, which also starts at $699. If you’re on a tighter budget, though, I’d advise checking out the Insta360 X5 ($549), GoPro MAX2 ($499) or the OG DJI Osmo 360 ($494). K. , where the 360 II is both more powerful and cheaper, it’s a total no-brainer. In my opinion, the 360 II is a much better buy thanks to the higher 60fps frame rate. In the U. All shoot 8K 360 footage, just not at 60fps.

Get instant access to breaking news, the hottest reviews, great deals and helpful tips.

Berdasarkan laporan, the osmo 360 ii is designed more or less the same as its predecessor. It looks the same, measures the same, and weighs the same. 4 x 1. That means it’s a squat-looking thing, especially compared to the lankier X6. 4 x 3. It isn’t small though, at 2. 2 inches, nor is it light at 6. 4 ounces, so if you’re after something more suited to mounting on a helmet, check out an action camera like the DJI Osmo Action 6.

Versus the OG Osmo 360, there have been no radical updates to the display, which still isn’t an OLED; no updates to the internal memory, which is still 105GB (although over double the X6’s 47GB); and no updates to waterproofing, which is rated at 33 feet (half the 66 feet of the X6).

Sebagaimana diketahui, the controls are essentially the same, with two buttons on the back for recording and mode changing, a power button, and most tweaks done via the menu system or app. And while I like DJI’s menu, it’s a little busy-feeling on the small display — the X6’s bigger display makes it slightly easier to use in the heat of the moment. I found the Osmo 360 II’s record button fiddly to press with gloves on. Overall though, no major complaints controls-wise.

Berdasarkan laporan, the osmo 360 ii uses the same quick-release mounting system as the previous gen, plus other dji cameras like the osmo action 5 pro, action 6 and osmo nano. However, DJI has made a welcome quality-of-life update: the mount is now bi-directional. Previously, you had to get the mount the correct way round, which was annoying, but now it doesn’t matter. It may not sound like a big deal, but it’s kinda like going from USB-A to USB-C and makes the camera a lot quicker and easier to mount-unmount during shooting.

Diungkapkan bahwa again, the osmo 360 ii has no major updates to connectivity, with wireless data transfer, usb-c transfer and charging, and 105gb of internal memory, which should get you around 90 minutes of 8k footage — fantastic when you fill or forget a card. There’s Bluetooth and 2. 4G for pairing to your phone, but DJI has added NFC connectivity which means you can pair the Osmo 360 II to your phone instantly just by placing the two together.

Diungkapkan bahwa where there has been a substantive update is lenses. The original Osmo 360 had non-replaceable lenses, which was a major drawback given all the competition had replaceable ones. 360 lenses are very easy to damage (in fact, my OG 360 was hit by a rock from a semi truck during testing, and DJI had to supply me with a replacement), so replaceable lenses are a huge deal.

Diungkapkan bahwa the osmo 360 had to be sent back to dji for repair, which would be fine if you purchased a dji care plan… only, you couldn’t buy one of those in the u. S. due to DJI’s ongoing feud with the federal government.

Berdasarkan laporan, thankfully, the simple solution has been employed, and the osmo 360 ii has replaceable lenses. Annoyingly, you can’t find official DJI replacement kits on Amazon (another repercussion of that feud with the government). K. In the U. , this isn’t an issue, and an official DJI lens replacement kit will cost you just £22 at Amazon.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, as always these days, dji’s stabilization is pretty darn good. In most reframed 360 footage, you’ll be cropping a full 360 view down quite a bit, giving ample headroom for software stabilization (which is applied automatically by the app/desktop app in post production). I noticed a few jitters in wider fields of view, but nothing major.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, in single-lens mode, the camera uses dji’s usual rocksteady in-camera stabilization, and it works a treat. As you can see in the single-lens footage below, everything is beautifully smooth.

Diungkapkan bahwa the osmo 360 ii’s headline feature is the most important: 8k/60fps. When recording high-octane footage, which is what 360 cameras are commonly used for, 60fps is a fast enough frame rate for smooth-looking footage. Fast-paced footage looks great at 60fps, with no choppiness whatsoever.

Diungkapkan bahwa the original osmo 360 and insta360 x6 could only shoot at up to 50fps, which they might as well not do. 50fps is better than 30fps at smoothing out fast-moving footage, but is only really applicable to European television operating at 50Hz. The standards for online content, like YouTube, are 60fps for high octane and 30fps for everything else.

Diungkapkan bahwa thanks to 8k 360 footage, there’s also enough resolution headroom to reframe to 16:9 and maintain 4k when exporting. This all means that the Osmo 360 II is the first (and, as I write, only) 360 camera to let you shoot high-octane footage at high resolution and at a high frame rate.

Diungkapkan bahwa the dual sensors in the 360 ii are the same 1/1. 1-Inch Square CMOS sensors as the OG 360. Frame rate is mainly decided by a camera’s image processing capabilities, and so that’s where the improvements have been made.

Berdasarkan laporan, unsurprisingly, given dji is no newcomer to all this, footage looks excellent. The lenses are sharp, while colors look vivid but natural — more natural than Insta360’s typically saturated look.

Diungkapkan bahwa obviously, as a 360 camera, the primary benefit is ultimate framing flexibility. Shoot first, choose your fields of view and camera angles later. Aside from the selfie stick dead spot under the camera (which always shows on 360 cameras), stitching wasn’t noticeable, even at ultra-wide FoVs or in 360 modes like ‘Tiny Planet’, which is great.

Diungkapkan bahwa with the new processing comes 14. in the equivalent SuperNight mode on both cameras at 8K/30p, the Osmo 360 II's footage looks brighter, sharper and less noisy than the OG Osmo 360. As such, the Osmo 360 II handles radical shifts in lighting very well, maintaining shadow detail and decreasing the frequency of blown-out highlights. 5 stops of dynamic range. This also benefits low-light performance, with the Osmo 360 II proving a substantial step up over its predecessor. A solid upgrade, helped by the new processors.

Diungkapkan bahwa like most 360 cameras, you can also shoot in single-lens mode at up to 4k/120fps, using the osmo 360 ii like a traditional action cam. There’s a new mode called ‘Boost’ video which supposedly offers better quality than the normal video mode.

Sebagaimana diketahui, i asked dji about this, but it was fairly tight-lipped on the technical explanation, telling me the mode simply widens the field of view to use more of the sensor — presumably the camera then oversamples the 4k output for a sharper image. As the whole (or most of) the sensor is being used, stabilization is affected, so standard video mode is better for shakier scenarios.

The Osmo 360 II packs some useful features for professional users or hardcore creators, including 10-bit color for extra flexibility when editing, and D-Log M for wider dynamic range capture when footage is going to be graded in post later.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the osmo 360 ii introduces a wind-shielded mic, helping to physically reduce wind buffeting alongside the in-camera wind reduction software algorithms. Overall, wind reduction is fine. There are three modes: ‘Standard’, ‘High’ and ‘Smart’ (which automatically adjusts between the first two). If you’re shooting in particularly windy conditions, like motorcycling, ‘High’ works well to reduce wind noise, although the microphones didn’t handle the loud noise of an engine particularly well, with some clipping — you can dial in some minus gain to help with this.

I wouldn’t say the Osmo 360 II’s internal audio is much better or worse than the X6, although both lose out to the Insta360 X5 — despite being a generation old now, the X5 still packs the best internal audio of any 360 camera I’ve tested.

Berdasarkan laporan, naturally, as a dji product, the osmo 360 ii can hook up wirelessly over osmoaudio to wireless dji mics, like the dji mic 3 or dji mic mini 2s. As they share an ecosystem, you get lots of control over the mics in-camera — control you wouldn’t get by simply connecting over Bluetooth. OsmoAudio is essentially Bluetooth, so audio quality in high dynamic range environments (like motorcycling) isn’t fantastic, but is more than enough for quieter scenarios and vlogging.

Berdasarkan laporan, the dji mimo smartphone app is fairly solid these days. A few years back it was rather basic, but DJI has made strides to compete with Insta360’s app and the GoPro Quik app. There’s not much between them now, although Insta360’s app remains the easiest and most intuitive to use, especially for a straight-to-social workflow.

Sebagaimana diketahui, mimo gives you a wide range of editing features, effects and export settings. Mimo feels more like a tool for whipping together quick client previews, assuming you’ll finesse footage later on a desktop. It lets you do the basics, but I find reframing via keyframes a lot more clunky on Mimo versus the Insta360 app. The Insta360 app makes it easier to put out smooth, polished content directly from your phone.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, dji has a big advantage for pros and serious creators, though. Both Insta360 and DJI offer desktop editing apps for more serious editing. However, pros will need their camera to fit in with existing workflows, and while both brands offer Premiere Pro 360 plug-ins, only DJI has them for DaVinci Resolve.

Berdasarkan laporan, the osmo 360 ii’s battery life is a mixed bag. It features a bigger battery than the original Osmo 360, boosted from 1,950mAh to 2,150mAh. Despite this, in my standardized indoor tests, the Osmo 360 II only managed 88 minutes at 8K/30fps versus 112 minutes on the original model. Both pale in comparison to the 2,600mAh Insta360 X6, which managed 117 minutes at 8K/30fps.

Berdasarkan laporan, that said, the og model dropped off a cliff at higher frame rates. The Osmo 360 II ran for 66 minutes at 8K/60fps and while it overheated after 45 minutes, it disabled its screen and ran for a further 21 minutes until dying. You’ll get longer while on the move, as wind chill will mean less thermal throttling. At 8K/50fps, the original camera only managed 30 minutes in my testing. Still, 8K/60fps is no easy task, so 66 minutes is impressive.

Berdasarkan laporan, at 8k/50fps, the osmo 360 managed 77 minutes and overheated after around 50 (but again soldiered on, thermally throttled, for another 25 minutes. The X6 managed 90 minutes at 8K/50fps, but overheated every 20 minutes.

Diungkapkan bahwa at 4k/60fps in single-lens mode, the osmo 360 managed just over 80 minutes. The X6, meanwhile, overheated at 33 minutes and only managed 56 minutes in total at 4K/60fps. Again, in the indoor stress test conditions, it overheated and thermally throttled itself after around 50 minutes, but kept on shooting for another half an hour before dying. Windchill will solve this. Like I said, the Osmo 360 II’s battery life is a mixed bag, but where it counts at 60fps, it’s impressive.

Berdasarkan laporan, oof. When I reviewed the original Osmo 360, my sentiment was: “It’s a good start, but needs work. ” Well, DJI has done the work, and a lot of it. The Osmo 360 II is the first 360 camera to reach 8K/60fps, making it ideal for creators who want the benefits of 360 recording without sacrificing frame rate.

Berdasarkan laporan, the osmo 360 ii isn’t perfect, and whether you need this or the insta360 x6 will, to a large extent, depend on what you’re doing or shooting. If your priority is a straight-to-social workflow, Insta360 still has the edge.

Diungkapkan bahwa however, the margins between the two are mostly minor, all except one: frame rate. — there’s now only one camera to recommend. If you shoot high-octane footage — motovlogging, snowboarding, skydiving, etc. It has to be the Osmo 360 II.

#363. Garmin Cyclists Can Now Make Themselves Appear on Waze in Real Time

📅 11 Nov 2026

Garmin Cyclists Can Now Make Themselves Appear on Waze in Real Time

Tanggal: 11 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://lifehacker.com/health/garmin-cyclists-can-now-show-up-on-waze?utm_medium=RSS

Cyclists who ride with Garmin gear can now appear as live, moving icons on the Waze driving app, and nearby drivers will receive an alert to slow down and watch for them on the road.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, for riders already using garmin devices, opting in costs nothing and adds a new layer of safety, particularly on roads where drivers may not expect cyclists. The feature is rolling out now, but you should be aware of its limitations.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, riders can simply opt in once through garmin connect. After that, sharing starts automatically when an outdoor cycling activity begins and stops when the ride ends. While a ride is underway, Waze users near the cyclist see a cyclist icon move along the road and receive a Live Cycling Alert reminding them to slow down and stay aware.

Diungkapkan bahwa the feature runs on livetrack, garmin's existing live location-sharing tool, which lets friends and family follow a rider's real-time location, speed, course, and more. Garmin says this collaboration extends that peace of mind to motorists, giving them greater awareness of their surroundings.

Berdasarkan laporan, garmin notes its location sharing is temporary and session-based. The rider's name, identity, and route are hidden, and no personal information is shared or displayed in Waze. Drivers see only an anonymous icon and the alert.

You'll need a few things to get this feature up and running:.

A compatible Garmin Edge bike computer or Garmin watch.

A phone running Garmin Connect with a data connection.

An outdoor cycling activity (the feature doesn't apply to indoor rides).

The good news is using the feature is free: LiveTrack costs nothing on compatible Garmin bike computers and watches, and Waze is free for drivers.

This new feature is a great safety perk, but there are real-world caveats worth considering:.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, this feature is for waze only. Alerts reach drivers only when Waze is open on their phone. Google Maps, which has far more users, is excluded, so a large portion of the drivers you share the road with won't see you this way.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, it depends on your phone's signal. Your position travels from the Garmin to your phone, then to Garmin's servers, then to Waze, and finally to the driver's phone. On a patchy rural signal, a few seconds of lag could put the icon on the wrong side of a bend from where you actually are. A rider who leaves their phone at home or whose phone loses signal simply won't show up on a Waze map, as a ride without a data connection is invisible to Waze.

Sebagaimana diketahui, finally, remember to treat this safety feature as an extra perk, not a guarantee. At the end of the day, it isn't a replacement for bike lights, bright clothing, and defensive riding.

#364. Climate Change Has Pushed the World's Ice Out of Its Safe Zone

📅 12 Nov 2026

Climate Change Has Pushed the World's Ice Out of Its Safe Zone

Tanggal: 12 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.wired.com/story/climate-change-abolishes-ice/

The world is no longer safe for frozen H2O.

New research published in Science on Thursday shows that the conditions that have kept ice, frozen soil, and snow stable are slipping away due to the burning of fossil fuels—and the implications are grave for the entire globe.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the climate of the past 12,000 or so years has been remarkably steady. That’s allowed for all kinds of wonderful things to happen, like human civilization flourishing. But rising temperatures are pushing the climate outside that envelope, and the new research looks at what the team behind the new findings has called the “safe operating space” for the icy, snowy landscape known as the cryosphere.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the scientists looked at changes to polar sea and land ice, mountain glaciers, permafrost, and snow cover over the past 12 millennia to analyze conditions that have allowed both civilization and other ecosystems to thrive. They then identified boundaries on those conditions that, if crossed, would upend the stability and safety humans have enjoyed for millennia.

Berdasarkan laporan, the results show an “accelerating and partly irreversible loss of cryospheric integrity. ” Arctic and Antarctic sea ice have both fallen outside the safe operating threshold, as have snow cover and the area of permafrost—frozen soil laden with carbon. While land ice hasn’t yet fallen out of its safe space, it’s on the brink. And because of warming that’s already been locked into the climate system, it’s likely to also fall outside the threshold in the coming centuries.

Berdasarkan laporan, while it may feel like the antarctic ice sheet or permafrost covering alaska are distant concerns, they’re anything but. The West Antarctic Ice Sheet, which a growing body of evidence shows is nearing the brink of irreversible decline, has enough ice to raise sea levels by 11 feet (3 meters). Permafrost, meanwhile, holds trillions of tons of carbon dioxide. Any degradation means that CO2, as well as even more potent methane, could end up in the atmosphere, accelerating global warming even further. Other examples of major risks abound, including how melting Greenland land ice could slow down or even collapse the ocean conveyor belt that helps keep Europe temperate.

“The consequences of a changing cryosphere extend beyond regions where ice and snow are disappearing,” says Albert Norström, a climate researcher at the Stockholm Resilience Center who co-authored the new paper.

Berdasarkan laporan, dipping outside the safe operating space doesn’t mean that the world will see 11 feet of sea level rise in the next year, a trillion-ton co2 eruption, or a day after tomorrow scenario. But it does mean that the odds of crossing dangerous tipping points are rising.

Sebagaimana diketahui, “as we scratch 1. 5 [degrees Celsius] and go above it, we are just really gambling with potentially triggering some of these Earth system tipping points,” Norström says. The safe operating space framework also “takes a broader perspective” that assesses slower changes over time and “how far, in this case, the cryosphere is moving away from the conditions that have supported a relatively stable Earth system,” he adds.

Sebagaimana diketahui, cutting emissions is the most obvious and straightforward way to stop the cryosphere from sliding further outside our comfort zone. But there are a growing number of proposals to pursue more radical interventions that could protect the world’s ice. Scientists have already draped glaciers in the Alps in blankets during the summer to prevent melting. Other researchers have explored techniques to pump cold sea water to the surface to help thicken ice and modeled whether a manmade barrier could stabilize the West Antarctic Ice Sheet.

Berdasarkan laporan, these geoengineering approaches have the potential to be costly, and there’s no guarantee they would work. They’d also do nothing to stop the root cause of warming: burning fossil fuels. Norström says emissions cuts are the most urgent way to protect ice and snow (and ourselves), but with the cryosphere sliding into a more dangerous space, “in principle, we shouldn't put the lid on” research for more far-flung interventions.

Diungkapkan bahwa “the safe operating space is a precautionary framework,” he says. “It ensures that we try to stay as far downstream from the point where these really potentially existential or huge consequences and risks can happen. ”.

#369. The Robot I Didn’t Expect to Build

📅 19 Oct 2026

The Robot I Didn’t Expect to Build

Tanggal: 19 Oct 2026 | Sumber: https://spectrum.ieee.org/agility-robotics-digit-5-redesign

Agility Robotics’ first practical robotic worker is nothing like I dreamed.

Author and Agility Robotics co-founder Jonathan Hurst next to his new Digit 5 humanoid robot worker.

Sebagaimana diketahui, agility robotics, the company i cofounded out of my robotics lab at oregon state university in 2015, has just launched digit 5. It’s designed to be the first humanoid robot that can safely and economically do useful work at scale, allowing us to bring tens of thousands of humanoid workers into the real world. Engineered to lift 23-kilogram bins onto high shelves and with a battery that can run for 90 minutes on a 9-minute charge, Digit 5’s goal is to handle heavy warehouse tasks shift after shift, filling the need for labor in jobs that are too physically stressful or too dull for humans to want to do.

Sebagaimana diketahui, digit 5 is what agility has been working toward for over a decade. But the robot is heavy and bulky, lacking the graceful natural motion of its predecessors, and it’s farther than I thought possible from the robot I dreamed of building when I started this company. To deliver a useful commercial product, Agility has taken a path that is very different from what I first imagined.

Sebagaimana diketahui, my dream has always been to build robots that combine locomotion and manipulation to move through the world and interact with it as people do. I seek a mastery of motion, achieved through devices designed to navigate the constraints of physics with elegance. When I started the Dynamic Robotics Laboratory at Oregon State in 2008, we began with a theory derived from decades of work in biomechanics: that a simple “spring-mass” model (a body supported by legs that act like springs) should be able to reproduce every known walking and running gait found in animals.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, we put theory into practice by building the bipedal robot atrias—short for “assume the robot is a sphere,” a joke among physicists about reducing a complex system to its simplest possible form. ATRIAS looked like a large microwave on stilts because it was only intended to demonstrate the physics of human walking and running. This was the first glimmer of achieving my dream; even though ATRIAS wasn’t designed to look like us, it still seemed natural, and even somehow alive, when it settled into a walking gait.

Diungkapkan bahwa with the success of atrias, the barriers to progress shifted from scientific to engineering and organizational, and a startup company seemed like the way to bridge the gap from a one-off research concept to an actual robotic product. I felt confident of two things: that I would be able to build robots that could go where people go, and that this capability would be incredibly useful. This combination of ambition and naivete is necessary for anyone to found a new company—how hard could it be?.

Diungkapkan bahwa good advice for starting a company is to understand a customer problem, and then find a way to solve it using your unique capabilities. We relied on our belief that this technology would enable new possibilities and trusted ourselves to figure out the business as we went. My cofounders, Damion Shelton and Mikhail Jones, and I did not do this. So we simply focused on building our first product: the bipedal robot Cassie.

Berdasarkan laporan, cassie was the first dynamic bipedal robot that researchers could buy, able to maintain its balance through active, fluid motion rather than careful, rigid steps. It was not intended to be commercially useful, and had no torso, arms, or head. It had ostrichlike legs, not because we were imitating ground-running birds, but as a result of engineering strictly for performance. We sold Cassie robots to Harvard, Caltech, the University of Michigan, the University of California, Berkeley, and a handful of other research institutions, ultimately saturating the market for US $250,000 bipedal research robots after having sold a total of 10 of them.

Diungkapkan bahwa atrias, cassie, and digit 4 evt [left to right] are on display at agility robotics’ robofab in salem, ore. The 70,000-square-foot facility has the capacity to produce more than 10,000 Digit 5 robots per year. Agility Robotics.

Berdasarkan laporan, because cassie’s hardware enabled research into the physics of walking and running, the legged-robot research frontier shifted to control software. Traditionally, engineers controlled legged robots with detailed mathematical models that determined how the machines should move. With Cassie, researchers pioneered the new approach of reinforcement learning for bipedal legged locomotion: A simulated robot learns through trial and error, and the resulting neural network controls the physical machine. This approach is what enables virtually all of the dynamic behaviors that you see on legged robots today, and Cassie looked alive as it recovered from stumbles while climbing stairs, ran 5 kilometers across the Oregon State campus, and broke the robot world record for a 100-meter dash.

Sebagaimana diketahui, cassie got us closer to being able to move through the world with confidence and grace, but to make it useful, we needed manipulation. After exhaustively exploring different configurations, we found that an upright torso helped the robot balance, while two arms mounted near the top of the torso allowed it to pick up large objects and to catch itself when it fell. Digit 1, which added a torso and arms to the Cassie legs, was our first mobile manipulation robot, and another step on the path toward a product that could do useful work for commercial customers.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, as we explored the first applications for digit, potential customers kept asking us: why legs? and why a humanoid? these were tough questions for me to answer, because they exposed a core business reality: it didn’t matter to agility robotics if we solved a cool science problem in a beautiful way. What mattered to the business was solving real problems for customers.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, after years of engagement with industry partners, we found one answer in warehouses and manufacturing facilities: moving bins. Because the task can vary widely from one deployment to another, it hasn’t been broadly addressed by single-purpose automation. Bin handling is a clearly defined task where two arms are needed to lift large bins up high and legs are the best way to balance and move in narrow spaces. Yet it was constrained enough to give Digit an economically viable first job while it developed a broader set of skills.

Diungkapkan bahwa in 2019, digit began demonstrating its capabilities to do real work. With Ford Motor Company, we showed how Digit 1 could carry packages from an autonomous vehicle to a front porch. We developed Digit 2 and 3 while working with a certain global package delivery company on moving and sorting cardboard boxes. Amazon tested Digit 4 on moving and stacking bins, and it became the world’s first commercially deployed humanoid at the logistics provider GXO. In 2024, Digit appeared on the cover of Time magazine.

Sebagaimana diketahui, despite digit’s apparent success, we began to run into conflicts between my dream and the needs of actual customers. If bins weren’t moving, our customers were losing money. We spent a huge amount of time and effort keeping our first deployments operational, which arguably eliminated any profit we made. We were no longer working with relatively patient university research labs. Agility has to sell robots to survive, and customers will only purchase robots that provide value. Yet this also kept our company learning and alive the way no lab demo ever could.

Sebagaimana diketahui, i had no idea how hard it would be, or that running a company would involve so many things that have nothing to do with solving technical problems: deployments across the country; shipping, service, and customer support; fundraising and investor relations; more fundraising; human resources and it; developing fleet-management software; managing a supply chain; and even more fundraising. I had no experience with any of these things. My career had focused on solving the technical challenges of robots interacting with the world, and it turned out that was only a tiny piece of building a successful robotics company. But Agility was the only path I saw to continuing the technical work and having an impact.

Sebagaimana diketahui, i knew that agility needed to focus more on robots as a product, but i didn’t know how to make that happen. Hiring the people we needed to run the company meant giving up an immense amount of control, but we had no other choice. We recruited a new executive team with the experience required to commercialize this new technology, and they quickly made changes that were both painful and necessary.

Berdasarkan laporan, digit versions 1, 2, and 3 [left to right] show the evolution of the robot from a dynamic walking platform into a useful mobile manipulator. Agility.

Sebagaimana diketahui, we had intended the next revision of digit, digit 4 evt (engineering validation and test), to be a relatively minor upgrade. But Agility’s new leadership insisted that the robot was missing key features that were essential if Digit was going to become a real product. So Digit 4 EVT instead incorporated a series of major changes in a highly compressed timeline, such as larger batteries and system-wide upgrades for safety and regulatory compliance, which added enough mass to dramatically alter the robot’s appearance and capabilities.

Sebagaimana diketahui, while early digits were headless, agility robotics was able to justify a head for digit 4 to optimize antenna and camera placement, and it turned out to be surprisingly useful for human-robot interaction. Christie Hemm Klok.

Berdasarkan laporan, i could only watch as others brought their own talents to bear to make digit into a successful product, in gut-wrenching ways that didn’t always align with my vision. I had to accept that Digit had grown far beyond me, and look for ways of influencing decisions rather than directing them. There were some especially difficult times when I felt like there were compromises made that didn’t seem necessary, but making those decisions was no longer my sole responsibility. In the moment, it was incredibly frustrating, as Digit 4 EVT took a few steps backward from my vision of how humanoids should look and move.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, agility is in our name because agility is core to the future of the company. And yet, through Digit 4 EVT’s commercial deployments, we began to really understand specific applications and what they required. I want Digit to be lithe and graceful. The design process became a ruthless triage, with aesthetics and elegance of movement being delayed over and over again in favor of brutal functionality. When people see Digit, I want them to like the robot, to understand what it can do at a glance, and to feel that it’s there to help. But with Digit 4 EVT, all of that was sacrificed to functionality, because of course it had to be—the customer just needs the robot to do the work. For an engineer whose mind lives more in the future than in the present, it has been hard for me to accept this trajectory. We mapped the first 10 use cases Digit would perform, and then began designing Digit 5 from scratch based on everything we had learned.

Berdasarkan laporan, digit 5 will be agility’s first real step toward a general-purpose robot. It marks our transition from imagining what a future humanoid robot should be to designing a product around the realities of customer deployments. These realities include things like European CE regulatory compliance, North American UL electrical-safety certifications, and Federal Communications Commission limits for electromagnetic radiation—all of which felt tangential to my dream for Digit, but were absolute requirements.

Sebagaimana diketahui, digit 5 is designed to be the first humanoid robot that can operate safely next to human coworkers while working 20 hours a day and lifting more than a human can. Christie Hemm Klok.

Berdasarkan laporan, customer requirements helped us realize that safety in particular was one of the most critical barriers to scaling. This seemed silly to me, because I’ve never felt that our robots were dangerous, but we have to prove that they’re safe. In Digit 4’s commercial deployments, the robots had to work behind physical barriers, separated from humans at all times, to meet insurance and regulatory demands. And since keeping the robots in safety cages severely limited their usefulness, enabling Digit 5 to operate safely around people became a primary design goal. We spent two years on this challenge.

Diungkapkan bahwa digit 5 is designed to be the first humanoid robot that can operate safely next to human coworkers. It will rely on an array of sensors to locate nearby people in a manner that’s certifiably safe, and then take actions based on that information. As a person approaches, Digit 5 is programmed to stop what it’s doing, set down its payload, sit on the floor, and cut power to its motors before the person gets close enough to touch the robot. This conservative approach reduces the risk to nearby people in a verifiable way, and we believe it’s the only approach that makes sense as a first step toward working alongside humans.

Diungkapkan bahwa yet this strategy also feels like a massive slowdown on the path toward robots becoming part of everyday life. Enabling coexistence with humans has influenced almost every aspect of Digit 5’s design: the shape of the legs and the body, the safety-rated sensors within protective housings, the isolated computers dedicated to safety, and more. All of these features increase the robot’s complexity, power consumption, mass, and physical size.

Digit 5 is Agility’s largest, heaviest, strongest, and most capable humanoid robot worker.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the robot’s design was driven by safety, with integrated protection for the robot and for the humans it will work around. Agility Robotics.

Diungkapkan bahwa weighing over 120 kg, digit 5 is a huge robot. The dock will deliver 240 amperes at 48 volts, which is enough current to make its thick charging cables visibly wiggle under the induced magnetic forces, while powerful fans blow air through cooling channels in the robot’s torso to keep the battery from overheating. National Institute for Occupational Safety and Health guidelines for human workers, which include repeatedly lifting 23-kg bins and reaching shelves 1. S. This requires motors with enough power and torque to lift the load, but also enough precision to delicately control the force Digit applies when it makes contact with the world. 75 meters high. It needed to achieve the lifting limits recommended under the U. To power those motors, we needed a large battery and a dock for rapid autonomous charging. Digit is designed to perform tasks like these for 20 hours a day—something no human can do. The battery and cooling system takes up about 75 percent of Digit’s torso, but it will allow the robot to operate for 90 minutes and fully recharge during a 9-minute break, enabling near-continuous work.

Sebagaimana diketahui, all of this extra bulk means that digit 5 can no longer run or jump the way previous generations could, and the svelte form i imagined has become physically impossible. But looking at the situation rationally, I believe this trade-off is necessary for any company that claims its humanoid can do this kind of work today: If you see a robot that looks like a human working in a factory or warehouse, it either can’t lift the required weight or can’t make it through the whole shift. In some ways, Digit 5 feels more like a forklift than the graceful humanoid I set out to build. And if it’s not covered with sensors, it’s likely not safe to stand next to.

Diungkapkan bahwa the most visible change with digit 5 is that humanlike legs replace the ostrichlike legs of our earlier versions. While the “backward” leg configuration was optimized for walking and running, we discovered that it created problems with squatting because the ankle will strike the ground. Digit 5 will spend a lot of time lifting heavy objects from near the floor, so we used a humanoid leg configuration with knee and hip motors that both contribute torque to help the robot stand up again.

Diungkapkan bahwa when digit detects an approaching human, the robot will lower itself to the floor and cut power to its motors. Agility believes this is the only near-term approach to verifiably reduce risk when the robot is working near people. Agility Robotics.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, other companies building humanoid robots have copied the human form without ever understanding its purpose. Yet I know that we arrived at this shape based purely on functional engineering choices. It’s very frustrating that, to an outside observer, it now looks like we discarded Agility’s distinctive leg design and simply did what everyone else was doing. Making a robot look like a human is the easy part—without the function to match, and the understanding of the physics underlying that function, the whole point of the human form may be lost.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, with the power, battery life, and safety features that we are designing into digit 5, we will have a truly useful robot. But it also compromises on some things that are core to my vision and mission. I understand why we made the choices we did and can justify them all, but together they leave me unsatisfied. It’s the curse of the engineer.

Sebagaimana diketahui, i believe digit 5 will be the scaling moment for agility robotics, the inflection point where we can begin deploying robots in large numbers. Its interchangeable tool interfaces and modular design will enable us to gradually upgrade its subsystems. While the robot will continue carrying bins, our road map includes many more tasks, from picking individual items and tending machines, to preparing parts for assembly and shipping, and eventually doing assembly work itself. It will be a platform for improvement, a source of data for future behavior training, and a viable product all at the same time.

Berdasarkan laporan, hurst stands between the previous version of digit, digit 4 [left], and digit 5. Christie Hemm Klok.

Diungkapkan bahwa but i cannot love digit 5. However, I now recognize that tackling these challenges was always necessary. Customers and product requirements didn’t ruin my vision; they revealed what my vision was missing. In the beginning, I envisioned steady progress on agility and dexterity, with each version becoming more dynamically capable. It’s the largest, heaviest, most expensive robot Agility will ever build, full of design compromises that enable it to be exactly the robot it needs to be right now rather than the robot I dreamed of. Instead, developing Digit 5 has required large detours to incorporate requirements that seemed unrelated to my original vision. This is how robots will achieve commercial success and make a real-world impact, which will bring me closer to my scientific dream as well.

Diungkapkan bahwa we won’t have a humanoid that matches the capabilities of humans until it achieves that mastery of motion that inspired me to found agility over a decade ago. I saw glimmers of it with the spring-mass locomotion of ATRIAS, and more glimmers with Cassie’s running gait.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, i know that such mastery is physically possible with the tools and hardware that we have right now, and despite all of its compromises, digit 5 will give us a practical foundation for pursuing that dream. I want every future version of Digit to be lighter and more graceful, to interact more naturally with humans, and to be better at manipulating objects and moving through the world, enabling robots to enter aspects of our lives that they haven’t been able to help with before. By the time I’m old enough to need assistance at home, I expect Digit will be up to the task.

Diungkapkan bahwa with digit 5, agility has built a robot that will be useful in our world. Now I’m getting back to work to make it beautiful, too.

This article appears in the November 2026 print issue.

Diungkapkan bahwa jonathan w. Hurst is the co-founder and chief robot officer of Agility Robotics and a robotics professor at Oregon State University.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, this is the most honest account i've read from a robotics founder. The tension between engineering vision and commercial reality is something every robotics founder will face. While Tesla and Figure are still showing demos, Agility has actually deployed robots in real customer environments, moved over 100,000 totes at GXO, and hit 98% accuracy at Schaeffler. That's real engineering for real problems. 75 m shelves. Digit 5's specs are driven entirely by what customers need: 20 hours of work per day, 9-minute charge, 23 kg lift to 1. Professor Hurst lays it out without spin.

Sebagaimana diketahui, why humanoid though? in particular, why bi-pedal? why use legs at all? are wheels surely better and easier? legs seem like unnecessary complexity. Wheels on 'legs" for suspension can be a great alternative. I don't understand the obsession with humanoid form?.

Sebagaimana diketahui, it seems to me that even at scale production, the robot we employ in industry should do jobs people cannot. Highly radioactive, highly toxic, and factors where the atmosphere needs to be unsuitable for humans. e. i. , oxygen-deprived environment or low pressure/vacuum. Or use them on the 3rd shift when people are less willing to work.

Sebagaimana diketahui, robots should increase manufacturing that was impossible to do in the past. We should be exploring new types of manufacturing, not replacing people in manufacturing that humans can do. That's how you create growth.
